Okay, so I'm gonna write an honest review for this game.
Yes, it does have it's down sides, including bugs, cheaters and loading errors.
But, it does also have it's good sides too.
One of the main factors I cannot stress enough about this game, is that it isn't pay to win.. it's play to win. You can't expect to do well on your first game, it won't happen. When I first bought the game, and loaded into my first match, I thought I stood a good chance. I was wrong. So. Very. Wrong. I quit the game, obviously, and stopped playing after a few games. However, now that I have come back to it, having learnt skills such as inventory managment, map locations, render distance tactics etc, I am beginning to get better, placing top 25 on most games.
Now that I've bigged the game up a little, you need to know the bad points. I won't go too in but here they are.
- You are going to find the occasional hacker.
It isn't a common thing, but when they pop up, they'll make you mad. You've got your gear, your guns, your armour and everything only to be greeted by a snap shot shotgun bullet to the face. RIP. Yes, hackers are an issue.
- Bugs.
Not that I have come across many in my time of playing, but I do see many people complaining about them.
- Loading errors
These I tend to come across when playing with friends. After clicking confirm on a game, the screen appears to say 'loading you in to the game momentarily' (or something like that). And that may be the case if 'momentarily' means a millenium. Just leave and reload that game.
That's pretty much all the bad points about this game.
Overall, this game is insanely fun to play - especially with friends - and I would 10/10 recommend to anyone considering buying this game.

I love TF2, it's one of my favorite games, but f*ck it, let's look at the many wise desisions TF2 made over the last year or so.
-Problem: Players are getting bored, and want new weapons to spice up the game.
-Solution: Create weapon skins only obtainable by buying a 6 dollar ticket, or going on the marketplace. Also, you can only get strange ones by getting crates only obtainable from the event that requires a full priced key from the shop.
-Problem: The Third Degree, Sun on a Stick, and Sharpened Volcano Fragment have glaring issues, and need serious tweaking.
-Solution: Update weapons that are already okay since last update, and shake them up a bit in hopes people will forget those weapons exist.
-Problem: Some weapons were broken in the last update.
-Solution: Eeeeeh, we'll work on it next update
-Problem: People are modding the game to cheat.
-Solution: Make all servers sv_pure_1, with VERY strict mod limitations, who cares about mods anymore, anyways?
-Problem: People are wondering when rd_astroid and pl_cactuscanyon are going to leave development.
-Solution: ..... Uuhhhh.
-Problem: The End of the Line update's map looks tricky.
-Solution: Scrap it, and put in some weird duck related thing. Players love ducks.
-Problem: People are anticipating the new Festive update this year.
-Solution: More weapon skins, and some lights to festivize any of the new weapon skins instead of making new, fancy festives. They won't tell the difference!
-Problem: The modding community is still upset over sv_pure_1.
-Solution: Close blinds, play some jazz at max volume, and figure out what ticket related update we should do next using the community's ideas instead of making a new halloween boss, festive weapons, new weapons, or anything that takes big effort on our part. Whatever is most profitable with the least effort... Maybe we should reskin non-stock weapons.... Naaaaah.
-Problem: MvM players are growing restless, due to the lack of updates, balances, new maps, ect.
-Solution: Make Mannpower.
-Problem: Pyro is incredibly unbalanced. It's weapons are either too good, useless, or some strange demonic combination of both that boggles the mind, and generally makes everyone upset in the process, including Pyro mains.
-Solution: Ehhh, throw some petty buffs at it with meaningless weapon changes that ignore the class's actual problems. People will get used to the Phlog, Volcano Fragment, Backburner, and Degreacer eventually.
-Problem: Many Heavy mains are getting sick of the constant, and quite frankly random, nerfs to the class. They also want something new and zesty to play with
-Solution: HAVE PYRO AND HEAVY DUKE IT OUT!!! Whoever wins we'll START the process of actually fixing! Sure, it might tear the fanbase apart, but hey! It will be a great way to advertise the new Matchmaking system!
-Problem: There's only, like, 10 people working on the game because we don't restrict to what our employees work on, and the community is getting upset at the sudden and jarring decline of any new, meaningful content or updates.
-Solution: Say absolutely nothing about it, and continue to work on the game in hushed whispers, rather then telling the community out next steps in keeping the game fresh, whether they're good ideas or not!
-Problem: Some weapons have still not been touched after being broken a few updates ago (Ullapool Caber, Pretty Boy's Pocket Pistol, Baby Face's Blaster, ect), and fans are getting upset.
-Solution: Update OTHER weapons that are already okay since that update, and shake them up a bit in hopes people will forget those weapons exist.
"Sir this is getting ridiculous, how long are we going to keep breaking weapons and not fixing them when the balance we added clearly made everything worse!?"
"Nevermore."﻿
Again, I love you TF2.... but you're tearing me apart here.

After forcing myself to spend time to try this game, I think it's time to review it.
Pros:
- Campaign (The East Wind) has a great plot. Though the ending was a little disappointing and more of a cliffhanger. But overall, a somewhat satisfying campaign, leaving you wanting for more.
- Soundtrack great at times.
- Graphics have been polished better than before. Played this in 2014 and it was quite bad.
- Editor is fun to mess around with.
Neutral: Did not try Multiplayer and I do not intend to try it.
Cons:

Arma 3 is one of the best games for your money (especially if you buy it on sale) simply because of the sheer potential. Whether you want to play single player, multiplayer, PVE, PVP, long campaigns, short missions, fly jets, fly choppers, drive tanks, trucks, IFVS, or create your own missions it's all there.
Arma 3 boasts the best ballistics of any game out there. Firefights are truly enjoyable, and thoroughly heart pounding. You can be getting shot at from 10m or less or more than 1000m. Bullets travel in arcs, and you must learn to adjust your aim according to the distance of your target. It is like for every weapon, and vehicular weapon. Concealment, and camouflage are also realistic, and effective and add to the feel of the game.
The multiplayer aspect is definitely this game's strongest point. There are a ton of different game types. From various sandbox survival mods, RPG mods like altis life, CQC oriented KOTH, to Zeus gameplay that allows scenarios/missions to be edited on the fly by a game master.
Now all this positive stuff isn't without some downsides. The most serious issue in my opinion is the way you get past obtacles is stupid as hell. Half the time you just clip through/into a low wall, or into a short set of stairs instead of climbing over it. I have accidently hit the key and walked through a tower wall to my death. This clipping can also happen unintentionally without using the key around doorways, into the floor, or through walls. As frustrating as this can be it is not game breaking, just annoying.
Commanding friendly AI is also a huge pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ and makes single player games more frustrating.
The hardware requirements to run smoothly are quite demanding, and could be beyond what some people's rigs can handle without looking too ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to play effectively.
*edit*
This is my nomination for test of time. I keep coming back to it, and it has ruined other military games for me.

After 200+ hours, i feel i could make a proper review. Here we go!
HOLY CRAP WHERE DO I START? This game. This game right here. Is some of the best multiplayer shooting action you can find on PC, a hefty price for something that good? This ain't no Overwatch. Because this charming, quirky, bloodfest is the low, low price, of 0.00 dollars. You heard me, 0.00 bills out of your bank account if you get this game. This, is by far, my favorite Valve game. So, gameplay? Phemoninal. Characters? Much like Left 4 Dead, This game has a wonderful cast of quirky, lovable characters. There is the mascot for TF2, some would even say the mascot for Valve itself other than Gordan Freeman and Gabe Newell himself, The Heavy. The one guy everyone loves, yet no one will play, the Medic. The guy everyone hates, but everyone else plays, The Sniper.  The character that no one likes to play against, or play as, The Spy. The definition of "mosquito with a knife" which in other terms, a glass cannon, The Scout. The character that everyone plays, and I mean everyone, The Soldier. The one class that can literally play the game for you sometimes, (find right server, the right spot, and the right players.) The Engineer, the one person in the world who can properly be called a black scottish cyclops, The Demoman, and the devil himself... probably, (or potentially Gordan Freeman), The Pyro. Was that long enough? BUT WAIT THERES MORE! Reading the comics with introduce you to another bunch of quirky people. (and a love interest, somehow). Yeah, there are comics. Thats ma- HOLD IT. I havent even doven into the hundreds of hats and such! Thats right, hats. May GabeN have mercy on us all. Though I dont think I should get into that. Thats a whole 'nother song and dance. Speaking of, the music. Its pretty good. Anyways, the many dollars that go into TF2 is one of many reasons why Valve is still afloat. Sure, they had their screw ups. Sure, the TF2 community is known for being part people who take the game WAAAAAAYYYY to seriously, part memelords who are here for fun, and hoovies, (my favorite!) and the minority. A odd combo of both, and some children under the age of 13. (im no different, but i at least try to mind my manners.) There is one more thing. The weapons. From miniguns the LASER ROCKET LAUNCHERS FROM THE FUTURE, from frying pans and fish, no really, fish. From robotic arms to every other thing that can be used to bludgeon, beat, maul, and (my favorite) smack the bad guys until they are on the ground. Its a weird bag of mischief and fun. Overall, Team Fortress 2 is a fun game, plain and simple. Many friends to make. Many enemies to stake. Many hours of fun, laughter, and even teamwork against waves upon waves of robots. Yes, TF2 even has a co-op mode. Its everything you would want from a shooter, and a 50 pounds of unique sprinkeled in. 10/10. And I hope this review, will show you that way to the fun times to be had here. I hope to see you there.

[/h1]"One of the best Simulators in the world. By far the best Military Sim I have ever seen."[/h1]
[/u][PROS]:[/u]
-You can run this on low settings preety well if you have a low-end system like me.
-If you have a beast system there are some mods to improve graphics (ENB's, Textures, etc.)
-The game is very lively. Lots of mods to fill in if you are bored.
-Eden editor will be coming soon so be hyped for that. (Not saying the normal editor is bad :P)
-The workshop has some awesome scenarios with a lot of detail (custom voices, custom guns & vehicles, etc.)
-Campaign mod is decent, some missions may be hard and frustrating but all worth it in the end.
-Extensive amount of vanilla weaponry and vehicles.
-Oh how could I forget EXILE!! One of the funnest mods for ARMA 3!
[/u][CONS]:[/u]
-Price of $60.00 USD.
-Pray to god you have friends that play ARMA 3 because from what I know you won't make many friends.
-If you live in far away from Europe or America (such as Australia), A3Laucher will take a long time to download mods like AIA Terrain Pack, and other maps, forcing you to torrent or pray someone uploaded to MEGA or MediaFire.
-DLCs are too expensive and should be given out for free or for (I'll be nice) $5 each being it lacks content and does not stand for the 20$ each price tag.
Overall this game is freaking awesome, if you are bored, GET THIS GAME. You will not regret it!

Pros:
Two maps with HUNDREDS of locations simulating miles and miles of fully accessable openworld.
No two operations are going to be the same.
Sandbox with diverse weapons for infanty.
Vehicals including multiple variants of cars, trucks, APCs, tanks, helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.
Active moding community to adjust everything including core gameplay, adding new maps/locations, enhanced medical systems, and more.
Bouts of boredom and anticipation followed by intense, heartpounding combat. Its the only game where my friends and I can talk about specific firefights we fought together and actually remember what we are talking about.
Cons:
Enemy AI in the base game is insanely accurate. Often able to hit targets over half a kilometer away with ironsights on an SMG. This is fixed with mods like "bCombat", or by careful editing of text files.
High system requirements, (you are usually lucky to get 45fps on a server). There are loads of guides online to maximize your performance, but the game is just so big that the processing power required is going to slow down the game. That being said a friend of mine can run it on a gaming laptop, so you don't need to be ridiculously high end, just dont expect a perfect 60fps experience even on a thousand dollar PC.

I bought this game a couple of weeks ago when it was on 50% off sale, mostly because I run native linux and wasn't sure how well the "Experimental Beta" was going to run on my rig.  My fellow Linux users told me how well it ran, so I figured I'd support Virtual Programming's effort by getting Arma 3 and hoping everything ran fine.
Pros:
It runs more than fine, it runs 55-62fps with mostly standard settings.  100% stable for me thus far, no freezes, crashes or other bugs at all.  With over 15 hours into the game (mostly single-player campaign, but several in multiplayer with other Linux-users), I can honestly say I have not run into any functional issues thus far.
As for gameplay, well I suggest you watch some gameplay videos on youtube if you're on the fence.  This isn't a casual pick-up shooter you play for 20-30 min and go back to work.  It's so immersive and in-depth, that's because it is a tactical combat simulation more than just a shooter.  The replayability seems limitless, and I can see why a lot of reviewers have thousands of hours of gameplay into this.
Cons:
For the Linux client, there is no official support (yet), and there has not been made any announcements that there ever will be any release from Beta.  That's cool, I like what Virtual Programming is doing and I'd like to support their effort (and help convince Bohemia Interactive that Linux Gamers are Gamers too, and our money is money too).
As such, there is no game-launcher, making running steam workshop mods very difficult.  I mean I've figured out how to change launch properties, but it's hard to find out the correct launch-tag name/syntax for each mod and really I'm having plenty of fun with the Vanilla game (for now) but would hope that Bohemia comes to the descision to plan for official Linux/SteamOS release (after all, Steam Machines are about a month away from full release!).  So really this is only a con for Linux-gamers (at the moment), but not having a functional launcher makes running mods extremely hard.
The only other con I can think of thus far is the AI.  It seems pretty shallow, and I could be wearing a full ghillie suit, proned out under a pile of bushes and trees and tall grass, and an enemy soldier half a click away sees my thumb protruding from a branch in 1/4 of a second and 360 no-look jumping headhoots me </hyperbole>.  At other times, I can walk up right behind them, have them not notice me, as I pull out my pistol and execute them like some contract hit.  And let's not get into your friendly AI...sheesh, talk about real REMF/POGUE types.
Anyway, the AI isn't as bad as I make it sound, it's just fairly crude and pretty much the only un-polished part of this game and could use some serious attention.
Final Thoughts:
Beyond that, I plan on sinking tons more hours into this game, and REALLY hope that Bohemia Interactive throws Virtual Programming a bone on their eON Wrapper (translation layer?)...it works, seriously.
Just watch this youtube video for a side-by-side comparison Arma 3 Linux to Windows:
For Linux gamers, currently totally worth it if you can find it for 50% off or more.  If it is announced that it will ever exit Experimental Beta and one day Linux will join the official ranks of Arma 3 support, then the full price is more than worth it and the future fun you'll have.  Outstanding game, been waiting for something like this all my linux-life.

Team Fortress 2, the sequel to the original game developed by Valve, is a first-person shooter game in which you work as a team. Guided by the Administrator, you either work for Reliable Excavation Demolition (the RED team) or Builders League United (the BLU team); two teams fight against each other in an eternal stalemate as a by-product of war. There are many game modes for this version, but the most important include Capture the Flag (Intelligence), Control Points, Attack/Defence, King of the Hill and Payload. For more information, please refer to many community guidelines.
The game has some advantages. One major advantage is the cartoon style; in a departure from all realistic graphics typical of FPSs, Valve has created a cast of characters you may not find in other games of this genre (except Overwatch, maybe), from a braggadocious Bostonian (Scout) to a German mad scientist (Medic). You can make a fandom out of this.
The cartoon style has its consequences, though. Even though the game is rated 15 according to the British Board of Film Classification, anyone younger than 15 can enter the game for free, enticed by the cartoon style, and discover the steep learning curve and fustration that may lead to future problems. But what else is new when it comes to first-person shoters?
While TF2 begins to show its age (don't forget that it is ten years old), many updates are given out by Valve on an indefinite basis. Some good, some bad, some faulty (á la Meet Your Match), these updates show that Valve is ready to keep the community and game alive as long as the company is still running.
Overall, Team Fortress 2 is really 'worth the wait' as Gabe Newell stated. If you want to depart from the realistic war games, this free to play game is for you.

After 200+ hours, i feel i could make a proper review. Here we go!
HOLY CRAP WHERE DO I START? This game. This game right here. Is some of the best multiplayer shooting action you can find on PC, a hefty price for something that good? This ain't no Overwatch. Because this charming, quirky, bloodfest is the low, low price, of 0.00 dollars. You heard me, 0.00 bills out of your bank account if you get this game. This, is by far, my favorite Valve game. So, gameplay? Phemoninal. Characters? Much like Left 4 Dead, This game has a wonderful cast of quirky, lovable characters. There is the mascot for TF2, some would even say the mascot for Valve itself other than Gordan Freeman and Gabe Newell himself, The Heavy. The one guy everyone loves, yet no one will play, the Medic. The guy everyone hates, but everyone else plays, The Sniper.  The character that no one likes to play against, or play as, The Spy. The definition of "mosquito with a knife" which in other terms, a glass cannon, The Scout. The character that everyone plays, and I mean everyone, The Soldier. The one class that can literally play the game for you sometimes, (find right server, the right spot, and the right players.) The Engineer, the one person in the world who can properly be called a black scottish cyclops, The Demoman, and the devil himself... probably, (or potentially Gordan Freeman), The Pyro. Was that long enough? BUT WAIT THERES MORE! Reading the comics with introduce you to another bunch of quirky people. (and a love interest, somehow). Yeah, there are comics. Thats ma- HOLD IT. I havent even doven into the hundreds of hats and such! Thats right, hats. May GabeN have mercy on us all. Though I dont think I should get into that. Thats a whole 'nother song and dance. Speaking of, the music. Its pretty good. Anyways, the many dollars that go into TF2 is one of many reasons why Valve is still afloat. Sure, they had their screw ups. Sure, the TF2 community is known for being part people who take the game WAAAAAAYYYY to seriously, part memelords who are here for fun, and hoovies, (my favorite!) and the minority. A odd combo of both, and some children under the age of 13. (im no different, but i at least try to mind my manners.) There is one more thing. The weapons. From miniguns the LASER ROCKET LAUNCHERS FROM THE FUTURE, from frying pans and fish, no really, fish. From robotic arms to every other thing that can be used to bludgeon, beat, maul, and (my favorite) smack the bad guys until they are on the ground. Its a weird bag of mischief and fun. Overall, Team Fortress 2 is a fun game, plain and simple. Many friends to make. Many enemies to stake. Many hours of fun, laughter, and even teamwork against waves upon waves of robots. Yes, TF2 even has a co-op mode. Its everything you would want from a shooter, and a 50 pounds of unique sprinkeled in. 10/10. And I hope this review, will show you that way to the fun times to be had here. I hope to see you there.

My life as an FPS gamer:
Age 8-11 Call of Duty series Campaigns & Medal of Honor Campaign
Age 12-19 Battlefield Multiplayer
Age 20-present Arma III Multiplayer with a great unit
People believed Battlefield was a step towards realism from Call of Duty. Arma III takes it even further depending on what you play. You don't get your usual run & gun gameplay like in Call of Duty or Battlefield. Here, you'll find a squad working together with real tactics and communication. The instinct to "get as many kills as you can, when you can" is a behavior frowned upon. You work as a team and it does not matter if you get the kill or someone else in your team does. What matters most is completing your objective, watching each other's backs, and returning home alive. You're not just dropped into a match and play a round either. You're thrown into a real time battle where you rely on the competence of your team to get you through.
Be cautious because the respawn system is not like any other FPS. Death costs you dearly. You don't just respawn at a teammate or a previously taken objective. You respawn back at your FOB and will have to rely on transportation to get back to your squad. This risk of death makes it all the more necessary to stay alert and work as a group instead of an individual. I cannot stress enough how important teamwork is in this game.

This game is loads of fun when it is working properly. At this point, however, that is not all the time.
They have finally added East Coast servers and they have optimized the game very well. The game runs so smoothly now for me, it is great. However, they messed with the loot system and it is awful. You used to be able to find an AR or AK in almost every building you went in. I have played about 10 games after the newest update and have only ever held an AR one time and an AK about three times. The loot is broken. It is not fun to run around with a pistol and shotgun all game. This could just be me, but I have definitely noticed a significant drop in the amount of loot I find.
It also feels like the range of the guns has been lowered. I have to aim so high above peoples heads in order to actually hit them. These people are probably only about 100 meters away. With a real AK or AR, you would not see that amount of bullet drop. I realize the game is supposed to not be realistic, but the amount of bullet drop in this game is not just unrealistic, it is just plain stupid.
Other than those two issues, the game feels really good now. The East Coast servers are a huge upgrade for us East Coast people and actually have people on them now. When they first came out they had almost nobody on them. With that said, the loot problem is the only real issue I have with this game right now. 171.6 hours I've put into this game. And yes, I have had some really fun moments in all of the three gamemodes that are open to us in the land down under. However where this game lacks is the "Admins" of these servers, particularly Altis life, an RPG gamemode where you basically have a second life, but in the glitchy world of Arma III. Yes it's true that us Aussie like to mess with people and have a good laugh, but when you use your admin privileges to spoil the experiences of people who actually want to play the game properly, that's where I loose my intrest to play the game.
Now that's that little ♥♥♥♥♥ fest is out of the way, let's get into the game itself. It looks good, it's a massive step foward from Arma II, which to be honest, is alot more fun than Arma III. The movment is fluid and looks good but can kill you at times, the infamous stairs have made a return, and can kill you if they want a good meme. Walls have also joined this trend, breaking your legs if you don't vault over them from the right angle, which gets old after a while. On to the gunplay, if you enjoy CoD or Battlefield, this  game will be be a huge shock to you, as it is far more realistic, and when I say realistic, I mean as close to realism that you are going to get in a game/simulator. vehicles are just as deadly, with both the handling and the connection you have to the server you decided to play on. I'm not saying the game is a complete mess, but it could be alot cleaner.
Both official maps, Stratis and Altis, are extremely detailed, given there size, however unlike Chernerus in Arma II, it can be a bit bare, but that's my preference, I prefer the dense bushland, rather than the open fields. Trees, and shrubs look better, they're more detailed with better models and textures, however if you have a low to mid range rig, it will kill it.
So, why all the good points but still the thumbs down? Remember that I'm an Aussie, and to me there either isn't any good servers to play on, and the lack interesting gamemodes to keep me hooked, that and the community can be rather salty at times, which is a major turn off factor to me, in my opinion. Some of you may think that this is a bit of a moan, which it is, I admit it. But to me, a huge factor in mulitplayer games is the community. If it's toxic as hell, then your experience will be a♥♥♥♥♥♥one, if you want to play by the rules, which is where Arma falls a little bit. If you were to buy this game though, Wasteland is a fantastic gamemode, which is where I give this game a huge thumbs up, and where most of my hours have been spent.

171.6 hours I've put into this game. And yes, I have had some really fun moments in all of the three gamemodes that are open to us in the land down under. However where this game lacks is the "Admins" of these servers, particularly Altis life, an RPG gamemode where you basically have a second life, but in the glitchy world of Arma III. Yes it's true that us Aussie like to mess with people and have a good laugh, but when you use your admin privileges to spoil the experiences of people who actually want to play the game properly, that's where I loose my intrest to play the game.
Now that's that little ♥♥♥♥♥ fest is out of the way, let's get into the game itself. It looks good, it's a massive step foward from Arma II, which to be honest, is alot more fun than Arma III. The movment is fluid and looks good but can kill you at times, the infamous stairs have made a return, and can kill you if they want a good meme. Walls have also joined this trend, breaking your legs if you don't vault over them from the right angle, which gets old after a while. On to the gunplay, if you enjoy CoD or Battlefield, this  game will be be a huge shock to you, as it is far more realistic, and when I say realistic, I mean as close to realism that you are going to get in a game/simulator. vehicles are just as deadly, with both the handling and the connection you have to the server you decided to play on. I'm not saying the game is a complete mess, but it could be alot cleaner.
Both official maps, Stratis and Altis, are extremely detailed, given there size, however unlike Chernerus in Arma II, it can be a bit bare, but that's my preference, I prefer the dense bushland, rather than the open fields. Trees, and shrubs look better, they're more detailed with better models and textures, however if you have a low to mid range rig, it will kill it.
So, why all the good points but still the thumbs down? Remember that I'm an Aussie, and to me there either isn't any good servers to play on, and the lack interesting gamemodes to keep me hooked, that and the community can be rather salty at times, which is a major turn off factor to me, in my opinion. Some of you may think that this is a bit of a moan, which it is, I admit it. But to me, a huge factor in mulitplayer games is the community. If it's toxic as hell, then your experience will be a♥♥♥♥♥♥one, if you want to play by the rules, which is where Arma falls a little bit. If you were to buy this game though, Wasteland is a fantastic gamemode, which is where I give this game a huge thumbs up, and where most of my hours have been spent.

Is it worth a buy?
For me, yes it has been, ive had more than my monies worth out of this game, but it hasnt been down to the core game.
For me, the core game on steam, is merely the tool i needed to have in order to access the vast amount of good mods available for pvp
This is where the game excels
However.......
The core game is plagued with a few faubles
Movement doesnt feel very fluid, some clunky actions and animations
Weapon switching in a gun fight means coming to a complete standstill while going through the animation of putting one weapon away and then gatting the other out, if you dont do this in cover, your likely to get killed
You cannot jump, you come running to a fence, you stop, and do some very slow step over
vehicle movement can be horrific, easily toppling vehicles on small obstacles
Stuttering and fps drops occur regularly. Ive read this is due to CPU bottle necking, as only 1 core is being used, no multi threading
The AI in the campaign are crackers. There either totally stupid or like Leon from the film by the same name.
Either they run around statled at slightest noise without a clue where you are shooting from, or they somehow see you 500m away, and heashot you with an assualt rifle
There are DLC available, but quite frankly for the price, and what was received, i feel like taking myself to a corner and having a bloo.dy good word with myself for being so stupid
All that said tho........
The modding community is why anyone should by this game
there are a very good selection of multiplayer mods available for arma 3, ranging from the basic 2 team kill frenzy of wasteland and King of the HIll, on to the base building mods of epoch and exile, even has a star wars mod and dinosaur mod
I will say that the majority of my hours were spent playing the zombie mod, Breaking Point. I enjoy playing this, primarily because i want to enjoy DayZ but cant in its current state. For anyone wanting a dayZstyle experience, with zombies, bases, dynamic events, factions, point system, pvp, this is the way forward for now
If anyone is considering buying Arma 3, i would recommend checking out the steam work shop for it, and see if anything there interests you, then wait for arma to go on sale (which it does, and free weekends too)

I'm not leaving a bad review because the game itself is bad. In fact the game is great. My problem is that if you are like me and don't have the time to sit in a vent channel waiting for an interview with an admin JUST so you can play on one of the very few populated servers, then you aren't going to have very much fun. the game play is great - but there is no room for a player that just wants to hop into a game here or there. And then theres the fact that if you arent interested in playing one of the mods, then your server options are limited even farther.  at the exact moment of writing this review, there are currently 4 public servers with more than 10 players on them. 2 of those four are mods. all 4 require you to register on their site, and then request an interview in their vent or TS server.
When i bought this game that's exactly what i wanted, a game. but trying to play on any of the servers i feel like i am attempting to find a second job. its just not worth the effort to play multiplayer.
Then lets get into the incredibly poor engine that BI has been putting bandaids on since arma 2. its so CPU bound, i feel like im playing games from the DX7 era. It also has all the bugs from arma 2 (do they even try to fix anything?) as well as a ton of new ones but remember! this is arma! bugs are features in disguise! the odds of you getting a solid frame rate over 30fps are pretty much nonexistant. It literally runs everything through the CPU outside of filters, and makes so few draw calls its laughable. DX12 will not fix this either as its not an API issue so we will likely see exactly the same performance as we do now but with more foliage in the upcoming expansion unless they are trying to slip the Enfusion engine in on us as a surprise (not even possible).
TL;DR: the game is fun when you can find servers, as long as you can handle watching a slide show and falling through everything.

This game is really quite good. It wholly deserves the 60 dollar price in my opinion, and that is true to form. There has been a huge amount of work put into the game. Its scale and the seriousness with which it was handled by its developers absolutely deserves them the full 60 dollars. This game puts even next gen games to the test. It is fantastic. I will relay some of my experiences with the game:
Personally I am a HUGE fan of the lighting in the game. The dark is really dark, and the light is really light. The light is in fact just beautiful. There is nothing like driving in the night with your headlights on, and stopping somewhere with the light of your headlights to work by. Or moving through the dark in the morning, with a flashlight and a lighthouse far above you to keep things clear. Even tracers are quite well done, and you will constantly be taken aback by the absolute beauty and accuracy of both the lighting and the environment.
On to the environment. The environment is enormous. Hills, plains, farmland, valleys. It is all very well designed and is covered by very accurate and realistic looking flora which all server the purpose of providing some very useful and much needed cover. The scale of things is just huge, and is enough to blow ones mind. It is really something, standing on a hill 1 km away from an enemy platoon on the face of another and exchanging fire. That is what battle is, and that is really the scale that stands true to the test as what Arma is really about.
The vehicles are also a great part of the game, they are all EXTREMELY meticulously designed, and appear to be very much the real thing. In some ways, different, but you will not mind your long commutes via chopper or land solely because of the eye candy that is your ride.
The gunfire is a bit disappointing, however. Firing ones gun is not as much a pleasure as it may be in other games. It does not convey the same detail or intricate beauty that other parts of the game do, and does not feel nearly so powerful. I am not sure as to why this might be, but the guns are just so... light. I would like to see some more impressively realistic muzzle flare and gun interaction.
Additionally, the AI in the game is very flawed and can certainly leave one disappointed, especially during showcase missions. When I would like to play with a fully interactive AI, I meet soldiers who are completely unresponsive, downright born with autism and having a heart attack, or are just altogether far too quick to respond and accurate, just like a robot. The AI opponents often leave one shaking their head at the huge holes in interactability, especially on missions where otherwise this would be the focus of the game.
In total, however, the game is huge. If you are interested in the sort of fully fledged MILSIM combat that this game has to offer, please get it. I assure you that there is nothing else like this out there, and this is a game of its own. The creators had a mission, and that mission was achieved. Be responsible when you are flying your intricately designed helicopters or blazing tracer rounds at enemy soldiers down the ravine. Its fun stuff, and you never know where that may lead.

I'm not leaving a bad review because the game itself is bad. In fact the game is great. My problem is that if you are like me and don't have the time to sit in a vent channel waiting for an interview with an admin JUST so you can play on one of the very few populated servers, then you aren't going to have very much fun. the game play is great - but there is no room for a player that just wants to hop into a game here or there. And then theres the fact that if you arent interested in playing one of the mods, then your server options are limited even farther.  at the exact moment of writing this review, there are currently 4 public servers with more than 10 players on them. 2 of those four are mods. all 4 require you to register on their site, and then request an interview in their vent or TS server.
When i bought this game that's exactly what i wanted, a game. but trying to play on any of the servers i feel like i am attempting to find a second job. its just not worth the effort to play multiplayer.
Then lets get into the incredibly poor engine that BI has been putting bandaids on since arma 2. its so CPU bound, i feel like im playing games from the DX7 era. It also has all the bugs from arma 2 (do they even try to fix anything?) as well as a ton of new ones but remember! this is arma! bugs are features in disguise! the odds of you getting a solid frame rate over 30fps are pretty much nonexistant. It literally runs everything through the CPU outside of filters, and makes so few draw calls its laughable. DX12 will not fix this either as its not an API issue so we will likely see exactly the same performance as we do now but with more foliage in the upcoming expansion unless they are trying to slip the Enfusion engine in on us as a surprise (not even possible).
TL;DR: the game is fun when you can find servers, as long as you can handle watching a slide show and falling through everything.

This game is really quite good. It wholly deserves the 60 dollar price in my opinion, and that is true to form. There has been a huge amount of work put into the game. Its scale and the seriousness with which it was handled by its developers absolutely deserves them the full 60 dollars. This game puts even next gen games to the test. It is fantastic. I will relay some of my experiences with the game:
Personally I am a HUGE fan of the lighting in the game. The dark is really dark, and the light is really light. The light is in fact just beautiful. There is nothing like driving in the night with your headlights on, and stopping somewhere with the light of your headlights to work by. Or moving through the dark in the morning, with a flashlight and a lighthouse far above you to keep things clear. Even tracers are quite well done, and you will constantly be taken aback by the absolute beauty and accuracy of both the lighting and the environment.
On to the environment. The environment is enormous. Hills, plains, farmland, valleys. It is all very well designed and is covered by very accurate and realistic looking flora which all server the purpose of providing some very useful and much needed cover. The scale of things is just huge, and is enough to blow ones mind. It is really something, standing on a hill 1 km away from an enemy platoon on the face of another and exchanging fire. That is what battle is, and that is really the scale that stands true to the test as what Arma is really about.
The vehicles are also a great part of the game, they are all EXTREMELY meticulously designed, and appear to be very much the real thing. In some ways, different, but you will not mind your long commutes via chopper or land solely because of the eye candy that is your ride.
The gunfire is a bit disappointing, however. Firing ones gun is not as much a pleasure as it may be in other games. It does not convey the same detail or intricate beauty that other parts of the game do, and does not feel nearly so powerful. I am not sure as to why this might be, but the guns are just so... light. I would like to see some more impressively realistic muzzle flare and gun interaction.
Additionally, the AI in the game is very flawed and can certainly leave one disappointed, especially during showcase missions. When I would like to play with a fully interactive AI, I meet soldiers who are completely unresponsive, downright born with autism and having a heart attack, or are just altogether far too quick to respond and accurate, just like a robot. The AI opponents often leave one shaking their head at the huge holes in interactability, especially on missions where otherwise this would be the focus of the game.
In total, however, the game is huge. If you are interested in the sort of fully fledged MILSIM combat that this game has to offer, please get it. I assure you that there is nothing else like this out there, and this is a game of its own. The creators had a mission, and that mission was achieved. Be responsible when you are flying your intricately designed helicopters or blazing tracer rounds at enemy soldiers down the ravine. Its fun stuff, and you never know where that may lead.

I really enjoy this game. I don't know how many campaigns I've done with various groups and servers, but I cannot recommend this game if the following applies to you:
Do you have an AMD CPU or a late 2008-2009 Intel CPU?
Do you have a entry level graphics card but not a flagship graphics card? Ei Gtx 960?
Do you have under 50 mbps internet speed?
If any of the above applies to you, then your experience will be severely hampered. The game runs off of an old engine that doesn't utilize modern hardware efficiently. The developers will NOT optimize this game because they've already set sail off to a newer engine that will probably come out a couple more years down the road. Don't be surprised if it'll be as soon as 2016 Pre-Alpha release. By all means, buy the game if you don't mind unstable/unfinished features, but you have been warned. Even on a i5 6600k and a gtx 970, I'm still dropping frames, and that's partly because of Mods (understandable) and the unstable engine that cannot handle the AI or assets put into the game (not understandable). Poor memory handling, terrible and inefficient scripting, and the list goes on. Again, you have been warned.

King of the hill- Start off with a weapon, 3 teams fight to control an area, heli's and land vehicles are used to transport you there, once in the AO you must fight the other teams till your team has the most players inside, gain weapons and levels from getting kills, assists, and holding the AO.
Wasteland - 3 teams, Opfor blufor, and indie Opfor and blufor are teamwork based teams, work together to capture missions kill ai and player. Indie are solo or group based teams, kill everyone steal everything.

Team Fortress 2.... An Overall Fun Game! With Most Games Released In 2007 Not Being Played Much Anymore, Its Pretty Neat To See Valve Keeping It Alive With Updates! But This is Not Going To Be Very Accurate With The Pyro Update Coming Soon... But I Thought I Would Give It A Try. (This is My First Review, So Dont Be Mad With Me if Its Bad.. (BTW I Made This In 5:00 In The Morning, So Mind Spelling And Some Grammar)
Pros About TF2:
1. Unique Artstyle. Not Many Games That Arent For Young Children Have A Cartoony Artsyle. Thats Why (For Me) The Game Never Gets Stale.
2. The Simple To Learn (And Fun) Controls. The Controls Are Extremely Easy To Learn And Remember. I Preffer To Use The Scroll Wheel To Be Honest, But Thats Just My Prefrence! And Dont Forget You Can Use A Controller To Play Too.
3. The Hats And Cosmetics. Fun Fact: This Game Is The First "War Themed Hat Simulator" It's Honestly Funny When You Think About It. But Being Serious, The Hats Are Quite A Fun Addition! Though Its A Tiny Bit Unfair With Skill Levels Being Judged By What Hat You're Wearing, The Abillity To Customise Your Loadout Both With Your Weapons And Your Hats Is Quite Cool.
4. The INSANE Amount Of Weapons (And Reskins). The One Thing That Seperates This Game From Other Games With Classes Instead Of Loadouts Is That You Get To Play However You Want. With The Sniper, You Can Either Snipe From Afar With The Various Sniper Rifles, Or You Can Charge Into Battle With The Huntsman! The Demoman With His Swords, Axes And Shields. And The Scout With His Mad Milk And Cutting Knife. Most Other FPS's With Classes Dont Usually Have This Customization. Lets Say You Want To Play Rifleman In Some Other Game, You Are Stuck With A Rifle, A Pistol, And Something Else. And Then Theres TF2, You Wanna Play As A Guy With A Bow, A Jar Of♥♥♥♥♥♥And A Frying Pan? Here You Go! Simply Put, TF2 Has Loads Of Weapons And Loads Of Playstyles. Nuff Said.
5. The Classes. The Thing I Probably LOVE The Most About This Game Is The Classes, They Arent Just Nameless Guys With No Personality, They Are Mercs Who All Have Reasons For Fighting. Valve Went Out Of Their Way To Give Each Merc Their Own Voice, Their Own Story, And They Even Gave Some Full Names! And Dont Forget The Meet The Team Videos, Experation Date, Some SFM's Made By Fans That Are Official, And Of Course, The Comics! The Comics Are Probably The Coolest Part! Most Games Dont Have Witty, Funny Comics Or Quick Videos To Explain The Characters, They Have Long, Boring Lines Of Dialoge That You Can Only Get After Getting A 100%! Simply Put, The Classes Are What Make The Game So Special.
6. The Updates. This Is Probably The Shortest Part Yet, Valve Regurlarly Updates The Game With New Weapons, Cosmetics And Maps. Enough Said.
7. The Workshop. Simply Put, The Ability To Submit Your Weapon / Cosmetic / Map To Valve Is What I Absolutely Love About This Game... Of Course I Could Never Do That Cause I Suck At Modeling And Coding And That Stuff, But Hey! One Day My Idea Might Get Put Into The Game! Who Knows?
8. The Saxxy Awards. Oh. My. God. The Saxxy Awards. I LOVE The Idea Of Having People Send In Videos And Get A Chance For Fame On The Internet. (Not To Mention The Sexy, Golden Saxxy Weapon) I Think One Day I Want To Help One Of My Friends Do That. (Of Course I Would Make The Story Board Since I Suck At Animation, Also [Obvious Plug] Check Out My Screenshots)
9. Unusuals. Another Thing I LOVE Is Unusuals, Again Having An Unusual Makes Everyone Think You're Amazing At The Game But I Digress. The Fact That There Arent Just Unusual Hats BUT Unusual Weapons Too Is So Cool. I Dont Have Any Unusuals (Or Australiums) Yet But I Will Get Them.... Once Halloween Strikes... And The Chance For Unusuals is DOUBLE!!!.... Or I Could Just Buy One... Speaking Of Halloween...
10. Events. Though Halloween Was Kind Of A Flop Last Year,I Still Love Halloween (Even Though I Missed Halloween 2016) And Smissmas Is Fun.. Mostly For The Naughty And Nice Crates... And Every Year There Are New Cosmetics And Weapons. And Let Us Not Forget Update Events! (Such As Invasion) Again, I Never Got To Play Invasion While It Happened But Still.
11. Mann Versus Machine. I Must Say MvM Is One Of My Favorite Gamemodes, Though Sometimes Frustrating (NEVER Play Engineer In MvM Unless You Are Ready To Cry) I Have Never Actually Gotten A Botkiller Weapon Or An Australium From MvM (YET) Botkiller Weapons Are Pretty Cheap On The Steam Market.... But Yeah... Thats It.
And Now For The Cons.I Absolutely LOVE This Game But.. No Game Is Perfect. Here We Go.
Cons About TF2:
1. Mann Versus Machine. You May Be Thinking: "Wait, Didnt You Just Talk About MvM" And Yes, I did, But Nothing Is Perfect. Three Problems I Have WIth MvM is: Difficulty And Learning Spike For Newer Players, Newer Players Do Not Know How To Play This, And Some Tricks And Strategys Are Needed To Play This Mode. Now Of Course It's Fine For Players To Be Ok At It, But There Should Be A Tutorial For MvM. Second Is Mann Up. Mann Up.. Mann Up... What Can I Say About It? First Of All It Is Quite Cheap For A Measly 0.99 Dollars, (Or 99 Cents) That Does Keep Some Inexperienced Players Out, But Not All. And Not To Mention How Difficult It Is, And How You Only Get Good Drops From The WAY Harder Levels. Overall MvM Is a Well Rounded Gamemode But... Third Is The Lack Of Updates Since 2013. (I Think) MvM Desperatley Needs A New Update, Valve Has Left It In The Dust For 4 Years. (And If They Dont Update In After November, 5 Years.) It Needs Either More Maps, More Missions, More Bots, Maybe More Vehicles  (Like The Tank, I'm Thinking Maybe Automated Sentries, And Walkers Like The Ones In Half Life) And More Drops (Maybe Silver Weapons Like Australiums And Maybe More Botkiller Weapons) Anyways I've Been Talking Enough About MvM On To...
2. The Lack Of Programmers. This Is Going To Be Very Short Cause Its Very Simple: Only 4-6 Programmers Are Working On TF2, Of Course They Have Lots Of Playtesters, But Not Many Programmers. This Can Result In Some Problems, Such As Bugs Glitches Or...
3. The Last Few Updates. Now I'm Only Going Back As Far As Meet Your Match Because Tough Break Added Alot And The Only Complaint About It Is How You Cant Do Contracts Anymore. Meet Your Match.. Meet Your Match... They Fixed Matchmaking Not Too Long Ago...No One Really Plays Pass Time...No One Plays Competetive Either...I Feel Really Bad For People Who Want To 100% All Achivements...... If Thats Even Possible... I Mean Tuning Merasmuses TV Is Practically Impossible. The Starter Class Packs Are Not Really Too Neccesary...The Keyless Cosmetic Cases Are Pretty Fun... Nobody Really Wears The Prinny Things... The Prinny Machete Is A Cool Reskin...I Think The Pyro Needed To Win The Most, Of Course I Would LOVE To See Some New Weapons For The Heavy... (Like A Shield That Replaces The Minigun, More Secondary Weapons, And Maybe Some Better Melee Weapons) But The Pyro Needs Balances And Bug Fixes The Most, His Fire Affect For His FlameThrowers Are Buggy, The Flamethrower Is Buggy In Itself And WAY Unbalanced, And Being A Proffetional Pybro, I Would LOVE More Weapons That Would Make My Job Easier. Scream Fortress VIII Was Kind Of A Dissapointment, I Hope This Year's Halloween They Bring Back x2 Chance For Unusuals, The Creepy Crawley Case Is Ok... I'm Only Mentioning The 6th Saxxy Awards Because It's Next, I'm Not That Suprised The Winglet won.. Again He's A Really Good SFM Animator. Last Years Smissmas Was A Bit Lazy On Valves Part, With Everything Being Community Made, But Still I Enjoyed It... And Thats Really It.
Overall TF2 Is A Fun Game, Play It If You Want! I Would Definently Recomment This Game! (Also I Ran Out OF Room, So I Couldnt Mention Inexperienced Players)

TL;DR:
Pros:
-Extreme realism (damage, movement, fatigue, healing, equipment, ect...)
-(sink or swim) training of very valuable combat skills used in real life and useful in other games
-very useful AI companions (most of the time)
-everything has a counter and can be taken down with the right equipment and/or exceptional skill and/or lucky shots
Cons:
-Extreme difficulty (probably harder than darksouls at times, save often between engagements and stay with your team)
-Characters occasionally feel emotionally stunted
-obvious "god mode" NPC sometimes (coughcoughfirstmissioncoughcough)
Too Long;Read it anyway:
One of the most realistic warfighter simulators to date.  As such, it's also difficult to the point where anyone who plays a "standard" FPS will quickly die due to lack of caution.  Everything is simulated to an extreme degree from the problems associated with exaustion and fatigue resulting in slower movement and trouble aiming, to the reality of taking fire causing tunnel vision, realistic injuries, and extremely quick death.
One of the first lessons you will learn in this game is to keep your head down and look for cover.  Always be looking for ways to find your enemies before they find you and never take any advantage for granted.  The second someone knows where you are before you know where they are, you are at a crippling disadvantage as it is all too easy to line up a steady shot and kill someone before they even knew you where there.  A good way to learn just how scary it is on the modern battlefield today for anyone involved since you'll find yourself relying on your AI and player teammates almost more than you rely on your own skills.  You might find yourself actually following around the AI for cues and clues on how to fight and the level of communication between both players and the AI allies is far above what most games have ever accomplished on a practical level.  Simply put, this game has NPCs that you may actually find a bit of value in compared to the inaccurate, incompetent, prescripted "spehshul farces" NPCs you see in other games
The actual campaign is pretty good too, giving you a good look (in my opinion) of what combat arms guys would actually deal with in a desprate situation (out numbered and out gunned in a hostile foriegn country with little in the way of support)  I wont tell you how things got this way, but right from the start, the entire remaining NATO forces (in that particular area of operations) are hanging on by a thread and fighting a larger, albiet less experianced, local military and it's extremely satisfying to survive each mission and see the desperate struggle continue.
Now as great as the AI is in this game, it's not without it's flaws.  They are skilled, but occasionally have path finding issues in vehicles that make you wonder who gave these guys their license.  In the campaign, occasionally the "god mode" will kick in and reveal that the character is obviouslly story critical before they actually are but it's rare enough that you won't be annoyed by it long and chances are that you'll be too busy trying to stay alive to notice it.
There is also the fact that I think that maybe they could have increased the emotional factor by allowing the characters to grieve a bit more over the loss of their buddies during and after combat, as sometimes it feels a little cold that they just ignore it other than a call out that someone's down.  You see it effect them every once in a while for certian characters but really it seems they either aren't really feeling it right then or are really good at not showing it which is something that legitimately happens so I find it forgivable for the devs to have not made the call outs for each death a little more emotional.  There is another factor I think could play into why they can keep it to "(number) is down" but for spoiler sake, I won't say that theory here.

Ive had this game sitting in my library forever, i tired playing the campaign awhile back and just couldnt get into it. Well today i tried out a co op server. About 8 hours later i realized I was extremely hungry and it was nearly 3 in the morning. After 1 session of playing i had plenty of super fun moments from my very first mission where our helicopter got shot down almost instantly upon entering the AO leaving me as the lone survivor all the way up to my last mission where we had an insane firefight with overwhleming odds. What really wraps the game together though is the sound...One second you're moving towards an objective and suddenly bullets cracking overhead becomes the only thing you hear. What makes this even more tense is you might not know where you're being shot from and even once you do find the bad guys, you have to fight through the recoil of your weapon and your fatigue in hopes you can land a nice shot on them. You are not Superman in this game, you can't mow down bad guys like Call of Duty and youcan die faster than you can blink if you're not careful. Really fun game if you want to get as close to combat as you can without actually being there.

Arma 3 is a very fun game with a lot of different styles of gameplay. If you're into playing cops and robbers try out a life mod. If you're into the post apocalyptic wasteland survival then try a vast array of zombie or survival mods. the game is very smooth depending on what pc you are playing on. I play at 60 FPS using NVIDIA's GeForce Experience optimized settings and the game looks beautiful. I am using a Core-i7 CPU and a GTX 970. If you have ever played DayZ Standalone I can safely say it will run either even with or much much better than DayZ, depending on what map, or what mod you are playing and how well it's optimized. Arma 3 is not a just a game with a lot of modded servers, but it has a few very fun gamemodes built into it, such as Wasteland and Altis Life. If you are planning on installing and playing mods such as a DayZ-like mod, then it is very easy to install and sometimes using a third party launcher such as A3Launcher can be a big help. It will have the most popular mods and all you would have to do is click a single button to install and simply join the server of your choice straight from the very same launcher. If you're into the military simulation style then          steam workshop has a lot of great gamemodes that can be real fun. Some of them you can play with friends by just creating your own gameroom within the game itself. Not requiring a server rental at all.
If you have a computer that can run other third person games at a good frame rate and you're into either games such as DayZ, H1Z1, or any PVP game for that matter. Or if you're into the roleplay style similar to sims, or a cops vs robbers. Get yourself Arma 3, you won't be dissappointed.

Arma 3 is probably the best FPS war game ever, as one other reviewer put it COD is for boys, Arma is for men. You will get to experience both the excitement and incredible the frustration that is battle. The online community is also pretty freaking awesome with a wide range of servers and game types from cooperative missions and King of the Hill to a GTA styled server called Altis Life. This game is so much more than a game. Ok, so you say you aren't a huge fan of the online scene and you will eventually finish the Arma campaign. Well, no worries my friend, you will NEVER finish all of the user created missions available to download. The online Arma creators community is alive and rich with well executed and engaging content. And that brings me to the editor. Can't find what you want online? Make it yourself. Do you want a game where you and several friend have to deliver cakes while being attacked by demon monkies? Well go and ♥♥♥♥ing make it! You can sink hour after hour into the Arma Editor. Sound crazy? Well it is. There are many games that have been developed off the Arma Engine and the Editor gives you alot of control (not complete but you can figure lower level stuff out) to create literally whatever the hell your crazy mind can come up with. So buy it because when you buy Arma you also buy endless gaming opportunities!
**EDIT**
With the release of the Eden update it just keeps getting better! Everything I mentioned earlier about mission creation just got a whole lot esaier and more intuitive. Bohemia is probably the last great developer that actually appears to care about it's users. It's amzing that years after its release the team is still pushing massive updates, FOR FREE!!!!! Arma 3 is a very fun game with a lot of different styles of gameplay. If you're into playing cops and robbers try out a life mod. If you're into the post apocalyptic wasteland survival then try a vast array of zombie or survival mods. the game is very smooth depending on what pc you are playing on. I play at 60 FPS using NVIDIA's GeForce Experience optimized settings and the game looks beautiful. I am using a Core-i7 CPU and a GTX 970. If you have ever played DayZ Standalone I can safely say it will run either even with or much much better than DayZ, depending on what map, or what mod you are playing and how well it's optimized. Arma 3 is not a just a game with a lot of modded servers, but it has a few very fun gamemodes built into it, such as Wasteland and Altis Life. If you are planning on installing and playing mods such as a DayZ-like mod, then it is very easy to install and sometimes using a third party launcher such as A3Launcher can be a big help. It will have the most popular mods and all you would have to do is click a single button to install and simply join the server of your choice straight from the very same launcher. If you're into the military simulation style then          steam workshop has a lot of great gamemodes that can be real fun. Some of them you can play with friends by just creating your own gameroom within the game itself. Not requiring a server rental at all.
If you have a computer that can run other third person games at a good frame rate and you're into either games such as DayZ, H1Z1, or any PVP game for that matter. Or if you're into the roleplay style similar to sims, or a cops vs robbers. Get yourself Arma 3, you won't be dissappointed.

If you run AMD....STOP NOW DO NOT BUY!!....You want to play ARMA then go buy INTEL.
I run the FX-6300 at 4.6ghz overclock......and that still strained a tad in populated towns....

Graphics card of 2GB or more is a must in multiplayer as grass can't be turned off and is VERY heavy on the card/CPU.
Poor optimization means poor servers...which in turn means slower transfer rates.....put it on an SSD....
....So after finding out my brand new gaming build wouln't run ARMA3 in playable FPS online I started to push it harder until it did....I play in awesome FPS (80+) on ultra in Campaign and manage a reasonably respectable 45-50 FPS online.
So yes it can be done, but don't buy it if you don't plan to swith to an Intel build.

This game is awesome if you are looking for an authentic military experience, I played the campaign so far and I think it offers a very good story with a lot of realistic missions, the islands are huge with a lot of villages to explore, the game includes a mission editor you can create your battles with.
Realism
The game offers a great degree of realism even if many features are simplified to be accessible to casual gamers
every vehicle is detailed with interiors and working gauges, all vehicles can be driven using a keyboard, mouse is used for camera, air vehicles especially helicopters are greatly simplified to allow ppl to use the keyboard to control them, it would not be easy to fly a realistic heli with just the keyboard+mouse as in real life controls are too complex and require precision that can only be achieved with the use of dedicated flight simulator devices (joystic+rudder).
All vehicles and weapons come with menus depending on their purpose, all ingame buildings are fully enterable and can be explored, doors and windows can be opened/closed
Multiplayer
The game offers a wide range of game modes, many of them created by players as the game is fully moddable and it is possible to create any kind of simulated environments and gameplay mechanics, some game modes are in my opinion unbalanced, others are awesome, there are a lot of roleplay communities in this game who created their own rpg and social environment within their hosted server, the possibilities the game offer are endless, game modes vary from standard Death Match to more elaborated Real World simulations, lag is generally not an issue on most servers
Modding
The game is fully moddable and there are a lot of player made mods you can find on the net
Graphics and Game world
The graphics are awesome and the game world is fantastic to explore, there are also animals around the game world, every object and building,terrain,plant is detailed and properly textured to blend with the environment,shadows are properly casted
SCORE 10/10      - Recommended

I really don't know what to say other than I like this game but it just hurts me inside. I have well gotten my moneys worth out of this, and the game is really cool, but there are some HUGE problems with it.
The game does this well: be a huge military simulator with an incredibly diverse modding community. There is a LOT of stuff you can do and play with this game. It reminds me a lot of GMod in that regards: You buy the game, but you actually get like 30 games within it.
The attention to detail is amazing. The realism is.. well, real. But I just can't get past the biggest problem with this game.
It is horribly optimized.
The game just chugs along, especially in multiplayer. It doesn't feel very smooth. For a game where part of the draw is the massive battles possible, when your FPS drops to like 15/12 in a server with more than 50 people, its awful. I just finished playing a game of King of the Hill, a popular MP mode where the 3 teams all battle for control of the single objective. Its fun... when it runs smooth. The mode brings straight to the forefront the main problem with ARMA 3. The game runs great and is cool when your playing at mid/long range with just a few players. But anything above 60 players for me, just completely slows the game down, and it gets even worse in CQC.
I don't care that "you aren't supposed to do CQC, your likely to get killed, blah blah blah", it STILL RUNS LIKE CRAP. Its a complete crapshoot any time you come across an enemy within 50m of yourself, which in urban environments is nearly 100% of the time. The game just slows down to a crawl and whether I live or die depends entirely on who gets the short end of the stick with lag. There have been many times when I have gotten the drop on an enemy several meters away, and the lag is so bad they turn around and kill me because I missed half my shots due to the horrendous framerate. Its godawful.
I recommend this only because for all its faults it is still a fun game when the performance issues don't bog it down. But if I could I would give this a neutral, because I can't understand how Bohemia developed a massive war sim without optimizing it for massive amounts of players.

After a brief stint with overwatch I came back to TF2 finding that I was enjoying it a lot more and wondering why. Here's some of the things I found: the gameplay of TF2 is a lot smoother, deaths and kills feel more like they're based off of skill. TF2 is a very visceral game, aiming and movement feels a lot cleaner. This is why deaths and kills are more enjoyable, because they aren't based off of a cooldown skill. All of these complaints over OW boil down to the gameplay becoming pretty convoluted over time, with constant balancing issues and classes that win simply because of hard counters (also resource management of cooldowns and ult charge, but that might be your thing). In TF2 there are counters, but I've seen every class reach to the top of the charts, and with enough experience you can be effective in any role... to a degree. Sometimes a team does need a medic, does need an engineer and does need a good demoman, but no one is going to ragequit over it if no one counter picks because everyone just wants to chill. The community of TF2 is leagues ahead of OW, I can't talk about competitive that much but community servers and casual play is always a chill environment. Yet on OW almost every single match just on quickplay has someone say get wrecked and gg easy, and let's just hope you don't have someone toxic on your own team telling everyone the various ways they're doing a♥♥♥♥♥♥job. Wait times are great for normal play and just a little longer for competitive (expected), I hardly have to wait even in the middle of the day on a Wednesday. The only gripe I have with TF2 at the moment are hackers and aimbots. It seems to be a pretty common occurance in normal modes, and they should definitely be more active about combating against it. It still happens in OW but not as often. Even then they get kicked pretty quickly.
So yeah, jump into TF2, it's a fantastic game and imo a much smoother experience gameplay-wise. Peace out.

This isn't the type of game you pick up start at point A and end at point B with the final cut scene 20 hours later, its a giant military simulation sandbox platform first and formost that allows custom scenarios and anything the community wishes to make. (atlis life servers, cops v robbers and tons of others i haven't tried)
This allows this game to have almost infinite replay value.
Its a military simulator, but unlike any you have seen before, it makes battlefield look like call of duty.
Need to infiltrate a compound? okay get your squad together, get them equiped correctly, check out the realistic map and your heading, compund is 3 clicks south mount up in a truck and roll out into the open world of atlis, get within visual contact range of target compound while low in a bush(1.5km away with a scope or binocs)
Evaluate compound and scene, scouts and equipment.
Plan your route of attack and moves.
1200m away
Sneak low in depression of terrain to avoid the realistic length of site of enermy ai.
800m away
keep crouched and hold fire command to squad to keep eliment of surprise.
500m away
tell squad to hold ground and stay low, go prone yourself and crawl into position 450m away from compound with overwatch on target, they don't see you, this will be a cakewalk
400m away
Order squad around and out of depression area in combat stance and to engage enemy while you open fire from your concealed position
Squad 300m away
Squad opens fire and you take your shot, you miss because of your stupid breathing is still heavy from being tired from all your movement overloaded with gear, You squad tries to find cover but is getting wiped out. You are reloading to take your second shot SNAP bullet from nowhere domes you and you are dead gg try again
This game makes you think, and plan, and not stick your head out too far, and take your time to get into the proper position(which would take realistic time(ages in a game) but is offset in campaign by the ability to speed up game to 4x normal speed with +/-, making those repositions when prone far easier.
This game is as realistic as it gets for military sims, and is a game that can't really ever be finished. If you are a completionist and this bothers you don't get the game, but it does have a completeable campaign and infinite multiplayer options so if you want a military sim with infinite replay value, mods options and community made scenarios, this is it.

I taught my girlfriend how to autorotate a hummingbird in ArmA 3.
That pretty much sums me up.
I've had years of experience in PC gaming but years of AWESOME experience in ArmA. I've spent 1500+ hours in the series and 700+ in ArmA 3.
ArmA 3 is one of the best games to define PC gaming at the moment. It's a game of unlimited customizability and scope. Want to attack an enemy base at night? Go ahead. Want to do that with a sniper instead of an assault rifle? Go ahead. Want to make a squad of AI's go with you? You can do that too. Don't want AI's? Then invite your friends into your game. Want to make your headgear different? Wear a smaller backpack? Equip yourself with more grenades and less ammo?
You can do that, because this is ArmA.
Stratis and Atlis are great templates of diverse and dynamic realistic terrain stretching miles on-end and if you somehow get bored of a 300 sq km terrain, you can go download every single map from any ArmA title and play on it instead. The game is the most moddable military game you'll see this decade.
In my opinion? The only con?
Optimization.
This game isn't going to run smoothly...on anything. The game is awesome and has 12km render distances and more than 200 AI in some battles. That's why it lags. But, it still lags (in my opinion) too much.
I run an I7 4770K and an R9 270X  and i run this game at less than 30 FPS at times. Yes, i used to have a store-bought vanilla PC that would run this at 3FPS on lowest settings at 360p but I'll be sitting here with a custom built and overclocked PC while my game runs at 23 FPS and my CPU running at 30% usage..,
That's the thing though, ArmA is one of the most CPU intensive games out there yet it has no multi-core optimization and runs like a 2005 32 bit program. It will not go over 2GB of ram and never uses >~30% of my 4770k.
If you are going to buy this game, make sure you have a very powerful and fast PC, especially in these sections:
CPU
RAM
HDD/SSD
and you'll probably love it.
Want this game but have a lower-end PC? I'm sorry, but you'll probably want ArmA 2 OA and mod it with DayZ Epoch to get the best experience out of an ArmA game.
Still tho, 9/10.

Aiming is difficult when accounting for the unrealistic recoil coupled with the laggy servers that makes the game nigh unplayable at times. If you're not hittingg people and point blank range, you're getting no scope hip fired by a pistol at a ridiculously unpausiblle range. EDIT: Further comments as of more playtime.
Hit detection is bad, both guns and cars are failing to hit designated targets due to consistent server issues and poor hit box coding. Damage is unrealistic and definitely not static. I rarely rate a game this high, but this one is a perfect 10/10
for the genre it represents vs. any competitive products out there.
Bar none, the BEST military simulation on the PC that is
available to the public and priced under $10000
Yes there are flight sims that do flight more realistic,
there are tank sims that do tanks more realistic, etc, etc, etc.
However, there are no other games that combine ALL the aspects
of a military simulation in one full package like the Arma series does.
Arma III is the continuation of the Arma series, which started out as
"Operation Flashpoint 1985".
OPF1985 was considered the best of it's time when it was released and the
Arma series has continued that tradition with many of the same developers
that created OPF1985.
With a simple quick mission builder, a full blown complex high-end mission editor,
mods, mods, and even more mods to make Arma III something really special to those
of us who enjoy these type of games.
If you want the same feature set, but more realistic you would have to actually be in the
military and have a security clearance and thousands of dollars.
But you can get close to the same thing that real militaries around the world actually train
with for less than $60 and you don't need to sign-up for service.
If you want to enjoy this, but can't afford it at full price or have an older or slower PC,
then Arma II almost as chock full of features and mods so if you can't get this, get Arma II.

People say this game is dead and has been for a long time, but I'd say otherwise.  I am newer to the game than a lot of people, but I still feel like I can express my opinion on it in a review.  This game is ADDICTIVE.  There are so many different ways to play it with all the weapons and you find yourself sinking many hours into these strategies.  There are tons of maps, official and custom made by fans, that can be played on, and they cater to many different fun and innovative play styles.  With all the weapons, hats, taunts, maps, and overall loads of diversity, this game is centered around creativity and using it to battle others.  Seeing as it's free and can be easily run on low-end computers, there isn't much of an excuse not to get it.  While many new players are subject to getting killed frequently, as with any new player to any game, I would highly recommend looking up tips and tutorials if possible.  Players often judge other players by their hats and will assume that players with free noob hats like Ghostly Gibus, Mercenary badge and Pyrovision Goggles are easy kills.  If you learn the basics of gameplay and practice, you could find yourself killing a tryhard and making them rage.  But don't worry about hearing their screams, you can't hear them in Casual.  There are also some exclusive free hats and items from other free games that I would recommend learning about trying to get.  And, if you really feel like you love the game enough, you can start spending money on it.  I'd recommend buying a Mann Co Supply Crate Key as your first purchase.  Don't open a crate with it, or open crates or cases at all.  Please.  You should wait the week for it to be tradable and use Backpack.tf or Scrap.tf to sell it for Refined Metal, and then buying some nice cheap cosmetics, which usually start around 1.33 refined (1 refined + 3 scrap or 1 reclaimed).  Since these are your first few cosmetics I'd recommend buying three all-class hats or ones for a class you really love that have a theme and look good together.  You can see how they look on Loadout.tf before buying and if they can even be worn together.  People might not judge you instantly anymore.
Overall, for a game that costs no money, this is an incredible deal.  If your computer can run it, which it most likely will, then I'd very highly recommend installing it.  You won't lose any money (yet) and you're very likely to find enjoyment for hours on end.

Despite being more of an arcade-ish game, I actually see this as more of a skill based PUBG. The problem is that in PUBG, there are many weapons and attachments, which is fine, but as a result, the gear you're using is completely down to RNG, meaning that it's very much a game of luck. H1Z1 is less intense, but rather than having tons of randomly spawning weapons and attachments, it has a smaller pool of weapons with no attachments. At first I though the obvious thing, oh, Battlegrounds is better, it has more weapons, but the fast paced nature combined with the fact that people have more of an equal opportunity to acquire good gear makes this game, in my opinion, much more enjoyable and fair. However, the movement system in PUBG is much more refined feeling, and the crates, with the exception of the limited Gamescom crates, have been free to open so far. I feel like if H1Z1 can polish up a bit and add some more diversity to the map, it has more of a competing chance with PUBG.
