If you've got a notion to play a game that's so open-ended you'll never reach the 'end-game', here it is. It has stuff, lots of stuff, and even more stuff on stuff-to-download sites. We're talking a plethora of stuff. That's a lot of stuff by the way.
Sure, other games have big sandboxes...not like this sandbox.
Having played Arma 1 and Arma 2 for ages it was only inevitable that Arma 3 would have to achieve something ridiculously awesome to surpass itself. Well...it did it.  Legos, Lincoln Logs, Erector Sets, Play-dough...it has it all. The editor gives a freedom no other game I've ever seen gives you, and they keep adding things.
This isn't your "play for a week and you're done" kind of game. This is a world, and it will crush you under its heel if you're not careful.
The community is huge by any standards. The support, well, refer to the community. ARMA established itself long ago as an environment unlike any other game out there. Extensible, moddable, mod-supported.  It's just that open.
Too many contributors out there have always been around to further extend what we had to play with, though I'd be hard pressed to remember all their names they know who they are and a big thanks for your works. While ARMA3 doesn't come with all the various initial campaigns, it has a community that fills that void.
Yes, ARMA3 can definitely use all the hardware you have in your system. I have a very, very nice system and it runs sweet at 4k. Though the time it may say I have on record seems a pittance it doesn't mean I haven't enjoyed it immensely. Hopefully I'll get more free time that will allow me to venture forth into this cool world some more.

Sand Box mods: such as wasteland, probably the most entertaining mod; again u spawn, survive, look for gear, kill and respawn. depending on the server; you get a variety of side missions vs AI which is fun to do (especially when the AI is so DUMB, basically bullet spunges + aim bot) however, it creates a good way for players to face each other off with ambushing overpowering etc.. there are other mods like epoch which is like DayZ if you know it; while it might be fun for 20 hrs of gameplay its gets extreemly repetetive and boring to the point that you might vomit if you play another hour ;)

Again since the AI is basically two things, bullet sponge and an aim bot. no work has been done on the enemy AI at all; they dont try to flank, they dont push your line, they do nothing but stand where they are and keep firing at you with a no scope weapons landing 600m shots... quite broken to overcompensate on such things to cover for the poorly designed AI, if any ;)

Ok so I avoided writing this for a long time now, since my old computer just wasn't up to par to play the game to its full potential. But here 3 years later I am finally caving and speaking on the game. Originally purchased when it was $20 for both games, which at the time was more than a good deal. After all the patches and support on both Just survive and KotK in Year 1 things looked to be headed in the right direction, but somewhere down the line development favored KotK way more than Just Survive. Fast forward to Year 3 and we have this product (still not any closer to finished btw), a game with horrible hit registration, literally one weapon in the game (AR-15), servers that will say your connection is bad and lock you out of weapons, and many more bugs than even the initial release! With over 1,000 hours combined both games I would hope for a more refined product to brag about, and not curse the devs for 3 years of just getting by. Yet they will still ignore the issues and the game will still have revenue, just based off of in game purchases alone! Don't get me wrong I love the game and the potential it has to become a very good quality and well designed game. Yet we still have heard nothing about even a console version which originally was announced in Year 1, aside from the occasional "More details to come soon" announcements. Lets not forget back in August the company announced a full version mastered and all to be released September 2016. So where does all this lead to me giving it a recommendation? To simply put it, this game is a great take and a new experience but you are better off waiting for a better product when it is done, or at the very least waiting for them to fix the more prominent issues with weapons and connectivity. I hate the way this game has gone downhill and hope for it to return to a better rep, but until then if you are going to purchase this game just be prepared for a lot of headache and a variety of patches and updates.

This game is extremely addicting. This game has a great idea, but it is not executed well at all. The best people in this game will tell you that.
There are multiple problems that make the game rather unplayable. I use the term unplayable lightly, as you will still be able to play the game, but you will rage all the time. Hit registration in this game is awful. I can watch pro's, that can two-tap anyone, not be able to do any damage because their bullets are not registering. Then i, myself, can two tap someone with a pistol.
Other issues: parachuting down, you can glitch out of the playable area. When you should be landing, the game will not have loaded properly, leaving you to die because others dropped before you and got guns before you. Even when you load properly, when you touch the ground, the game has a hard time determing when that actually occurs, making you have to wait a few seconds to actually 'land'.
OVERALL: I would highly suggest not buying this game until it at least makes it to a beta. This game seems like it will remain a forever alpha, as the developers are focused more on micro-transactions than actually making the game better. I bought the game for $10 during a sale and got my money's worth, but I sometimes feel like I wasted my time.

I have to say that along with Arma 2 & Operation Arrowhead, this is hands down the best way I have ever spent money on Steam. In fact I have bought 3 copies for friends since my own purchase.
I bought initially for the new Epoch Mod, which at time had not been released, and found many other game modes to play, in the mean time. From Wasteland to King of the Hill to Life and later Battle Royale and Breaking Point.
I would say that half my hours have now been spent in Epoch for Arma 3, I have to say I am personally very fond of what they have produced so far and am excited for the mods further development.
What ever brings you to buy Arma 3 though I do not think you can fail not to be impressed by its scope and depth, nor remain unimpressed by the ingenuity of its modding community.
Buy it! Play it! Love it!
Update for Apex Expansion
Overall so far disappointed in the expansion, Tanoa is beautifully detailed but resource heavy on your PC. Buildings are only 50% enterable compared to 99.9% of Altis a huge step backwards in map design and execution.
Whilst there are new factions, weapons and vehicles there are still no women in the Arma 3 world!
Would i still recommend Arma 3, hell yes! Would I buy the expansion version? Harder to answer in the positive, but if on offer and within your budget it would be good to have the new map and units and vehicles and weapons to access despite the expansion's other failings.
Now using the Eden Editor to make missions and edit maps and it opens up a whole other dimension to Arma 3's potential and playability. So much still to learn and loving still!

I can't think of anything to comment so I'm just going to post a Blueberry Strawberry Raspberry Buttermilk Pancake recipe.
1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1 1/4 teaspoons white sugar
1 egg
1 cup milk
1 cup buttermilk
1/2 tablespoon butter, melted
1/2 cup fresh or frozen blueberries, thawed
1/2 cup of fresh or frozen strawberries thawed
1/2 cup of fresh or frozen raspberries
1. In a large bowl, sift together flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda and sugar. In a small bowl, beat together egg and milk and buttermilk. Stir milk and egg into flour mixture. Mix in the butter and fold in the blueberries, raspberries, and strawberries Set aside for 1 hour.A
2. Heat a lightly oiled griddle. or frying pan over medium high heat. Pour or scoop the batter onto the griddle, using approximately 1/4 cup for each pancake. Brown on both sides and serve. EnJoy

I dont have many hours on this game yet, but I would like to give my review of this game. This review will be coming from joe shmoe nobody that isn't a pro at any game what so ever. I've noticed some really harsh reviews about this game. Most of the harsh reviews I can completely understand where they are coming from, but I have a hard time agreeing with them because the game is still currently in Early Access. Now, I have no clue how long this game has been in Early Access, but i dont think you can fairly say a game shouldn't be buggy while in Early Access. Thats what most of the harsh comments are complaining about (The bugs). I completely agree. This is, by far, the buggiest game I have ever played. There are an insane amount of bugs that are super annoying, but, again, this game is in early access. I don't think its fair to judge this game on bugs yet. If this was full release, I would be very angry i wasted money on this game. So with that said, I want to explain why I give the thumbs up for recommendation to this game. If you set aside the bugs and whatever that this game has, This is probably one of my favorite games to play online. I'm not much of a FPS high octane gamer (not claiming that this is FPS high octane game just the competitiveness comparison). In fact, Im very terrible at those type of games, but I really really enjoy this game. This game is so fun once you get into a very rare smooth running game with little bugs. I don't think I've played a match without some type of bug, but Ive played some that were tolerable. This game, as many have said, has super great potential. I think this game could very well be one of the top played games in steam if they fix these bugs. So to sum things up, this game is EXTREMELY BUGGY, but at the same time EXTREMELY FUN. Im a pretty calm headed player, but this game has found a way to make me a little irritated at times. My suggestion is, if  you can look past the bugs, I highly recommend this game. Especially if you have friends willing to play with you. Just prepare to restart the game very often and sometimes having to play a game with your keys not properly working all the time. Your weapon being locked due to slow internet, though you have perfect connection. When playing this game, go in knowing it is buggy. Always expect a buggy game. If you always keep that in mind, push that focus aside, and enjoy the game for fun it has, this game is great. I actually love the idea of this game and I really really hope they fix this game before full release. This game will probably ruin my life if it becomes a smooth running game. I hope this review gives a better insight from just negative reviews. I've noticed some really harsh reviews about this game. Most of the harsh reviews I can completely understand where they are coming from, but I have a hard time agreeing with them because the game is still currently in Early Access. Now, I have no clue how long this game has been in Early Access, but i dont think you can fairly say a game shouldn't be buggy while in Early Access. Thats what most of the harsh comments are complaining about (The bugs). I completely agree. This is, by far, the buggiest game I have ever played. There are an insane amount of bugs that are super annoying, but, again, this game is in early access. I don't think its fair to judge this game on bugs yet. If this was full release, I would be very angry i wasted money on this game. So with that said, I want to explain why I give the thumbs up for recommendation to this game. If you set aside the bugs and whatever that this game has, This is probably one of my favorite games to play online. I'm not much of a FPS high octane gamer (not claiming that this is FPS high octane game just the competitiveness comparison). In fact, Im very terrible at those type of games, but I really really enjoy this game. This game is so fun once you get into a very rare smooth running game with little bugs. I don't think I've played a match without some type of bug, but Ive played some that were tolerable. This game, as many have said, has super great potential. I actually love the idea of this game and I really really hope they fix this game before full release. This game will probably ruin my life if it becomes a smooth running game. -The vehicals leave you wanting more variety
-The drones are too inconvenient
- $18 (CAD) dollars for some helicopters, and another for some guns? I bought the extreme support version before it came out, so I don't have to buy the DLC (because I had hope) but that is rediculous for people to have to pay that
Overall: Unless Bohemia gets their heads out of their asses and makes some content and fixes the damn game, don't buy it. Do a lot of research into this before even thinking of buying it. If you plan on pumping it full of mods and fixes, then you might be fine. Be warned.

I definitly recommend this game. Why? No matter what kind of game you want to play, you find it in ArmA3. If you want an authentic tactical expierence, download some mods like ACE/ACRE and join a realism unit. More intrested in survival? Then hop on a wasteland or dayz server. Team Deathmatch? Then battleroyale is for you. Even if you like roleplay (altis life) or sector control (king of the hill) you will find what you are looking for.
Graphics: 17/20, the game looks great overral, with beautiful landscapes, lightning and weather.
Sound: 7/10, nothing too fancy here, but nothing bad either. If you want great sounds, then just download a mod.
Storyline: 10/15, way better campaign than ArmA2, but let's be honest, there are better campaigns around. Don't play this game if you intend to only play it singleplayer, then you will be dissapointed.
Gameplay: 28/30, absolutly great. The diversity of guns and vehicles in the main game is already great, and there are tons of mods around to get more weapons and vehicles. The scenario editor allows you to create simple and fun scenarios in a matter of seconds, and more advanced scenarios if you have the scripting expierence.
Optimization: 12/15, lot's of people complain about this, which is something I don't understand. You don't need the best PC in the world to run this game on high settings, and you can adjust every setting in the game, allowing you to get the best perfomerance possible. For me, it runs fine on very high-ultra settings on a i3-3240 3.4GhZ duo core and a GTX 750ti with 40fps in multiplayer.
Controls: 6/10, there is a great amount of controls to learn, which means there is quite a big learning curve for them. Aside from that, the default interaction menu is pretty horrible and glitchy, but then again, there are mods to fix this.
Overal: 80/100. Just buy this game, I have enjoyed over 400 hunderd hours in this game, and still counting.

I've spent most of my time playing Invade & Annex, Public and Private 77th JSOC servers. Public provides broad perspectives to casual teambuilding strategies. That are commonly interpreted by the majority population. A server consists of up to 60 players(Non AI). Squads are assigned by an active HQ(Usually Me). 4 Pilot Slots, 1 UAV Slot, 1 Sniper&Spotter, and 5 Fireteams. Alpha through Echo as commonly referred.
When joining the server you're teleported to a starting area( Airbase ) which could be actively under attack. The rendering AI has a capacity to allow 100+ Enemy Units on the field of operation. Typical Operations to eliminate objectives usually include 1-3 Enemy Aircraft that respawn until the subobjective radiotower is destroyed per mission. 4-8 Enemy Armor, 2-5 Enemy Technical Offroad, and 5-12 enemy squads consisting of entire fireteams(Medic,Engineer,AT,Marksman,Autorife,Squad Lead).
Going back to HQ, it's my responsibility to handle the server population consisting of about 40-50 players at any given time. I coordinate through different communication channels to taxi fireteams to their appropriate LZ's. Or provide reinforcements to their position. I coordinate with pilots to setup laser targeting with squad actuals(Lead). All in a realtime manner while handling new spawning players to the server. Those new recruits are then taken by pilots ready for tasking to the appropriate locations. It's crucial for Squad leaders to handle their own seperate LZ - Landing Zone perimeters; To allow pilots to reach a safe location for reinforcements.
Private server is a whole different dimension to Arma 3. After completing bootcamp with the JSOC. with about a 10% pass rate. Those qualified are in for a real treat. Complete tactical realism, with TaskForceRadio. Where knowing what to do in situations becomes a reflex, no longer having to think of what to do. Those in the fireteams flow instinctively and go to a whole new level.

I was really excited to try Arma 3, and I really tried to like it. The single player is decent, the gameplay is great, everything looks beautiful and sounds awesome.
Why am I not recommending this?
The multiplayer.
If you don't want to be in a server with 400+ ping, or that is empty, you'd better love being in a sims-esque server where only whitelisted people can pick up things, and claim it is 'RP'ing as a criminal' to shoot you for no reason.
Servers that function as actual combat game modes are great, except it costs in-game currency to use vehicles and new weapons (earned through getting kills), and you spawn quite far from anything. Added to that is the frustration of being shot in the back by teammates, or run over by them any time you get close to the action. Also, you need to level up to use different weapons (which you have to buy once you unlock them) but you earn XP at such a low rate compared to the amount it takes to level, it's just not worth the trouble. I can see it being fun if the servers weren't mostly all RP servers that don't allow you to do anything unless you become whitelisted, or the community was a little less trigger happy towards anyone they do not know personally, regardless of the team.
It has amazing potential, but the multiplayer is awful, and that was pretty much the selling point for me. If you enjoy singleplayer tactical hyperrealistic shooters, you will love it. If you're getting it for the multiplayer, you'd better either be ready to apply for a whitelist for the worst RP servers I have ever encountered (childishly immature, seems completely unmoderated), or be ready to be teamkilled every time you leave your spawn zone. Most servers have extremely high ping, meaning the large selection of servers isn't too large when you eliminate 80% that are unplayably laggy and most of the rest are empty.

I definitly recommend this game. Why? No matter what kind of game you want to play, you find it in ArmA3. If you want an authentic tactical expierence, download some mods like ACE/ACRE and join a realism unit. More intrested in survival? Then hop on a wasteland or dayz server. Team Deathmatch? Then battleroyale is for you. Even if you like roleplay (altis life) or sector control (king of the hill) you will find what you are looking for.
Graphics: 17/20, the game looks great overral, with beautiful landscapes, lightning and weather.
Sound: 7/10, nothing too fancy here, but nothing bad either. If you want great sounds, then just download a mod.
Storyline: 10/15, way better campaign than ArmA2, but let's be honest, there are better campaigns around. Don't play this game if you intend to only play it singleplayer, then you will be dissapointed.
Gameplay: 28/30, absolutly great. The diversity of guns and vehicles in the main game is already great, and there are tons of mods around to get more weapons and vehicles. The scenario editor allows you to create simple and fun scenarios in a matter of seconds, and more advanced scenarios if you have the scripting expierence.
Optimization: 12/15, lot's of people complain about this, which is something I don't understand. You don't need the best PC in the world to run this game on high settings, and you can adjust every setting in the game, allowing you to get the best perfomerance possible. For me, it runs fine on very high-ultra settings on a i3-3240 3.4GhZ duo core and a GTX 750ti with 40fps in multiplayer.
Controls: 6/10, there is a great amount of controls to learn, which means there is quite a big learning curve for them. Aside from that, the default interaction menu is pretty horrible and glitchy, but then again, there are mods to fix this.
Overal: 80/100. Just buy this game, I have enjoyed over 400 hunderd hours in this game, and still counting.

I've spent most of my time playing Invade & Annex, Public and Private 77th JSOC servers. Public provides broad perspectives to casual teambuilding strategies. That are commonly interpreted by the majority population. A server consists of up to 60 players(Non AI). Squads are assigned by an active HQ(Usually Me). 4 Pilot Slots, 1 UAV Slot, 1 Sniper&Spotter, and 5 Fireteams. Alpha through Echo as commonly referred.
When joining the server you're teleported to a starting area( Airbase ) which could be actively under attack. The rendering AI has a capacity to allow 100+ Enemy Units on the field of operation. Typical Operations to eliminate objectives usually include 1-3 Enemy Aircraft that respawn until the subobjective radiotower is destroyed per mission. 4-8 Enemy Armor, 2-5 Enemy Technical Offroad, and 5-12 enemy squads consisting of entire fireteams(Medic,Engineer,AT,Marksman,Autorife,Squad Lead).
Going back to HQ, it's my responsibility to handle the server population consisting of about 40-50 players at any given time. I coordinate through different communication channels to taxi fireteams to their appropriate LZ's. Or provide reinforcements to their position. I coordinate with pilots to setup laser targeting with squad actuals(Lead). All in a realtime manner while handling new spawning players to the server. Those new recruits are then taken by pilots ready for tasking to the appropriate locations. It's crucial for Squad leaders to handle their own seperate LZ - Landing Zone perimeters; To allow pilots to reach a safe location for reinforcements.
Private server is a whole different dimension to Arma 3. After completing bootcamp with the JSOC. with about a 10% pass rate. Those qualified are in for a real treat. Complete tactical realism, with TaskForceRadio. Where knowing what to do in situations becomes a reflex, no longer having to think of what to do. Those in the fireteams flow instinctively and go to a whole new level.

I've only played this game for about 300 hours,but numbers don't matter. I know what to say about this game.
Lets start off with a nice little summary of the game.
ArmA III,the sequel to Arma II,continues it's theme of Military Simulation in a near-future setting,on the Islands of Altis and Stratis,south of Greece. The game features a three part campaign and many multiplayer gamemodes,ranging from Team Deathmatch to Sector Control.
But summary's are useless. I'm going to tell you what you SHOULD know RIGHT AWAY.
First off,DON'T ENTER THIS GAME TREATING IT LIKE CALL OF DUTY/BATTLEFIELD. This game is a LOT more realistic than "shuut the gun and dey ded".
DON'T THINK YOU CAN JUST DIVE IN. This game has quite a large learning curve,so expect to die a lot at the start. If you want to practice,first do Bootcamp, then VR Training,then complete the campaign on Regular/Elite. You should be ready after that.
Finally, DON'T ENTER THIS GAME TO PLAY NON "ARMA" GAMEMODES.This means gamemodes like Breaking Point,Epoch,or Altis Life. These gamemodes,in my opinion, don't really represent what Bohemia was trying to achieve. Im not calling these gamemodes BAD,they're ♥♥♥♥ing great, I just think that you should also look at the "Military Simulation" gamemodes,like Invade & Annex, Co-operative missions or KOTH
Lets now do what I like to do when reviewing games, Categorize and Pro-Con-ize. Im a weird man.
WORLD DESIGN
+Big,but not big enough to make you bored of travelling
+Diverse areas (Urban,Forests,Plains,Mountains)
+Dynamic weather system (Fog can get to the point where you cant see 2 metres in front of you)
-Too open (In my opinion. Needs more Woods and Urban areas)
GRAPHICS
+♥♥♥♥ing Gorgeous
+Very customizable
-Demanding (If you dont have a good PC,expect 20-15fps)
GAMEPLAY
+Excellent blend between realism and lots of action
+Makes you afraid of just a war by how dangerous this game can be
+Sometimes,I friendly fire because I thought that a teammate was AI (Yes,its that ♥♥♥♥ing good)
SINGLEPLAYER
+Great as practice for new players
-Not the best campaign i've seen
MULTIPLAYER
+The most ♥♥♥♥ing diverse amount of gamemodes
+Easy to find a favorite
+Co-op missions with friends can be the funnest thing you will ever do
-Most was community made (which is still great,but that means that Bohemia didn't really do any of the work,they just posted a bunch of categories)
COMMUNITY
+Mods can range from better graphics to ♥♥♥♥ING DINOSAURS AND STAR WARS
+Friendly,Respectful community that doesn't hate on noobs
-Where there is good,evil tends to follow in its wake (Almost every server I've been on has had a troll on at least 2 times a day)
THE FINAL VERDICT
Buy this ♥♥♥♥ing game. Do you like Military?BUY IT. Realism? BUY IT. Role-playing?BUY IT.This has become my favorite game of all time,and the only thing that I think will beat it is ArmA IV.

Big fan of the ARMA series and A3 does not dissapoint. I haven't given up as much of my life on this as with previous titles. That has nothing to do with the quality of the game but more down to me having a vast library of 'life vacuum' games.
They have incorporated so much into this game but sadly have arrived in the form of DLC. Luckily I didn't pay that much for the game first time around. It is always a pleasure being able to play a game built purely for PC. As the spin off MODS available are astounding and with such an active community you are never going to get bored of this game. The core engine on A3 is much improved and offers some fantastic postures and firing positions. So no longer are window ledges too high or some walls that little bit too high to fire from. You can adjust your posture to accomodate this.
Multiplayer is obviously where this game really shines and there are a plethora of servers out there for you to really fit into. We used to run our own server with a very unique way to playing the game and tried to keep it SF orientated with few air assets on call or artillery. It now seems some gaming clans or servers have taken this a step further some are very rigid and disciplined. This allows the game to be played as it should be played. If you don't fall inline or just like to blow the base up and annoy everybody else then expect a ban. You get assigned to a fireteam with a TL. Your TL talks to High Command for your orders. Then you line up for deployment with a dedicated Helo pilot to drop you on Target. Great fun and ordered.  That is just one game mode developed by the community and the organisation of a clan.
The modern setting isn't really my bag but it does work. I prefer current as opposed to future. However there are lots of mods out there to sort that out.

One of the funniest games I've played, and yes, my hours are in fact very small. At least i think so, because this game is just so addictive, it actually squeezed 20$ from me somehow (thus I'm finally able to review it and add people lol).
Great gameplay, varies in classes playstyles, with mini classes included if you equip certain loadouts (demoknight, freakin mini sentry frontier justice engineer from hell, others).
Great variation in cosmetics, taunts and weapons (both stat changing weapons and skins/reskins). You really cant expect a f2p game to give away cosmetics for free, though you can actually find one for free if youre premium (spend any amount of money on the game).
Sadly, this game's been lacking changes in terms of gameplay, new weapons (not skins), etc. Though I believe they've been working on the pyro update for a long time now, so not really an issue for me anymore unless it sucks on launch.
Although there's been a HUGE VAC ban wave for both tf2 and csgo, there's obviously still hackers, maybe not playing right now, but they're developing new hacks to bypass VAC's database (I'm assuming it's called a database).
The community is ok, I mean, it's not wrong to taunt after each kill but it really frustrates people (aka me lol) when they've been on a really bad streak either irl or in game and have a random gibus soldier random crit me and randomly taunting. Though seeing them instantly die afterwards is pretty funny, it's still annoying. BUT, most of the community, at least as I've experienced, is from decent to excellent. There's tons of helpful players, and tons of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, but that's something that almost all multiplayer games suffer to some extent, so it's passable.
In conclusion, great game, great gameplay, helpful/cancerous/meme community, microtransactions aren't advantages, and the lack of new content is hopefully going to be fixed soon. A little biased review, mainly because I usually focus on good things more than bad things, but I've really not felt anything bad with the game recently.

I have about 200 hrs into King of the Kill (includes old h1z1 [release] and new).
This game has come a long way from where it started, when I purchased it on release.
Updates every month and new additions to the game content is good.
Gameplay: H1Z1 has a unique kind of mechanics that no other game has. Not only is movement jittery and sketchy, it's not smooth at all. It used to be a lot worse on release.
The game is in third-person and first-person.
The point of KotK is to be the last surviver out of about 165+~ players in one game.
You can achieve 2nd place without killing anyone.
The game can be very difficult for new players that know nothing about the game. For those like myself that are pretty good (can get top 5-10 with ease), the game is quite enjoyable.
It's a 9/10 from me considering there's no other game that gets my anxiety to skyrocket like H1Z1 does.
There's lots of idiots that play this game as well. If you're in a car then someone may chase you in their car and jump out and shoot your car. Meanwhile, you drive away fast and they waste all their bullets trying to shoot you. Most autistic players I have ever seen. Literaly no point in doing that.
There are two ways to play this game.
1) run towards enemies and try to kill them and be killed in the process.
2) run away from enemies and try to survive to the end.
FYI, number two (2) is the way to win.
Also, cheaters are still a thing, although they are rare nowadays.
How to spot a cheater:
They are Royal rank and are constantly in the kill feed. They get about 20-30 kills in Solo.
Thank you for reading!
UPDATE EDIT: April 7th, 2017.
The new update as of April 6th:
I cannot believe it! The devs really nailed it with this update! The game plays SOO smooth now! No jittering, no weird movements, doors open quickly, picking up items is very quick, going in and out of vehicles is quick, such a great improvement i'm impressed!

One of the funniest games I've played, and yes, my hours are in fact very small. At least i think so, because this game is just so addictive, it actually squeezed 20$ from me somehow (thus I'm finally able to review it and add people lol).
Great gameplay, varies in classes playstyles, with mini classes included if you equip certain loadouts (demoknight, freakin mini sentry frontier justice engineer from hell, others).
Great variation in cosmetics, taunts and weapons (both stat changing weapons and skins/reskins). You really cant expect a f2p game to give away cosmetics for free, though you can actually find one for free if youre premium (spend any amount of money on the game).
Sadly, this game's been lacking changes in terms of gameplay, new weapons (not skins), etc. Though I believe they've been working on the pyro update for a long time now, so not really an issue for me anymore unless it sucks on launch.
Although there's been a HUGE VAC ban wave for both tf2 and csgo, there's obviously still hackers, maybe not playing right now, but they're developing new hacks to bypass VAC's database (I'm assuming it's called a database).
The community is ok, I mean, it's not wrong to taunt after each kill but it really frustrates people (aka me lol) when they've been on a really bad streak either irl or in game and have a random gibus soldier random crit me and randomly taunting. Though seeing them instantly die afterwards is pretty funny, it's still annoying. BUT, most of the community, at least as I've experienced, is from decent to excellent. There's tons of helpful players, and tons of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, but that's something that almost all multiplayer games suffer to some extent, so it's passable.
In conclusion, great game, great gameplay, helpful/cancerous/meme community, microtransactions aren't advantages, and the lack of new content is hopefully going to be fixed soon. A little biased review, mainly because I usually focus on good things more than bad things, but I've really not felt anything bad with the game recently.

A hat is a head covering which is worn for various reasons, including protection against weather conditions, ceremonial reasons such as university graduation, religious reasons, safety, or as a fashion accessory.[1] In the past, hats were an indicator of social status.[2] In the military, hats may denote nationality, branch of service, rank or regiment.[3] Police typically wear distinctive hats such as peaked caps or brimmed hats, such as those worn by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. Some hats have a protective function. As examples, the hard hat protects construction workers' heads from injury by falling objects and a British police Custodian helmet protects the officer's head, a sun hat shades the face and shoulders from the sun, a cowboy hat protects against sun and rain and a Ushanka fur hat with fold-down earflaps keeps the head and ears warm. Some hats are worn for ceremonial purposes, such as the mortarboard, which is worn (or carried) during university graduation ceremonies. Some hats are worn by members of a certain profession, such as the Toque worn by chefs. Some hats have religious functions, such as the mitres worn by Bishops and the turban worn by Sikhs.

ARMA 3 is a unique type of shooter. The simulator shooter, which was in theory meant for trainee soldiers to have an idea of how a combat situation would unfold. However in practicality it is used in a variety of different ways. Yes, they are storyline missions that offer the players a realistic format of how warfare would work. Regardless, in my experience and opinion the fun of the game is made by the community itself.
The community is where the game excels. They are countless game modes that they have created from Wasteland to Battle Royale and the ever so popular Role Play servers (a few I have played from the countless on offer). The community is hard working and devote to the game therefore there will always be support, as with ARMA 2 which is still played by many people today.
Where the game falters however is the features that make the game what it is supposed to be. Realism. The inventory has always been difficult and hard to use, even in its predecessor, not much has changed there. It is very hard for beginners to start and get use to the game controls but the more you progress the more you learn.
It’s a game in which the players needs to spend time on and sink their teeth into, before they fully appreciate the experience. Furthermore they need to be a social gamer, as my most memorable experiences are with friends and the community.
Rate a solid 8/10 for gamers who want something different from there shooter experience.

The follow on to Bohemia's ArmA series delivers just like the rest.
If you were a fan of other games such as ArmA 2 for any reason, from the Mil Sim to mods such as DayZ or unique mission files, you will enjoy ArmA 3. It's just like it's predecessor except it has much improved visuals and gameplay mechanics. Not to mention a new setting with ever increasing content through DLC packs and coming maps in the future. Oh, and the community is generally pretty mature. Well... more than other games. :P
Although the core gameplay mechanics of ArmA 3 may not suite every player due to it being inherintly slower paced, there is still something for everyone in ArmA 3. If you enjoy simple TDM, DayZ and it's multiple varients, King of the Hill, Wasteland or another Life Mod. There is a playstyle for everyone and you are most certaintly getting you money's worth when you purchase ArmA 3. Most people haven't even played the campaign yet are still logging thousands of hours on the game due to the diverse options in multiplayer.
No game is without faults. For those with a slightly lower end rig whom are used to playing games such as Minecraft, Garry's Mod and Counter Strike, you may have slight problems depending on what you play on ArmA 3. Some life mods give even me, with a fairly top-mid range rig, some grief. There are also other problems not relating to performance I've known friends to have. For example, one of my friends will crash if he runs dual monitors on ArmA 3, but then again, he's weird.
TLDR. It cost £8.50 or $13 to watch a new film in 2D in the cinema that lasts for 2 hours. $6.50 per hour of entertainment. It costs £35.99 / $56 on steam for ArmA 3 (cheaper on♥♥♥♥♥ and so far I've played for 617 hours and counting. That's $0.09 per hour of entertainment and counting. So yeah, it's worth it.
Oh, and did I mention? There's a tonne of community content. Literally, if you printed all of the coding onto paper, it would probably weigh over a tonne.

I have put up posters all around my neighborhood advising parents to keep their children away from stairs and rocks, lest they end up dead or swallowed whole!

A hat is a head covering which is worn for various reasons, including protection against weather conditions, ceremonial reasons such as university graduation, religious reasons, safety, or as a fashion accessory.[1] In the past, hats were an indicator of social status.[2] In the military, hats may denote nationality, branch of service, rank or regiment.[3] Police typically wear distinctive hats such as peaked caps or brimmed hats, such as those worn by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. Some hats have a protective function. As examples, the hard hat protects construction workers' heads from injury by falling objects and a British police Custodian helmet protects the officer's head, a sun hat shades the face and shoulders from the sun, a cowboy hat protects against sun and rain and a Ushanka fur hat with fold-down earflaps keeps the head and ears warm. Some hats are worn for ceremonial purposes, such as the mortarboard, which is worn (or carried) during university graduation ceremonies. Some hats are worn by members of a certain profession, such as the Toque worn by chefs. Some hats have religious functions, such as the mitres worn by Bishops and the turban worn by Sikhs.

Pros:
-Smooth Gameplay
-Great Classes
-Great Customization
-Simple yet alot of room to work with
-Lots of custom gamemodes
-A still farely decent competitve scene. (Professional)
Cons:
-Community isnt too toxic, but more than average.
-Competitive mode is broken. Cant find a game.
-Very very small team of developers still working on this game.
-Low population of players compared to other modern fps games (obviously)
Overall, I really dont understand why anyone who is a fan of FPS games WOULDNT have this in their library. Its free, try it out and you wont be disappointed.

Arma 3 is a military sandbox that tops its own niche. There are many aspects that have been improved off of Arma 2, but also some that remain—looking at you AI— untouched.
Pros:
—New and improved graphics
—No mouse acceleration
—weapon and equipment customization
—Slightly better AI *being incremently improved
—over 30 different land, air, and water vehicles to choose from
—Huge 270 km squared main island and 20 km squared smaller island
—New underwater mechanics (diving)
—Advanced bullet and penetration ballistics
—*When everyone works together cooperatvely to accomplish a mission,theres a certain feeling you get that other games don't quite have
Cons:
—action menu interface is a bit clunky *sometimes dangerous
—AI are still sometimes incredibly stupid
—only runs on 2 cores at any available time by default *tweakable in launcher settings
—Can only use 4 GB max RAM due to Arma being a 32-bit program
—Does not give full naked eye FOV unless you stay zoomed out
—body armor is a bit too* protective
—Sometimes Arma physics go wrong and flips your vehicle (rarely)
So, obviously the pros outweigh the cons here leading me to conclude that I would definitely recommend this game to others.

I have been with the serie since the first Arma and played countless of hours with A1, A2 absolutely loving the experience. My main interest in Arma games was always the mil sim part (not interested in any rpg/zombie modes) and so far A2 OA is the best for that. Sadly Bohemia got creative and put the A3 in the near future, with more futuristic forces what pretty much killed the "realistic mil sim" part for me.
But still A3 is a great game. It's unbelievably moddable so I was able to get my modern military fix quickly with user created units.
So, the good:
-upgraded graphics engine
-gigantic map
-bipods! Yea, after few years they put bipods in game!
-shooting from vehicles - same as with bipods - finally!
-new more smooth and natural animations
-game is super moddable
-as usual great mission editor (I pretty much spent all my time creating my own missions).
-driving is way more enjoyable than in any prev Armas
Now the bad:
-no female soldiers/civilians -(if COD could we can too)
-insane gun swaying and bobbing, gets infuriating
-stamina - your soldier will fall on his face after running for 10 seconds
-compare to A2 not that many various units
-still no tank/apc interiors
-lots of people reporting insane lag/fps issues MP and SP.
Its a great game, and you can pretty much mod it to whatever you want - rpg/zombies/survival (blah...booring)/ military ops/racing- peek your fix.
Still, if you are looking only for realistic military sim - get Arma 2 Operation Arrowhead and put the ACE mod into it - it will be insanely good and sadly better experience than A3.

Experiences with helicopters:
Very first game: Get in small chopper with five guys and fly for about six minutes to meet a contact. Upon reaching him, I promptly shot him as I didn't see a nameplate.
Some time later: Get in back of dual rotor troop transport with ~6 other troops. Get near LZ, high power shot passes through the hull behind my head, whistles past me and wrecks my SL who was briefing us on the mission.
Several days later: Time to try the pilot class. What could go wrong? I task myself with evacing a small squad on the ground under heavy enemy fire. I get about a kilometer away, when enemy AA takes out my engine and some other fancy control things. With what I could control, I maneuvered around while trailing black smoke calling MAYDAY over the group chat. I hit the ground hard, somehow still intact, and grind along the terrain for at least a hundred meters, tearing my rotor off on a nearby tree and hitting a few enemy soldiers during the powerslide. I crawl out of the wreckage barely alive, and talk through the radio to reassure them that I survived. I then hear the ground team over the radio saying that their mission was now a rescue op. To them, they saw a helo closing in to land, only to crash in the most violent way possible, pretty much cutting a path to me. They made it just as I got shot up.
Bravo Squad's final stand: This happened earlier today and had my heart pounding, our ten man squad was deployed in the open completely surrounded by enemies. Within seconds of disembarking, enemy fire cut down a few of us, who we were forced to leave up on the hill. We all scrambled down in different directions to find tiny pieces of cover while we waited for our attack chopper to open fire. He did, but was promptly hit and crash landed a quarter mile away. With our remaining men, we moved down the valley toward the wreckage, finding him incapacitated next to the cockpit. On a quick head count, we found that our combat medic had been killed in the opening wave and we had no way to save him in the field. While our SL called for a medevac, I picked up the pilot and pulled him into a small house, which we quickly garrisoned. By this time, we were down to five of our original team, plus one of our own wounded and the pilot. Our requests for a medevac quickly turned into an extraction request, which was accepted by a pilot nearly 10km away.
We held for several minutes, until we started to hear the chopper getting close to our position. My SL had been shot in the face through a window, along with our marksman. The incoming pilot essentially told us that we had ten seconds after he touched down to get on board or he would have to leave. Aware of this, I picked up the heli pilot, an engineer picked up our SL, and our other autorifleman followed behind us, giving covering fire. the engineer reached the chopper. loaded our SL into the back and jumped in, giving supporting fire. I reached the chopper next, and just as I got the pilot inside, a shot hit me in the back and incapacitated me. Our rifleman turned to me, and in that moment got shot in the arm.
He just yelled at our pilot to go, the fire was too much to stay. Not even five seconds after dustoff, an enemy sniper caught him.
You could say I'm enjoying the game.

You know that feeling when you get a steam notification, but it's just another raffle group you joined announcing their fifth giveaway that day? The whole really happy to interact with other people but just end up hating them all instead? Yeah, TF2 has really gotten there for me. I used to play it a couple years back everyday after school and I'd have a lot of fun. After awhile I found other games and decided to let this old friend have a break. Come a year later, and what used to be a cherished memory had become a game about levels and ranks instead of good ol' fashioned fun. I decided I wasn't interested in the road that Valve was taking it, so I jumped ship again. Now we're here, another year later, and I decided to pump another fifty hours into this game begrudgingly. I've never been amazing at the game, but no matter where I go people are just rude or annoying (sometimes a perfect mixture of both.) I don't mean some of the players either, the majority of the people I play with are just salty teenagers or twenty-somethings who can't have a little fun and must make sure that they have the highest kill streak, and gloat all the while too. This really doesn't matter though, the mute button exhists, and you don't have to look at the chat. Just think of this as a minor problem. What's not a minor problem is the "new" (it's new to me) match making system that screws you over more often then not. I'll sit there loading a game and right when client info is sending, turns out the game's been over for a minute and a half and voting for the next map has already begun. I miss the days you could just look at a list of servers all stating which maps were being played, and you could just pick your favorite. It's overall just a negative experience for me and my friends who have stuck around on and off with the game like me. You may be saying that complaining about a free game is stupid becasue you didn't pay for it. Well, I've "payed" over eighthundred hours and several hundred dollars in items. I love this game, that's why I criticize it in a desperate attempt to make it fun again. I don't recommend downloading TF2, now would be an awful time to start.

Experiences with helicopters:
Very first game: Get in small chopper with five guys and fly for about six minutes to meet a contact. Upon reaching him, I promptly shot him as I didn't see a nameplate.
Some time later: Get in back of dual rotor troop transport with ~6 other troops. Get near LZ, high power shot passes through the hull behind my head, whistles past me and wrecks my SL who was briefing us on the mission.
Several days later: Time to try the pilot class. What could go wrong? I task myself with evacing a small squad on the ground under heavy enemy fire. I get about a kilometer away, when enemy AA takes out my engine and some other fancy control things. With what I could control, I maneuvered around while trailing black smoke calling MAYDAY over the group chat. I hit the ground hard, somehow still intact, and grind along the terrain for at least a hundred meters, tearing my rotor off on a nearby tree and hitting a few enemy soldiers during the powerslide. I crawl out of the wreckage barely alive, and talk through the radio to reassure them that I survived. I then hear the ground team over the radio saying that their mission was now a rescue op. To them, they saw a helo closing in to land, only to crash in the most violent way possible, pretty much cutting a path to me. They made it just as I got shot up.
Bravo Squad's final stand: This happened earlier today and had my heart pounding, our ten man squad was deployed in the open completely surrounded by enemies. Within seconds of disembarking, enemy fire cut down a few of us, who we were forced to leave up on the hill. We all scrambled down in different directions to find tiny pieces of cover while we waited for our attack chopper to open fire. He did, but was promptly hit and crash landed a quarter mile away. With our remaining men, we moved down the valley toward the wreckage, finding him incapacitated next to the cockpit. On a quick head count, we found that our combat medic had been killed in the opening wave and we had no way to save him in the field. While our SL called for a medevac, I picked up the pilot and pulled him into a small house, which we quickly garrisoned. By this time, we were down to five of our original team, plus one of our own wounded and the pilot. Our requests for a medevac quickly turned into an extraction request, which was accepted by a pilot nearly 10km away.
We held for several minutes, until we started to hear the chopper getting close to our position. My SL had been shot in the face through a window, along with our marksman. The incoming pilot essentially told us that we had ten seconds after he touched down to get on board or he would have to leave. Aware of this, I picked up the heli pilot, an engineer picked up our SL, and our other autorifleman followed behind us, giving covering fire. the engineer reached the chopper. loaded our SL into the back and jumped in, giving supporting fire. I reached the chopper next, and just as I got the pilot inside, a shot hit me in the back and incapacitated me. Our rifleman turned to me, and in that moment got shot in the arm.
He just yelled at our pilot to go, the fire was too much to stay. Not even five seconds after dustoff, an enemy sniper caught him.
You could say I'm enjoying the game.

Half of a peeled and diced carrot, 1 (14 ounce) can of coconut milk, 1 tablespoon of green curry past. 2 Skinless boneless chicken breasts halved and cubed. ( WTH IS CUBED? )  2 cups of chicken stock, 1/4 cup of chopped green onions(Where do you even get this?) 1 lime, juiced. That's about it.
Step One
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Stir in the garlic and carrot, and cook 5 minutes. Mix in 1/4 the coconut milk. Stirring constantly, bring to a boil. Mix in curry paste. Place the chicken in the pot, and toss to coat.
Step Two
Reduce heat to low, and pour in the chicken stock. Cook until heated through. Stir in remaining coconut milk, lime juice, and green onions. Continue to cook and stir at least 10 minutes before serving.

This game... Well, the story is: if you hope for a campaign, it's here, but it is one of the worst i've played - after 5 hours of a "meh" 1st campaign, comes the second one, where a greek insurgent has a terrible accent... polish, to be exact (no racism against poles, i am one, and our accent does sound awful). But the multiplayer - as addictive as it can get. Good balance when it comes to co-op - it always is a challenge to beat the ai. Though it does obviously have some bugs, sometimes.
Pros:
- Fresh and new compared to BF and CoD... and in my opinion somehow better than both.
- Quite good graphics
- A nice choice of weapons in MP... though there could be more
- A LOT of creativity from the devs
- Finally, a truly team-based FPS
- A lot of customisability for your character - though it's not Rainbow Six Vegas 2 level of it.
Cons:
- The campaign is crap - enemies hitting you from impossible angles, a pretty bad story... though better than CoD:G
- Even if you have a beastly PC, there will be a frame rate drop when driving in vehicles if you have you view distance too high (as infantry, i use 8000 m, i have to use 1200 in vehicles)
- Bugs bugs bugs... Though the devs patched a lot of them already.
Overally, the game is a 9/10. It would be a 10/10 if the campaign was a tad better, and if not for bugs which actually hurt the gameplay (sinking into a pier when trying to climb it) it would be definitely the best FPS on the market. It is the best when it comes to team play and realism though. Definitly recommend.

Community makes this game.
The campaign is okay and the base gameplay is actually pretty good. There's a fair selection of cars, guns and aircraft. But, where this game really shines is the community.
Head to the steam workshop for some custom missions and even make your own if you know what you're doing. It's amazing what these people can do! The hitman series, sniper alley, and the extrensive 'FR' series are some of the best!
You can stay in the workshop, though I recommend you head over to
for some mods! They make the game infinitely more fun and interesting. My favourites are TRYK's uniforms, Peral's A10c, British Armed Forces, the HLC guns packs, Wake Island, and a Chinook pack if you don't have the Heli DLC.
Finally, Arma 3's best feature, multiplayer. Sooooooooo many good game mode mods await you there. Wasteland, Epoch and Breaking Point for some DayZ-esque mods- all great. If you want a hunger games type experience you can try Playerunknowns Battle Royale, which is really fun (especially with friends to team up with). Finally, Arma 3 Life/Evolution RPG is an amazing mod- much like island/city life for ArmA II and an improvement on the already fun Altis Life. I recommend watching youtube videos of each.
So yes, I recommend, especially if you have a friend to play with. However, it's good even if you don't/

You know that feeling when you get a steam notification, but it's just another raffle group you joined announcing their fifth giveaway that day? The whole really happy to interact with other people but just end up hating them all instead? Yeah, TF2 has really gotten there for me. I used to play it a couple years back everyday after school and I'd have a lot of fun. After awhile I found other games and decided to let this old friend have a break. Come a year later, and what used to be a cherished memory had become a game about levels and ranks instead of good ol' fashioned fun. I decided I wasn't interested in the road that Valve was taking it, so I jumped ship again. Now we're here, another year later, and I decided to pump another fifty hours into this game begrudgingly. I've never been amazing at the game, but no matter where I go people are just rude or annoying (sometimes a perfect mixture of both.) I don't mean some of the players either, the majority of the people I play with are just salty teenagers or twenty-somethings who can't have a little fun and must make sure that they have the highest kill streak, and gloat all the while too. This really doesn't matter though, the mute button exhists, and you don't have to look at the chat. Just think of this as a minor problem. What's not a minor problem is the "new" (it's new to me) match making system that screws you over more often then not. I'll sit there loading a game and right when client info is sending, turns out the game's been over for a minute and a half and voting for the next map has already begun. I miss the days you could just look at a list of servers all stating which maps were being played, and you could just pick your favorite. It's overall just a negative experience for me and my friends who have stuck around on and off with the game like me. You may be saying that complaining about a free game is stupid becasue you didn't pay for it. Well, I've "payed" over eighthundred hours and several hundred dollars in items. I love this game, that's why I criticize it in a desperate attempt to make it fun again. I don't recommend downloading TF2, now would be an awful time to start.

The most famous of the classic blunders, we're told, is getting involved in a land war in Asia. Arma III should be at a healthy remove then, centered as it is around the battle for a fictional Mediterranean archipelago. It certainly plays all the right cards: vaguely foreboding news montages, not-so-vague allusions to real-world conflicts, and realistic weaponry and other military miscellanea. Here is the modern shooter, dressed for success.
But what's to be said for the wisdom of appending a campaign mode to a game that has traditionally been appreciated as a multiplayer creative suite? There's a blunder for the modern era. The Arma series is known foremost as a platform: a malleable assembly of characters and military objects, and rules to govern their behavior. Modding enthusiasts leverage in-game editors and a relatively ungated code structure to produce their own playable content in lieu of formal designs, and to great effect. It was odd, then, to see some lamenting the relegation of Arma III's campaign to three downloadable post-release entries. There's a stubborn canard that asserts a video game's single-player campaign, if offered, must be its nominal flagship, even when in practice it's a secondary (or tertiary) concern for player and developer alike.
But a campaign was promised, and so a campaign must be delivered. NATO forces are in the midst of a drawdown on the island of Stratis, when the once-friendly local forces lash out in a surprise attack. A multistage affair ensues, playing out in a dull triptych: Survive. Adapt. Win. The grunt tasked with doing that surviving, adapting, and winning is one Corporal Kerry, who reacts to every order he's given with a beleaguered protest ("You want me to do what??"), which is a curious trait for a soldier with a non-zero amount of experience. You, as Kerry, take on an escalating part in an escalating war, eventually graduating from a follower role on Stratis' meager 20 square kilometers to commanding a squad on Altis and its staggering 270 square kilometers. There are a few vague allusions to an overarching plot involving a British black-ops group and some suspicious earthquakes, but neither plot point stakes much of a claim on the proceedings.
The campaign is a strange beast, torn between an earnest attempt to render the tedium and dispassionate remove that color modern warfare, and the Hollywood bombast that colors Modern Warfare a la Call of Duty. This is the sort of conflict where acronyms (NATO, FIA) fight acronyms (CSAT, AAF) over acronyms (LZs, OPs). But it's also the sort where trite wartime quotes fill the interstitial screens, and where the only attempt to characterize the enemy force is an epithet--"greenback"--that's occasionally spat. Arma III is content to let you idle while an ally goes through a lengthy, inaudible, and ultimately inconsequential discussion with a checkpoint guard, or direct you to report in to characters whose only purpose is to refer you over to talk to your commanding officer a few yards away. It restricts your character's movement speed to a controlled jog--elbows in, gun stock squarely nestled on the shoulder--and sends you humping across the hills and valleys of Altis for miles without encountering anything worth loosing a round at. Then an electric guitar wails, a bomber starts strafing your position, and you're forced to bug out at the same ponderous pace that you entered with seconds ago.
The fractured nature of Arma III's campaign makes for an uneven experience at best, but that variability does have an accentuating effect when things fall into a more natural stride. For one, there's a real fragility to Kerry and his unit. So when Bohemia dangles the carrot of an escape helicopter before you at the end of one grueling mission, and then snatches it away with an untimely bit of antiaircraft fire, Kerry's horror-struck pleas of "no no No No NO!" take on a bitter pathos. The introduction of the island of Altis is another high point, presenting a rigorous mission that sees Kerry attempting to rearm and regroup after being stranded behind enemy lines. When Arma III isn't trying to show off a fancy new military gadget or weave in its half-baked tale of black-ops intrigue, when it's leaning on the more tangible drama of a botched rescue or frantic coms chatter, it simmers in a way most shooters can't.
It helps that your forces aren't punctuating every explosion with a string of expletives, of course. But for the better part of the campaign I supplied my own. Not two skirmishes into the Survive campaign's relatively tame first level, it seems I'd already died more times than I had in the entirety of Dark Souls, and that game's motto is "Prepare to Die." I'd hop off five-foot-tall ledges and crumple into a bloody heap. I'd get gunned down while looking at the full screen map, after being prompted to look at the map. I'd open up the help menu for instructions on some trial-by-fire task, and get killed while reading them. I'd succumb to razor-accurate shots fired by enemies in distant hills, enemies who never seemed to have a scope on their guns when I eventually overcame them. Some of these instances were learning experiences, and not soon repeated. Others felt like side effects of the campaign's delay and piecemeal release schedule--what Arma veteran would have welcomed a long-awaited mode that leads with a thorough introduction to controls he or she is already familiar with?
The campaign is a strange beast, torn between an earnest attempt to render the tedium and dispassionate remove that color modern warfare, and the Hollywood bombast that colors Modern Warfare a la Call of Duty.
Arma III uses the full keyboard for its array of possible actions, split between personal affairs like toggling flashlights and binoculars, and issuing orders to your squad. Much of the heavy lifting is foisted on the mousewheel, of all things, which scrolls through contextual actions for almost anything that's to be done in the game. The controls alternate between instrumental and overly finicky, but they never cease to be an aspect of Arma III that requires constant attention. The unwieldiness does lend combat a certain gravitas, however. Most modern shooters grant an athletic flourish to the act of killing; here, the satisfaction of downing an enemy comes from the knowledge that he won't be shooting at you anymore, not in how adroitly you head-shotted him.
There isn't such a positive spin to be put on Arma III's artificial intelligence, however. It's particularly damning, because the strategic underpinnings require a close coordination with squadmates that the game's engine isn't prepared to give. Teammates follow commands at their leisure, if they follow them at all. During one marathon trek across the island, I reached my destination with only two of my eight-man squad in tow. Looking back from the top of our hilltop destination, I could chart the lost squad members like dropped breadcrumbs--one trapped on a rock, four frozen solid in the middle of a field, and the last determined never to leave the two-story building he'd wandered into of his own volition. All attempts to order a regroup returned a chorus of firm but vexing "Negative." So much for "no man gets left behind," then.

This game's alright. I've yet to come across anyone russian, any trolls, nor any particularly angry people. Each class is easily distinguised from one another whether you have cosmetics items or not. Most game-changing things are available without paying money, even if it takes a while.
Now that we've gotten all that stuff out of the way, there are multiple game modes. Out of these modes you can choose what maps you'll be entered in. There's a capture the flag, which is one of the few modes I can't actually provide details for, but I'm sure is like most CTF modes. They have a king of the hill mode, where both teams try to capture a single "capture point" (I have little experience with first person shooters, so I don't know how many games use the concept). There are also two modes, forgot their names, where in one the blue team (sorry, "Blu" team) tries to push through two points while the red team tries to defend them, and in the other mode both teams try to get to all five points. In the last mode, one team tries to push a cart to the end of the rail it's on, while the other team tries to stop them. They do have variations of these modes, but I haven't tried them.
There are nine classes to play as, all of which might employ different strategies. First, my personal favorite, the scout goes much faster than other classes and has a double jump to start. They capture or hold objectives twice as fast as other classes. They have a scattergun (basically a shotgun, a lot of classes have variations of shotguns), a pistol they can unload and reload very quickly, and a baseball bat.
Second, the soldier, can deal a lot of damage at a moderate range. They have a rocket launcher, which deals a ton of damage if you manage to get a direct hit and decent damage if you get it to land near them, a shotgun (What did I tell you?) and a shovel, which is just another melee weapon.
Third, the pyromaniac's main thing is using a flamethrower. Anything hit with the flamethrower is set on fire, taking damage over time unless it's taken care of through numerous ways. He also has... *sigh*... a shotgun, and a fireman's axe as a melee.
Fourth is the demolitionist, who uses a grenade launcher to get enemies hiding behind cover, a sticky bomb launcher to essentially lay mines, and a bottle as a melee weapon.
Fifth is the heavy, who has an immense amount of health, wields a large machine gun, yet another shotgun, and just punches things as a melee attack. This is by far the most straightforward class in the game, but not necessarily the most useful.
Sixth is the engineer, who can make three or four buildings, depending on whether you consider the teleporter to be one or two buildings. These buildings require scrap to build. The engineer can make a dispenser to get health, ammo, and scrap without ever leaving his fortified area. The engineer can also build a turret, one of the most annoying things to go up against. These... These
can do immense damage if nobody knows how to take care of these (especially on the harvest map with what minute experience I have). They can be disposed of by a spy (more on that later) or a good demolitionist. The last of the engineer's buildings is the teleporter, for which you need to build both the entrance and the exit. It's one way, and neither will work while the other doesn't exist. In his arsenal, well, I'm going to be honest, there's no reason to do anything but use the wrench. You use it to help build, and it does massive damage compared to about any other melee weapon (except backstabs, more on that later).
Seventh, the doctor heals using a healgun. Once you've been healing enough, you can make you and one other player invulnerable for a time. The other weapons in the doctor's arsenal include the syringe gun, a weapon affected mildly by gravity you can use to defend yourself, and a bonesaw, this class's melee weapon.
Eighth, the sniper has a long range weapon you can use to instantly kill most enemies with a headshot. I've tried against AI, and it's easier said than done. All the advice I can give you is if you notice an enemy goes a particular way most of the     time, anticipate it. I can't tell you much about the weapons the sniper has. I can, however, tell you about...
Ninth, the spy is by far the most unique class. It can temporarily turn invisible at the cost of the ability to attack for that time, look like someone on the enemy team, backstab with a butterfly knife to instantly kill anyone, sabatage buildings, and has a pistol with similar reloading time as the scout.
All of these characters have different versions of weapons you can obtain at random. My personal favorite is the holy mackeral for the scout, simply because it tells everyone if you even slapped someone with the fish. The game even shows "fish kill!" on the top right corner of the screen, where kills are shown, when you kill someone with it.
The humor in the game is fantastic, if you can hear it above everything else.

Team Fortress 2 (TF2) is a team-based multiplayer first-person shooter video game developed and published by Valve Corporation. It is the sequel to the 1996 mod Team Fortress for Quake and its 1999 remake, Team Fortress Classic. It was released as part of the video game bundle The Orange Box in October 2007 for Microsoft Windows and the Xbox 360. A PlayStation 3 version followed in December 2007. The game was released for Windows as a standalone entry in April 2008, and was updated to support OS X in June 2010 and Linux in February 2013. It is distributed online through Valve's digital retailer Steam, with retail distribution being handled by Electronic Arts.
In Team Fortress 2, players join one of two teams comprising nine character classes, battling in a variety of game modes including capture the flag and king of the hill. The development is led by John Cook and Robin Walker, creators of the original Team Fortress. Announced in 1998, the game once had more realistic, militaristic visuals and gameplay, but this changed over the protracted nine-year development. After Valve released no information for six years, Team Fortress 2 regularly featured in Wired News' annual vaporware list among other ignominies. The finished Team Fortress 2 has cartoon-like visuals influenced by the art of J. C. Leyendecker, Dean Cornwell, and Norman Rockwell, and uses Valve's Source game engine.
Team Fortress 2 received critical acclaim for its art direction, gameplay, humor, and use of character in a multiplayer-only game. Valve continues to release new content, including maps, items and game modes, as well as community-made updates and contributed content. In June 2011, it became free-to-play, supported by microtransactions for in-game cosmetics. A 'drop system' was also added and refined, allowing free-to-play users to periodically receive game equipment and items by use of a random number generator. Though the game had a unofficial competitive scene for many years, support for official competitive play through ranked matchmaking and an overhauled casual experience was added in July 2016.

Tips for staying alive in Arma 3 in multiplayer:
. Stay low in cover all the time, if you poke your head up without knowing exactly where the enemy is you will die
. Never trust chopper pilots, the majority of them are idiots who think this game is Battlefield 4 and you can parachute right into the middle of a warzone unscathed
. Choppers are fragile and easy to destroy, don't use them unless you know what you're doing, I downed two choppers on my first game just firing blindly at the pilot
. Reviving teammates actually makes people like you unlike in other FPS'
. Stay away from ladders they're deathtraps
. Always walk when going down any form of stairs
. Just because you don't see the enemy doesn't necessarily mean they aren't there
. Make sure you have very very good eyesight in this game as you will be fighting enemy players you can barely see at a distance
. Staying low doesn't necessarily work in open spaces, run like hell if you hear gunshots, sometimes you might make it
. If you hear gunfire clicking loudly then that means you're getting shot at, so get the hell out of there
. Firing your weapon is sometimes the worse thing you can do in Arma 3 as it just gives away your position, only fire when you can hit an enemy
. Don't go offroad unless you're good at spotting small rocks, your tires can and will break

ArmA 3 is the best war simulation game you can get today. The different multiplayer gamemodes you can play and all the mods thats in this game is insane, especially the RP communities that starting to become a massive thing in the gaming industry.
Even though ArmA 3 is the most realistic and full of gaming potential, it can be quite hard to find a community that you click with, typically you need to find some friends from outside and get them into this too, Then theres the time consume-
which basicly means, if you got a girlfriend that you have to spent time with, you either have to play ArmA 3 together or drop either ArmA or the GF(This is the best choice aha), then theres also the hardware issues. When I started playing ArmA 3 my Geforce Experience program automatically chose Ultra for all the settings, which my PC didn't really enjoy, so I crashed and lagged a lot, so I chose to look into the configs, and saw that it all was on Ultra, so I turned it to medium.(This was with a single GTX-660TI GPU), and now later I have bought 2(SLI) 970. So what have we learned yet?
Bad things
1st. Community play(Singleplayer is boring and etc.)
2nd. Time consuming.
3rd. Hardware issues.
Good things
1st. Awesome experiences with both RP and other kind of gamemodes.
2nd. Meeting people from all over the world, and forming an virtual community.
3rd. A really good solution if you want some competitive realistic war scenarios.
4th. A lot of online users, so you shouldn't worry about not finding a server for your favourite gamemode.
All in all, I find ArmA 3 one of my favourite games, which is why I have chosen to say that I think you should buy this game if you want something realistic and "fun" but really time consuming.

This created the Combat Update, the single worst update I think I have ever seen in a popular game OTHER THAN the 'Meet your Match' update for TF2. It completly changed the combat mechanics of the original game and promised fair recoil compensation, improved hit reg, and an overall better feel for the game. Movement is complete trash. ENAS is extremely overpowered in close range combat and it was fine the way it was.
Hit Reg is almost as worse as ever, showing lots of  'oddshots' where players are shooting straight on a player and getting no damage markers.
There are countless other issues wrong with the new update (which I will not go into detail about), but the worst part is is Daybreaks complete ignorance towards any sort of useful improvements. So far their most recent updates have been making it easier to join servers and other features :(.

Tips for staying alive in Arma 3 in multiplayer:
. Stay low in cover all the time, if you poke your head up without knowing exactly where the enemy is you will die
. Never trust chopper pilots, the majority of them are idiots who think this game is Battlefield 4 and you can parachute right into the middle of a warzone unscathed
. Choppers are fragile and easy to destroy, don't use them unless you know what you're doing, I downed two choppers on my first game just firing blindly at the pilot
. Reviving teammates actually makes people like you unlike in other FPS'
. Stay away from ladders they're deathtraps
. Always walk when going down any form of stairs
. Just because you don't see the enemy doesn't necessarily mean they aren't there
. Make sure you have very very good eyesight in this game as you will be fighting enemy players you can barely see at a distance
. Staying low doesn't necessarily work in open spaces, run like hell if you hear gunshots, sometimes you might make it
. If you hear gunfire clicking loudly then that means you're getting shot at, so get the hell out of there
. Firing your weapon is sometimes the worse thing you can do in Arma 3 as it just gives away your position, only fire when you can hit an enemy
. Don't go offroad unless you're good at spotting small rocks, your tires can and will break
