Introduction: Before I start, I have 760 hours on H1Z1 and started playing right at the end of preseason 2, and I have reached Royalty in a few of those seasons. I have a good understanding of the game and it's mechanics. i've watched this game "evolve" over the various preseasons, whether it evolved for the good or the bad is really up to the player. With that being said, the majority of the people who have been playing for a good while like me, agree that H1Z1 really has taken a turn for the worst. Before you start to blame the new players for wanting the game to be easier for them or the advanced players for wanting some sort of change in gameplay mechanics, none of their opinions really mattered in the first place, let me explain why. Daybreak Games is the one to blame for this game's downfall, not the players or community, the devs. They didn't change the game because of the new players who wanted the game to be easier because they kept getting 2 tapped by the good people. The devs want more money, period. Honestly, I'm having trouble typing that with confidence just because the game is now dying because of their poor decisions to cater to brand new players rather than enforcing a "skill gap". They're digging themselves a hole and it might be too late to update the game out of the bottom of it.
Gameplay Mechanics: My biggest point to make about mechanics has to be the recoil. The combat update ruined this game and I cannot force that statement enough. The new AR-15 recoil especially made spraying WORSE and all it did was lower the skill gap. Daybreak should have reliazed that horizontal recoil was completely unique to H1. Seriously, what other game can implement something as dumb as horizontal recoil and have the game do good? The answer is no other game besides H1Z1. It was the most fun and unique aspect to the game which oddly made sense while you were playing. Switching to vertical recoil was just taking away the uniqueness of the game and just turning it into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mainstream game. Next, the movement. If you have ever played PUBG, you know how it feels when you move compared to pre-combat update H1Z1. It feels slow and sluggish, which is exactly what post combat update H1 feels like. The pattern is starting to form, Daybreak is making H1Z1 as close to PUBG as possible. This really sucks to see for the veteran players because we play this game because its NOT PUBG. This review is already long so I'll leave it with those 2 main points.
Unneccesary Changes: Daybreak is known to ignore big issues within the game while spending their time on trivial things to add to the game that nobody cares about. Examples, in the most recent update, new gun models were added. Someone explain to me why we needed that? Anyways, some more examples I won't go in detail with are new crates, new POIs, a new menu, I could go on but you get the point.
Unqualified Developers: I want to know what college or university these people attended, or better yet if they even finished high school. Some of the things these people do are so beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I physically can't even comprehend the reasoning behind it. An example is in the combat training or deathmatch mode, who's idea was it to have a set loadout that cannot be changed by the player, (i.e. AR/AK, shotty/smh, pistol) just let us make our own loadouts with our preferred weapons in whatever slot we're comfortable with. It seems like whenever the community asks for something, Daybreak does the polar opposite. We asked for better hitreg, a better shotgun spread/damage, and the reversal or fix to desync. What did we get? The ♥♥♥♥ing combat update.
I think I'll stop there, if you want more info just go on the H1 reddit, there are tons of great informative people on there. If you read my review all the way through, you're a beast. If you found it informative, a thumbs up would be much appreciated. There are definitly points I missed in this review, so if I catch any I'll be sure to make an edit at a later time. My final verdict is I can't reccomend you this game in it's current state. Thanks for reading.

ArmA 3 is the best war simulation game you can get today. The different multiplayer gamemodes you can play and all the mods thats in this game is insane, especially the RP communities that starting to become a massive thing in the gaming industry.
Even though ArmA 3 is the most realistic and full of gaming potential, it can be quite hard to find a community that you click with, typically you need to find some friends from outside and get them into this too, Then theres the time consume-
which basicly means, if you got a girlfriend that you have to spent time with, you either have to play ArmA 3 together or drop either ArmA or the GF(This is the best choice aha), then theres also the hardware issues. When I started playing ArmA 3 my Geforce Experience program automatically chose Ultra for all the settings, which my PC didn't really enjoy, so I crashed and lagged a lot, so I chose to look into the configs, and saw that it all was on Ultra, so I turned it to medium.(This was with a single GTX-660TI GPU), and now later I have bought 2(SLI) 970. So what have we learned yet?
Bad things
1st. Community play(Singleplayer is boring and etc.)
2nd. Time consuming.
3rd. Hardware issues.
Good things
1st. Awesome experiences with both RP and other kind of gamemodes.
2nd. Meeting people from all over the world, and forming an virtual community.
3rd. A really good solution if you want some competitive realistic war scenarios.
4th. A lot of online users, so you shouldn't worry about not finding a server for your favourite gamemode.
All in all, I find ArmA 3 one of my favourite games, which is why I have chosen to say that I think you should buy this game if you want something realistic and "fun" but really time consuming.

I enjoy the concept, and it can be fun because the game does offer a bit of a challenge, although I would disagree whole heartedly that this is anywhere close to being a true or even quality realistic combat game.  I find myself at odds with these claims for several reasons:
1. It's difficult to control how much sound you put out.  This isn't realistic whatsoever.  Neither is the distance at which you hear player actions, such as footsteps.  I was honestly expecting it to be realistic here.  No biggie I guess..
2. The controls aren't realistic.  They don't even make it remotely easy to perform basic minute-to-minute actions with the default controls, forcing you to scroll between pulling out guns and choosing to interact with a door.  You also don't get much control over interactable objects like doors.  I'd have thought that being stealth was a major factor in 'realistic' combat, but not in this game.
3. A lot of strategy in this game is based around flaws in the way the game is designed.  One example is looting.  Loot doesn't even appear until players are within a certain distance of a location that will spawn loot, and it's usually within the same time frame that it appears.  When coming upon a town to loot (or if you're hunting other players), a common strategy is to simply stalk the perimeter looking for spawned loot objects (chairs, sofas, filing cabinets, etc).  If you see one, then you know you're about to get to shoot at somebody.  Really lame.
Basically there is no stealth in this game.  It has a bunch of vehicles and "open world" environment, but in the end this falls light years short of being a true realistic combat game, much less user friendly.  Devs really need to go through a year of UX before they are unleashed upon the world.  These are some major oversights.
Other cons:
1. The learning curve for the controls is higher than it needs to be.  It took almost 30min to change just a few basic controls, which wound up getting double bound and unbound without any indication to me that it was happening.  This is a MAJOR flaw and I've personally heard from 3 friends that this is the reason they do not play this game.  Stupid and shallow I know, but honestly it's supposed to be a fun game.  When you jump in and get frustrated just trying to get your controls down, that is a red flag that some major fixes need to be done for them.

I enjoy the concept, and it can be fun because the game does offer a bit of a challenge, although I would disagree whole heartedly that this is anywhere close to being a true or even quality realistic combat game.  I find myself at odds with these claims for several reasons:
1. It's difficult to control how much sound you put out.  This isn't realistic whatsoever.  Neither is the distance at which you hear player actions, such as footsteps.  I was honestly expecting it to be realistic here.  No biggie I guess..
2. The controls aren't realistic.  They don't even make it remotely easy to perform basic minute-to-minute actions with the default controls, forcing you to scroll between pulling out guns and choosing to interact with a door.  You also don't get much control over interactable objects like doors.  I'd have thought that being stealth was a major factor in 'realistic' combat, but not in this game.
3. A lot of strategy in this game is based around flaws in the way the game is designed.  One example is looting.  Loot doesn't even appear until players are within a certain distance of a location that will spawn loot, and it's usually within the same time frame that it appears.  When coming upon a town to loot (or if you're hunting other players), a common strategy is to simply stalk the perimeter looking for spawned loot objects (chairs, sofas, filing cabinets, etc).  If you see one, then you know you're about to get to shoot at somebody.  Really lame.
Basically there is no stealth in this game.  It has a bunch of vehicles and "open world" environment, but in the end this falls light years short of being a true realistic combat game, much less user friendly.  Devs really need to go through a year of UX before they are unleashed upon the world.  These are some major oversights.
Other cons:
1. The learning curve for the controls is higher than it needs to be.  It took almost 30min to change just a few basic controls, which wound up getting double bound and unbound without any indication to me that it was happening.  This is a MAJOR flaw and I've personally heard from 3 friends that this is the reason they do not play this game.  Stupid and shallow I know, but honestly it's supposed to be a fun game.  When you jump in and get frustrated just trying to get your controls down, that is a red flag that some major fixes need to be done for them.

Be prepared to have to drop another $30 on DLC. Unfortunately Bohemia has decided it wants to milk its community. How original.
Bohemia is not a AAA title company, although, looking at their income begs to differ. Bohemia creates simulators for real world militaries and private contracting companies and turned their more "player friendly" aspects into a game franchise.  This means that you should expect over complicated controls schemes, little content in the way of storylines or variety of missions.  However this game stands out in it's physics and community invovlement.  This game features very intricate ballistic mechanics and has all the necessary mechanics to teach you how to navigate, at night, underwater, or in the middle of a desert.  In truth however, the playability of this game comes from the community made missions and servers which have everything from "roleplay life" missions to "deathmatch" style point and shoot adventures. Player interactions in the Arma series has always been a bit cumbersome. It is sometimes hard to navigate obstacles and terrain on foot, and STILL (this is the third edition of this game afterall) lacks the ability to jump in anyway. This game is also very processor intensive, so be prepared for lower than normal frame rates.
Everything else said, Arma 3 is a very fun game, provided you can find multiplayer missions you like. My biggest complaint is their campaign of downloadable content. It seems almosty as if they created a full game, and then released half of it for full price with the otherhalf costing extra.

Arma 3 is an experiance everyone should see. Although it is buggy at times, it makes up for it with its content and stellar world. There is so much content in this game. You can play Altis Life where you roleplay as a civilian, drug dealer, Cop, and much more. Or if your kinda bored of roleplaying and want some heavy gun play go to King of the Hill where you get nothing but non stop action and fun. Plus there is Wasteland where its an action pack survival wasteland. There is also mods like Breaking Point and Epoch. These are fun as well if your trying to get a Dayz feel but don't wanna buy Dayz standalone. Now to gameplay, Arma is known for its bugs. It can get frustrating and annoying. At times your character desynch's making it hard to play. These do come often when the server is filled and a lot of things are going on. I mean it is a HUGE game. Now for the gun element. Gun play is very fun and tactical. Arma isn't one of those games that you run and gun. Actually that is what gets you killed. Arma is more about positioning and patiance. Flanking, knowing your enemy where abouts, and being able to get an angle on him is a must need traits if you wanna be succesful in a gun fight. Also being prepared is a key element, the more prepared you are the better chances you have. Its more about the gunnar than the actual gun. But as great as it is, gun fights can also be glitchy. Some enemies take multiple shots and don't die. Some get hit but die after walking 50 meters. These glitches do occur. To my final conclusion Arma is a 9/10. I think its content and massive world overshadows its multiple bugs. It is very buggy though so if you hate a buggy game this one isn't for you but if you can handle a few bugs try it out.

I find myself at a loss for words when I attempt to describe the feelings and emotions I encounter when I reminisce of my early days of playing Arma 3. First, before I pass my worthy judgement, I’d like to preface this review with the fact that I was totally new to the FPS and shooter genre upon purchasing Arma 3. I have never played CS:GO in my life. In fact, I’ve played very few FPS in my life. I dove into Arma totally unaware of the steep learning curve. Most of all, I purchased the game without realizing that this title would affect my perspective on PC gaming as a whole.
Arma 3 is a beautiful game. It encompasses the rush of a multiplayer FPS, the adventure of a creative sandbox, the strategy of a hardcore simulation, and a deep love for teamwork in one graphically magnificent open-world masterpiece. I’m not going to mention multiplayer teamwork in this review for the sake of the reader, as it’s something you have to experience yourself, and something I could talk about all day.
While Arma 3 is an amazing game, I discourage those who are faint of specs to steer clear of this-- at times-- just as taxing on your rig as on your wits.
I can go on and on about Arma 3, and still have something new to share. Like the classic Skyrim, you find something new in Arma 3 every day. If you want a game where victory and achievement is spoonfed to you, I discourage you from purchasing this costly concoction.
But if you prefer a difficult, cinematic, challenging, realistic, heart pounding, PTSD instilling war simulator?
Welcome home.
This is War.
This is Arma 3.

How to start?
Well, TF2 is a sacred cow of gaming. You can't really say that you don't enjoy it without being called a noob.
Let's begin by saying that on the premise, TF2 is a near perfect game. And it looks super fun! You get to run around a kill stuff, while at the same time earning supply drop stuff (that requires money to open, of couse >:() and it looks like a game you'd want to get as soon as possible.
However, there are... quite a few flaws with the game.
Firstly, you can't really get in to the game very easily. It... well, just seems to gimmicky. I don't enjoy some of the aspects of the game, like crates. It's really confusing at first.
Next is the fact that you have no idea what on earth is going on in the game until you spend hours playing it. Further discouriging people from playing it. Probably spelt that wrong.
And finally, the game just doesn't seem very appealing to me. That's really all I can say.
But for a free to play, I like it.
If it costed $60.00 USD, I wouldn't even consider buying it.

*waits hours to download this behemoth*
*Loads up a mission because I think I'm a boss; wonders why I get 28 fps on a GTX 760oc
*adjusts graphics to lowest settings... gains 2 fps; gives up entirely on fps
*Starts to play the mission*
Immediately i noticed that it was quiet... Too quiet. We were in a valley advancing toward... something. I didn't read the directions because i thought i was a boss. So here I am sneaking through the grass lookin all camo'd up when out of nowhere i hear a scream and an explosion followed by "HE'S HIT" *radio static* one of my comrades to the right found himself on the recieving end of a grenade launcher, but I was still like "It's all cool, It's just a game, I'm bout to 360 noscope double-tomohawk wreck these fools and.........
Then something happened:
I realized I had no idea who shot my teammate. There aren't markers, there arent hints as to where the enemy is. Son you better have one hell of a surround sound to hear where them bullets be flying from cause this aint COD. You think you good at battlefield? Well that means you can kill one enemy on easy in arma, and son I hope you don't use a controller.
By this time I'm just laying in the grass doing my best not to die. I start shooting at the one enemy that is actually visible.  It took 2 magazines for me to hit him. I only have 5. Now 2 of my teammates are dead so there are only 3 of us left, I start to realize how serious this is getting.. I mean... I have to come back to my family!
I unload another mag on a guy that stuck his head above a rock. My aim seems to have gotten slightly better as realize that 3 round bursts are bae. THEN right as im running out of ammo I feel the muscle fibers of my left arm being tore as a caseless 6.5mm shell tears through it. I react quickly and roll behind a rock to heal myself.
So i pull out a medkit and start workin on myself and my guy gets done and i'm like "Im not healed"...
But oh right, this is arma... Medkits dont heal you. They just keep you from dying.
Now i'm behind my rock and it's starting too look like some real american sniper "I'm ready to come home"♥♥♥♥♥♥ I was looking forward to PTSD at this point.
I look over to my left to find my squads ammo bearer dead. I do a quick mall cop roll over to him, grab his MG and his vest, and roll back over to my rock; getting shot again in the process. I use my last medkit behind that rock and prepare to go full rambo.
I make sure i have ammo in the clip.. there were 67 rounds left. I wait for a gap in the gunfire then i go from prone to a crouch realquick. Now I'm seeing slow motion, I can barely aim because im caughing up blood from being hit (I'm not making this stuff up, folks) I spot the enemy, fired off atleast 20 rounds, then he finally got done reloading and proceded to kill me with 2 shots.
As I lie there, fading out of conciousness, a computer monitor slowly appears in front of me and eventually I realize that it was all a game. I may need therapy.
I later found out there were only 4 enemies. That was normal difficulty. You will die, and you will die often. Me, nor my friend despite being very good at fps games, have never fully completed a mission. I have 255 hours as of writing this.

I wrote a review for this game quite a long time ago, but by now that I think about it I like playing Arma for none of the reasons that I had talked about. Previously I had talked about the mechanics that Bohemia had put into the base game, but I've now come to realize that Arma has become one of those games that are instead defined by the people that play it and mod it. You can take my word for it that Arma is well worth your time if you get a group of talented players/scenario creators, but if you need more proof then allow me to ramble on about a particularly rememberable instance that was thanks to the group I happened to have found, if for nothing else but to write a 'love letter' to people so gratious enough to let me tag along.
The scenario of the day was as follows: Me along with the rest of our group of about six were highered by the powers that be within NATO and the US (cus reasons I assume) to go to some base on some island to find something. Don't worry, we would know it when we see it. They gave us an A-10 and several helicoptors of sorts so it was expended to run into a lot of unfriendly locals.
We were also told not to take anything larger then 7.62 or Homing. So we ended up with a pilot on call, a Squad Leader, MG gunner, a guy with a handy dandy target designator, a medic, and myself. Given that I often times opt to do medic duties I was lost for a role, so I just picked up the highest caliber, semi-automatic sniper I could find, slapped a suppressor and scope on it and went with everyone else to the helicoptors. The pilot checked the helicopter to make sure everything was fine, while we sat in the back making jokes.
"I went to Chasington once," someone yelled over the helicoptors rotors. "It was like this!"
After an uneventful ride to the forested area we were to land, we make our way up a small hillside to overlook the adjacent valley. Directly in front of us we find a small house surrounded by troops and an armored car. They seem to outnumber us. We each pick a target, mine being a man barely visible behind a window. The fight would begin on the SL's word. After a few seconds he stands up from our position and lets loose a grenade towards the truck, followed in quick succession by my rifle shot and the MG to finish up the rest. In a matter of a few noisy seconds and some well placed shots we clear the house.
Then another group on the hillside opposite ours tears into us for tearing into their friends. Immediately we lose our Designator, along with the MG and myself taking a round while we all retreated to a rock for cover. The SL gets on his radio to talk to our Air while me and someone else fire back at the two guys shooting us. We both drop them after a minute, and our very frazzled selves make it to yet another hill that overlooks the base, bringing the armored car with us.
I will say this about Arma, they manage to make some impressive views when it comes to scale. When we crested the hill we could see for miles across a sparsely wooded valley with a town and military base at its end. The base was our target. And next to our target was a very scary, and very operable Self-Propelled gun guarded by some troops. We all collectively♥♥♥♥♥♥a brick foundation and the SL gets on his talkie to radio the A-10. The pilot tells us he'll be there in five minutes and to keep the tank lazered. Good thing we grabbed the designator off our dead guy.
To pass the time we muse about the tank, how many people are in the valley, and what the A-10 run will look like. I hobble over to the guy holding the designator and ask him for the range to the infantry. I provides a number and I range the rifle. The A-10 begins to swoop in and we can barely hear it. We can however see two bombs drop from its wings and impact the tank. The plum of fire reaches forty meters in the sky. We all cheer a bit and plan our next move off the hill and to the base. The pilot tell us there are dozens of guys in the base so we decide to hang back for a bit.
"Hey, can I take a shot at those guys by the tank?" I ask our SL.
"Go for it."
With immeasurable glee I grab up the new designator guy and make him my spotter. He constantly gives me the distance to the group of guys running to the tank. I take aim at the lead man and fire off a shot that explodes on the guy's upper body, sending him backwards. As the designator makes a comment about the hit I take aim at the second guy and fire off three more shots. One of them impacts the guy in the leg and he falls to the ground. Satisfied, and with new orders to get in the truck I stop shooting.
Unbeknownst to us there are atleast fifty people coming up the hill at us after that airstike. In the interest of time lets just say that we got pretty shot up and retreated back a ways with three out of the original five that landed. After quite some time we get some reinforcments and grab another, much larger helicopter to take us right to the base. Apparently we were running out of options. Its me and the newly spawned Designator dangling over the Chinooks back ramp, our SL and MG gunner on the two guns and our medic in the center.
Halfway to the base our medic 'falls' out of the helicopter and manages to safetly land somewhere with a parachute. We have a laugh about it and start to fly over the base. Round start to ping off the sides of the heli as our pilot yells for the side gunners to shoot back. The sparadic firing escalates to a full on machine gun barrage right up at us. Round start to ping around the rear ramp and into the cargo bay. The guy next to me on the ramp takes several rounds and falls out of the back. The pilot yells that we have a fuel leak and we rapidly descend towards the dirt.
We impact the ground and thankfully don't explode. Yet. The pilot yells for everyone to get out. We spread out and deal with the few stragglers that are still shooting at us. We weight our options and decide to just walk into the base. As carefully as possible we sneak into the base, taking a round in our direction here or there. After entering the main gate we are greeted by the rotting welcoming committee. In the base's assembly area are about fifty dead bodies and some blown out vehicles. Thank god for air support.
We move up to the building and assemble at the front door. Someone inside fires a shot through the door and we rethink our decisions. We decide to throw every grenade we have through the door to the hiding troops. Afterwards, me and the pilot charge into the house and double tap the guys inside. We then start to look around for whatever it is we were supposed to find.
They were right, we would know it when we see it. We grab as much of it as we can each hold and haul♥♥♥♥♥out the way we came. We leave in such a hurry no one notices that our MG gunner takes a shot and dies a little ways from the gate. We regroup near some trees on our way to a car nearby. We look back to see where our gunner is, but a round hitting the tree by us convinces us to leave on the car anyways.
I jump into the driver seat with the pilot in the passenger spot and the SL riding in the back. I haul♥♥♥♥♥down the road to get away from the base. After awhile we slow down, have a laugh about everything, and the pilot directs me back to base.
For continuitie sake the mission apparently ended as follows: the people who hired us said they weren't gonna pay us for finding their package, but our SL threatned to tell on them about what was actually inside. They shut up, pay us, and we go on our merry and blood-soaked way. A funny end to a great time of a scenario created by the pilot. Since then he's made and found a lot more. Sometimes in these scenarios I'm on a .50 cal covering a squad, sometimes I'm defusing an IED in the middle of a crowded street as people watch me, and sometimes I'm even leading a squad. However, thanks to the group I play this game with, it is never dull.

*Buys game*
*waits hours to download this behemoth*
*Loads up a mission because I think I'm a boss; wonders why I get 28 fps on a GTX 760oc
*adjusts graphics to lowest settings... gains 2 fps; gives up entirely on fps
*Starts to play the mission*
Immediately i noticed that it was quiet... Too quiet. We were in a valley advancing toward... something. I didn't read the directions because i thought i was a boss. So here I am sneaking through the grass lookin all camo'd up when out of nowhere i hear a scream and an explosion followed by "HE'S HIT" *radio static* one of my comrades to the right found himself on the recieving end of a grenade launcher, but I was still like "It's all cool, It's just a game, I'm bout to 360 noscope double-tomohawk wreck these fools and.........
Then something happened:
I realized I had no idea who shot my teammate. There aren't markers, there arent hints as to where the enemy is. Son you better have one hell of a surround sound to hear where them bullets be flying from cause this aint COD. You think you good at battlefield? Well that means you can kill one enemy on easy in arma, and son I hope you don't use a controller.
By this time I'm just laying in the grass doing my best not to die. I start shooting at the one enemy that is actually visible.  It took 2 magazines for me to hit him. I only have 5. Now 2 of my teammates are dead so there are only 3 of us left, I start to realize how serious this is getting.. I mean... I have to come back to my family!
I unload another mag on a guy that stuck his head above a rock. My aim seems to have gotten slightly better as realize that 3 round bursts are bae. THEN right as im running out of ammo I feel the muscle fibers of my left arm being tore as a caseless 6.5mm shell tears through it. I react quickly and roll behind a rock to heal myself.
So i pull out a medkit and start workin on myself and my guy gets done and i'm like "Im not healed"...
But oh right, this is arma... Medkits dont heal you. They just keep you from dying.
Now i'm behind my rock and it's starting too look like some real american sniper "I'm ready to come home"♥♥♥♥♥♥ I was looking forward to PTSD at this point.
I look over to my left to find my squads ammo bearer dead. I do a quick mall cop roll over to him, grab his MG and his vest, and roll back over to my rock; getting shot again in the process. I use my last medkit behind that rock and prepare to go full rambo.
I make sure i have ammo in the clip.. there were 67 rounds left. I wait for a gap in the gunfire then i go from prone to a crouch realquick. Now I'm seeing slow motion, I can barely aim because im caughing up blood from being hit (I'm not making this stuff up, folks) I spot the enemy, fired off atleast 20 rounds, then he finally got done reloading and proceded to kill me with 2 shots.
As I lie there, fading out of conciousness, a computer monitor slowly appears in front of me and eventually I realize that it was all a game. I may need therapy.
I later found out there were only 4 enemies. That was normal difficulty. You will die, and you will die often. Me, nor my friend despite being very good at fps games, have never fully completed a mission. I have 255 hours as of writing this.
11/10 will die again. Many times

This game 9 diffrent classes, each one unique. These include the classes the Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper and to finish it off the Spy. Each class has diffrent weapons to change your playing style and make your loadout unique. This game is a multiplayer with many game modes as payload, ctf (capture the flag), Arena, Mannpower, Man Vs. Machine, Control Point and many more, including a competitive scene. This game doesn't get old no matter the amount of time you play, as you may see people who have a lot of playtime on the game. Yet with that being said there are people who you will come across who have a lot of experience on the game making it difficult to get good at the game when you're just getting into the swing of things, yet with a new feature in the game the higher level someone is can tell new players who to avoid. Along with select gamemodes there are gamemodes added in by the community, like new maps for your favorite gamemode, dodgeball, deathrun, etc. I bet if your curious about said game and a parent/ guardian/ whatever the game has a very cartoonish demeanor making said violence seem like something out of a child-friendly cartoon, yet if you're younger avoid earlier mentioned community gamemodes due to some player's being mean to said child, try to use mic if older than 15 due to people making fun of your voice aswell.
Yet besides all of the afformentioned problems the game will give you never ending entertainment and can still have the game seem as fresh as the day downloaded, and that's coming from someone with 500+ hours, and with some avid players having 2000+ hours. I recommend you play this game no matter your age, unless your still a fetus, just don't. Yet if you aren't feel free to join this loving community where you can make new friends and relationships, and after reading this and you decide to download this game all have to say is, "Welcome to the TF2 community and all are welcome!"

I wrote a review for this game quite a long time ago, but by now that I think about it I like playing Arma for none of the reasons that I had talked about. Previously I had talked about the mechanics that Bohemia had put into the base game, but I've now come to realize that Arma has become one of those games that are instead defined by the people that play it and mod it. You can take my word for it that Arma is well worth your time if you get a group of talented players/scenario creators, but if you need more proof then allow me to ramble on about a particularly rememberable instance that was thanks to the group I happened to have found, if for nothing else but to write a 'love letter' to people so gratious enough to let me tag along.
The scenario of the day was as follows: Me along with the rest of our group of about six were highered by the powers that be within NATO and the US (cus reasons I assume) to go to some base on some island to find something. Don't worry, we would know it when we see it. They gave us an A-10 and several helicoptors of sorts so it was expended to run into a lot of unfriendly locals.
We were also told not to take anything larger then 7.62 or Homing. So we ended up with a pilot on call, a Squad Leader, MG gunner, a guy with a handy dandy target designator, a medic, and myself. Given that I often times opt to do medic duties I was lost for a role, so I just picked up the highest caliber, semi-automatic sniper I could find, slapped a suppressor and scope on it and went with everyone else to the helicoptors. The pilot checked the helicopter to make sure everything was fine, while we sat in the back making jokes.
"I went to Chasington once," someone yelled over the helicoptors rotors. "It was like this!"
After an uneventful ride to the forested area we were to land, we make our way up a small hillside to overlook the adjacent valley. Directly in front of us we find a small house surrounded by troops and an armored car. They seem to outnumber us. We each pick a target, mine being a man barely visible behind a window. The fight would begin on the SL's word. After a few seconds he stands up from our position and lets loose a grenade towards the truck, followed in quick succession by my rifle shot and the MG to finish up the rest. In a matter of a few noisy seconds and some well placed shots we clear the house.
Then another group on the hillside opposite ours tears into us for tearing into their friends. Immediately we lose our Designator, along with the MG and myself taking a round while we all retreated to a rock for cover. The SL gets on his radio to talk to our Air while me and someone else fire back at the two guys shooting us. We both drop them after a minute, and our very frazzled selves make it to yet another hill that overlooks the base, bringing the armored car with us.
I will say this about Arma, they manage to make some impressive views when it comes to scale. When we crested the hill we could see for miles across a sparsely wooded valley with a town and military base at its end. The base was our target. And next to our target was a very scary, and very operable Self-Propelled gun guarded by some troops. We all collectively♥♥♥♥♥♥a brick foundation and the SL gets on his talkie to radio the A-10. The pilot tells us he'll be there in five minutes and to keep the tank lazered. Good thing we grabbed the designator off our dead guy.
To pass the time we muse about the tank, how many people are in the valley, and what the A-10 run will look like. I hobble over to the guy holding the designator and ask him for the range to the infantry. I provides a number and I range the rifle. The A-10 begins to swoop in and we can barely hear it. We can however see two bombs drop from its wings and impact the tank. The plum of fire reaches forty meters in the sky. We all cheer a bit and plan our next move off the hill and to the base. The pilot tell us there are dozens of guys in the base so we decide to hang back for a bit.
"Hey, can I take a shot at those guys by the tank?" I ask our SL.
"Go for it."
With immeasurable glee I grab up the new designator guy and make him my spotter. He constantly gives me the distance to the group of guys running to the tank. I take aim at the lead man and fire off a shot that explodes on the guy's upper body, sending him backwards. As the designator makes a comment about the hit I take aim at the second guy and fire off three more shots. One of them impacts the guy in the leg and he falls to the ground. Satisfied, and with new orders to get in the truck I stop shooting.
Unbeknownst to us there are atleast fifty people coming up the hill at us after that airstike. In the interest of time lets just say that we got pretty shot up and retreated back a ways with three out of the original five that landed. After quite some time we get some reinforcments and grab another, much larger helicopter to take us right to the base. Apparently we were running out of options. Its me and the newly spawned Designator dangling over the Chinooks back ramp, our SL and MG gunner on the two guns and our medic in the center.
Halfway to the base our medic 'falls' out of the helicopter and manages to safetly land somewhere with a parachute. We have a laugh about it and start to fly over the base. Round start to ping off the sides of the heli as our pilot yells for the side gunners to shoot back. The sparadic firing escalates to a full on machine gun barrage right up at us. Round start to ping around the rear ramp and into the cargo bay. The guy next to me on the ramp takes several rounds and falls out of the back. The pilot yells that we have a fuel leak and we rapidly descend towards the dirt.
We impact the ground and thankfully don't explode. Yet. The pilot yells for everyone to get out. We spread out and deal with the few stragglers that are still shooting at us. We weight our options and decide to just walk into the base. As carefully as possible we sneak into the base, taking a round in our direction here or there. After entering the main gate we are greeted by the rotting welcoming committee. In the base's assembly area are about fifty dead bodies and some blown out vehicles. Thank god for air support.
We move up to the building and assemble at the front door. Someone inside fires a shot through the door and we rethink our decisions. We decide to throw every grenade we have through the door to the hiding troops. Afterwards, me and the pilot charge into the house and double tap the guys inside. We then start to look around for whatever it is we were supposed to find.
They were right, we would know it when we see it. We grab as much of it as we can each hold and haul♥♥♥♥♥out the way we came. We leave in such a hurry no one notices that our MG gunner takes a shot and dies a little ways from the gate. We regroup near some trees on our way to a car nearby. We look back to see where our gunner is, but a round hitting the tree by us convinces us to leave on the car anyways.
I jump into the driver seat with the pilot in the passenger spot and the SL riding in the back. I haul♥♥♥♥♥down the road to get away from the base. After awhile we slow down, have a laugh about everything, and the pilot directs me back to base.
For continuitie sake the mission apparently ended as follows: the people who hired us said they weren't gonna pay us for finding their package, but our SL threatned to tell on them about what was actually inside. They shut up, pay us, and we go on our merry and blood-soaked way. A funny end to a great time of a scenario created by the pilot. Since then he's made and found a lot more. Sometimes in these scenarios I'm on a .50 cal covering a squad, sometimes I'm defusing an IED in the middle of a crowded street as people watch me, and sometimes I'm even leading a squad. However, thanks to the group I play this game with, it is never dull.

You get injured and if you heal you will walk slower, carry too much and you won't be able to move, realistic stamina, etc. The amount of weapons and vehicles is nice but nowhere near the competitors. Yet those few weapons have the most realistic damage and ballistics of any game I've played.
Now after seeing that you are probably asking why I didn't suggest this game to others. Well the game has a lot of cool features and is very promising in all the different ways you can play. But the game is unplayable at times and is very unreliable. In single player a $2000 dollar computer will run at 40-50 fps on all maxed out video settings. (That being one of the major faults of the game itself; a game shouldn't require two to three thousand dollars for a computer to run single player at subpar frame rates.) That same single player also has one of the worst AI systems in a game. If you're in the line of fire prone with your group of guys they will shoot you to get to the enemy. This happens more often than you would think, and it’s such a problem your squad mates will often kill each other. The enemy AI is far superior in combat and you will find yourself leaving your AI squad behind so you can actually accomplish missions because they tend to get the attention of the enemy AI which seems to target you first no matter what. The enemy AI can see you through bushes 800m away crawling through the 3ft tall grass. So if you want a stealth shooter go somewhere else. In fact if you want a better AI and squad experience go buy the original Ghost Recon because it had a better AI and squad system than this game.

WHO CARES ABOUT SINGLE PLAYER JOHN!
Ok then, so you give up on the single player and you go to multiplayer expecting a similar experience without having to worry about the AI. You'll start up a moderate sized 40 man server that has a ping of 30 when you join that is about full and your system will bog down to 10-15 fps. You go around a corner checking for enemies in a town and you won't be able to move your gun fast enough and you'll get owned over and over. If you try to be in a vehicle with a person who has a junk computer, good luck seeing anything.
All in all, great features on a horrible performance platform, and to make up for it you need a server for a computer.

The game is a lot of fun to play, but the negitives simply overwhelm the positives...
1) The game is STILL $60! It's a great game - don't get me wrong, but that price is just too much for a game that's been out  for a little more then 2 years now.
2) DLC's are extremely overpriced. It costs around $20 just for a small helicopter DLC.. Seeing as we've already paid a large $60 - you'd think we'd get a bit more content.
3) Optimization is a joke. I run a 2700k at 4.6ghz backed with a GTX 970 and still get 20-30 FPS on some larger servers. For a game considered "Modern", that's pretty terrible.
4) BUGS! There are sooo many bugs you'll end up breaking your keyboard. Sometimes you'll randomly die, your vehicle will randomly explode, server will crash,  and the game will just crash randomly. Also they use BattleEye for anti-hack which is very good for catching hackers, but has an extremely high rate of false positives! I've been globally banned before just for changing out my graphics card, or altering some simple windows settings. They might unban you, but will take a good week to respond to your appeal.
5) AI is pretty bad.. At times the AI will just stand still not doing anything, other times they'll turn around and snipe you in the face from 5000m. The best chance to actually kill the AI is to hide on a hill 1000-2000m away and snipe them.. Attempting to engage them in closer combat will generally result in instant death. While this does retain the hardcore aspect of the game, it also does knock down the realism when you're forced to constantly snipe. I highly recommend PVP rather then the annoying PVE combat.
6) This one seems simple. While the servers are loading, i don't see why they can't sort themselfs in realtime? I'm sick of having to constantly click a sorter column to "refresh" my sort sellection.

A tactical sim, that only has aspects of a game.
ARMA III is not intended to be a "game." It does not have the action most are used to from today's millitary shooter genre. What it does have, it has in spades. A deep simulation environment that spans accross some of the largest landscape to be placed in a title thus far. A plethora of weapons and set ups allow for equipping the perfect blend of survival and attack. The ability for user made content to be easily added to the base of the files, adds for creativity and fun. ARMA III is a title that asks you to make your own fun. It will not be for everyone, and even those who may enjoy camping out with a sniper rifle for hours on end, may find it dry and cumbersome. However, if you are looking for one of the more realistic takes on millitary shooters. ARMA III will have what you are looking for. Even if it doesn't, it gives you the tools to make it.

The game is a lot of fun to play, but the negitives simply overwhelm the positives...
1) The game is STILL $60! It's a great game - don't get me wrong, but that price is just too much for a game that's been out  for a little more then 2 years now.
2) DLC's are extremely overpriced. It costs around $20 just for a small helicopter DLC.. Seeing as we've already paid a large $60 - you'd think we'd get a bit more content.
3) Optimization is a joke. I run a 2700k at 4.6ghz backed with a GTX 970 and still get 20-30 FPS on some larger servers. For a game considered "Modern", that's pretty terrible.
4) BUGS! There are sooo many bugs you'll end up breaking your keyboard. Sometimes you'll randomly die, your vehicle will randomly explode, server will crash,  and the game will just crash randomly. Also they use BattleEye for anti-hack which is very good for catching hackers, but has an extremely high rate of false positives! I've been globally banned before just for changing out my graphics card, or altering some simple windows settings. They might unban you, but will take a good week to respond to your appeal.
5) AI is pretty bad.. At times the AI will just stand still not doing anything, other times they'll turn around and snipe you in the face from 5000m. The best chance to actually kill the AI is to hide on a hill 1000-2000m away and snipe them.. Attempting to engage them in closer combat will generally result in instant death. While this does retain the hardcore aspect of the game, it also does knock down the realism when you're forced to constantly snipe. I highly recommend PVP rather then the annoying PVE combat.
6) This one seems simple. While the servers are loading, i don't see why they can't sort themselfs in realtime? I'm sick of having to constantly click a sorter column to "refresh" my sort sellection.
The game is great, but feels and runs like it's on an engine made in 1995.

A tactical sim, that only has aspects of a game.
ARMA III is not intended to be a "game." It does not have the action most are used to from today's millitary shooter genre. What it does have, it has in spades. A deep simulation environment that spans accross some of the largest landscape to be placed in a title thus far. A plethora of weapons and set ups allow for equipping the perfect blend of survival and attack. The ability for user made content to be easily added to the base of the files, adds for creativity and fun. ARMA III is a title that asks you to make your own fun. It will not be for everyone, and even those who may enjoy camping out with a sniper rifle for hours on end, may find it dry and cumbersome. However, if you are looking for one of the more realistic takes on millitary shooters. ARMA III will have what you are looking for. Even if it doesn't, it gives you the tools to make it.

Lets say you actually get into a game after restarting the client 3-6 times and then waiting for 10-25 minutes in queue..
You parachute down with a 50/50 chance of landing gracefully or cliping into the map, bouncing forever, getting stuck in place, or just not being able to do anything at all.

You can win simply by hiding all game.

Sometimes your guns simply.. dont fire.
You're never really sure if you can kill someone, you kinda just shoot and hope you randomly get a headshot. That for me just really messes up the whole 'rewarding' factor of getting kills.
In games like CS, Overwatch, and Battlefield i actually feel in control of the situation. I know that if i out smart/out skill my enemy i can take them down. If i die, i know why i died and i dont really get the felling that i was just unlucky. With this game, i could get the jump on someone.. fire a few rounds into what i think is someones head but it doesnt always register that way. Ultimately, its just a VERY frustrating multiplayer expirence.

Roughly 8 or so years ago this game was pretty much king of the online FPS genre and Valve ruled the world. Now it's present day and Valve still rules the world but they took their used-to-be crown jewel and realized that the company name "Valve" and their poor excuse for an Engine that Source is will sell anything they put into it. Mercilessly defiling the grave of a once pretty excellent video game, the "Development Team" have beat this dead horse so much that honestly the species isn't even recognizable anymore. While I could rant and rave about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ economy system and how the once groundbreaking TF2 crafting system is now the most irrelevant thing in gaming history now, I rather just cover the gameplay.
At its core, TF2 is fun to play, but that's really about all that can be said about it. The Gunplay in this game is terrible, it really doesn't exist at all. The fact that people still praise source as an FPS platform really baffles me (unless you look at some people with actual brains like Respawn Entertainment) but the way weapons work in Team Fortress can only be described as numbers being assigned to player inputs. That being said, the quirky classes and synergy with a proper team makes the game really shine in specific objective gamemodes like Payload and SOME Capture Point maps. All that aside, the introduction of new Weapons of TF2 was basically the beginning of the end since the new issue of balancing multiple combinations of a particular class became borderline impossible and you had classes running around filling totally unrelated roles or being broken at one specifically important thing. For example, if you look at the Loch and Load for Demoman for an example, or the Direct Hit for Soldier, setting up buildings as an Engineer pretty much becomes impossible due to the inability to outrepair the massive burst damage without getting killed yourself. Suddenly, a single weapon has nullified a major aspect of a different class, significantly modifying the game balance of an Offensive vs Defensive team line up. Finally, in regards to weapons, the mystery of an enemy's loadout creates a massive issue in gameplay due to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ design choices such as the Dead Ringer for Spy. Without me getting into detail about this ♥♥♥♥ing horribly designed class, killing a spy is pretty much a gamble in terms of player-visual feedback since the Dead Ringer also conviently "lies" to the killer in the Kill Feed, causing a level of confusion. While this is neat from a mind game perspective, when ACTUALLY killing a spy, the player has no idea IF they REALLY did kill the spy or not all because there is no preemptive way to know if the enemy is using a different Inviswatch or not without having encountered the enemy beforehand.
Cutting my rants about this game early, I can't reccomend this game anymore, the changes to Team Fortress 2 over the past 5 years or so have ground this game into an unsavory paste that you can remember it  being good at one point, but then you realize it's been sitting in the cabinet since 2007 and you realize that going back to try it agai is just going to make you sick to your stomach.Not to mention, the remainder of this fanbase is mostly Source Engine/Quake fan boys that will vigorously jerk their♥♥♥♥♥♥to the concept of "rocket jump skill cielings" and the artifical bloom reset of the weapons in Team Fortress 2, but you are so much better off playing a game that hasn't been raised from the dead and brutally♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by its creator more than 5 times over the course of 10 years.
Final verdict:
Don't waste your time with this♥♥♥♥♥♥anymore. A once wonderful game has once again been ruined by the greed of its directors and is now beyond saving. If you want to play a F2P shooter that is better, then go play Dirty Bomb or shell out the money to play Overwatch so you can spend countless hours playing the same 5 Maps as the same character for the next 10 years with the rest of the community.

Arma 3 is the sequel to the ultra-hardcore military simulator, Arma 2, which while Arma 2 focused on modern military, Arma 3 uses experimental weapons or near future systems. (Such as the Future Force Warrior project, and the Comanche helicopter which is called the Blackfoot in this game.)
While it is odd that they decided to go 20 minutes into the future, the game has its quirks, retaining military sim everyone likes, and if you don't like how it is like that, there mods aplenty the community has for this game.
As for the DLC, I got the Extended Edition when it was on sale, so I can't exactly complain at them, the current DLCs, which is Karts, Helicopters, and Marksmen, add neat concepts to the game, although you must purchase the DLC to use the equipment. If you have the base game, your best bet is nab em' when you see that sale sticker.
If your into hardcore tactical games, then its worth a shot, otherwise, if your the impatient type that prefers a close range style of hardcore shooters, I would give this a pass, since this game does focus on long-range at times.

Apart from that this is definitely the best military sim at the moment.

I'll go ahead and say that I've played this since the Alpha stage of the game and I have to say that ArmA III has come a long way since then.
ArmA III is a great way for you to explore a more detailed tactical shooter. This is more than shooter with pretty maps and sights. This is more than just a "Shoot 'em up and knock 'em down" kind of game. This IS a simulation, a simulation of what armed combat can look like in reality, unlike the movies and shows. YOU are down there, boots on the ground, standing shoulder to shoulder with your squadmates and fighting to either seize a town or fighting for your life when you're the only one left. The sounds are down right amazing and the detail on the rifles are wonderful.
When you are with friends and fighting alongside others, communication is KEY to succeeding and achieving victory! Communicate with the people driving the tanks or any armored vehicle and combine arms to tackle enemy armor and air units, as well as communicating with the ones flying attack helos and jets. Combine all of those elements and you've got yourself an unforgetable experience of awesomeness. And all of this gets better if you find yourself a Mil-Sim unit!
You can specailize yourself in any MOS (Military Ocupational Specialty). From Rifleman to AT Specialist, helicopter and/or fighter pilot, you can learn all of this in this game!
Of course threre are mods which alters the realism of this game to a more hardcore level which I highly recommend you doing.
Ladies and gentlemen, if you are looking for a detailed Mil-Sim tactical shooter, then ArmA III is for you, remember, communication is the KEY to success!
Good luck, fellow virtual soldier!

Edited Review: After having this game be the first out of all of mine to surpass 1000 hours, there are definitely some pro's and cons that I have noticed while playing the game. Lets start off. Pros, the modding community, probably the best experiences I've had while playing this game is through mods, for example RHS, Arma 2 Imports like CUP, along with the 200 other mods that I have that have shaped my playthrough experiences. Large scale combat on a large scale map, this is one of the most defining features of Arma 3, not many games can simulate combined arms gameplay, while yes games, for example Battlefield include the combined arms aspect, and also weapon physics like bullet drop etc, Arma just does it way better, not many games can simulate Tank combat supported by Mechanized Infantry, along with support from artillery and air power. I could go on and on about the pro's, graphics, weapons, not too futuristic in the sense of technology unlike some games, but every game has some cons. First off, the engine used to run the game, while yes the map of Altis is one of the best terrains, if the server gets clogged, the engine curls over and dies. Another one of the problems that I find with Arma is the limited infantry movement controls, while yes Enhanced Movement makes up for that, I think this is one of the things that should built into the base game, along with the Rapelling mods etc but at this point I'm being picky. Also, not that I'm a feminist or anything but like where did the Altis women go, it's weird not to see women in the game, not necesarily as soldiers of NATO, CSAT, or AAF, but at least have them as civilians. Even though there are some glaring cons of Arma, I think the variety of the situations you can find yourself in, is what takes the cake, for me at least.

Well, This is my review for KOTK>
Pros:
>No pay2win, its completely skill based
>Crossair customization, Graphic customization, Sound configuration, Control binds, etc. are all here. it has everything a pc game should
>Lag prevention Tactics, a.k.a you are not going to get killed by someone whos lagging across the map because there weapons get locked until there ping improves.
>Good anticheat, BattleYE does its job as invasive as it is.
Cons:
>Buggy, but not as buggy as people make it out to be, Alot of the major bugs like being booted out my parachute or car, have dissapeared over the past few months for me, so its obvious they are fixing them
>Servers, they're fine most the time, but i find 1 issue being if Eu is down, i cant switch to na, as i cant get into the eu servers to switch to na, if that makes sense, i think they should allow you to choose server region in the launchpad.
>Semi-poor matchmaking, ngl, this works in my favour most the time, but i feel sorry when i see bronzes in the same games as diamonds etc, i get it, its hard to find 200 people of the same rank, but this is like putting silver 1s with global elites in cs. it just doesn't work. at least make it similar ranks.
>"Poorly optimized" my pc is decent, it runs it at 100+ fps on max, but i know that it can vary on certain PCs, you may be like me and have no issues whatsoever. or you may just have a gpu that simply wont look at the game, it seems AMD ones inpaticular seem to struggle with this game, despite no NVIDIA gameworks features being present.
Conclusion: the game is good, bugs are wayyyyyy over exaggurated by reviews, but theyre still there, skins are not the only focus as they revamped the whole game twice in the space of 10 months. and more updates are still coming. servers are mediocre, but not the worst ive seen, ive seen FAR far worse servers.

I have dumped about 40 hours into this game, and while there are still some bugs, for the most part this game is rounding up to be one of the more uniqe games in my library.
The "Battle Royal" style of game has become more popular in the recent months with games like "The Culling" sharing its likeness with King of the Kill, however different in its own respect.
King of the Kill has nailed some game aspects like its map size (never feeling too big or small), the simplified crafting, and the balanced spawn of firearms in the game all make for a fun expirence.
The only Issues I have with the game is its hit registration. Sometimes it will be on point, having a predictable bullet drop and recoil patterns. Other times it will feel like you're not even shooting bullets, with recoil and bullet drop all out of wack for no apparent reason. Even if your bullets hit, sometimes they wont register. You'll hear the sound of the hit, only to be killed and see that they have 100% health (without any body or helmet protection).
That is really my only complaint with the game, other than that, I think this is one of the most entertaining games that I have played in a long time.

Firstly, my friend bought this game for me, and I enjoy playing WITH HIM, and that is the only reason I have so many hours invested into this game at this point, and still continue to play. I didn't have a lot of experience with similar types of games before, and I'm not a great player, so I can recognize when I've been outplayed vs just being tilted, but I feel like this far in I can leave a "seasoned" review. Honestly, it seems the devs for this game are just totally incompetent. They cannot fix one tiny thing without breaking half a dozen other things, almost every update. They've "fixed" hit reg at least a handful of times since I started playing, horrible dsync, silent footsteps, broken doors, broken floors, massive(!!) teaming, cheese kill mechanics (that they "fixed"), random car explosions (esp when you spawn in Africa), unlootable loot, unhittable Chinese players (but no region or ping locking!) No rewards or incentives for winning duo or fives games. First queue of the day, guaranteed DC. Tab out, DC. Afk four minutes, DC.  No new maps or game modes, but there are pay-to-play "events." Can't seem to fix any of the known issues, but can pump out new $3.50 loot crate themes like hot cakes. I wanted to love this game and not be a negative nancy about the devs like it seemed most of my friends were when I picked it up, but I definitely see it now for what it is.

I mostly played this game pre-F2P update and since the beginning of this year after mostly quitting for like 6 years or so during which time I tried to play it very few times per year.
I have got to say that today this game is definitely almost a completely different beast and it's disputable whether you can still call it a "beast" anymore, but nevertheless I still think this game can be better than it ever was during its 10 year lifespan. All it takes is a little more than just a bit of effort from the Valve part.
Let's look at this from this perspective - if everything about this game worked like a charm, if all of its mechanics were fixed, if the matchmaking wasn't broken, if every single weapon was balanced to the point of lack of annoyance on the receiving end and viability on the user's end... What more could you ask for? It all only depends on Valve's responsibility for their mistakes and aspirations to make up for them. The core gameplay of this game might as well be everything that I could ever ask for, it's just that everything around this core is mostly rotten at this point and the core itself is inedible and will make you grind your teeth on it if you try to consume it by itself even though arguably it shouls be the most tasty part.
I'm writing this review on a day preceding Jungle Update, which will probably come out tomorrow and amongst the promises of new content from Valve is there still anything MORE that we need to get from them as soon as possible besides fixing the things that are currently broken? This game has a lot of features and weapons that no one ever uses, because they're just unusable and fixing all of this to the point of them becoming quality content would still be the biggest update this game would ever get up until this point just because so many already existing things would suddenly become actually available to the players.
The recent balance changes blog post gave me some amount of hope that the future of this game might not be as dark as everyone sees it though. It is very clear that it's all about communication now and we as a community should do everything to let Valve know what exactly is wrong with the game. Please do not waste this opportunity and send them feedback about even the most minor things that bother you, it's our chance to get this game out of this deep hole it is in right now and we should make use of it.
Or idk maybe they won't do anything and sending walls of text of feedback is pointless lol. It's still worth trying though just for the possibility that TF2 will become better as it has underlying potential to be greater than it ever was.

Arma 3 is an immersive, challenging, and fun mil-sim in which players can do pretty much whatever they want. There are 2 maps (not counting virtual reality world). These maps are not the tiny arena fps style maps. They are sandbox environments that include multiple towns and cities. First is Stratis, a medium sized island that includes 1 main airfield, several military camps and towns, and 1 medium-large city. Secondly is Altis, a HUGE and open, yet annoyingly desolate and deserted island. Altis has 4 airfields (if you count the dry lakebed runway), several cities, and numerous towns. Altis can be a little boring with less than 50 players on a server, as the map is too large for low-population servers. Altis can also seem very empty and frustrating without vehicles, which brings me to the next topic. There are less vehicles and weapons available in arma 3 than there were in arma 2, even if you purchased helis, karts, and marksmen dlc. There is a huge gap in the weapon diversity, so far as there being NO shotguns in the game at all (mods can fix this). Speaking of mods,  Bohemia has done a great job with mod support. There are only 2 problems with modding arma 3. 1: Good luck trying to find a server with all of the mods you want to play with. 2: Some mods, a lot of the time not even graphics mods, can significantly hurt the already poor performance of the game. Thankfully, Arma 3 has an awesome editor that you can use to make any kind of mission you want. Bohemia also made a set of tools for modders to use. Bohemia added weapon attachments, a huge step forward for infantry, but unfortunately, the awful fatigue system will often cause you to not be able to run, when running is a huge part of the game, especially on altis.  The game itself plays much, much smoother than arma 2 did. Obviously, it being the newer arma game, it has much better graphics, animations, and physics. For performance, Inte/Nvidia users should get decent framerates (assuming you aren't running a 480 and an I3), but AMD users, particularly those using AMD CPU's/APU's, tend to be stuck below 40fps. My GPU is an R9 285 and my CPU/APU is an A-10 7850k, and I get 70fps in singleplayer, but 40 fps in multiplayer (My internet connection is fine, I don't have problems with it in other games or applications). Hopefully Dx12 will help with this, but for now, AMD users are having trouble getting decent framerates.

Need more incentive? As well as a dev team that updates news for the fan base weekly and is STILL improving the game (and plans to continue doing so), there is also the modding commmunity for Arma - which is second to none. I mostly played this game pre-F2P update and since the beginning of this year after mostly quitting for like 6 years or so during which time I tried to play it very few times per year.
I have got to say that today this game is definitely almost a completely different beast and it's disputable whether you can still call it a "beast" anymore, but nevertheless I still think this game can be better than it ever was during its 10 year lifespan. All it takes is a little more than just a bit of effort from the Valve part.
Let's look at this from this perspective - if everything about this game worked like a charm, if all of its mechanics were fixed, if the matchmaking wasn't broken, if every single weapon was balanced to the point of lack of annoyance on the receiving end and viability on the user's end... What more could you ask for? It all only depends on Valve's responsibility for their mistakes and aspirations to make up for them. The core gameplay of this game might as well be everything that I could ever ask for, it's just that everything around this core is mostly rotten at this point and the core itself is inedible and will make you grind your teeth on it if you try to consume it by itself even though arguably it shouls be the most tasty part.
I'm writing this review on a day preceding Jungle Update, which will probably come out tomorrow and amongst the promises of new content from Valve is there still anything MORE that we need to get from them as soon as possible besides fixing the things that are currently broken? This game has a lot of features and weapons that no one ever uses, because they're just unusable and fixing all of this to the point of them becoming quality content would still be the biggest update this game would ever get up until this point just because so many already existing things would suddenly become actually available to the players.
The recent balance changes blog post gave me some amount of hope that the future of this game might not be as dark as everyone sees it though. It is very clear that it's all about communication now and we as a community should do everything to let Valve know what exactly is wrong with the game. Please do not waste this opportunity and send them feedback about even the most minor things that bother you, it's our chance to get this game out of this deep hole it is in right now and we should make use of it.
Or idk maybe they won't do anything and sending walls of text of feedback is pointless lol. It's still worth trying though just for the possibility that TF2 will become better as it has underlying potential to be greater than it ever was.

STORY TIME CHILDREN:
Me and my friend downloaded this mod for Arma 3 called DUWS (Dynamic Universal War System), and we had the best arma moment ever.
we had to take a outpost somewhat close to our home base, so we gathered our squads that were badly injured by the battle before (his was completely wiped), healed them up, got new soldiers, and drove near the outpost. Ofcourse, we parked the truck far away so it will stay safe. We moved the the objective, to find Friendly AI (the only way you can play this game is with AI unless you have hundreds of friends that have Arma) battling with the enemy forces. So me and my friend decided to help them out by flanking them, since they looked like a small group. We pushed up with our squad, and got into position. BTW, it was night time, so we had NV :). our only cover was sandbags, and we thought it would be ok since it was a "small group". we told our squad to hold their fire, and began plucking them one by one.
Well, thats when the mortars started blowing up 50 feet from us, and the enemy found us. About 200 feet from us was a shack, and we had no choice but to sprint up there for cover. my medic was injured, so i told him to patch himself up. He did so, and carried on. The enemy was surrounding us from all sides, and we were beginning to feel ♥♥♥♥ed. Our squad was getting injured, as were we, and we still needed to take the objective. We stayed there for a good 10 minutes trying to fight them, and we werent getting anywhere in this firefight, because more and more kept appearing. next thing i know, my medic is down ( I had two medics) and two of his squad mates were down, and i only had 2 squadmates left. Him and I didnt know what to do, the firefight was so intense, we didnt expect this much of a battle. We sat there like ducks, playing tower defense, until my medic got shot. Out of everyone we needed, it was him, so we needed him alive at all costs. Emotion was starting to kick in, as i was getting really nervous ( i havent saved in a while, and you can only save at home base), and we were running out of options. The enemy was still surrounding us, and me and my friend were low on ammo and soldiers. About 5 minutes later, we were making progress finally. we were still at the same broken down shack, that looked ancient and ruined, but less and less gunfire was happening. at that time, only my medic was left, and his squad was wiped ( again). We saw all of our soldiers die, and we didnt wanna die like they did. I realized i forgot about my medic, and so i checked on him. it showed he was still alive on my hud, but i just wanted to make sure. so i turned around were he was last seen by me, and all i saw was a soldier, bloodied up, with both of his hand on his head. I knew that was him, but i didnt believe he was dead. My exact words on skype were "Dude, DUDE, DOOD, MY MEDIC, HES DOWN, WTF WERE FUDGED UP". All we could do was hope we dont die, or we can still revive eachother. we moved up, since the gunfire died down, onto this complex/base thing, were the enemies were earlier, hoping we could go cap the objective over there. but of course. they werent dead, they were just farther back. I had a assault rifle, and, ofcourse, i was feeling a little confident with myelf, and ran to a hut 400 m west of the base/thing, so i can just push up, and take them down. my friend stayed back, playing tower defense. Well, the "pushing up" idea of mine was a completey horrible idea, because i was getting my behind handed to me. I ended up doing the same thing my friend was doing, and just played tower defense (best way i could describe it atm). i was injured so bad i couldnt sprint, and my friend was 100 m away. I told him to make his way here, as he did, and we were finally reunited 5 min later. We were holed up in a tiny hut, just the two of us, with our squad mates dead far away. it was this moment in game i realized we werent gonna win this fight. Me and my friend decided to make our way back to base, trying to dodge the mortars. we made it about 1000 m, until shooting started happening again. I got shot, and killed. my friend revived me, and we fell back into the trees, away from the fire. we were safe. we walked back to the trans vehicle we drove here, and drove back to base. It felt empty. It felt like something was missing. The soldiers. we failed to protect them.
10/10 would get PTSD again

This is the best game I've played by far. Or at least, certainly better than Overwatch.
upsides:
-9 unique classes to choose from, each having it's own unique playstyle, weapon unlocks, (for different play styles) hats, skill caps, etc. You can main or play as only one, or all of them, it's your choice. (pyro main over here)
-Hundreds of cosmetics to choose from, leading to many different loadouts. You can have a serious-looking Soviet general Heavy, a pyro always in the Christmas (or Smissmas, as it's called in TF2) spirit, (my pyro loadout) a scout stuck in the 1950s, an alien spy with a banana on his head and so much more.
-Different unique gamemodes to choose from, with each having its own variety of maps to choose from
-Many different "subclasses" to play as using different weapons and playstyles. (Examples: Demoknight, hoovy AKA friendly heavy, combo pyro, battle engi)
-You don't have to fight, you can be friendly if you want. Just be warned that not everyone will treat you the same way.
-One of the most active and dedicated communities on Steam
downsides:
-Many hackers, since it's f2p
-Valve rarely updates it, and sometimes no effort is put into updates
That's it...
Overall, I do recommend this game.

I mostly played this game pre-F2P update and since the beginning of this year after mostly quitting for like 6 years or so during which time I tried to play it very few times per year.
I have got to say that today this game is definitely almost a completely different beast and it's disputable whether you can still call it a "beast" anymore, but nevertheless I still think this game can be better than it ever was during its 10 year lifespan. All it takes is a little more than just a bit of effort from the Valve part.
Let's look at this from this perspective - if everything about this game worked like a charm, if all of its mechanics were fixed, if the matchmaking wasn't broken, if every single weapon was balanced to the point of lack of annoyance on the receiving end and viability on the user's end... What more could you ask for? It all only depends on Valve's responsibility for their mistakes and aspirations to make up for them. The core gameplay of this game might as well be everything that I could ever ask for, it's just that everything around this core is mostly rotten at this point and the core itself is inedible and will make you grind your teeth on it if you try to consume it by itself even though arguably it shouls be the most tasty part.
I'm writing this review on a day preceding Jungle Update, which will probably come out tomorrow and amongst the promises of new content from Valve is there still anything MORE that we need to get from them as soon as possible besides fixing the things that are currently broken? This game has a lot of features and weapons that no one ever uses, because they're just unusable and fixing all of this to the point of them becoming quality content would still be the biggest update this game would ever get up until this point just because so many already existing things would suddenly become actually available to the players.
The recent balance changes blog post gave me some amount of hope that the future of this game might not be as dark as everyone sees it though. It is very clear that it's all about communication now and we as a community should do everything to let Valve know what exactly is wrong with the game. Please do not waste this opportunity and send them feedback about even the most minor things that bother you, it's our chance to get this game out of this deep hole it is in right now and we should make use of it.
Or idk maybe they won't do anything and sending walls of text of feedback is pointless lol. It's still worth trying though just for the possibility that TF2 will become better as it has underlying potential to be greater than it ever was.
