Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

I've only been playing for a couple of months but I can tell you that this game is nowhere near ready to be played on the large scale it is now. There are still a ton of issues and the development team seems to take two steps back after moving one forward with every patch or update. The problem for me was that as a new player there is absolutely no way to properly train. The practice/training mode is just plain terrible as you can never find any loot, the weapons don't re-spawn apparently. It took me almost a month to get any confidence at all in gun fights because the only way you can practice for it is to queue a game and hope you land in a populated area and fight as often as possible. The problem is that a lot of these players have been playing for so long that they've mastered two tapping or first person shotgunning. Meaning that unless you get the jump (hiding) on them you stand almost no chance.
The amount of two taps I've been getting is insane; I can't even play the ♥♥♥♥ing game anymore. Every encounter is now 5 shots or less. If you don't immediately two tap you're dead. What is the point of even looting for body armor when my last 7 or 8 deaths out of 10 are from a series of head shots in under 2 seconds. If there was a way to improve helmets to take additional shots I wouldn't be in such a rage at the moment but still...
The game also has probably the worst development team in recent memory. Every "update" causes more issues, the hit registration is still off and there still is some bug or glitch I encounter that ruins my game around 5-10% of the time. They are either severely understaffed or incompetent, neither bodes well for them. I'm ashamed to say I spent around $60 to get crates for new skins and that wasn't even enough to get an ultra rare item. I'm done giving my money and time. I'll patiently wait until someone else develops a similar game and play that instead. The only reason I've played as long as I have is because it's a unique and fun (when there aren't bugs/issues) but I've simply had enough.

I started playing this game in 2012 on my first ever Steam account which I made specifically to play this game ( I've had 3 accounts since). I've had great memories from this games, a lot of nostaligia is filled within the maps I used to play on. A new UI, A Competitive mode? I was just unable to find a good server, and even when I did, Most people were using some insane varients of weapons I had never heard about. Don't get me wrong, Weapon varients were still present in the past (pun not intended) but the game was completely different now, almost impossible for me to enjoy.
In conclusion I think it would be near impossible for me to enjoy this game the same way I did in 2012. It will be very hard for Valve to revive this game and I'll just observe what this game turns out to be. Still reccomending as it has a chance to improve, come on, it's Valve.

I am much newer to the Arma franchise, and just played Arma 2 for the first time a couple months back. I really enjoyed it and decided to look into Arma 3. I wasn't sure how well it would run as my laptop is not built for gaming, and doesn't even have an integrated graphics card.
Despite Arma 2 only running around 20 FPS on the lowest settings, I decided to buy Arma 3 during the Steam sales. I was very surpised how well it runs considering my PC specs. I'm averaging just under 30 frames in single player - even during battles - and that's with the video settings varied (some on high, some on low).
As of writing this I have only clocked a couple of hours, but it so far seems better optimised than Arma 2. Not great, but it definitely runs well after some tweaking. I highly suggest buying Arma 3 if the previous titles run on at least 20-25 fps

upsides:
-9 unique classes to choose from, each having it's own unique playstyle, weapon unlocks, (for different play styles) hats, skill caps, etc. You can main or play as only one, or all of them, it's your choice. (pyro main over here)

-One of the most active and dedicated communities on Steam
downsides:
-Many hackers, since it's f2p
-Valve rarely updates it, and sometimes no effort is put into updates
That's it...
Overall, I do recommend this game.

Arma 3 has everything a MilSim junkie wants: realism, action, and fantastic graphics. Add superb modability and you have the best retail Military Combat Simulator on the market today!
Pros:
- Requires high-end hardware to power excellent graphics
- Realistic combat mechanics
- Campaign is not an oversight, and provides a great tutorial to the gameplay, do this BEFORE multiplayer
- Modable multiplayer: many different multiplayer game modes, and an active online community
Cons:
- Requires high-end hardware to power excellent graphics. This game will not run very well on your 5 year old potatos ;)
- May be too realistic for Call of Duty Prepubescent Cussing Simulator players
- Slow-paced action. Expect to lay prone on a hilltop gazing through a scope for half an hour or more sometimes, especially in multiplayer :P
- Hardcore multiplayer community. Many of the online players are MilSim players who roleplay and/or take the game realisticly, and seriously. Screw around and you WILL be bodyslammed.
TL;DR: I WOULD recommend this game to pretty much everyone I know, and everyone I don't know. That being said, this game is NOT for everyone! If you like fast-paced action arcadey shooters (Quake, CoD, CS:GO, etc.) that rely on twitch-skills, you most likely will not enjoy Arma 3. But tactical shooters are more fun anyways, so get it and play it ;)

Arma 3 has everything a MilSim junkie wants: realism, action, and fantastic graphics. Add superb modability and you have the best retail Military Combat Simulator on the market today!
Pros:
- Requires high-end hardware to power excellent graphics
- Realistic combat mechanics
- Campaign is not an oversight, and provides a great tutorial to the gameplay, do this BEFORE multiplayer
- Modable multiplayer: many different multiplayer game modes, and an active online community
Cons:
- Requires high-end hardware to power excellent graphics. This game will not run very well on your 5 year old potatos ;)
- May be too realistic for Call of Duty Prepubescent Cussing Simulator players
- Slow-paced action. Expect to lay prone on a hilltop gazing through a scope for half an hour or more sometimes, especially in multiplayer :P
- Hardcore multiplayer community. Many of the online players are MilSim players who roleplay and/or take the game realisticly, and seriously. Screw around and you WILL be bodyslammed.
TL;DR: I WOULD recommend this game to pretty much everyone I know, and everyone I don't know. That being said, this game is NOT for everyone! If you like fast-paced action arcadey shooters (Quake, CoD, CS:GO, etc.) that rely on twitch-skills, you most likely will not enjoy Arma 3. But tactical shooters are more fun anyways, so get it and play it ;)

Do not get me wrong, this... game? is amazing. I hesitate to call it a game, but it really depends on your playstyle. You can go on Roleplay servers, or you can PVP. The usual hardcore users of this product however usually use it as a base for massive coop operations, including vehicle platoons, artillery support (manned and operated in a realistic manner by players) and infantry squads. You want to realistically call in a fire mission for the artillery? This is your game. You want to call in close air support for a strike on a sniper/tank/building? This is your game. You want to indulge yourself in close quarter combat with your squad? This is your game. You want to hunt down IEDs and the insurgents who placed them? This is your game.
Ok now, these massive coop operations are made possible and realistic by the modding community. This is a fact, the base game is (to the best of my knowledge) not ever used when it comes to any serious servers or communities.
The modding community supplies the realistic radio communications, the real word weapons, the medical simulation, better sounds, better graphics in some cases, better AI (!!!) and all kinds of maps, so YOUR platoon can deploy anywhere from Alaska to Zimbabwe. AND it brought you bipods (seriously Bohemia, how did it take you so long to implement freakin bipods in the game...)....
This modding community made the game more realistic and created the fanbase it has today. Arguably the most attention Arma got in years came from the Zombie mod (not a fan btw, but still).  And now Bohemia comes along and wants to charge you for DLC. Alright you might say, what is the DLC?
The DLC includes things as long range capable rifles and tools to be more accurate.
It also includes things like new helicopters and slingloading vehicles/objects.
These are argueably some of the main features for the marksmen and helicopter DLC respectivly.
Now, these features where added by the modding community YEARS ago. In arma 2 already. For absolutely free. They still exist in Arma 3 too. I do not see the need for the publisher to charge this amount of money for features the community pretty much figured out on its own. I would rather donate that money to a beatiful website called ARMAHOLICS and to certain mod developers on there. And arma 3 is a triple A game with a triple A price. As others pointed out already: People who preordered, played in the alpha etc. paid MORE money than people who waited for the steamsales to kick in. I can get the whole game cheaper and including DLCs than the chaps who where loyal to bohemia and this franchise in the first place.... what the ♥♥♥♥ .... seriosuly. That is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, even from a marketing perspective.
Here is my advice: If you are looking for the real arma experience (large-scale coop, usually vs. AI with differing amounts of military realism) buy the base game. Then find a appropriate server or group to play with. They will teach you how to mod the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of this game and you will never need the lame DLCs.

Do not get me wrong, this... game? is amazing. I hesitate to call it a game, but it really depends on your playstyle. You can go on Roleplay servers, or you can PVP. The usual hardcore users of this product however usually use it as a base for massive coop operations, including vehicle platoons, artillery support (manned and operated in a realistic manner by players) and infantry squads. You want to realistically call in a fire mission for the artillery? This is your game. You want to call in close air support for a strike on a sniper/tank/building? This is your game. You want to indulge yourself in close quarter combat with your squad? This is your game. You want to hunt down IEDs and the insurgents who placed them? This is your game.
Ok now, these massive coop operations are made possible and realistic by the modding community. This is a fact, the base game is (to the best of my knowledge) not ever used when it comes to any serious servers or communities.
The modding community supplies the realistic radio communications, the real word weapons, the medical simulation, better sounds, better graphics in some cases, better AI (!!!) and all kinds of maps, so YOUR platoon can deploy anywhere from Alaska to Zimbabwe. AND it brought you bipods (seriously Bohemia, how did it take you so long to implement freakin bipods in the game...)....
This modding community made the game more realistic and created the fanbase it has today. Arguably the most attention Arma got in years came from the Zombie mod (not a fan btw, but still).  And now Bohemia comes along and wants to charge you for DLC. Alright you might say, what is the DLC?
The DLC includes things as long range capable rifles and tools to be more accurate.
It also includes things like new helicopters and slingloading vehicles/objects.
These are argueably some of the main features for the marksmen and helicopter DLC respectivly.
Now, these features where added by the modding community YEARS ago. In arma 2 already. For absolutely free. They still exist in Arma 3 too. I do not see the need for the publisher to charge this amount of money for features the community pretty much figured out on its own. I would rather donate that money to a beatiful website called ARMAHOLICS and to certain mod developers on there. And arma 3 is a triple A game with a triple A price. As others pointed out already: People who preordered, played in the alpha etc. paid MORE money than people who waited for the steamsales to kick in. I can get the whole game cheaper and including DLCs than the chaps who where loyal to bohemia and this franchise in the first place.... what the ♥♥♥♥ .... seriosuly. That is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, even from a marketing perspective.
Here is my advice: If you are looking for the real arma experience (large-scale coop, usually vs. AI with differing amounts of military realism) buy the base game. Then find a appropriate server or group to play with. They will teach you how to mod the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of this game and you will never need the lame DLCs.

我可以负责任的这样说。杀戮之王，他是一个好游戏。值得去玩，我们先说优点和缺点。
优点，游戏拟真，代入感比较强烈。玩家之间的激烈竞争，道德考验，技术考验，完美体体现在了游戏中。
生存，杀死你的敌人，意味着一切，你甚至需要注意你的队友，会不会朝你开枪。
==
缺点，一些游戏性的问题。
第一，游戏中道具并不充足，而且部分道具几乎没有作用。
第二，我总是感觉降落就发生火拼，死去一半的人，比较无理取闹。许多人落地死，甚至连武器都没有。
第三，我很难在游戏里找到一起玩的朋友。五排组队，朋友之间很少交流，不确定会不会互相开枪，也不愿意多说什么，因为知道你总会死，或者我一会就出局了。
然后我比较欣赏开发商封锁中国IP的做法。我觉得这样一款游戏，他必然受到道德考验，以及安全考验问题。玩家是否会恶意组队，是否会利用游戏系统以及漏洞破坏游戏平衡性，一款好游戏都会受到此类考验。我欣赏开发商的做法，当这款游戏受到中国玩家的考验时，他封锁了中国地区IP，成功完善了他的安全系统，满足了他的平衡系统。。
不过你依旧可以使用加速器进行游戏。

ArmA 3 is my favorite game of all time.
Out of the box ArmA offers an immersive, deep and tense military simulation experience that can't compare to any other videogame. The feeling of being under fire with your life-that's-worth 2-hours is so immersive that I often scream of fear and fun.
But to only play the base game is not understanding ArmA. ArmA is a platform for content. There are literally hundres of mods for ArmA 3. Most of those mods are of top-notch quality. Do you want to play on a tropical island? During world war 2? Naval Warfare? Transform ArmA into a flight sim? You name it, it can be done thanks to the amazing game structure bohemia interactive provides.
That said, ArmA is not for everyone. But everyone I have recommended it and with whom I've played it (about 5 people now) loves it to death (literally).
On top of all ArmA looks the best of almost all pc games. Not because of all the pretty bumpmaps and lighting effects, but because of the scope - one moment you are underwater in a submarine while on the other you may be riding in a tank and firing on detailed bases and enemies while using thermal vision or picture-in-picture. You do need a 1000-dollar rig to even attempt to play this game, but then again: this game is not for everyone.
If you've ever wanted to go to war without risking your life or destroying other people's, go buy this game now.

It has it's flaws, but, Arma 3 for me is still possibly the finest war game out there.
This game is one for the gamers though, casual players be warned. Arma has always and hopefully always will have a tough learning curve. Enemies are accurate and deadly on even the easiest settings and the control system is complicated enough to make your head explode. From the numerous controls for simply running around, leaning around corners, commanding troops and changing optical sights, to the things like zeroing your sights and ranging up targets, Arma will have you confused for awhile.
Stick with it though and learn the game and you will realize you have to act like a soldier to survive.
Unlike many fps's, you simply cannot get away with blitzing around, guns blazing. Shots need to be accurate, cover is your only life saver and good use of tactics and planning will win out over Rambo-ing your way through. This makes for a wonderful game, very different to the majority of other games out there and a stand alone in terms of war simulation.
Is it war? No. Is it far closer than anything like Battlefield / CoD / Heroes and Generals etc....Yes, by a long long way.
Online is much the same thing, although, people tend to be a little worse than Ai's so you can get away with a little more. Some of the mod's of this game alone have gone on to warrant their own games (DayZ), which for me shows how different this game is compared to the rest of the market. A mod of this game is different enough to anything else out there, it got it's own stand alone game, not many other titles can say that.
Playing online isn't always easy. Skill is generally going to win out and that can be tough sometimes if you play online and are new to the game. The mod's (such as epoch), that start you with no gear can more be about finding the right server sometimes. I'm currently playing on two different servers, one is very full and packed full of people just wanting to kill you on sight, no warning, no nothing. The other is a generally quiet server, very friendly and much more survivor feeling. Both other great game play experiences, but of a very different nature. One has you avoiding anywhere built up and laying low a lot until you manage to get a weapon, then you start looking for oppurtunities to pinch gear and hold people up. The other has you heading into built up areas hoping to find vital equipment such as building materials, food, drink and weapons. You look to help others out and often find yourself leaving your safety to help those in need.
Now, the game isn't perfect. Time to talk flaws.
Bugs. There are a decent handful of bugs. I had one mission in the main game that all the cars spawned into the floor and I couldn't complete the mission (as part of the mission was to drive one of the said cars to a location).
Another had my artillery support stop working....leaving me to try and take out 4 tanks and about 2 dozen people with what amounted to sticks and stones.
Restarting these levels from scratch fixed both, but, can be tough to swallow if you found it a struggle getting that far the first time.
Online has bugs too. Climbing over stuff or falling a foot or two from something can sometimes result in injury. Doors will sometimes decide they will no longer work and will either not close or not unlock. A restart of the server (most restart every 4 hours) usually solves that problem though. Vehicles can simply despawn and lose you a lot of gear. The servers tend not to remember a lot of what goes on in the last 3-4 mins before a restart.
With most of the bugs in this game though, they are patched fairly quickly and although frustrating, aren't deal breakers for me. You're not required to own the DLC either to play on servers that have that DLC running (or so I was told) which is good value for money if you're thinking of being more an online player.
Overall, I'd give Arma 3 a 9/10 ........ Bugs removed, a larger single player set of campaigns and perhaps some slightly better optimising (which isn't bad) would push it to a 10.
UPDATED:
Nearly two years on from this review and Arma is still my game of choice for having fun. It's gotten bigger, recently it's even become slightly more optimised with the addition of 64bit. It's even managed to getting buggier at times but has always seemed to do enough to fix just enough to be fun more than frustrating.
The mods are what keeps the game alive for me after all these years and they continue to grow and improve. Arma is a messy beast to code for, so, mods can feel one step forward two steps back at times but they manage to keep crawling forward regardless.
Overall, I'd suggest you buy this game and find a server to play on. You can meet a great number of good people (In amongst all the asshats) and honestly, after 3200+ hours in game, I'm still not bored. New stuff continues to happen, things continue to surprize.

It has it's flaws, but, Arma 3 for me is still possibly the finest war game out there.
This game is one for the gamers though, casual players be warned. Arma has always and hopefully always will have a tough learning curve. Enemies are accurate and deadly on even the easiest settings and the control system is complicated enough to make your head explode. From the numerous controls for simply running around, leaning around corners, commanding troops and changing optical sights, to the things like zeroing your sights and ranging up targets, Arma will have you confused for awhile.
Stick with it though and learn the game and you will realize you have to act like a soldier to survive.
Unlike many fps's, you simply cannot get away with blitzing around, guns blazing. Shots need to be accurate, cover is your only life saver and good use of tactics and planning will win out over Rambo-ing your way through. This makes for a wonderful game, very different to the majority of other games out there and a stand alone in terms of war simulation.
Is it war? No. Is it far closer than anything like Battlefield / CoD / Heroes and Generals etc....Yes, by a long long way.
Online is much the same thing, although, people tend to be a little worse than Ai's so you can get away with a little more. Some of the mod's of this game alone have gone on to warrant their own games (DayZ), which for me shows how different this game is compared to the rest of the market. A mod of this game is different enough to anything else out there, it got it's own stand alone game, not many other titles can say that.
Playing online isn't always easy. Skill is generally going to win out and that can be tough sometimes if you play online and are new to the game. The mod's (such as epoch), that start you with no gear can more be about finding the right server sometimes. I'm currently playing on two different servers, one is very full and packed full of people just wanting to kill you on sight, no warning, no nothing. The other is a generally quiet server, very friendly and much more survivor feeling. Both other great game play experiences, but of a very different nature. One has you avoiding anywhere built up and laying low a lot until you manage to get a weapon, then you start looking for oppurtunities to pinch gear and hold people up. The other has you heading into built up areas hoping to find vital equipment such as building materials, food, drink and weapons. You look to help others out and often find yourself leaving your safety to help those in need.
Now, the game isn't perfect. Time to talk flaws.
Bugs. There are a decent handful of bugs. I had one mission in the main game that all the cars spawned into the floor and I couldn't complete the mission (as part of the mission was to drive one of the said cars to a location).
Another had my artillery support stop working....leaving me to try and take out 4 tanks and about 2 dozen people with what amounted to sticks and stones.
Restarting these levels from scratch fixed both, but, can be tough to swallow if you found it a struggle getting that far the first time.
Online has bugs too. Climbing over stuff or falling a foot or two from something can sometimes result in injury. Doors will sometimes decide they will no longer work and will either not close or not unlock. A restart of the server (most restart every 4 hours) usually solves that problem though. Vehicles can simply despawn and lose you a lot of gear. The servers tend not to remember a lot of what goes on in the last 3-4 mins before a restart.
With most of the bugs in this game though, they are patched fairly quickly and although frustrating, aren't deal breakers for me. You're not required to own the DLC either to play on servers that have that DLC running (or so I was told) which is good value for money if you're thinking of being more an online player.
Overall, I'd give Arma 3 a 9/10 ........ Bugs removed, a larger single player set of campaigns and perhaps some slightly better optimising (which isn't bad) would push it to a 10.
UPDATED:
Nearly two years on from this review and Arma is still my game of choice for having fun. It's gotten bigger, recently it's even become slightly more optimised with the addition of 64bit. It's even managed to getting buggier at times but has always seemed to do enough to fix just enough to be fun more than frustrating.
The mods are what keeps the game alive for me after all these years and they continue to grow and improve. Arma is a messy beast to code for, so, mods can feel one step forward two steps back at times but they manage to keep crawling forward regardless.
Overall, I'd suggest you buy this game and find a server to play on. You can meet a great number of good people (In amongst all the asshats) and honestly, after 3200+ hours in game, I'm still not bored. New stuff continues to happen, things continue to surprize.
Spend your money....

This is a great game for anyone looking to have a hardcore realistic feel. Its customization is the best I've ever seen including everything you can think about However my only complaint is it requires a lot of power to run. My laptop met all the minimum and recommended settings except for the reccommended graphics card and I thought I would be fine. But I was very wrong because when I first launched I multiplayer I got a very unplayable 5-8 fps. Now things are a little better if I join a low populated server. I usually play KOTH and nowadays I am lucky to get anywhere near 20 fps without joining a server with less than 30 people and having the settings the lowest possible. So if you have a powerful machine I would go for it. However, if you don't have that fastest PC on the block then I wouldn't be too hasty to get this without doing some research. My final rating is 8 out of 10, but in the future maybe with some optimizaton tweeks that will change.

THIS IS A COMBAT SIMULATOR, NOT AN FPS! I cannot stress that enough. Having said that some of my most memorable gaming moments came from this game. I can remember moving through a town, we were so close to the objective, then an explosion. A guy in my squad had stepped on a mine, then came another, and one more after. The enemy opened fire and we had to dive for cover. My squad quickly attempted to return fire but it seemed we were pinned, and there were three of my buddies still laying wouded in the open. Unsure of their condition I charged forward grabbing the first guy and pulling him behind cover, then the second and soon after the third. Miraculously I wasn't hit by gunfire, but we had problem, our medic was one of the three wounded. Without a field medic to stabilize the wounded they would surely die. I called out over the comms for anyone who could help, there was a long pause...then a response, a pilot just happened to be dropping off a squad nearby and was happy to evac them to HQ. We eventually managed to drive the enemy off, allowing for medevac to pick up the wounded and fly them to safety.
It still sounds to me like something that would be scripted in a singleplayer campaign, something where you are surrounded by npcs and you are merely along for the ride, just for entertainment. The truth is, these were all real players, fighting as a team, trying to save three members of their squad. It's player interactions like that that make this game incredible.
TLDR: This game is awesome, I cannot reccomend it enough!

Bloody good game.  With 3 weeks of gameplay, I can honestly say that I spill a lot of blood in the game.  My own blood.  With 150 players in each round, you are sure to run into several game veterans that can shoot off your helmet and pop a load of lead into your cranium faster than you can aim down your iron sights.  Survival is the name of the game and your random insertion into the map makes it a challenge to find weapons, armor and health kits--making the game new every match.  The map is probably 8 miles square and a vehicle can help you move around...if you can find one.  Otherwise, get running to the safe area before the toxic gas consumes you.  The gas moves survivors to a tighter and tighter area of the map until it’s mano a mano.  “Hunger Games” for the masses, and in my case misses.  With 50 hours of gameplay under my belt, I can now hit opponents, but not usually with lethality very often.  This game takes some patience, but it is fun/suspenseful and gets the adrenaline flowing.

This game takes some patience, but it is fun/suspenseful and gets the adrenaline flowing.

There is a lot of controversy around this game.  This game is not easy, so don't expect it to be.  It is a true military simulator.  Now three things get hated on a lot in this game that I wish to clear up.  This game takes place in the future.  This is often hated upon, but this game does it differently than other games.  This game has a very realistic and down to Earth future.  In fact it shows the most in its vehicles which are rather sleek and well designed.  Compared to Arma 2 it does have less vehicles, but it doesn't feel empty because the vehicles aren't clones of one another with just one new difference.
Now second is a problem that dramatically effects the game for some people.  The game is very laggy no matter your settings.  For me I run between 25 and 35 FPS on a 660 graphics card, and a 4 core processor.  There is a few performance enhancing mods, but nothing major.
Finally the biggest complaint in the reviews.  The content in this game is considered to be lacking.  What people do not understand is the fact that this game is more of a template than anything.  This game has a huge community with amazing mods and missions.  The point was not for the base game to be full of content, but for the player base to design the content.  Arma 3 has one of the best modding communities I have ever seen, and some mods are a must have for me.  MCC is one of the best to me, because you can make a full mission in about 5 minutes.  This game is a template for content.  I highly recommend this game to those who enjoy a challenge and tactical combat.

There is a lot of controversy around this game.  This game is not easy, so don't expect it to be.  It is a true military simulator.  Now three things get hated on a lot in this game that I wish to clear up.  This game takes place in the future.  This is often hated upon, but this game does it differently than other games.  This game has a very realistic and down to Earth future.  In fact it shows the most in its vehicles which are rather sleek and well designed.  Compared to Arma 2 it does have less vehicles, but it doesn't feel empty because the vehicles aren't clones of one another with just one new difference.
Now second is a problem that dramatically effects the game for some people.  The game is very laggy no matter your settings.  For me I run between 25 and 35 FPS on a 660 graphics card, and a 4 core processor.  There is a few performance enhancing mods, but nothing major.
Finally the biggest complaint in the reviews.  The content in this game is considered to be lacking.  What people do not understand is the fact that this game is more of a template than anything.  This game has a huge community with amazing mods and missions.  The point was not for the base game to be full of content, but for the player base to design the content.  Arma 3 has one of the best modding communities I have ever seen, and some mods are a must have for me.  MCC is one of the best to me, because you can make a full mission in about 5 minutes.  This game is a template for content.  I highly recommend this game to those who enjoy a challenge and tactical combat.

Ah the good ol' Arma III. Lets get started.
Arma, a mil-sim game by Bohemia, how is it played? Custom game modes. Yes, there's a campaign, yes you can do the mil-sim related tasks and wage war against other mil-sim players, but this game isn't typically played like that. Custom maps like: Altis Life, King of the Hill, Battle Royale Mod, etc are how most people end up playing and enjoying this game.
As of this writing I play this game, for the most part, once or twice a week, but as you can see I've logged hundreds of hours on this game. That should speak quite a bit in regards to the fun factor. Whether you want to Role-Play with other players (who 50/50 just shoot anyways), play a giant game of king of the hill with big guns and vehicles, or just play an hour long survival last man standing kind of game... Arma III offers it.
Downsides to this game, bugs, lots of them, expensive DLC, and one of the most poorly optimized games I've ever played. The game would greatly benefit from a way more optimized engine that doesn't tank a modern PC under 60FPS by just being in a town.
Once again, that said, you can spend hundreds of hours entertaining yourself in the world that is Arma and I do highly reccomend this game for all shooter fans.

Ah the good ol' Arma III. Lets get started.
Arma, a mil-sim game by Bohemia, how is it played? Custom game modes. Yes, there's a campaign, yes you can do the mil-sim related tasks and wage war against other mil-sim players, but this game isn't typically played like that. Custom maps like: Altis Life, King of the Hill, Battle Royale Mod, etc are how most people end up playing and enjoying this game.
As of this writing I play this game, for the most part, once or twice a week, but as you can see I've logged hundreds of hours on this game. That should speak quite a bit in regards to the fun factor. Whether you want to Role-Play with other players (who 50/50 just shoot anyways), play a giant game of king of the hill with big guns and vehicles, or just play an hour long survival last man standing kind of game... Arma III offers it.
Downsides to this game, bugs, lots of them, expensive DLC, and one of the most poorly optimized games I've ever played. The game would greatly benefit from a way more optimized engine that doesn't tank a modern PC under 60FPS by just being in a town.
Once again, that said, you can spend hundreds of hours entertaining yourself in the world that is Arma and I do highly reccomend this game for all shooter fans.

Now, I havent played this game much lately, not because it is stale but because my taste are changing, which is something I enjoy about this game. I have no PC friends, so in Altis Life I ran by myself a lot. Now (my taste has changed) I have been playing a milsim group with some guys I have met on here. I really enjoy it. They are very relaxed, and I always talk crap about a squad because I just like to pick on them, and the dude that runs the group I talk to almost everyday about anything. I started out with zero friends on steam, now because of this game I have met 4 people that live in my state, and also I have 7 friends now on my list that I play with regularly. This game is a blast and if you like military simulation games, this is the game for you. You can be anything from a grunt or medic to driving tanks, or helicopters/planes. Just rememeber to take some time to learn the controls, and remap them where you like them.

ahh who remembers good old Operation Flashpoint. Not that crap modern sheit, but BI's Operation Flashpoint. There are some that don't know that Arma is it's direct ancestor btw. Anyways when I was young (too young for the game ill bet oooo edgy) i sank a good few thousand hours into OFP Cold War Crisis and its expansions. Eventually i played Arma 2. i wasn't really very impressed due to the crashes and the actual graphical look of the game was horrible. Some sorta film grain gone wrong
Then the recent free weekend rolled around for Arma 3. I was so impressed that i had to buy myself a £95 headset - and that was the cheapest price for it. I'd probably have a few more 10s of hours in the game, but its the studying time of the year. But this game. Sure it has a weird looking stealth-inspired vehicles, but its Arma. It's moddable, and BI encourage you to mod, unlike almost every other company. That means you get things like Iron Front (an Arma 2 mod turned into a full game turned into an Arma 3 mod, confusing i know) that features WWII campaigns with maps and units to play with in the editor. It means you get JSRS, a sound mod that changes so many sounds in the game - the one i notice the most is the jets. the jets sound real, and when you wear a surround sound headset or have surround speakers, it sounds real. makes me feel like i'm in the Lake District for some reason. (the RAF does training there).
and then theres the multiplayer. i'm not even going to go further than saying the best servers are the 77th JSOC co-op EU1 and EU2. unless youre murican. if youre murican, you lag. go away. if youre a kid, dont even touch my favourite servers. if youre looking for a group that actually plays together as a team, go no further than the 77th. the rest of the co-op servers cant actually work co-op if they got paid to do it. idk even know why im writing a review i just wanted to tell you about the best server on arma. and that altislife sheeit is for kids who shouldnt even be playing the game. you want to roleplay go play♥♥♥♥♥♥♥gmod
anyway everyone tells a funny story so this one time on 77th its late night irl, its dark ingame too. barely anyone is online. so im leading a squad, and we are driving from the airport to the AO south east of pygros in a HEMTT transport. it takes so long the squad in the back starts shooting rabbits from the back and talking about stuff soldiers talk about, idk. half an hour later, literally, we are nearly there. i cant see the AO, but its just over a hill in front of us. then theres a sound... and then another sound, like a rocket. so yeah a jet comes out of nowhere. entire squad leaves and im left on my own in base.
10/10
tl;dr
OFP CWC is Arma, Arma 2 had a bad film grain effect, Arma 3 free weekend, got headphones, mods like Iron Front and JSRS, RAF does training in the Lake District, 77th JSOC owns the best 2 servers in the game - americans and squeekers stay out, altislife is for kids that should go back to gmod, and finally i drive a HEMTT transport full of soldiers to their death by jet.

I hope that these devs do as they say they would and say they have apparently and hire some new talent and fix this game because it could be and probably would be one of the funnest games I have ever played.

The downside of this is they have one huge map, Altis, and that's all that's really there(No one plays Stratis which is the only other map and it's a lot smaller). So, you're pretty much stuck with the same map, same buildings, same roads, same cities, etc., etc. It would have been nice to have a bit of variety, at least from an official source as opposed to having to download maps from the modding community(Which are mostly maps imported from ARMA 2). This isn't to say that Altis is boring or a badly designed map -- it's quite the opposite! -- but having spent 100+ hours on the same map you do wish for a bit more especially after two years of development(Including Alpha and an expansion/season pass).
The scale of the game was really brought to light in one of the first mods created for the game back when it was in Alpha; the co-op game mode Invade & Annex. This mode basically opened up the entire map for deployment from a central base complete with side missions that were entirely up to the players(100 or so) to take out. Missions required teamwork, coordination, squad based compositions, transport management, scouting, air support and heavy and light armour to complete. You would be deployed anywhere on the map with your squad to take on an objective and it was purely simulation based where you followed the chain of command to tackle objectives, requested support and had to wait for air/infantry/armoured support to arrive. There really was nothing like it in any other game and still isn't as far as i'm aware.
Speaking of mods this game has a lot of popular mods which, one could rightly assume, may even spawn standalone games of themselves given the huge amount of interest in them and the sheer amount of players who buy ARMA III specifically for some of the mods on offer. To name a few:
The mods are really entertaining and while some are very simple and add onto the base experience they make the base game that much better although I would question why some mods simply were not developed by Bohemia to begin with and released with the game as standard.
Controls are pretty janky. The animations are stiff and can get you killed. It takes a long time to learn all the controls and then even longer to relearn the controls for specific servers that have keys bound to different keys than what other servers have as standard. It's not a bad thing having all these controls as they do make a difference but what's bad is the animations which force you into a full animation loop which is slow, cumbersome and essentially makes you a free kill. For instance, if you want to holster your gun your character will stop. He will then initiate the animation. Put the gun away. Then he will stand up. Only then will you be able to move your character again and you can't interrupt these animations. You can't even run or walk while they're being performed which is simply frustrating and downright bad design. If you're in a firefight and mistakenly take out a pistol instead of your rifle prepare for five seconds -- if you're lucky not to die while this is happening -- of animation hell where you're left with pulling your hair out, screaming at the screen while you're in the middle of the battlefield, standing up and, rather hilariously, carelessly taking your primary from your shoulder with zero ♥♥♥♥s given.
Needless to say, the animations are pretty bad in most regards. Animations that can't be interrupted and require you to spend 5seconds performing the most simplest of animations is just bad by any stretch of the imagination. I don't think anyone can defend it and i've never heard anyone try to.
Performance is a huge setback for this game for the main reason that online performance, the core of the game that people are here for, depends entirely on the server you're on and the scripts it uses. If it's a poor server that doesn't get reset every so often you'll see your frames drop by 50-60%. You could be at 60FPS and then, due to the poor server, you're down to 15-20FPS no matter what computer you have. It's just one of those things you have to accept. You will also experience random freezes and random dips in performance even if you're on a good server. Some freezes can last from 2 seconds to 10 seconds or even longer. This has nothing to do with your computer. It doesn't happen so often that you'll find yourself dying over and over but it happens enough to be notable and strangely enough it doesn't seem to happen in firefights but mostly when you're sitting around doing nothing or just driving on an empty road. It's questionable to say the least.
Having said that i'm running the game on close to ultra settings with an FPS of around 30-40 for the most part on a Windows 7 64bit PC, no SSD, 4GB DDR3 RAM, an i5-750 CPU at stock speed(2.67Ghz) and an AMD r9 290 4GB graphics card. There's still slowdowns and performance still largely depends on the server i'm on and what mod it is. In single player my frames will easily double and be consistent with no performance drops.
I probably should have started off with single player but I felt a pros over cons is the best way for the flow of this review. The single player isn't great if i'm to be honest. Enemy AI will spot you from a few miles(or km's) away before you even have a chance to see them. You'll be told by the AI leader to target and kill an enemy at X distance or to proceed to location Y only to die because you can't see the three aimbot AI perched three kilometers away on a hill with assault rifles seemingly sniping at you. You'll die a lot and it will only feel like a cheap death. Deaths are just cheap in the SP campaign which is reflected in one of the earlier missions where you enter a minefield and get blown up instantly which is the game's way of saying: "Trial and error, you'll know next time." It's cheap and it's bad design for a game simulation or not. The story itself isn't great either.
It's worth the money. There's no game out there like it and there's no game that offers as much as ARMA III does in terms of sheer scale and simulation. There's a few negatives to go against the game but ultimately this is definitely something you should have in your game library if you even remotely enjoy shooters or military shooters of any kind.

ArmA 3's campaign is divided into three episodes: Survive, Adapt and Win.

At the end of Adapt, the full force of NATO's military arrives on Altis after recieving a distress signal from Miller. However, Miller himself is nowhere to be found. If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

This game requires patience and has a pretty mean learning curve. But once you get the basics and can get past the clunky engine, there is no end to what you can do. If ever there was a game to really push yourself into, this is it. This is about as close as a game gets to a RW emulation of war and combat. It gives you the feel of long, boring, drawn out situations (like being on guard, walking a patrol, or riding in a convoy), punctuated with moments of dire intensity. If you're on the fence about Arma 3, start with the original game (arma / operation flashpoint) or arma 2 (which is almost perpetually on sale) and see how you feel about them first.
This game is NOT for everyone, but as an actual soldier who has experienced a combat deployment, I give this my recommendation.

Okay, so I have significantly less hours clocked into this game than most review writing players, but I think it's fair to give my first impression.
I used to play Arma 2 a little, and it always sort of disappointed me. It was a great idea. A large map, lots of possibilities as to what you can do, and incredible realism and attention to detail. The issue was, the game was really, really, REALLY clunky. Didn't even feel like it was finished, in my opinion. But the idea of it was astounding. I mean, we got DayZ from Arma 2.
Then along came Arma 3. It took the great idea that was Arma 2 and made it playable. Fluid animations and improved com chatter alone instantly made a difference.
If you haven't played any Arma before, here's a quick rundown, from my experience. It's a game where you can walk two kilometers with no clue as to what your objective is, finally reach your supposed destination, get in a small firefight, and die in the first few seconds. Bullet to the head. Boom, down. No red stuff on your screen, no suppression effects, you're just down before you can even soil your pants.
And it's actually incredibly fun.
Name another game where travelling itself is enjoyable enough that the firefights are secondary? Maybe you can. I can't.
As an example:
I'd bought the game a few hours prior and I decided to play off a mod called Hetman: War Stories (Get it if you buy this game, btw). So I boot it up, set the time to midnight, and anxiously await as it loads a random scenario for me. It starts with a panning shot over the wonderfully large island of Altis. It's all lit up in green, like I'm watching from some sort of neato-night-vision-helicopter-thing. Then it types out a small scenario, something about a village and enemy forces and whatever, and I watch in awe as plummet towards the surface and into the eyes of a soldier on the ground.
Everything's dark. I switch on my nifty little goggles and everything's lit up: the night sky, the trees around me, the rolling hills in the distance. I see some markers indicating my squad members, and my leader commands me to regroup. I'd love to admire the scenery, but instead I take off down the hill, gawking as I go, and regroup with my AI comrades and head off in the direction the squad leader points.
For about thirty minutes or so, we don't see any foot soldiers. Occasionally, a helicopter will whiz overhead, and my buddies would eat the dirt to try and hide from it, so I'd dive down on my belly and hope I don't get shot, squatting in the bamboo-looking reeds and keeping my eyes to the sky. This went on for a while, and the pure tension in conjunction with the scenery immersed me completely.
Then we finally get to a village. My trigger finger's getting itchy, and I go sneaking up the side of the hill all gung-ho like while the others are firing up from below. I find a perch in a building's second story and take out a few guys while the others find their way up the hill after me.
Then we get in a firefight, with enemies literally on all sides. Everyone's calling out where enemies are, but even with the goggles it's still kinda dark and I can't see, and sure enough I get wounded, clipped in the leg or something. I go down, try to heal myself, and as I do so I see the guy looking down at me, his gun raised. This isn't like a normal video game, where I know my character's going to die so I panic or begrudgingly accept my fate. My stomach dropped. Seriously, like I'd swallowed a brick, and I tried to wriggle away but he managed to land one more lucky shot and end it.
Everyone in m squad died except for one, who I switched to and ran to the hills until I could find another group, constantly hearing bullets crack around me the whole way.
Okay, that story was long. But the point is, I didn't even last more than, what, 5 minutes in a firefight? And this instantly became one of the best experiences I've ever had in a video game, from the moment I dropped in to the moment my main character, a character with MY NAME, got shot down in a little Mediterranean town in the hills of God-knows-where.
Just buy it. The price is high, yes, but if you're going to spend $60 on any game, let it be this one. On a less sentimental note, the modding community's fantastic, and you'll never run out of things to do. Graphics are great as well, and gameplay flows nice with enough functions to feel like you have real control over your character, your squad, your vehicles, everything.
Oh, and if you buy it, try to get friends to buy it as well. I know I personally can't lead a squad to save my life yet (honestly, they all die under my command) so having someone to give you pointers and play squad leader in co-op missions would be ideal for sure.
10/10 purely because I can't go any higher.

PROS:
-Great game with tons of mods and gamemodes
-The community is huge and there is always going to be players
-Graphics are simply beautiful
CONS:
-Game is unoptimized
-Game may initially be overwhelming to newcomers of the series.
-Lack of more in-depth audio options may be a turnoff for us 7.1 surround users or those who just want a greater level of control.
MY REVIEW
Your experience and mileage may vary depending on what you do with ARMA 3. You can go all vanilla, and play campaign or simple multiplayer, or you can go with the huge modding community. The mods are really what make this game great. Not in the mood for simple deathmatch? Play king of the hill with 120 players! Not in the mood for that? Try Epoch or Survival!
The gameplay is solid and the experience is worth it. There is only one con and it may affect you depending on how you like to experience games.
You are more than likely not going to get 60 FPS in this game, and probably will be hard to get a solid 30 without the occasional dips. This game is highly unoptimized on multiplayer. The game runs fine with single player campaign, but with multiplayer, the netcode is completely weird. Some mods i can get 60 FPS in, some i can barely hit 30. Regardless if i run on ultra or minimum settings, you will only usually have the same FPS the server has.
This was a BIG problem initially, then i just got past it. The gameplay more than makes up for it, and the experience is more about the community. Hopefully this will be rectified soon, however i highly doubt it, especially if you look at DayZ.
Audio customization is a problem i have in particular also. With all the customization ARMA 3 allows with the interface, they barely have any settings for audio. Mostly just the general "Master", "Chat", etc. I wish i could choose which sounds' levels i could adjust.
I bought this game with the intention of playing EPOCH since DayZ' latest update ruined everything i liked about the game, and in the end i barely play EPOCH. Mostly Survival and King of the Hill. Great gametypes and i also highly recommend ATLIS Life.
In ARMA 3's current state i would rate it a 7/10.

Arma 3 is a classic example of what happens when a company simple creates a game that is too ambitious for their own good. A "military simulator" of combined arms gameplay, the scale of the game, the world, and the things inside of it is massive. And while normally that massive scale would be a good thing, it's become clear to me over my many hours playing it that Bohemia Interactive has simply bitten off more than they can chew.
To be fair, I have only played the Wasteland gametype, and I have no interest in other types. All my experiences are based on that.
This game has the worst desync, hit detection, and general instability and clunkiness I have ever seen. Many times I have aimed directly at stationary targets right in front of my face and got nothing for the bullet. Players consistently zip and zap an teleport hither and thither as the server struggles to keep up with everything happening, and the frames per second are quite low even on a very competent PC like mine.
Large down time is interspersed by periods of being one-hit-killed, or from players simply living through the bullets you send his way. The inconsistency of infantry combat is incredibly evident from the first minutes you engage in it. In a game that strives for military realism when applicable, I cannot fathom why the most important parts of a game such as infantry combat are the worst parts of this game.
The only reason, I think, that a game like Arma 3 has a player base is because there is not any competition in terms of the military simulation sandbox game. If any other game had such a horrid execution of infantry combat, it would be inexcusable. Controls are not heavy...but clunky and unresponsive. Player menus in the game are the worst I have ever seen in a game, and you will often fumble through lists of commands and struggle to perform simple tasks like opening doors or simply checking the inventory of a corpse.
I've had fun with Arma 3. I really have. I still will play it, but it's only possible to play this game and have fun when things work. And with Arma 3, that simply is not a reliable amount of time. Kill trading happens very often, and the unreliability of infantry combat reduces the only working strategy to "stay far far far away and snipe at other players." I've only played this much because of friends that also play it, but more and more my sessions simply end in me staring at my screen with a gaping mouth, dumbstruck that somebody soaked up a dozen bullets and somehow one shotted me from the grave.
The DLC weapons are all high caliber killing machines, rendering the base level of weaponry basically useless. Enemies are bullet sponges for any caliber below 7.62, so thinking you can play this game with an assault rifle with 5.56 rounds or 6.5 caliber rounds is only a pipe dream. Fights are dominated by ridiculously high caliber weapons, like 9.3 or .50 caliber rifles, which betrays the realism that this game, I think, strives for. Other players can certainly soak up five, six rifle bullets at times and still stay up. The delay between hitting players and watching them go down can be LITERALLY a second or more, meaning you will shoot precious bullets at enemies that are "down".
With games like Battlefield, Call of Duty, and Counter Strike...Arma 3's only excuse for such pitiful execution of what should be the core pillars of gameplay is that it is so massive.
More isn't always better, and I think Arma 3 proves that.
TL;DR Arma 3 has its moments of genuine enjoyability, but the inability to execute simple and regular commands and the horrid infantry experience ruins most of the time spent in-game.

In it's current state KotK is one of the most buggy and broken shooters you'll find. With poor optimisation and a company driven by nothing more than money with no regard to it's player base, Daybreak is really pushing the limits.
On the other hand, the game concept is something you won't find elsewhere in this style and it has a lot of potential. Once you're actually able to join a game you'll see that graphically, it looks fairly nice (with the odd few clipping errors here and there). Gameplay wise the game is very balanced too, in which respect a new player is able to join with absolutely no disadvantages or advantages other than personal experience. Although money hungry, all microtransactions are thankfuly kept cosmetic.
You'll compete to be the last man (or team) standing in games of up to 200 odd people at peak times. Winning won't come easy and you'll likely be faced with tens or even hundreds of loses before you reach that end goal. With enough practice and determination you'll get there, and it will feel great.
There is a fairly large learning curve which may take a while to get the hang of but if you're willing to put in the time and practice, it will prove rewarding. Along with that, the community isn't so bad either, you'll meet some nice people and have hillarious encounters although as with any game there is a fair bit of toxicity. Of course if it's not for you, you can always toggle voice chat & stick with friends in teams of up to five.
You'll spend countless hours in this game having your patience tested while you wait in a thousand player queue and if you have a short temper you'll easily rage at the poor servers & game breaking glitches/bugs cutting your game short that you'll certainly come across. Along with that, idealistically, you wan't a better PC than the recommended on Steam due to it being so intensive.
However, overall the game is something painfully amazing. If you're someone who is willing to look past the bugs every so often and if you enjoy competitive & 'tryhard' player vs player action, then this is certainly a game for you.

The thing with Arma 3 is , you don't just get arma ,you also get access too all the other game modes created by the community for this game.
I find myself playing mods of arma rather than actual base game arma 3 which is good but also boring.
where to start with arma.. well the pro's
Beautiful Maps which are gigantic, you can be wandering for at least 2-3 hours sometimes and you only hear players around you but not actually engaged in combat with, because they are in the next city but you can hear major warfare breaking out so you bunker down with your squad and get ready for heavy incoming from the enemy.. but you are west of the city and they move south, but you sit there waiting for the enemy to come through youre ready made ambush but it never happens. In the back of your mind you know the enemy has gone but the solider inside tells you to wait to get the kills. but they never come and the battle you was about to have at 2am... never happened but before you finally move 5 hours have passed and it is now 7am and time to sleep.
Vehicles
vehicle variety is fairly good to keep you busy driving or sailing or maybe fancy a helicopter trip around the map to take in the beautiful scenery...
Combat
Where to start with arma 3's combat.. Well it can be epic the size of the battlefield makes battles ferocious .. upto 40 enemies coming at you from all directions with a vast array of vehicles. you just have to bunker down get on voice chat and battle for your life. because this is arma at it's finest. But they is also a downside to Combat .. due to the maps being so huge finding these battles can be hard and most of the time its like walking round a apocolyptic  world and becomes boring. Also the movement mechanics can sometimes be a little clunky changing direction or viewing mode so be prepared at all times.. because changing position or view when a enemy has got close can cost you your life. so be smart.
Graphics
Well it looks absolutely amazing no cartoon design here peeps this is realism at its best. few things could do with a remodel or what have you but all games have these things so overall Arma 3 looks absolutely amazing.
Community mods
This game has it all. If you have arma make sure to check out the community on steam and also elsewhere this game has hundreds of game modes and complete mod packs which change the game completely.
I play Altis life , Breaking Point and Wastelands mainly but these mods are just the touch of a ice berg compared to how much content this game has is unbelieveable
the Con's.
Optimization.. Well this games biggest issue.. some days i will jump on a server and i will be up in the mid 80's on fps and game runs smooth as silk, then others i log in and im grinding to a halt at around 15fps.. this is where Arma needs work. they have patched it alot but damn this game can frustrate you till you quit. my friends use all different set ups and we all have the same issues regardless of using intel vs amd. i think its just the day in which you log in as to wether the server is going to allow you to play at all.  if by chance you log in and its running smooth just never log out so you don't have to deal with crippling fps drops or lag so bad you play for 3 hours and travel so far across the map you wait for the achievement to pop up at the top saying "level complete" until  suddenly the character stutters and you reappear where you logged in 3 hours ago and realize everything you have done has been lost...  Welcome to arma 3.
Really arma isn't that bad but it does have poor optimization so take that into account  before purchasing.
Overall Arma 3 is fantastic and really good fun . would i recommend it yes! would i recommend it when it's not on sale .. no.  the fact you get  hundreds of mods and such which the community has created makes this game a bit of a bargain when it is on sale. but wether or not you can play the game when you want due to shockingly bad fps rate is the issue why i wouldnt pay full price for this game.
overall arma gets 7/10 from me.

If you like fast past Firs person shooter's with loots of action, then your in the wrong place.
Arma 3 is a FPS but it is so much more, it is "trying" to be a war simulator.
Now i am saying "trying" to be a war simulator because it has not lived up to the category "simulator" in my eyes.
Example if you expect a plane to have a realistic targeting system, you are going to be disappointed. There is no targeting pods in the game and i don't see them coming in to the game.
But setting the "simulator" term aside Arma 3 is the best War game for a group of people that don't like the fast past game types that other war games have.
You can go on foot, drive trucks, tanks, boats and fly choppers and planes.
Even swim and drive underwater vehicles.
And all this on a big 270 km2 island.
And best of all it has MOD support and a mission editor that is close to only stopping at your imagination.
It does have issues in some areas like performance and not a very intuitive way to use mods, but overall it s a good game and can give lot's of fun to you and your friends.

Hello potential buyer looking through the reviews. Why should you buy Arma III out of all the first person shooters, when COD has basically destroyed the genre. Well let me tell you why you should buy this game. Arma III is a realistic military shooter that simulates every real life thing you would experience in real combat, realistic physics, bullet drop, Weapon Zeroing, fatigue, every little item simulates real life combat. This game is in my opinion one of the best Military FPS shooter out there alongside Halo, Battlefield, and Battlefront. Arma III is first person and third person and features 40 weapons (Assault Rifles, LMGs, SMG's, Sniper Rifles, Marksman rifles, but alas no shotguns yet) last time I checked and over 20 vehicles (Tanks, APC's, Transports) and helicopters. It features several weapon attachments and several body armors and uniforms to choose from. The game is stunningly beautiful you wont find a more beautiful detailed game, the developers put a lot of work and time into graphics and boy did they give you what you pay for. It features 2 large scale maps span across 274 km of terrain (1.6 million placed items)(50 towns and cities). With such high detailed really requires a good computer, I have a ASUS republic of gaming computer with a Geforce GTX 860M and It usually runs Arma at a smooth 60 fps in almost all places including heavy combat and cities, but my computer doesnt work well when it runs high detailed mods/missions from the community. So if you dont have a good computer you probably should wait till you have a good computer. But fps and graphics aside its a very beautifully detailed game when your computer is made for these types of games. I have rarely ever ran into any graphics bugs or any poorly textured items, aside the random long necked marine in a helicopter or the pure white eyes of marines.
While the game's story faces criticism I think its a well planned thought out story a story you would expect from a war between NATO forces and the local CSAT and AFF forces in the year 2035, the storyline is split into 3 Acts and each is extremely long so youll be sure to get a few days out of it, I wont go more into just so I dont spoil it. The game features showcases and a boot camps so you can learn and play with the basics of the game weather its ground combat, air combat, or showing off new things in the game. Boot camp helps introduce you to the basics of the game. Before I go into the controls let me say about one of the things that makes Arma III great, the Steam Workshop community allows you to download missions and mods that adds some really great stories to continue on the game, also add some really great and new weapons or uniforms, and some really great maps some like wasteland and remakes like WWII and remakes from Arma II & OA. The community in Arma III is helpful and not once have I ran into some angry little child like I would in COD most people are mature and friendly players who help out and dont yell at you or trash talk. The community is great and friendly and the developers and game makers listen and help the community out unlike some other games.
Moving onto the controls and game play, to put it bluntly this is not a friendly game to new players you are going to have to spend hours and hours learning the controls and learning how to play because of the realistic gameplay every single thing you do needs to be carefully planned out and played. The controls are complicated and you will take a long time to learn and play them and when you do play you will use almost every key on the keyboard while playing the game. This game will beat you up if you dont learn the controls or try to run and gun. This is not Call of Duty there is no running and gunning, to survive youve got to move up cautiously, use cover, pick out targets and control your accuracy, which can be controlled with Arma's 19 different stances to improve concealment and  accuracy. So if you want a fast paced shooter where its easy to play and just shoot people and they die, Arma is not the game. Arma requires patience you have to work to survive and get those most wanted kills but when you do you will be filled with satisfaction. Tanks and APC's and helis also require skill, communication, and the same caution used in ground combat. And Air travel is no easier, as much as I want to do a cool Strafe run with an attack helicopter I cant cause Ill likely get shot down. The multiplayer really makes this game, Bohemia really put their heart and soul into and boy did they make it great, Arma III has one of the most largest diverse multiplayers of all the FPS's. The servers are great and plenty of ones to choose from, one of the ones Ive been playing the most is Invade and Annex made by someone great who I cant recall (feel free to comment the maker of that great game mode and be sure to check it out yourself)
However the AI in this game still need improvement, Enemy AI can either be dumb and take 50 bullets or shoot you dead center in the head and kill you. The Friendly AI are a bit smarter but usually rely on you to hold their hand and kill your enemies. However they are usually very helpful and smart when they want to be, but usually work best under well with a good a squad leader. The enemy AI can be deadly and coordination but are sometimes stupid so you must treat them just like you would any other real player. AI will most likely see improvements in the future and possibly personality traits such as feeling when over run or less likely to stand still and take bullets or salvage bodies or take abandoned vehicles.
I understand that $59.99 is a lot of money to pay for a game that's been out two years, but trust me I can say without a doubt every dollar and penny is worth it, the developers and game designers spend every penny and dollar improving Arma III and they regularly update the game, However if you are struggling for money just wait for Arma's regular sales, Arma III will fall to $30 and Im sure after long enough it will drop into the lower twenties and even lower. The DLC however is a different story. I got both DLC's with the recent sale and saved some money. While I like the new helis and guns in the marksman and helicopter dlc I believe that they could have already have been in the game. Its overpriced I can agree and youd be best off either not buying it or waiting for sales. Hopefully more ground vehicles and possibly shotguns will be included and hopefully wont be as expensive. On a later note the Zeus DLC is very fun and really adds new gameplay to the game unlike others, to put it bluntly think of Battlefield's Commander but with more power and control, way more....
So as a returning veteran from Arma II and OA I can say without a doubt and confidently that Arma III is one of the Greatest Military Shooters out there, Equally standing  up there with Halo, Battlefield, and Star Wars Battlefront. This is Arma III one of the most visually realistic military shooters of all time. You make the stories, you fight the battles, you decide the out come. Will you stand defiant with your team mates and tell your stories, or will you become another causality of the Battlefield. I give Arma III a 9/10 or on another scale a 95/100. Survive, Adapt, and Win.

This game is a pure masterpiece.
Why? You ask... Well, for many reasons. Firstly, this game is for nearly every type of first person shooter player. It's got many different classes with unique skillsets and abilities. There are also different weapons that you can equip for these classes that brings a fresh alteration of how the class is normally played. Providing many different playstyles that follow the main concept of the class. All of the different classes also have their own characteristics and personalities that can be humorous to listen to and distinguish themselves from other classes. And also, TF2 let's you play your own way. With techniques like rocket jumping and cosmetics you can get to personalize your character with. It's no wonder why so many people play this game.
Though, like every game, it has downsides, and same does TF2. Because it gives you a lot of freedom of how you play. It's open to many players using this to their advantage to grief, troll, abuse and many more nasty acts. And because admins aren't on Valve servers. It makes it so that hackers can roam freely on servers. Thankfully you can kick people or report people who are hacking so that they eventually get VAC banned.
Overall, I genuinely recommend this game to you. There are great upsides that overshadow the downsides and plus, It's free! Meaning you can try it for free and see if you like it or not.

I gave this a shot over the free weekend and here's what I learned:
1. You need an incredibly modern and powerful gaming PC to run attractive graphics with this. My system is 5 years old,  570 GTX can barely run this at the lowest graphics settings possible, and that's barely getting 30 fps.
2. The amount of key mapping you need to do to make this even somewhat manageable as a "game" is insane. Basically, you need one of those 7 or 9 button gaming Mice, because you won't have enough sensible keyboard key locations to cover all of the crap.
3. For a game where voice communication is extremely necessary, the voice comm functionality in this game is quite limited, but that's not really an issue because everyone is going to be using TS3 anyway...
4. Good luck finding a decent server to play on. Most of them are run by fascist bronys. Others are run by incompetent admins and you can count on getting spawnkilled by your own team over and over until you leave and find a different server.  No, I'm not kidding.
5. The game isn't worth 60 dollars.  The rest of the game (that's right, you don't actually get the whole game for 60 dollars, you need all of the DLC too because the only good weapons are locked)  is going to run you even more.  So it's over $100 game that isn't worth playing unless you have a $2,500 computer and a $120 mouse.
6. It seems like, if you met all of the requirements above,  the game *could* be enjoyable.  Just know what you are really getting yourself into...

(TLDR at bottom)
Graphics - Awesome
Campaign - Sorta cool but a bit buggy but I guess they are fixing those things.
-Weapons - Not ALOT of weapons but there are plenty of them and there is the marksmen dlc which adds some more weapons and I'm pretty sure that the 'Apex' dlc will also add more weapons and vehicles and a new faction.
-Optimization(Singleplayer) Pretty good actually
-Optimization(Multiplayer) Not so very good but the bad performance isn't bohemias fault,except maybe some of it but heavy scripted missions like King of The Hill which is an pretty huge(up to around 120 ish players) requires alot of scripting for points and keeping track of xp and cash and saving that and there is alot more than that going on, but the point is that this decreases you fps quite alot so if you're getting more than 30 to 40 fps you probably have a pretty good computer.
-Vehicles - I WANT MORE HELICOPTERS.
There are more gamemodes like Zeus which isn't very popular atleast not the public servers because the Zeus is usually very ignorant and just makes a bad experience overall for the players and doesn't take it slightly seriously.
Wasteland is also a cool gamemode, "basebuilding",finding weapons,vehicles,stores,missions.
The reason i put basebuilding in quotes is because you're actually just moving barricades but it could turn out to be something cool but then there are the server wipes and for every server restart all the vehicles dissappear so there is sort of no point of building a base instead you could enjoy the PvP,
on some servers some teams (blufor,opfor) builds a huge base together which is pretty cool and the other teams try to attack it and so on.
Altis life is also a very common mode,get money,more money,die (because of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t),do illegal stuff and then finally go to jail, good gamemode.
Then there are modded-survival servers,exile,desolation,epoch and probably more. getting into the modded servers can be a struggle at first then you have no idea where to download the mods and install them and then you never find any servers but it you usually get it sorted out after a while.
Then there is the editor for creating missions which usually means you need to learn their scripting language depending on how complex you mission is.
Staircases, or just stairs those things tend to kill you sometimes because thats how it is in real life because this game is a military simulator-sandbox and in the military your most feared enemy are stairs.
TL;DR: Arma 3 = Fresh memes and evil staircases.
