Why? You ask... Well, for many reasons. Firstly, this game is for nearly every type of first person shooter player. It's got many different classes with unique skillsets and abilities. There are also different weapons that you can equip for these classes that brings a fresh alteration of how the class is normally played. Providing many different playstyles that follow the main concept of the class. All of the different classes also have their own characteristics and personalities that can be humorous to listen to and distinguish themselves from other classes. And also, TF2 let's you play your own way. With techniques like rocket jumping and cosmetics you can get to personalize your character with. It's no wonder why so many people play this game.
Though, like every game, it has downsides, and same does TF2. Because it gives you a lot of freedom of how you play. It's open to many players using this to their advantage to grief, troll, abuse and many more nasty acts. And because admins aren't on Valve servers. It makes it so that hackers can roam freely on servers. Thankfully you can kick people or report people who are hacking so that they eventually get VAC banned.
Overall, I genuinely recommend this game to you. There are great upsides that overshadow the downsides and plus, It's free! Meaning you can try it for free and see if you like it or not.

Okay, let me just go ahead and get this out of the way, this is not anything like COD, Battlefield, or most other major Shooters. This is a simulation of war at its very finest. With a HUGE amount of variation with weapons, vehicles, and even character customization. However, the game isn't focused around mechanics entirely. It has a 3 part campaign (Survive, Adapt, and Win, four if you count the Prologue campaign.) You can add even more to that list with community made content from the Workshop. There is a fully functional editor so you can create your own Scenarios with. ( If you're new to the series, you might have some problems with the editor at first, but you will start to understand eventually. )
My only gripe with the game is that their is a massive learning curve for the first 3-4 hours. You will find yourself being dominated by your opposition most of the time. Luckily, there is the Prologue campaign, the Bootcamp, and the VR Training missions that do a great job at explaining the changes and improvements since ArmA 2.
The story of ArmA 3 will put you in the boots of Corporal Kerry, a United States soldier who is apart of a joint NATO peacekeeping force in the Republic of Altis. The 3 playable in game forces are the same with any ArmA game, BLUFOR (NATO & FIA), OPFOR (CSAT), and the Independent AAF, each with their own exclusive weapons and vehicles.
No matter which side you fight for, if you find yourself commanding a large army, you cant just send them all at the objective at once and pray to god that it works. No, you must use REAL tactics and have a good strategy, utilizing your supports and making every asset count.
If you want a game where twitch reflexes do not instantly win the game, this is a good game to check out. However, if you do not have a good system and are cash strapped, I advise you wait for a sale to come out, you can usually pick up the game and ALL of its DLC at a discounted price during that time.

A long time ago when I only had played 50 hours of arma i wrote a review recomending this game. I am proud to say that after over 300 hours of playing the game I am still nowhere close to finishing it. the game is good and focus mainly on small squad infantry gameplay with light armored vehicles. you can however still find tanks, helicopters, rubber inflatable boats (orange, green, black ones) and Jet planes. the game may boast destruction however it is disapointing that after pounding a house for 5 minutes with mortars to see the thing just sorta sinks down into another pre made model that makes it look destroyed. despite that though you can still get in terrifying moments with the whiz, snap, and crack of bullets all around you and your heart rushing as an attack chopper comes in for another straifing run to finish off the last of your fire team. Yet for every time like that youl find an equal for it in just plane stupid things wheather its a team member firing an rpg into your chopper just as you take off or you coming down to a gentle landing only to have the entire thing go up in a ball of flame. Along side that you will find that the gameplay can be enhanced greatly with mods however mods are some of the hardest things to play multiplayer with. Mods make the game 10x better however to just browse servers with mods and then play them is almost impossible. this is mainly because when joining a server it doesnt go through the simple steps of looking at all the mods you have then activating the ones that the server has, and installing the ones you are missing. Instead I find you and a group of friends who own the game need to agree to install the exact same mods and then launch your own private game so that nothing gets messed up. and finnaly to top this off you need to find your niche in arma wheather it be in the hardcore super realism folks who do 1 life only stuff or the Altis life folks who promot role play and gameplay as a civ.
So to sum this up
Pros
-AMAZING GAMEPLAY
-tons of mods
-in game editor (soon to be enhanced with an official 3d editor)
-creative DLC's (Karts and Zeus)
Conts
-game isnt really solidly built and much work still needs to be done on the server browsing
-better support for mods needed
-DLC's which have content that should have been in the game from the start (Helicopters and Marksmen)

There's a famous World War I quote that says warfare is "Months of boredom punctuated by moments of extreme terror."  Replace "terror" with "frustration" and this game does, indeed, give you the True Combat experience written on the tin.
From the description and tutorial missions, I was expecting a military simulation with experiences like "The commander ordered my squad over the radio to go to grid point 134-190 and hold the bridge, so we mounted up in an APC and fought out way there to hold the line against the enemy advance."  Basically, I expected a much deeper and more realistic version of Battlefield -- like the Falcon 3.0 and Gunship 2000 military sims I played when I was a teenager but with infantry and tanks and tactics and whatnot.
What I got is... nothing like that.
The single-player is more like what I would call a "walking forward simulator."  Seriously, my left middle finger started going numb from holding down W while following the squad leader character across a field for 15 minutes while only encountering two enemies.  Of course, when I DID encounter enemies I tended to get shot in the head pretty quickly because the AI can see right through the oh-so-realistic scrub brush that covers the landscape whereas all I could see was the tangle of bushes in front of my face with a big red "TARGET" box floating in the middle of them.  Then the squad leader guy stepped on a landmine (the only one in the world apparently -- of all the luck!) and I started following some other guys across another field for even longer, only this time with an ambush of several lethal bushes a few minutes out from the save point.
After snoozing my way all across the field and then getting killed in the same spot about a dozen times I thought "Okay, maybe the real draw here is the realistic chain-of-command combined arms multiplayer scenarios, let me try that."  So, I popped into multiplayer... and didn't see any of that either.
There were scads of "RPG" servers where I could play as a random villager, AKA playing Walking Foward Simulator toward the corn field at the edge of town and trying to earn a bit of money to buy food at the market and not starve.  True combat gameplay, right?
There were "Wasteland" servers where you spawn in the middle of the continent somewhere with nobody around and only a vague suggestion of what you'r supposed to be doing ("fortify a base, gather supplies and hoard them") and of course a half-hour walk to the nearest point of interest.  I wandered around the airport for 10 minutes looking for supplies or a vehicle, found nothing, shrugged and disconnected.
There were also "King of the Hill" servers which at least featured combat.  Well, actually they mostly featured waiting for helicopters to respawn.  The objective was to go from my team's base to occupy a town about 1.5 kilometers away, which equated to a half-hour walk, a ten-minute drive (assuming you didn't run over a bush, which would pop your tire and then it's back to the half-hour walk) or a one-minute helicopter ride.  So, helicopter was the obvious choice, but those only spawn every few minutes.  Half the time some jerk would crash his truck into the helicopter and destroy it so we'd have to wait again.  On the occasions I actually got to the airspace over the town, I would jump out of the helicopter, open my parachute, and generally be shot to death while dangling in the air.  The one time I parachuted out early and walked for a minute to get to the town, I survived for a good while sneaking into the town but didn't run into any enemies to fight... eventually I got bored of that and ran to a tower to see if I could snipe people from the top, but as soon as I peeked out over the railing I got shot in the head.
So, was it realistic?  You bet.  Months of boredom punctuated by moments of extreme frustration.  Was it fun?  Not really.  I had a lot more fun playing LUFTRAUSERS while waiting for it to download.  Overall a colossal disappointment.  I'm so glad it was a "free trial weekend" -- I would have cried tears of rage if I had actually paid for this thing.

My mother would probably scorn me by saying this about any media related to war, but...
This game is magnificent, beautiful, epic, brilliant even. the sound-track is not too bad either!
I absolutely love the way the game controls, especially compared to the stiff nature of its predecessor, Arma 2. This is particularly noticable when focusing on vehicles. In other words the vehicles handle like a dream due to the improved physics model (PhysX). apart from the third party physics engine implementation, the engine seems to have seen new additions and reconfigurations, such as the improved AI (still not perfect, especially when driving). The textures are decent, considering the scale of the game, but definatly an improvement over Arma 2. Animations are miles better. The details of objects such as weapons, vehicles and various common geometry scattered around the large expanse of the two vanilla maps (Stratis and Altis), are great!
I find great delight in oogling at such a realistic landscape, which in the case of the vanilla maps, apparently are modelled from real locations, Agios Efstratios (Stratis) and Lemnos (Altis)! There is a lot of content on offer with Arma 3, notably the ZEUS gamemode which is really exciting to play. Its when a player takes control of sort of an RTS perspective, defending, attacking and messing around with spawning objects and AI while other players run around as normal soldiers, adapting to the unpredictability of ZEUS's actions. It's quite a fun game mode and no two sessions are the same. There are a load of other standard game modes along with the ability to play scenarios either made with the editor, workshop or built in ones such as 'Escape from Altis', which is one of my favourite scenarios provided by BIS, its great to play with some friends. In fact, with a clan or a load of friends this game is a lot more fun. Don't get me wrong the Single player content which is similar, is also really really good.
Speaking of the single player experience, one of the most notable additions to this iteration of the series is the semi-decent campaign. missions are fairly good and diverse, making use of the space it has to play with. As well as the good voice acting, which seems to immerse me into the war torn Greek islands of Stratis and Altis.
Despite all the good things in the game, of course it has problems. One that sticks out like a sore thumb to me is the performace relative to the hardware. Servers seem to have problems, too. As connecting to a friends, has failed on multiple occasions, seeming to be randomly stubborn towards other players joining your server, despite inviting them.
This is no casual shooter, although some elements have leaned that way as opposed to the other installments in the series.

When I previously reviewed this game the circumstances were less than ideal to get a proper view of it. Not only were my computer specs lacking in order to run the game well; there was also less content and more kinks to be worked out in the game.
As of now, post-Apex preview yet pre-Apex launch, I can say the game has vastly improved on a technical level and had some content boosts to keep its tight, bony stomach from digesting itself.
With the introduction of Apex comes a shift in the status of the game: Arma 3 is no longer acceptibly a standalone game much in the same way that Arma 2 is, meaning one is unlikely to simply buy just Arma 3 and be content their purchase. Like A2:OA, one will be heavily pressured to buy Apex in order to see the game as it truly feels it was meant to be played.
Arma 3 plays nicely on a mid-high end system, and the improvements between installments are major, however the base game is just too slim to make a proper meal. This $40 investment pay simply for the plate on which to pile your dinner, a dinner which will cost you $35 more and still taste like a ceramic plate. Luckily, as of recently one can now pay an extra $40 or so for another dish to go along with your meal, one already piled high with food that tastes a bit like cocaine and swimming trunks.
In short: In order to play this game one must pay $40 (was previously $60, 40 is far more acceptable now). In order to play online one must fork over the entry fee of $35, because good luck finding any pure vanilla servers, and good luck hopping into the one remaining Chinook after a 40 minute siege that you barely survived and RTB 20km away. And finally, post the 10 or so days until Apex officially releases, good luck finding a server that doesn't rely on Apex content as most of it far outweighs the base game content.
Previous score was about a 6.5/10, but the price change bumps it to a 7.5 for the base game, and a 8.7/10 for the complete package.
Seriously, Apex feels like it adds more content than the base game contains.

I was really hopeful about ARMA.  As it is, it was pretty lame.  Maybe it'd be better if I had a super fast computer, AND everyone had the fastest internet known to mankind.  It is almost as realistic as WarThunder, but jumpy, jagged, and with laggy multiplayer.  Some say the controls are confusing, but I don't agree.  The controls are a little different, but you get used to them fairly quickly.  Some of the confusion comes from putting more than one action with the same button, switching based on whether it is a tap or a hold.  I referenced the controls menu a bunch, but there are numerous tutorials, guides, training scenarios and other practice available right in the game.
I really appreciate how realistic it is in that there are no markers for the enemy, and it only takes a couple of hits to kill you.  Unfortunately, it always takes at least 4 bullets to kill an enemy.  Unless you hit the face.  The helmet will not do, you must hit the face or neck.  This is actually pretty hard to do when you are at distances of 100+m, which you usually are engaging at those distances +/- 50m, and when they shoot more accurately than you because you have been walking/running everywhere and thus have less fatigue.  Avoid ever sprinting, even though the map is bigger than any map in any other game you've ever played in, just be patient and take 2-4 minutes to walk to the next battle.  "If you run, you'll just die tired".
I went into a multiplayer game and saw helicopters flying around in crazy upside down positions, crashing and falling to the ground.  Perhaps a contributing factor was the fact that it was a 70+ person game.  When I joined, I saw in the chat room that players were complaining about the lag, as I quickly downloaded a 3.4 MB setting file from the server.  Obviously, my joining the game clogged their upstream pipe.  This happened a couple times in the game as new players joined, lag spiked.  Perhaps a fix of this could be a download mirror used for all servers, or something to save on server bandwidth.
This game made me laugh at how unpolished it was at several points.  Mostly this was for multiplayer lag jumps, but it was funny when I tried my first multiplayer mission and my trooper, who was not the squad leader, would not stop calling out orders to everyone every 10 seconds.  I tried figuring out why I was issuing all these commands, but it happened without my pressing buttons or anything close to the squad command buttons.  It was also funny because the in-game voice chat toggle button defaults to [Caps Lock], so when I returned to typing out messages they were SHOUTING HALF THE TIME.  Oops. I couldnt figure out how to stop ordering everyone to regroup with me, nor could I find the enemy (it was a co-op mission), so I decided to try something else.  In my second multiplayer game, I was starting to get the hang of it.  I died plenty at first, sure, but there was always a nice helicopter pilot ready to take us to the battlefield when I respawned.  I'm REALLY GLAD I didn't have to walk all that way, because if I did, once would have been enough for me to quit.  I was starting to get the hang of it, and even a few kills.  Someone finally got me while from a higher building, and I was returning to the battlefield in a helicopter.  I started typing to my teammates while riding in the heli, and even though I was typing a message, when I used spacebar during the message, it caused me to jump out of the helicopter without a parachute.  I died before I could finish typing out my question, but in a way it answered a different one.  I decided to stop playing multiplayer and try the campaign.
In the first mission it was funny to have an enemy blazing away full tilt at my essential NPC partner, and for him to not even notice the enemy was there, walking on by.  I would have preferred my AI teammate to actually engage the enemy, but I'm sure walking up and shoulder checking him as he walked by was pretty effective. In the same mission, I snuck up on a machine gunner in the same first mission and wanted to see what the "action" button would do when I got close.  It turns out, instead of knifing him or doing some other crazy-cool CQB maneuver, I pulled out my medical kit and started bandaging him while he turned his MG on my face and opened up.  In the second mission, I wasn't able to progress because one member of my squad spotted an MRAP that he REALLY wanted me to destroy, even when our mission didn't call for it.  The rest of our squad was fine to go to the Rendezvous point, but that NPC squad member kept yelling for us to take out the group of enemies by it.  The squad leader kept yelling for him to return to formation, and I just kept walking through the forest for a while, hoping that he'd return at the next script line for the story.  He didn't.  I ended up going back to the last autosave and taking out the rest of them, by myself (after 20+ tries), without backup.  I was a little glad I did, because when allies engage the enemy, they die as fast as the enemy does.  Which is as fast as you do.  Which is QUICK.  I never neded up finishing that mission, because even when I knew generally where the enemy was coming from, I couldn't see them to shoot them.  But they sure could see and shoot me through all the leaves and bushes in the forest.  I died over and over.  I'm sure it was a bit like 'Nam, and just as fun.  So I decided to uninstall.
If it weren't for that, the campaign at least has great production value, on par with Call of Duty.  The voice acting, scripting of scenes, and music all are top notch.  It is ready for Oculus IR, and maybe I'd enjoy it more if I had a computer that wasn't at least 6 years old.   I am usually a simulation enthusiast, loving realism even over gameplay (hey, I like WarThunder, where you also have a hard time identifying who is an enemy and you die in 1-2 hits).  However, this was just not very enjoyable.  ARMA is like fighting on 3 or 4 battlefield 3 maps at once, with 100 players.  That sounds fun, and it could be.  As it is, however, it tries to do entirely too much (for my computer).  It ends up being a laggy, frustrating mess.  It'd be fun at a convention, on a LAN, with  computers with monster video cards, because the draw distance is intense.  But I was frustrated, not having fun, and ready to uninstall after just a few hours.

The core concept of this game is amazing, and I really hope another dev comes along and makes it correctly.  As it is, it's nothing but a huge money-grab from Daybreak.  It's in EARLY ACCESS, yet the only updates they do are putting new crates in.
- This game is buggy and glitchy as hell.  In 10-20% of my games (not exaggerating), I encounter a common bug that makes the game think you're stuck inside a vehicle.  If it happens while parachuting down, your parachute will dissapear and you'll fall to the ground, unable to move or perform any actions.  If it happens while you're in a car, you'll suddenly exit your vehicle for no apparent reason, but be unable to move or perform any actions.  In both cases others see you in a vastly different position to where you are on your screen.  This is only one of the many bugs that will ruin a game.
- Alt-tabbing often causes the game to crash (probably about 15-20% of the time).
- A bug that seems to come up constantly (like ~50% of games) is that suddenly your voice chat won't work, and you can't hear any voice chat.
- Queing as a team is a nightmare.  You can't invite non-friends, and if you're not the person who started the lobby, you can't invite anyone.  There is no chat/voice function in the lobby.  Furthermore, oftentimes when joining a queue, some people won't get it, putting half the team into the game and the other half still on the lobby queue.  If you've died and you exit the game, you stay in the group but have no way of knowing who is alive still and no way of knowing when everyone is ready for the next queue.  Every game starts with, "Is everyone on the main screen?" followed by, "Does everyone have a queue?"
- Oftentimes players crash on the loading screen.
- Inconsistent spawn times based on loading give some players a HUGE advantage.
- FPS is often low compared to other games, even on high-end machines.
- There is no spectator mode, a year after it was promised.
- Hit registration on this game is ♥♥♥♥ing awful, especially if the person is moving.  The lag compensation doesn't work well either.
- There is no region/language lock, leading to the Chiners.  Because of the way the game's lag compensation and hit reg works, if you have a high ping it benefits YOU.  A lot of people from China play on the NA servers for that reason, and they teleport around like Nightcrawler, making them almost impossible to hit.
- There are quite a few cheaters in this game, with cheats ranging from aimbots to ESP, etc.
- The weapons/items balance ranges from inconsistent to bizzare.
- There are relatively few different types of weapons and items.  There are a fair amount of grenades, but the grenade mechanics are horrific.  There are two rifles, one shotgun, and a revolver that are viable weapons.  There are only 3-4 other pistols in the game, all of which are non-viable other than in the first 1-2 minutes of the game.  There's no weapon selection, no choice, nothing.  They need to add things like SMG's, or at least weapon attachments to spice up the boring AR/AK meta.  Melee weapons are laughable, even in the beginning stages of the game.
- Gun/item spawns are completely imbalanced.  You'll sometimes search 2 houses and find *zero* weapons, whereas sometimes you'll search one house and find 3 rifles and a shotgun.  Also, weapon spawns are TOO frequent, especially AR, AK and shotguns.  When I spawn and land somewhere and search a building, I should be EXCITED that I just found an AK/AR.  Currently, if I spawn and don't find an AK/AR within the first minute, I'm upset.
- Grenade throwing mechanics are horrific.  The biggest issue is that they take up a weapon slot, and to use them you oftentimes have to manually switch them; this is a nightmare in the late game especially.  To use them in the middle of a fight, you have to open the inventory, switch the grenade (and each type of grenade takes up an additional spot) with the weapon, and hope you have enough room in your backpack to put your revolver in it, otherwise it won't switch.  Throwing grenades is also super-clunky, and needs a lot of work.
- Car mechanics are stupid.  Usually, if you're on foot, and someone in a car sees you they will drive at you as fast as they can and then exit the car while it's going 50mph.  They *instantly* exit the car, and often they will suddenly just appear in a place that the car just drove past.  Because of this, they gain a huge advantage since they are already aiming at you, but you have to guess where they will pop out.  Also, the fact that they can exit a car going full speed with zero downside is a huge oversight in game mechanics.  They should have a split-second of vulnerability or at least take damage.  The lategame typically becomes everyone in a car zooming around each other like sharks, waiting for someone to accidently flip their car.  There should be a mid/late game EMP that kills all cars.
- Sound is very inconsistent.  There are times when an enemy will suddenly be very near you without you having heard them approach, and there's times when you'll hear them a mile away.
- Parachute mechanics are awful.
- There is only ranked for solo.  Ranked for duo/5's needs to be implemented.
- Lack of game modes/options.  There should be multiple maps, night/day mechanics, options to change weapon/item spawn amount, and maybe EMP.  When you queue, and get to the loading area, it should indicate a RANDOM map, then ask players to vote on night/day cycle, spawn frequency, and EMP.  Majority wins.
- There is no meaningful way to train or test.  The "training" server is a joke, and the weapon, item and car spawns don't re-appear, meaning you're going there to get next to zero items, with 30-50 others.  There's no way to put yourself into the map and, say, try the sniper rifle out alone.
Until they start actually making meaningful updates to the game rather than just cosmetic items for the money grab, I cannot recomend this game, or devs that treat their games and their customers this way.

Facts:
I have no issue with concept of this game, however as a new player there are a lot of flaws. Aiming is terrible, (even with mouse smoothening off and raw mouse input on (Steel Series Rival)) the sound is subpar, and the biggest offense is the tacked on training mode. This game teaches nothing to new players, and the training mode is more tacked on than a secondary COD game mode.
In all seriousness the training mode is lackluster leaving the player to not understand game mechanics and spend several hours learning rudimentary things that really should be in a tutorial.
Oppinion:
Being able to hop out of a car going 60 mph and still shoot straight immediatly is an extreme annoyance and personally is an extremely unbalanced option. I appreciate the fact that your weapon length is taken into account so you cant aim directly beside corners, you have to back away from them to aim properly, but the annoyance is there is no CQB weapons in the game like SMG's, which could utilize the weapon length factor into account and allow you to hug corners better, but this is neglected by the developers due to there being no SMGs....
The inaccuracy of weapons is an extreme annoyance as well, being able to compensate or somewhat alleviate recoil should be an option but sadly at my level doesn't appear to be possible. Klashnikov Rifles should be a tiny bit more accurate, in my oppinion.
And finally, the moving system, it is just my oppinion so feel free to disagree, but in my oppinion the movement system is clunkier than an old PS2 RPG game. Seriously it's really really bad.

I've put a lot of time into this game, even before they split into two different games, and I'm starting to question why I even continue playing. It seems that over time, this game is gradually getting worse, and not in the sense that I'm getting bored of it or it's too repetitive. I'm referring to the fact that it seems that this game now has more bugs than ever before, even when the game first launched. The queues are horrendous, you're only able to play about 7 out of every 10 games you queue for because of a bug where you get teleported out of your vehicle and are unable to move, and not having anything done about the bugs to make the game better.
At one point, I loved this game. It was fun, my friends and I had a blast playing 2s or 5s and stacking up shirts / crowns for winning, but even that is gone. You no longer receive a reward for winning other than satisfaction, I guess. It's really upsetting. Another thing that has gotten worse over time, would be the server stability itself. Far too often I find myself being rubber-banded or stuck to an object for 15-20 seconds at a time throughout the course of the game. Sure, you can say it's my internet but it's not, it happens to everyone I'm playing with at the same time.
That being said, this game is still worth playing if you find yourself getting it for a discount, potentially. This game is absolutely not worth $20 in it's current state, and there's no improvements in sight. You'll find Daybreak employees in streams or on reddit talking about what's coming soon, but they can't even put in a hotfix without causing even more bugs. The game has not had a single bug fix in over a month, so I ask, what are the developers actually doing?

CONS

While it might be interesting to learn about real combat, it is not fun.

The crosshair still exists for some reason, which isn't realistic.
The run speed is at a maximum of 18km/h (5m/s), which isn't realistic.
In game fatigue is like an assumption of what real fatigue is like.
Bots actually require 3 bullet hits to die, they bounce backwards each time they get hit.
2. Too clunky
Movement keys are too clunky. Z for crouch, X for high knee. Just press once for crouching, two for high knee.
3. Weapons
It's horribly backwards. As if the ARMA military was stuck in time.

You then fight.
Now I am not going to get into all of the bugs in this game, that would take the length of a college thesis paper. Let me start by saying that I have had fun with this game, as you can see by my playtime. But that playtime has been plagued by bugs, glitches, low FPS, and a constant feeling of "Why didn't they...?" in the back of my mind. I never got into ArmA 2 because of its FPS problems, netcode, clunky and unintuitive controls, and just bad game design. ArmA 3 has fixed NONE of these problems.
- First off, the performance. The Real Virtuality engine is an engine from the ♥♥♥♥ing 18th century being held together with duct tape and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Server performance still affects client performance. This is a joke. If the server gets overloaded, you are going to be looking at a framerate in the low 20s. This is why performance is so inconsistent.
- The player controller is the same one from ArmA 2. This♥♥♥♥♥♥controller cannot play more than two animations at once, on the legs and the torso. Full body animations like switching weapons require the player to stop moving because of this. Again, this is a joke. Animations are also very stiff and crappy looking.
- Same old bugs and glitches from ArmA 2 that were never fixed. You can lean into walls and see through them, much worse if you're using 3rd person. Grass pops in right in front of your eyes. Objects like rocks are incredibly glitchy and can randomly kill you. Vehicle physics are almost non-existent and you will explode from the smallest crash. VOIP is incredibly laggy and sounds like it's coming out of a 90s phone.
- Game is supposed to use DX11 when in reality it still uses mostly DX9, one example is shadows. ArmA 3 still uses ♥♥♥♥♥♥ stencil shadows instead of soft shadows, even on max settings. Aside from that, visually the game is nothing special. It has nice sunsets and a decent draw distance but up close it's quite ugly. Low res textures are a problem.
- The game is billed as a "military sandbox" by Bohemia and a "military simulation" by PC Gamer but ♥♥♥♥ing NOBODY plays it as one. 99% of servers are gamemodes like Wasteland, Epoch, and Altis Life; gamemodes more suited to Grand Theft Auto than a game with as much potential as ArmA 3. Worse still Bohemia has done nothing to prevent this aside from adding that useless End Game gamemode that nobody plays. I was lucky enough to find a server that plays the game as the combined arms game it's supposed to be, and I played a lot on that server, but the FPS was so bad (~25) that I eventually stopped playing.
- Stemming from the issue above, tactical PvP just isn't a thing. There is some tactical PvE which I have enjoyed playing, but if you ever wanted to shoot at another player instead of those Terminator bots that can snipe you between the eyes from 2km away with a .45, you're out of luck.
- 3rd person. Everyone uses it, or rather abuses it. It's impossible to get the drop on someone in CQC because he's looking at you from around the corner using 3rd person. "Don't play it", you might say. That's impossible, because I have never seen a public server with it disabled. "Don't use it", you might say. Again impossible, because that guy looking over the wall at me will shoot me when I come around the corner unless I use 3rd person to look over the wall too.
- Updates are a farce. Game's been out for 2 years and only NOW we're getting bipods, really? The DLC is another joke, 30 euro for two helicopters and a couple of guns, wow Bohemia what a ♥♥♥♥ing deal.
- "Never half♥♥♥♥♥two things. Whole♥♥♥♥♥one thing." - Ron Swanson. Driving physics are completely broken if you go anywhere that isn't a flat surface. Plane mechanics are pick-up-and-play. Guns sound like crap and basic stuff like keeping a round chambered doesn't happen. The only saving grace is the combined arms aspect, but alone they're terrible to play.
I'm going to stop here because I could go on all day about how♥♥♥♥♥♥this game is and what it could have been if the devs cared at all. I never write long reviews, but how much I love the concept of this game and how awful the execution is made me. This game is NOT worth 50 euro, maybe 20 at best. The only good things here are the insanely huge maps and moddability of the game.
The only reason this game is popular is because there is no other game like it.

If you were the smart shopper that decided to read reviews before by this game, congratulations. You already outsmarted me. I bought this game because I had imagined something relatively like Battlefield or Call of Duty but on a much larger and more realistic scale. Well instead, I got an overly realistic, laggy, impossible campaign game that breaks if you try to play 1 mod. Personally, I would not recommend this game to anyone. I found absolutely no enjoyment in this game. I've played with some friends on a Wasteland server and it was fun until it became Minecraft faction servers in which case you build a base and wait for it to get raided while spending days trying to find someone else's base just to return and find that an x-ray modder has already taken it out. If I was given the opportunity to get a refund for this game, I would in a heart beat. The campaign is impossible even on the easiest difficulty because 1: The guiding voice (example: World at War sniper mission with Reznov when he tells you to wait for the bombers) gives you the most basic and obscure directions and expects you to figure it out (i.e. the mortar team in the forest. finding the mine detector.), 2: The hostile AI will drop you in less than 3 shots and you'll never know where they came from and just keep respawning at a check point and trying to find a way to get past them without dying, 3: You're friendly AI can and will die in combat and the medic rarely heals anyone or tries to revive anyone. Multiplayer wasn't as bad as long as you were among friends. A friend and I would play Zeus (a gamemode in which one player is able to do anything while the other players just play and wait for the Zeus player to do something) and mess around with vehicles. The vehicles were probably the only thing about the game that I didn't hate except for the artillery. There are no instructions or help tips or anything to help you fire the artillery vehicles. There is no hit indicator as to whether the shell even made contact with the ground or hit four miles to the right of the target. The aircraft are another thing I hated mostly because the were nearly impossible to fly. If you tried landing a jet or a helicopter, you were better of grabbing a parachute and hoping for the best because more than likely the aircraft was just going to explode on contact with the ground even going less the a half of a mile per hour. So overall, I would rate this game 2/10 just because not all of the vehicles and gamemodes sucked.

Pros:
+ Unusual gameplay makes this one stand out.
+ Weapons all feel unique.
+ Crafting system makes sense for the most part.

- Lack of weapon variety.
- Unlocking cosmetics can be a pain.
- Pistol balance feels a bit poor at times.
- These guns can have trouble hitting the broad side of a barn.
- Oh and in case I forgot: HACKERS!
Summary:
This game is great with friends, and when no one is hacking. Unfortunatly, this game is incredibly annoying when playing solo, agianst hackers, or when you get blasted point blank with a shot gun a second you land. I would also recomend having a defibulater on hand when you first start playing. Winning your first match, be it solo, duo, or fives, may cause your heart rate to get a little insane.
Overall:
8.5/10 when playing with friends.
7/10 when not playing with friends.

The missions generally fall flat on their face the moment something unexpected happens that the code monkey who scripted it didnt think of.   The menu system is the most user unfriendly interface ever created by man or beast.   Good luck telling your squad to do anything in the middle of a fire fight.  If that doesnt ruin it all the actual firefight mechanics themselves usually revolve around exploiting cheap weaknesses in the ai like not being able to use stairs, generally being dumb and running into open space.  To beat this game all you need is the ability to avoid the AIs magic 500m perfect headshot ability and ofcoarse an incredibly high tolerance to badly engineered user intefaces, save game corruptions and generally randomly borked up s*** happening all over the place.
In short this game if anything demonstrates how graphics, physics and general hollywood'ism of computer games is ruining them and taking the spotlight of the core mechanics that they once had.

Still very much in the heart of the modding community. Great support from the Dev's on this front. Game has it's issues, mainly with vehicles bouncing over the landscape. Really not as well optomised for current hardware which is a real shame. Best advice I can give you is make sure the graphic settings are on high. The Arma game engine has a bad habit of forcing the CPU to perform grahics tasks if you set LOW/MEDIUM detail levels - on old PC's this helped where the CPU was often more powerful than the GPU - however in current machines with highly dedicated graphics processors even a "low end" graphics card should be run on high detail.
Multiplayer is great in this game, suggest trying the EPOCH, WASTELAND, and "INVADE&ANNEX" mods. EPOCH will require a big download as it's a total conversion with zombies and cool stuff, Wasteland is a straight mod mainly for PVP group/solo with lots of options for good fun and constant action. Whislt the invade and annex mod is great for large scale CO-OP PVE, with 30-60 players versus the NPC army.

Arma 3 as of pre-DLC was excellent. Runs much better on less up-to-date hardware than its predecessor. Has a wide range of settings with a built-in FPS gauge in the settings menu that really comes in handy. Other notable gains over its predecessor are a host of innovative gameplay mechanics, along with the usual suspects of arma styled gameplay.
I have recently been playing a boatload of King of the hill on some of the larger servers, and i have to admit the ability of the engine to do what it does is flawless. However it is ruined.
How is it ruined you ask? Simple. Bohemia has transmogrified into a money-grubbing DLC-pushing ♥♥♥♥♥ of a AAA wannabe. Its so cool to get into a really intense battle, run out of ammo, look to a fallen comrade for a replacement weapon only to be greeted with a "pay us money, this is a 'premium' weapon" message. Im pretty sure i payed for a full game, not some cheap mmo.
Obviously the way that Operation Arrowhead was passively incorporated into arma 2 just wasn't earning them the money they wanted. So all that there is to do is tell people to stay away unless you plan on paying at least 75$ for the entirety of this game. It's really sad to see it go down like this. If you have any interest in simulators and military games then this is something oughta pick up, this game blows any other military game i've ever played out of the water. The modding community is fantastic and they create top-notch content that they update regularly, the devs even with DLC put any mechanics in said DLCs up for free for modders to implement into their mods. This game is a no-brainer for a military minded individual with cut-throat tactics and harsh consequences for not thinking, this game has quite a learning curve but it's one that is highly satisfying, I can honestly say this game has become one of my favourites, easily.
I've installed many mods, played vanilla, played all kinds of scenarios this game is absolutely limitless to a talented map editor and the tactics you can create to engage the enemy are extremely varied. The AI can be a bit dippy on their own but that being said with certain mods they will kill you before you blink twice. This game holds helicopters, drones, tanks, planes, light armour, heavy armour, artillery, boats, cars and guns of many types and variations, in one mission you may have to play logistically and transport items in convoys, defend from assaults and ambushes and the like, hell, you might even be the one ambushing, JDAMs, carpet bombs, comanche attacks, artillery strikes of all kinds, mines, RPGs, HMG/GMGs you name it, you can pretty much play the game to your leisure unless the mission calls for otherwise.
This game is definitely for the hardened player but I recommend everyone who would be interested to give it a go and with that I recommend taking a look at the modding community with mods like AGM and MCC4 as a basic mod set, this game is great with or without mods but those two in particular will give you a hugely increased experience.
I'll leave this review off now with rating this game 10/10, it hits all the right spots for me and forces me to think carefully instead of going in guns blazing like an idiot, you must outwit your enemy before they do the same to you. Britbong out.

Unlike the Call of Duty, Counter-Strike, or Battlefield franchise, this actually puts an actual vibe and thrill of a "war simulator". How? You may ask. May have some glitchy heads that turn in a 180 degrees, which is basically the only bug I know of, it'll look weird but it won't distract or mess with your gameplay besides looking at how funny or bizarre it looks. The rest... IT'S GREAT, smooth gameplay, cooperative teams, and the sounds, GOD THE SOUNDS IN THIS GAME! The gunshots sound so really with the crackle and pop in the distance, I heard it can make somebody have a war anxiety panic attack, but that's just a rumor. :)
Jeez what else... the vehicles are so badass and useful! I mean the damn armored vehicles gotta watch out for grenades when it's close, ready to explode. Also, the weapon loadouts are also so damn useful too and will have a reaction when you loadout with your equipment. For example, if you were to carry an LMG, heavy pistol, some big♥♥♥♥♥armor, a rocket launcher, and every other♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of equipment, you're not going to be running at 20mph with all that weight. You're going to slow down and have your stamina run quick. As for a marksman or sniper, they run faster but pack less equipment.
Like I've mentioned, this game is far beyond the Call of Duty, Counter-Strike, and Battlefield franchise. As you all may know, those following franchises have this thing, this thing. This thing is, how do you explain it? Oh yeah, this thing they have is this targeting thing. I don't like it. What do I mean when I say "this targeting thing"? You know if you played these games, when you spot an enemy, they have their username above their character in red text. I'm sure you don't like it either. How Arma 3 setups their targeting system is through the players and really in depth. For example, say you see an enemy on the hills, you can't see his name or anything. Just his character appearence to see if he's wearing enemy uniform. So how do you let your team know that there's an enemy on the hills? Voice chat ofcourse! I really like it because well, because, to all the respect to my Arma players. You sound like actual soldiers that'd use their military communication system. This is where things get in depth. How you spot their location isn't just through the voice chat, you can't just say,"There's an enemy on the hills!" Especially if you're surrounded by hills. No. You have to give the coordinates of the enemy's location. Like the coordinates for the enemy on that hill is North East 280, ofcourse you tell those coordinates through your compass. Your squad/team will look into that direction and will easily spot the enemy without having to look around.
The game modes are great and very tactical, considering you only have one life in each game mode. YOLO. That's what makes your team become serious about this game. There are more useful teamates than there are trolls. Trolling in this game will make you a HUGE♥♥♥♥♥♥ But even though most of the people on this game have the opportunity to shoot your♥♥♥♥♥ they won't because they know how much of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing someone would've ever done, and the fact that your squad/team will turn around and kill you for friendly fire. LOVE THE GUNS, LOVE THE SOUNDS, LOVE THE GAMEMODES, LOVE THE TACTICAL, LOVE THE PLAYERS, LOVE ARMA 3!   10/10

My only major complaints/problems with the game are:
-The lack of ping lock, allowing other region players (Asia mostly) to play on NA servers and pretty much flying around on your screen making it very hard to kill
-The lack of banning for people who team up in solo matches
-The fact that the November update still hasn't come out... and it's December.
*Post-December Update Edit*
So, the game was FINALLY updated... we got a new season (or preseason), we got some new skins, they sorta kinda fixed the shotgun and they fixed one of the major exploits... was this patch good? No. Was it bad? No.
Daybreak has some major issues at their headquarters, they are either understaffed or just dont give a ♥♥♥♥ when it comes to this game sometimes. To their credit they did address one of the major problems, the shotgun and now its about 95% consistent, which is much better than the 50/50 you'd get pre-patch. However, there are still many exploits and bugs they haven't addressed. Daybreak I know you care about your fanbase and want to see this game do well, so for the love of god address some of these issues please!
- Ban. Teamers. In. Solos. Add a different reporting technique for reporting teamers rather than Ctrl+R, perhaps do Ctrl+"any other letter" if you see this player is teaming in solos... It's the most frustrating thing ever to be killed by teamers in solos, believe me.
- The snaking/prone glitch was addressed in the most recent patch, yet people are still doing it... fix it. Don't allow for people to get into a car while prone, simple. There's no reason that you would legitimately ever need to get into a car while prone if you WEREN'T trying to preform some type of exploit.
- Reduce the solos que time in lobbies. The wait time, once you spawned into the Fort Destiny Box used to be like 90 seconds, now it is around 150 seconds, I know we're talking about the difference of a minute but it's noticable and quite annoying, at least lower it to 120 and meet in the middle.

Arma 3 is immersive: as one of the best (if not THE best) military simulators on the market, A3 surrounds you in a variety of breath-taking environments and puts you in the center of the action. You'll receive radio transmissions through bursts of static, hear the wind go by, feel the ground shake when a tank rolls by. Everything from the weather and lighting down to the recoil of the gun in your hand is so finely tuned and detailed, that the only closer you could get to realism is to enlist.
Arma 3 is dynamic: it has an arsenal of mods just waiting to alter the game a little more one way or another. With a community thriving on creating more and more for the game, the sky is the limit for what can be done. No two missions will ever be repeated the same way. AI learn and adapt to situations, forcing you to do the same or die, and with a fully destructible environment, nowhere is safe until the enemy are all dead.
Arma 3 is intense: you'll know this when you hear the bullets snap past your head and you're holding your dead teammate in your arms. The smallest firefights can shift the course of an entire battle. Life or death can be determined just from which way you decide to lean. Teamwork is tantamount to success, and unlike many modern shooters, there are no "lone wolf heroes", no one guy rushing the enemy line and winning the game for everyone. You work together or you die. There is no third option.
Arma 3 is the game you want when nothing but the best will do.

I was hesitant about the title initially, many of the bugs I found during the beta were still present at release. The UI is clunky, and several of the showcases were regularly impossible to complete due to bugs in the game. For example, in the infantry combat showcase my squad never moved beyond the scripted event in the beginning where a team member got hit.
It's been a while after release however, and the game has shaped up nicely. You won't find a combat experience like this anywhere else. The UI is still clunky, but show me a sim that doesn't suffer from this and I'll be a happy man. The showcases work reliably, the combat is smooth, it runs well, and the free portions of the DLC have helped the playability tremendously. If you're looking for a combat simulator this is the best one available. Sound effects are top notch, suppression mechanics and bullet physics are superb, and the vehicles are well integrated into the game.
If you're looking for a more realistic Battlefield game, this is probably too far into the realism category to be fun for you. Insurgency may be more up your alley although it lacks vehicles.

I recommend Arma 3 but Bohiema Interactive have to really step up their game development if they want to please the Arma community and its player-base more. I'm not saying this is a bad game, all I'm saying is that there's always room for improvement. I still have the impression that Arma 2 is a better game than Arma 3 is content wise, however I'd still recommend Arma 3 based on it's AI and other improvements alone.
- 66 vehicles and 53 weapons (*some require DLC).
- Huge maps w/ detailed environments (Altis 270 Km^2, Tanoa 100 Km^2).
- Large variety of third-party assets/mods (40,000+ just on Steam).
- Over 1500 public and private servers (circa 2015).
- Realistic (simulated) combat and engagement scenarios to suit most playstyles.
- Sounds effects are now more realistic, however mods can improve this.
- BattleEye fails to ban/stop hackers 95% of the time.
- Lacking in choices of armament and ordnance/munition types.
- Low quality interior and exterior vehicle textures.
- No visible vehicle interiors for IFV's and MBT's (coming soon?).
- Steep learning curve for new players. Veterans won't have problems.
- Terrain not rendering properly (hilltops become invisible from long distances).
- Uses a dated game engine from which can't be upgraded and restricts what you can do in-game (i.e. not being able to drive a vehicle into the back of a V-44X or CH-67).
If this miltary simulator is not for you, there are a heap of community mods and custom-made content to keep you entertained for hours on end. Make sure you check out the Steam Workshop for custom missions and mods. Despite my listed cons, Arma 3 is an excellent addition to the Arma franchise and I'm definately looking forward to what Bohiema Interactive have install for us through the 2017-2018 Arma 3 Roadmap and beyond. I just hope Bohiema Interactive don't make the same mistake of not being able to implement a new engine (or newver version of it) in the next Arma game.

Team Fortress 2 is a First person shooting game. It has various classes from healing class to class that is so evil that has a  flame thrower to flame the enemy gamers. Team Fortress 2 has alot of weapons. They have their own good and bad points. For example for now theres a weapon called "The Backburner" for the class "Pyro" that has +150% extra ammo cost for airblasts but can crit enemies from behind. The extra ammo cost is obviously a bad thing but doing critical damage from behind kind of evens it up. Obviously there are some weapons that are better than others and are waiting for their nerf (Making the weapon crappier) and some that are really bad and need a buff (Making the weapon better). Team Fortress 2 has 3 main modes. Community servers, Casual and Matchmaking. Casual is a game where you get XP from each game and get leveled up the longer you play. Same is the Matchmaking but Matchmaking is harder than casual usually more experienced players play there but cause of lack of updating the system there are bugs and glitches in the Matchmaking so not alot people play Matchmaking. Community servers are just servers where you can fool around in or get practice so are Casual servers but casual servers have their endings and starts and you get xp on Community servers you just play usually 24/7 on server selected maps. Meaning the servers are up all the time and maps change in correct order or how current players choose them. Also Team Fortress 2 as a game has alot of cosmetics most known: Hats and miscs. Miscs can be worn with hats meaning for example you can wear a Familiar Fez at the same time Le Party Phantom for the spy. But 2 hats cant be worn at the same time. For example you cant wear Familiar Fez with Human cannonball (That is an all-class hat). Hats are usually worn by only one class meaning Scout cant
wear a hat that spy owns or sniper cant wear a medics hat but there are exceptions. For example the cosmetic Dead of Night can be worn by all the classes. Basically you have one shirt and you can wear that on Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Enigneer, Medic, Sniper, Spy. Then there are multi-class hats. Like the Private Eye that is for Medic, Spy and Demoman. Then there are various tiers of hats. Normal, Unique, Strange, Vintage, Genuine, Unusual, Collectors, Community, Self-made, Valve. (Same occurs to weapons, taunts).  Then theres taunts. Taunts are things that classes can use using their action key bind. These can be used to make your class do a specific animation. Team Fortress 2 has various gamemodes so called: Capture the flag, Control points, Payload, King of the Hill, Attack/Defence and the special gamemodes: Payload race, Misc, Mannpower and Pass time. I aint gonna speak about them too much cause you can check them out if you download the game by yourself! :) Lets get back to the tiers of hats the Normal is the tier of weapons that players have at the start. They are basically the stock weapons, unique is the tier of weapons that you can unlock, find, buy from the Mann Co. Store. Same occurs to hats. Then Genuine is the tier when you got the item by doing a specific quest for example downloaded some game that was a Sponsor for example then Vintage is basically very old, very old items in the game have that quality. Then Strange is basically weapons that read the stats how many kills you have gotten by killing with the weapon thats strange or if its hat then by how many kills you got wearing that hat. Then theres Unusual they are hats, weapons, taunts with special effects basically for example if hat has a effect of Burning Flames then The hat basically shows the effect of burning on top of your head. Then theres collectors, collectors items are items that you get by combining 100 of specific item in a Chemistry Set. Then theres Community, community items have the effect of community sparkle and are given to people who were/are helpful in the community. Then theres Valve that is just for the creators of Team Fortress 2 as a whole. These weapons have overpowered stats and are basically hard to fight aginst. Then the Self-made is for the people who created that specific item using Steam Workshop and their item got chosen as ingame item by Valve. These items also have the effect of Community Sparkle. Also all the qualitys have their own color ingame (basically the name of the item gets colored the color the tier is). Normal: Grey (#B2B2B2) Unique: Yellow (#FFD700) Strange: Orange (#CF6A32) Vintage: Blue (#476291) Genuine: Green (#4D7455) Unusual: Purple (#8650AC) Self-Made: Light Green (#70B04A) Community: Light Green (#70B04A) Valve: Pink (#A50F79). Parading over a hill with a large rock on it, with a view of a small town and an enemy barracks, my small team of 3 investigates an area where enemies are. Finding a small group of enemies, my team fires upon the group, and the group fires back. One of my team members gets hit, and he groans quite loudly. I request that he gives me his health pack so I could heal him, because he wasn't able to, and still I am not able to heal him. Instead, I heal myself, and feel quite guilty doing so, while I see my teammate get brutally shot to death. my third member runs into battle, slightly helping, but soon gets gunned down. I was quite hurt, groaning and unable to run, hiding behind the rock, occasionally firing full auto near enemies, and almost crying at the sounds of pain I heard from my own character. I was stranded, and noone could help me. I soon died, leaving a hero's body on the ground. The feelings that this game can put into you when you truly put your mind to it and immerse yourself in it is amazing. The graphics are beautiful, if you have the right processor, and the selection of equipment is massive. I would highly recommend this to people who like realistic military sims, and hope they like it. The only downside to this is that the vehicles are not actual vehicles, so you can't judge how they look compared to how they really look. All in all, this game is brilliant.

The Good:
+Large arena with a variety of settings and scenery
+Gameplay mechanics encourage players to stay on the move
+Randomness of spawns in conjunction with above means every game feels drastically different
+First or Third Person view options make it easier to fit your playstyle (stealth vs aggressive)
The Bad:
-Graphics are decent, but lots of "floating" trees items "stuck" in surfaces
-Customization options are too difficult to unlock, mostly tacky rainbow clothes
-Players can cheat to spawn with weapons at the beginning of the game
The Ugly:
---Where are the zombies?
---Pay-to-Play in daily events
---Microtransactions in an unfinished game
This is a really, really fun game. For those who are familiar with Left 4 Dead, classic CoD, or any other arena style game that requires weapon pickups, the learning curve is fairly simple. The arena, however, is much, MUCH bigger. Spawn by parachuting in at a random location in a large map, gather weapons and gear as quick as you can, and make a game plan to make the most of your one life and make it to the top. Despite what you might assume, there are no zombies to shoot, kill, or avoid. (Though, it'd be a nice inclusion in my opinion)
If you're looking for a fun new survival challenge in a large PvP format, this game is worth checking out.
Essentially, it's last man standing with a time limit in the form of poison gas. As games go on, the gas encloses "safe zones" - which acts as a way of weeding out stragglers and campers. Once you get to the last 20 or so people, the active safe zone (which gets smaller as the game progresses) is small enough to keep things from being to crowded yet still forces players to fight for the win.
There is a customization aspect to the game, as you can unlock clothing for your avatar in the form of loot crates as you play. However, this function feels vastly overshadowed by microtransactions... Considering the game is still "unfinished," it seems strange that microtransactions are even implemented. Earning loot crates from regular play is extremely tedious, and doesn't feel like it's worth the trouble. Loot crates are overpriced, and don't really give great rewards often unless you buy over $50 worth. Seems like a racket to me.
As with any unfinished game, it has it's share of bugs. I feel as though the developers spend more time planning new microtransactions and Twitch events than they do working on bugs. They're on the final stretch for finishing the game, so fingers crossed they divert their focus accordingly.

Team Fortress 2 is a First person shooting game. It has various classes from healing class to class that is so evil that has a  flame thrower to flame the enemy gamers. Team Fortress 2 has alot of weapons. They have their own good and bad points. For example for now theres a weapon called "The Backburner" for the class "Pyro" that has +150% extra ammo cost for airblasts but can crit enemies from behind. The extra ammo cost is obviously a bad thing but doing critical damage from behind kind of evens it up. Obviously there are some weapons that are better than others and are waiting for their nerf (Making the weapon crappier) and some that are really bad and need a buff (Making the weapon better). Team Fortress 2 has 3 main modes. Community servers, Casual and Matchmaking. Casual is a game where you get XP from each game and get leveled up the longer you play. Same is the Matchmaking but Matchmaking is harder than casual usually more experienced players play there but cause of lack of updating the system there are bugs and glitches in the Matchmaking so not alot people play Matchmaking. Community servers are just servers where you can fool around in or get practice so are Casual servers but casual servers have their endings and starts and you get xp on Community servers you just play usually 24/7 on server selected maps. Meaning the servers are up all the time and maps change in correct order or how current players choose them. Also Team Fortress 2 as a game has alot of cosmetics most known: Hats and miscs. Miscs can be worn with hats meaning for example you can wear a Familiar Fez at the same time Le Party Phantom for the spy. But 2 hats cant be worn at the same time. For example you cant wear Familiar Fez with Human cannonball (That is an all-class hat). Hats are usually worn by only one class meaning Scout cant
wear a hat that spy owns or sniper cant wear a medics hat but there are exceptions. For example the cosmetic Dead of Night can be worn by all the classes. Basically you have one shirt and you can wear that on Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Enigneer, Medic, Sniper, Spy. Then there are multi-class hats. Like the Private Eye that is for Medic, Spy and Demoman. Then there are various tiers of hats. Normal, Unique, Strange, Vintage, Genuine, Unusual, Collectors, Community, Self-made, Valve. (Same occurs to weapons, taunts).  Then theres taunts. Taunts are things that classes can use using their action key bind. These can be used to make your class do a specific animation. Team Fortress 2 has various gamemodes so called: Capture the flag, Control points, Payload, King of the Hill, Attack/Defence and the special gamemodes: Payload race, Misc, Mannpower and Pass time. I aint gonna speak about them too much cause you can check them out if you download the game by yourself! :) Lets get back to the tiers of hats the Normal is the tier of weapons that players have at the start. They are basically the stock weapons, unique is the tier of weapons that you can unlock, find, buy from the Mann Co. Store. Same occurs to hats. Then Genuine is the tier when you got the item by doing a specific quest for example downloaded some game that was a Sponsor for example then Vintage is basically very old, very old items in the game have that quality. Then Strange is basically weapons that read the stats how many kills you have gotten by killing with the weapon thats strange or if its hat then by how many kills you got wearing that hat. Then theres Unusual they are hats, weapons, taunts with special effects basically for example if hat has a effect of Burning Flames then The hat basically shows the effect of burning on top of your head. Then theres collectors, collectors items are items that you get by combining 100 of specific item in a Chemistry Set. Then theres Community, community items have the effect of community sparkle and are given to people who were/are helpful in the community. Then theres Valve that is just for the creators of Team Fortress 2 as a whole. These weapons have overpowered stats and are basically hard to fight aginst. Then the Self-made is for the people who created that specific item using Steam Workshop and their item got chosen as ingame item by Valve. These items also have the effect of Community Sparkle. Also all the qualitys have their own color ingame (basically the name of the item gets colored the color the tier is). Normal: Grey (#B2B2B2) Unique: Yellow (#FFD700) Strange: Orange (#CF6A32) Vintage: Blue (#476291) Genuine: Green (#4D7455) Unusual: Purple (#8650AC) Self-Made: Light Green (#70B04A) Community: Light Green (#70B04A) Valve: Pink (#A50F79). This is my first review for any game on steam ever. With that said, this game either had to be darn good or just a steaming pile of **** to inspire me to finally write a review. One might ask, "Well, which one is it?"(If you want the short answer, there will be a TL;DR at the bottom) Well, it's hard to say, really. I know I said that the game had to be either great or terrible to inspire me to write about it, but hear me out. The concept for H1Z1: KOTK is
Daybreak really did a great job making a simple, and almost mindless (Which is a good thing for me) game that is just plain fun. As someone who enjoys games that you can't beat (ex. COD: Zombies), or games that you can get really good at (ex. Super Smash Bros Melee), I'd wholeheartedly recommend this game to people who enjoy the same types of games that I do.

This is where the praise ends though... Oftentimes, I find myself frustrated with this game. Why? Trust me, it's not because I'm getting rekt. It's actually the treasure trove of bugs this game is
with. The devs really screwed the pooch here, folks. While some bugs are worse than others, I plan on talking about only one bug here today. I will call this bug the "Standstill bug". Where do I even start? This bug is the bane of my existence. Basically, when you're in a vehicle, there is a chance that your character will just up and get out. That's not the worst part though. When you get out YOU CAN'T MOVE. Also, you cannot shoot or even switch weapons. This is a real problem that ruins my experience with this game. Another more minor complaint of mine is the fact that there is no spectating or killcams. You just die and exit. Almost like the game is saying "Hey, shoo!". When I'm playing with friends, this would actually give me something to do, instead of hoping they die fast so you can join a game together again. This last complaint can be chalked up to nitpicking, but I'll share anyways. Many times when I'm in a long distance fight, I can never see my enemy! Call me a noob, but the fact that I die and dont even know what hit me has made me really grit my teeth more than that darn standstill bug. The binoculars SORT OF help, but even then... I still find it difficult to spot enemies. Yes, I turned up my render distance in case you're wondering.

BUT, aside from these frustrating negatives, I DO recommend this game. After all, it
in early access. One thing you have to give the devs credit for is that if you told me that it was just a buggy game, I never would have known it was an early access game. If I had to rate this game, I would give it a 6/10. Just iron out the kinks and you'd have an amazing game. With the kinks... it's "Good, I guess".
TL;DR: Good concept for a game, but it has it's fair share of glitches. 6/10 needs some new features and bug fixes, but aside from that I recommend it.

This is my first review for any game on steam ever. With that said, this game either had to be darn good or just a steaming pile of **** to inspire me to finally write a review. One might ask, "Well, which one is it?"(If you want the short answer, there will be a TL;DR at the bottom) Well, it's hard to say, really. I know I said that the game had to be either great or terrible to inspire me to write about it, but hear me out. The concept for H1Z1: KOTK is
Daybreak really did a great job making a simple, and almost mindless (Which is a good thing for me) game that is just plain fun. As someone who enjoys games that you can't beat (ex. COD: Zombies), or games that you can get really good at (ex. Super Smash Bros Melee), I'd wholeheartedly recommend this game to people who enjoy the same types of games that I do.

This is where the praise ends though... Oftentimes, I find myself frustrated with this game. Why? Trust me, it's not because I'm getting rekt. It's actually the treasure trove of bugs this game is
with. The devs really screwed the pooch here, folks. While some bugs are worse than others, I plan on talking about only one bug here today. I will call this bug the "Standstill bug". Where do I even start? This bug is the bane of my existence. Basically, when you're in a vehicle, there is a chance that your character will just up and get out. That's not the worst part though. When you get out YOU CAN'T MOVE. Also, you cannot shoot or even switch weapons. This is a real problem that ruins my experience with this game. Another more minor complaint of mine is the fact that there is no spectating or killcams. You just die and exit. Almost like the game is saying "Hey, shoo!". When I'm playing with friends, this would actually give me something to do, instead of hoping they die fast so you can join a game together again. This last complaint can be chalked up to nitpicking, but I'll share anyways. Many times when I'm in a long distance fight, I can never see my enemy! Call me a noob, but the fact that I die and dont even know what hit me has made me really grit my teeth more than that darn standstill bug. The binoculars SORT OF help, but even then... I still find it difficult to spot enemies. Yes, I turned up my render distance in case you're wondering.

BUT, aside from these frustrating negatives, I DO recommend this game. After all, it
in early access. One thing you have to give the devs credit for is that if you told me that it was just a buggy game, I never would have known it was an early access game. If I had to rate this game, I would give it a 6/10. Just iron out the kinks and you'd have an amazing game. With the kinks... it's "Good, I guess".
TL;DR: Good concept for a game, but it has it's fair share of glitches. 6/10 needs some new features and bug fixes, but aside from that I recommend it.

The one and only modern combined-arms military simulator.
Bohemia Interactive continues their legacy of excellent military simulators stemming from the original Operation Flashpoint games (now ARMA: Cold War Assault) and Virtual Battlespace. ARMA 3 is a slightly different beast from its predecessors, as it is set in the near future. In other words, the weapons, uniforms, and vehicles are not the regular M4s, Abrams tanks and T-80s. This is something that you should note as it could be seen as a big concern for the avid milsim player. Nevertheless, Bohemia Interactive is mod-friendly and there are now plenty of weapon mods available for download via Steam Workshop, or at Armaholic.
Personally I began playing Operation Flashpoint shortly after its release in 2001. I fell in love and continued playing the game for many years. Then came ArmA (Armed Assault) which in my opinion was decent, but it would take ARMA (not an abbreviation of Armed Assault) 2 for me to sink into again. With a membership in one of the absolute best tactical gaming communities the love manifested itself even further.
ARMA 3 had a shaky launch, and according to many veterans it seemed released slightly too early, even for its Alpha and Beta versions. However after much patching its present engine is much more stable than ARMA 2's and with recently released DLCs (along with them free platform updates) it boasts impressive ballistics physics as well as an imported flight model from Take On: Helicopters.
The campaign of all ARMA games after Operation Flashpoint: Cold War Crisis, albeit not something that most players devote their time to, have not been as fleshed out in terms of story. ARMA 3 isn't an exception in this case, and offers a pretty weak campaign in terms of story. Perhaps it was Operation Flashpoint's multiple POVs from its characters as well as the genuine feeling of advancement through the ranks (as David Armstrong) that immersed the player more in that game's campaign.
All-in-all in terms of its multiplayer gameplay, you should note that you will experience lag at times if you are playing on a 40-man server on a fleshed-out map like Invade and Annex. But for the true milsim experience, I must recommend joining a dedicated community that creates content and campaigns for co-operative and/or TvT play.

Team Fortress 2 is a First person shooting game. It has various classes from healing class to class that is so evil that has a  flame thrower to flame the enemy gamers. Team Fortress 2 has alot of weapons. They have their own good and bad points. For example for now theres a weapon called "The Backburner" for the class "Pyro" that has +150% extra ammo cost for airblasts but can crit enemies from behind. The extra ammo cost is obviously a bad thing but doing critical damage from behind kind of evens it up. Obviously there are some weapons that are better than others and are waiting for their nerf (Making the weapon crappier) and some that are really bad and need a buff (Making the weapon better). Team Fortress 2 has 3 main modes. Community servers, Casual and Matchmaking. Casual is a game where you get XP from each game and get leveled up the longer you play. Same is the Matchmaking but Matchmaking is harder than casual usually more experienced players play there but cause of lack of updating the system there are bugs and glitches in the Matchmaking so not alot people play Matchmaking. Community servers are just servers where you can fool around in or get practice so are Casual servers but casual servers have their endings and starts and you get xp on Community servers you just play usually 24/7 on server selected maps. Meaning the servers are up all the time and maps change in correct order or how current players choose them. Also Team Fortress 2 as a game has alot of cosmetics most known: Hats and miscs. Miscs can be worn with hats meaning for example you can wear a Familiar Fez at the same time Le Party Phantom for the spy. But 2 hats cant be worn at the same time. For example you cant wear Familiar Fez with Human cannonball (That is an all-class hat). Hats are usually worn by only one class meaning Scout cant
wear a hat that spy owns or sniper cant wear a medics hat but there are exceptions. For example the cosmetic Dead of Night can be worn by all the classes. Basically you have one shirt and you can wear that on Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Enigneer, Medic, Sniper, Spy. Then there are multi-class hats. Like the Private Eye that is for Medic, Spy and Demoman. Then there are various tiers of hats. Normal, Unique, Strange, Vintage, Genuine, Unusual, Collectors, Community, Self-made, Valve. (Same occurs to weapons, taunts).  Then theres taunts. Taunts are things that classes can use using their action key bind. These can be used to make your class do a specific animation. Team Fortress 2 has various gamemodes so called: Capture the flag, Control points, Payload, King of the Hill, Attack/Defence and the special gamemodes: Payload race, Misc, Mannpower and Pass time. I aint gonna speak about them too much cause you can check them out if you download the game by yourself! :) Lets get back to the tiers of hats the Normal is the tier of weapons that players have at the start. They are basically the stock weapons, unique is the tier of weapons that you can unlock, find, buy from the Mann Co. Store. Same occurs to hats. Then Genuine is the tier when you got the item by doing a specific quest for example downloaded some game that was a Sponsor for example then Vintage is basically very old, very old items in the game have that quality. Then Strange is basically weapons that read the stats how many kills you have gotten by killing with the weapon thats strange or if its hat then by how many kills you got wearing that hat. Then theres Unusual they are hats, weapons, taunts with special effects basically for example if hat has a effect of Burning Flames then The hat basically shows the effect of burning on top of your head. Then theres collectors, collectors items are items that you get by combining 100 of specific item in a Chemistry Set. Then theres Community, community items have the effect of community sparkle and are given to people who were/are helpful in the community. Then theres Valve that is just for the creators of Team Fortress 2 as a whole. These weapons have overpowered stats and are basically hard to fight aginst. Then the Self-made is for the people who created that specific item using Steam Workshop and their item got chosen as ingame item by Valve. These items also have the effect of Community Sparkle. Also all the qualitys have their own color ingame (basically the name of the item gets colored the color the tier is). Normal: Grey (#B2B2B2) Unique: Yellow (#FFD700) Strange: Orange (#CF6A32) Vintage: Blue (#476291) Genuine: Green (#4D7455) Unusual: Purple (#8650AC) Self-Made: Light Green (#70B04A) Community: Light Green (#70B04A) Valve: Pink (#A50F79).
