Army 3 has been out a while now. It had a long Beta testing stage and has been through many updates since its full release. It’s the 3rd major instalment in the Arma Series, created by Bohemia Interactive. Whilst the Arma series is undoubtedly the king of military sim Arma 2 always felt clunky as a game. Frequent bugs, poor mechanics and terrible net coding always left me feeling a little cold. Fortunately, Arma 3 is a marked improvement on it processor and here is why:
-Vastly improved visuals including great textures, antialiasing, draw distances, lighting and shadows.
-More developed mechanics; everything from new stances and animations to better ballistics and physics.
-Modern setting, drawing on the latest military technology for one of the most accurate military sims to date.
-Fantastic realism; no bulls**t kill streaks or regen health, one shot kills and detailed ballistic models.
-Beautifully detailed; From vehicles and environments to character models and gun models, the attention to detail is second to none.
-Pin point sound design.
-Unparalleled strategic freedom, switch between first and third person and perform complex operations using the vast array of equipment.
-Massively improved net code, less frequent characters that can morph through walls.
-Mod and community support! Whilst this isn’t new to the Arma franchise (let us not forget DayZ!) Bohemia and the community insure that new content keeps the game fresh and alive. Also there is a nice variety of mulitplayer modes hosted by the community.
-Good array of PC options and supports for TrackIR, multi monitor and various control setups.
-Annoying DLC, allot of it seems tacked on or something that could have been added in a free update (ie. Go Carts).
-Very incompetent AI (still), they seem to literally dance in front of your gun fire...
-Pretty poor single player (again), missions lack depth and characters with no notable story line to think of.
-Performance issues; although there are improved visuals the game is still CPU dependent which destroys performance (espically in multiplayer).
-Despite good sound design the voice acting is pretty terrible and the soundtrack is instantly forgettable.
-Lack of dedicated servers for those wanting an easy, unaltered and straight forward experience.
-Lack of clear tutorials could leave new players confused and unguided.
This game is most definitely worth the purchase ONLY IF you like military sim. This isn't for everyone; someone looking for the casual/fast moving FPS genre may want to turn back as its very slow paced. Yet, the moments of action often will leave you in awe. This is a massive improvement of Arma 2 and by far one of the best military sims on the market but Bohemia could take further steps to improve on the issues of mentioned that have plagued the franchise from the beginning.

Suddenly, tracer fire flies right by you, and your IC is hit, the Combat Medic crawls to him, but suddenly he is hit as well. You've got a choice: drag either of them to safety and patch them up, or dive for cover. Being a hero, you naturally grab your medic, with the intent of reviving him and getting to the IC ASAP. It's all good though, you respawn and set off on another patrol.
Seriously though, buy this game, it is so varied, and there's so many mods available as well. The community is brilliant, both in clans and on forums like Reddit.

It's all good though, you respawn and set off on another patrol.

If you love realistic war games, this is it. No armour that counts down to zero here. A bullet to the head is just that. Expect to be humiliated... in spades. This is a very unforgiving game, if you die, it's your fault. Don't think you can run around like in any other FPS here, that won't work. Team play is absolute key in this game. It is hard, brutal and absolutely gorgeous. The graphics is very realistic, and sure. Had they used UE4 for instance, the game might have had better rendering. But you'd be hard pressed to be disappointed in that regard when it comes to this game. All around a very good war simulator, because that it exactly what this is. If you ever wondered how it would feel like being surpressed by gun fire, just play this game. Because in other more 'gamey' titles, you are most of the time not very afraid of bullets, and the occasional hit. You'll sure be in this one. I strongly recommend this title.

Hello guys,
I dont even know where to begin. Im playing this game for more than 3 years and more than 2,7k hours (when im typing this) witch is alot time and now i get into this phase where im writing this. Fistly i would like to talk about the game itself as a product of VALVe and then about the problems in the game itself. So i started playing this game in late 2015 when i saw a video of gameplay on YT, since then this game ment so much to me and i loved it. But as the time continue and the E-sport start to grow bigger VALVe started to focus more and more on other games mainly DOTA 2 and CS:GO as they would and will make them way more money ( wich cant be blamed when VALVe is a firm that need to make money) but they left TF2 way way behind and almost forgot about it for good. Even when we get few signs of hope like Gun Mettle and Meet your match updates, still this game is slowly sinking into void. For me the main problem I see the care (or rather the not care) of develophers. Looks like they run out of ideas how to make this game fresh and joy to play and they rather focus on other stuffs. As next problem i see the community itself, this game ( with kinda cartoonish graphic) take alot of attention from young players (talking about 9-13,14 yo), from which is very difficult to get propper feedback on pretty much anything, so develophers came with idea to ask pro players for their advices to help this game. Well i can say it was atleast contraproductive, as the majority of community (im not shy so say atleast 98%) are just casual players (as me). So if you want to make money you need it to make it for majority of players (the majority that spends money in this game), but then we getting back to community and developers. We all are trapped in this endless circle, something significant needs to be done before it will be too late, it really tears my hearth, because i really love this game. Now lets get into the problems directly in game. Biggest doom in game are cheaters. Its already some time from last VAC wave and  the occurence of cheaters is bigger then it was ever before. You need to be really lucky to not get atleast one cheater on 1 out of 3 servers. Something needs to be done about it immediately, before it will be too big to stop it. Next problem is report system, totally not funktioning. With that we getting once again back to develophers and our endless circle. Next not as significant are random crits, with whom I can live, but it would be little step forward to remove them for GOOD (from casual servers). Next on the list is poor weapon balancing, and the upcomming weapon balance update is like cherry on the cake.
With that i would like to thank everybody make it to these words and i wish somebody from TF2 team would see this and i would like to know their opinion on all of this. (you are free to to share it everywhere)
with fingers crossed and tear in eye, i pray for this game.

Let me start by saying that I have been a fan of this company since 1999 when I bought a copy of Everquest. I had such high hopes for H1Z1 following it through all of development and playing both closed and open betas. I played the day it came out when the servers were so overcrowded you could hardly ever even join a server, I played throughout the introduction of the battle royale system and subsequent realization by SOE turned Daybreak that battle royale was vastly more popular than their main iteration of the game. I watched how as soon as SOE was aquired by a hedge fund and turned into Daybreak how the entire game model turned into a means of producing revenue. This review is not like the plethora of others listed here saying that gun hitboxs are not working properly or that Chinese players and cheaters are prevalent everywhere. This review is mainly here to point to the reasons why this game has become what it is and why it will probably never become what the players want it to be.
TLDR Reasons why the game is not worth buying:
1: Development rolls out hundreds of new skins for players to spend money on rather than fixing game crippling bugs
2: Company is owned by a hedge fund solely focused on earning as much profit for as little effort as possible.
3: Weapon hitboxs do not function properly and all efforts at addressing them fail
4: Chinese players and cheaters exist on every server there is
5: Poor communication from development team and zero transparency about agenda and roadmap

APEX EDIT: A lot of the stuff I said about Arma 3 has been completely changed with the release of Apex, so I'm overhauling this review.
I had made remarks about Arma sometimes feeling like a 5-star game with intermittent lapses into "terribly buggy" territory, and while that still happens, the vanilla non-modded gameplay has come leaps and bounds since my review. AI is worlds better (but still not perfect) and many bugs have been squashed, so I have to applaud the devs for their outstanding work in continuing to improve the experience. Not many devs out there do this.
The fact still remains that you really should be playing this multiplayer, as it greatly enhances the experience. Even if you get absolutely, incomprehensibly enraged by your shitdick idiot of friend who has the unique ability to make any combat situation irreparably worse, you will find yourself hard pressed to put this game down. It does take a certain methodical approach & tactical mindset to pull off an operation flawlessly, which I admit is something many don't have the patience for in favor of big explosions and air strikes and kamikaze helicopter attacks. If watching enemy positions, marking up a map, and discussing plan of action for like 5 minutes (or more) sounds too boring, you might not like Arma 3's pace. Communication especially is a key skill which I admit I've found myself needing to work on at times- when rounds are flying and there's a very important message to get across you need to be able to articulate a message like "Technical, 500 yards to our east, over by that low house with blue shingles!" instead of "Shoot the thing! THE THING! OVERTHERE THE THING F**KF**KF**K THE THIIIIIING!"
Realism is great, that hasn't changed. The graphics have aged well, but are now starting to look a little on the dated side. Still though, with the advances in processing power since release you now get to turn up your view range even further.
Mods really enhance the gameplay experience, although too many can start to alter your performance for the worse: I'm currently trying to figure out an issue where sometimes the first shot from a rifle causes a MASSIVE frame drop stutter. Vanilla is smooth as butter, but just be careful how many mods you try stacking on top of each other.
Apex adds a lot of really cool stuff, and is well worth the price, by the way. Other DLC arguably less so, Karts especially. I personally have purchased all DLC except Karts and don't regret any of the purchases.
Finally, the issue from my original aside still persists: with an Xbox360 controller, armed helicopters are impossible to fly because "rotate right" and "fire" are bound to the SAME BUTTON. This greatly inhibits both right turns and attempting any sort of attack run. Hmmmm, why? That seems just lazy to me and it still hasn't been fixed!

APEX EDIT: A lot of the stuff I said about Arma 3 has been completely changed with the release of Apex, so I'm overhauling this review.
I had made remarks about Arma sometimes feeling like a 5-star game with intermittent lapses into "terribly buggy" territory, and while that still happens, the vanilla non-modded gameplay has come leaps and bounds since my review. AI is worlds better (but still not perfect) and many bugs have been squashed, so I have to applaud the devs for their outstanding work in continuing to improve the experience. Not many devs out there do this.
The fact still remains that you really should be playing this multiplayer, as it greatly enhances the experience. Even if you get absolutely, incomprehensibly enraged by your shitdick idiot of friend who has the unique ability to make any combat situation irreparably worse, you will find yourself hard pressed to put this game down. It does take a certain methodical approach & tactical mindset to pull off an operation flawlessly, which I admit is something many don't have the patience for in favor of big explosions and air strikes and kamikaze helicopter attacks. If watching enemy positions, marking up a map, and discussing plan of action for like 5 minutes (or more) sounds too boring, you might not like Arma 3's pace. Communication especially is a key skill which I admit I've found myself needing to work on at times- when rounds are flying and there's a very important message to get across you need to be able to articulate a message like "Technical, 500 yards to our east, over by that low house with blue shingles!" instead of "Shoot the thing! THE THING! OVERTHERE THE THING F**KF**KF**K THE THIIIIIING!"
Realism is great, that hasn't changed. The graphics have aged well, but are now starting to look a little on the dated side. Still though, with the advances in processing power since release you now get to turn up your view range even further.
Mods really enhance the gameplay experience, although too many can start to alter your performance for the worse: I'm currently trying to figure out an issue where sometimes the first shot from a rifle causes a MASSIVE frame drop stutter. Vanilla is smooth as butter, but just be careful how many mods you try stacking on top of each other.
Apex adds a lot of really cool stuff, and is well worth the price, by the way. Other DLC arguably less so, Karts especially. I personally have purchased all DLC except Karts and don't regret any of the purchases.
Finally, the issue from my original aside still persists: with an Xbox360 controller, armed helicopters are impossible to fly because "rotate right" and "fire" are bound to the SAME BUTTON. This greatly inhibits both right turns and attempting any sort of attack run. Hmmmm, why? That seems just lazy to me and it still hasn't been fixed!

There we sat, a small squad of eight men. All ready for the order from our captain. Then a voice could be heard. It was another man screaming. Then gunshots, then silence. Our squad leader told us to move up into a defensive position and lay wait in ambush for the convoy to come along. So we did, then we heard a TON of gunshots. Yet we still waited. Then we heard women screaming, then children. We knew the gunshots were AKMs and we thought they were in a firefight with civillians in the middle. Then the trucks came. Truck after truck, I counted 7. Everyone in my squad just stared. Then I noticed the others were standing up. I stood up too in case I was missing something. Then I heard a whistle and the commander exploded, same with his second-in-command. I ran away, and never saw my squad again.
I hope you like my story of a somewhat realistic interpration of the game. This is a REALLY good game. No doubt, but I don't think I like the semi-futuristic time period in the game. I would have preferred something in the more near future. In the end thought It's an awesome game, and once you finish the campaign, You can spend countless hours playing multiplayer. And if you get bored of that you can enjoy the power of full steam workshop integration and download other people's scenarios!

ArmA is a simulator game compared to those pesky arcade games. Nobody can 360 you here, nobody can quickscope you either. This is the real MLG.
Try to go on a rush and see yourself getting shot. It's all about tactics, how good your teamwork is and how efficient you play.
Pros
*Unimaginably good UI. Game gets every command as I want to transfer. No problem.
*Good netcode. Even with 200ms, you hardly feel the lag. Most match lookups have no problem at all.
*Stunning graphics. Yes, it can use a better thing or two, but it is a simulator game and gives you the simulating graphics too. Not to mention a large variety of adjustables for graphics.
*Total realism. Okay well maybe except the magical first aid kits, rest is pretty much correct.
*Brilliant single player campaign. Unique for me.
*Multiplayer with mod support. Let it be EPoch or Altis Life, Zeus or whatever you can think of, there's a mod related to military.
*I can count these up to infinite, but just get the game and see for yourself.
Cons
*Bad low graphic performance. or I have a really ancient GPU. Ge-Force 610M gets ~30fps with everything at lowest, 100% scaling with 768p. Drops down to 17-18 on really hammering areas.
*Game's way too CPU intensive. I can go for a CPU stress test with this game. Maybe I should type this as a Pro. 2 in 1 program :P
*Way too costly. 124TRY for vanilla version and 159TRY for Extended. Even with 50% discount, it felt like it was a full priced game to me. If you're not fan of ArmA series or really want to get this game, I can't recommend it without a discount.
*A bit complex commands. Takes a few hours to get used to it, hell, it can even be days. Also not everyone can play this game. Takes a bit of extra buttons or few macros for quick responding to situations.

I have this set as my favorite game on my steam profile for a reason.  The game itself looks amazing, and looks even better when you realize it came out 4 years ago.  It calls itself a "Tactical Military Simulator", but it really is much more than that.  True, you can experiance realistic millitary simulations in Arma, but if that is all you use the game for, you are missing out.  The community is incredible, and with great support for those who wish to modify the game.  Huge amounts of user-created content keep the game fresh, in addition to regular paid and free DLC.  It is true that doesn't run the best, but it is still definitely playable, and a lot of people who complain about "WAAAAHHHHH, I ONLY GET 30FPS WITH DUAL 1080TIS, WAAAAAHHHHH" don't realize that this is a very CPU-intensive game.  Performance also greatly depends on what kind of server you are playing on, and what mods/gametype that the server is running.  With an I5-4690k overclocked to 4.6ghz and an R9 280X, I get between 30-60fps 85% of the time, which in a slow-paced game like ArmA is all you need. Anybody who's played Arma III for any length of time has at least one story to share from their experience. Maybe it's the time your transport helicopter got shot down over enemy territory and as the only survivor you had to sneak up on an investigating patrol and hijack their humvee to make it back to base alive. Or it's the time you got cornered in a house with an enemy squadron closing in and nothing but a sidearm on you and still came out on top. Or maybe it's the time you got spotted by an attack helicopter after assassinating an enemy officer and had to make a quick escape on an ATV while dodging the torrent of rockets raining down from above.
Even in the uneven but mostly excellent campaign, the best stories come from your own actions and the decisions you make for your own survival. That makes Arma III a game you just have to experience to understand.

I've been considering H1Z1: King of the Kill for a long time but I've been scared by the massive amount of negative reviews, however a friend finally convinced me to give it a go late December 2016 and judging by the player numbers (40k+ at peak) it can't be that bad, can it? Nope, not really, so I gave it a go.
At time of writing I've logged 79 hours and not really encountered any serious issues. Yes I have to delete my character every time I start the game cause else it won't load and yeah it takes 10 extra seconds and surely it is annoying.... yes that should have been fixed long ago or hotpatched bla bla bla bla bla.... but the gameplay itself seems fairly "bugfree" so far and that's really what I care about - at least it is comparable to A LOT of other games with "Very Positive" reviews that are considered to play fine without bugs and so on.
So far I've experienced about 10 unlootable items (you can see them, but can't loot them), landed underground and been unable to play that round, had the game quit on me at the end of a round a few times and hmm... that's probably about it. It never crashed on me except after ending a round and loading to the menu and apart from the bugs mentioned above I haven't had any issues.
Would really like to see a spectate feature for Duos and Fives modes so you can follow the teams ongoing struggle till the end rather than sit around glaring at a boring static frame for ages. (Seems to be a planned feature.)
I've got little clue about Daybreak but from what I can tell they've managed to put together an experience that I find to be very enjoyable, at times super intense and often quite funny.
The game might have deserved the negative reviews back in the days but at time of writing this I think H1Z1: King of the Kill is indeed a very decent game with a super high entertainment value. Definitely recommended!

My story on Arma 3... This was not made up, I wrote this review for what it was likef or the first time... Before the war started... I remember watching on T.V. Where landing craft was landing on the Beaches and men were getting killed... I landed in the airport and I remember how people were signing up for the army. I ran through the grass in California, rushing to the airport to head to Afghanstan. After I landed, we landed in Europe somwhere. It get us half an hour to get though training. I fell asleep after a day. I woke up hearing the transports going by of Officers. I got up and looked around, I decided to go aboard my Heilcopter. I looked outside, the driver closed the Heilcopter down after my new sqaud got in. I looked as we passed the terrain, beatiful. Then we were going accross the sea. I still had my pistol out and tried to quickly figure out where my gun was. Then, I saw land, the same land and beach I saw on T.V. We landed a mile or two away from the beach. I didnt have time to figure out my equitment so I rushed with my sqaud. My sqaud was getting ahead of me. Heilcopters and airplanes were everywhere above me. I kept running, my sqaud split up, I kept falling my objective to follow my leader. I looked ahead and saw fences and tons of troops. I finally got my gun out and rushed accross grass and fences.
All of a suddden, gunshots started to fire, I didnt know where so I kept running. A sharp pain in my hand and I dropped to the floor taking cover. I kept crawling until my worst enemy was in front of me: The fence. I decided to get up and run, I kept running until I reached the troops running in the dirt.  Then, my sqaudron started to move out to the town. On my way I saw men surrounding a man. The man was dead, I heard gunshots all over again. The man checked the boddy and the dead man got up. The sniper was shot by his own teamate.  I rushed to where the sqaudron was and they healed the man, appolgizeing. I kept rushing through, all of a sudden, "Mission accpomplished men, onto the next objective"! I lost my team everybody spreaded out. A Heilcopter was picking a man up, I rushed to it and it took off without me. I decided to head back to where I ran through the fences. I kept running, I noticed that I was thirsty, I was tired. I kept running, trying to figure out my radio. Pressing buttons all over. All of a sudden, I pressed one button and talked into it: "Hello, Hello this is Robert, this is my first time fighting and I need a medic!" I repeated the same sentence this time louder. No reply came to me and I was worried I would die
Sweat came accross my face as I looked into a empety Heilcopter. I got in and he took me further into the fighting, not back to H.Q. I never knew when the battle was gonna be over. I frogot my Journal on the other Heilcopter and noticed this Heilocopter from H.Q. The ride was longer, we passed many farms in ruins and a city. The heilcopter stopped and dropped me off, alone. Another Heilcopter came in and quickly a man jumped out of it. I remember a attack Heilcopter above me. I ran to the village and was shot multiple times. I turned quickly and got on the ground, I was shot in the back.
I fell asleep. I woke up back at H.Q. wondering what was happening. "go go go!" A man shouted as cars passed by. I was eager to get back into the Chopper. I got in and there was a bigger, new sqaud in the Heilcopter. They wispered plans to eachother. I started to write my first battle but time went by and everybody got out. "Robert, go go go!" First off, this game is amazing. It has something to suit everyone, even though it is a military simulator. This is because of a dedicated community of modders. So if you don't want to be a soldier, get on an Altis Life server and fish or something. If you want the fight a gladitorial battle to the death, try Battle Royale. If you're into zombies there Breaking Point or Overpoch. If you want a strict PvP mode that plays similaryly to BP or Overpoch, get Wasteland. There is so much that this game has to offer that I couldn't begin to list it all. This game like every other is not without flaws, however unlike many games, the dedicated community of modder also takes care of that with their own patches and fixes. Seems like Bohemia Interactive did everything right with Arma 3, and the opposite with DayZ Standalone.
EDIT: DayZ Standalone actually seems to be coming together, although rather slowly. But, back on topic, with almost one-thousand hours of playtime on Arma 3, I can say that there are very few (noticeable) issues within the game. And most of them stem from mods that aren't properly configured. All in all, there are few games of this scale that have a truly dedicated and helpful community, and developers that work so closely with the community of players. It really forms the base of some of the best experiences that I personally have had with any videogame.
EDIT #2: So coming up, just shy of 2000 hours of playtime, and I can still say that I'm firmly hooked by this game and series. It's given me some of the most intense moments that I have ever had in any videogame. As such, I'm nominating Arma 3 for the Steam Awards 2017 'Mom's Spaghetti' award.

The Game is a Great Step Up from Arma II, it still has its Issues but most of these have been around since Arma I (Latency, Desync, Massive Lag in Towns on smaller Rigs etc etc).
I myself dont really enjoy the whole futuristic enviroment, the Guns seem Gimmicky and handle weirdly. (Im used to Arma II with Tons of Mods.) But the Mechanics they have added give alot more flesh into it all.
The addition of the new Flight Model has made flying a bit more hard, but once you get the hang of it its really not that bad.
The Game is actually playble and I've got to say it is better Optimized then Arma II, or at least it feels that way.
In my opinion though the game starts to really become fun when you join a Realism Unit and have all the Mods, which have added so much playability to the game ( Tons of Maps, Weapons, Vehicles, Uniforms, Gameplay Mechanics, Better AI, the list goes on and on.)
Arma III came with 2 Maps, Stratis and Altis, which if were honest eventhough Altis is HUGE does get boring over time, luckily through modders all the old AII maps got added, and theres more and more Maps being made every month.
Vehicles: Vanilla has some nice Vehicles, but again sparsity which got fixed by Modders, same with Weapons etc.
Which brings me to my conclusion, ARMA III is vastly superior to ARMA II in the sense of Graphics/Performance/Mechanics but is only really saved by the great Modding Community thats out there!
One big thing that is missing though is I44 ! That is needed ASAP.
For those of you out there on the fence about Arma III, if you did enjoy Arma II then get it, if you are new to the Armaverse then I'd suggest thinking about it if your into more intricate shooters. But be aware that to get the Fullblown Arma Experiance you need to join a Realism Unit, of which there are TONS out there! I can reccomend a few: 51st Scottish Brigade- my own Unit ^^, 15th MEU- for those who want huge scale Operations same as 506th and 16AA. These are the bigger names out there who know what they're doing. And if your new to Arma i'd suggest swerving away from brand new Units, since it can get quite well Intense.

I am a army vet and have been longing for some military action for years since leaving the service. I waited too long and should have played this sooner because it is almost everything I desire from a military simulator. The other day I was thinking how great it is being back in the army without the disadvantages and useless activities that army life brings. No drills, no inspections and no hurry up and wait attitude and especially no getting yelled at because you missed a dust bunny in a corner behind a shelf somewhere.
First The BAD~
Unfortunately as good as this simulator is there is one major glaring problem which will make you pull out your hair constantly. What I'm talking about here is the really dumb AI. I am really not sure how the developers completely overlooked this aspect of the game. The enemy AI is extremely stupid and has magic aimbotting skills.
One time I was doing some scenario and enemy troops have been called to the area to look for me, so I was about 500 m away laying in prone position behind some rocks and looking at them with my binoculars watching their movements. The AI looked like they where basically fighting their own coding. They would walk, then spin, then fire a couple rounds at me and then continue walking. Rinse and repeat this till I finally left.
Another time I was in prone position in a house on the second floor with no prior enemy contact, All doors closed, somehow the AI knew where I was laying on the floor and headshotted me with an M60 through the wall.
So far I have talked about the enemy AI, but once you get control of a squad you will start screaming at your pixel friends and people in your house will think your ptsd is acting up again. Fear not, we all have these outbursts playing with an AI squad in arma 3. They are simply the most useless squad members on the planet. They act like if you actually took civilians off the street, gave them a rifle and started throwing commands at them in a war zone. They are clueless and useless. The squad control UI is horrible and during heated exchanges you will be fumbling with numbers and f# keys on your keyboard trying to give quick commands.
Although are AI improvement mods which slightly fix the AI like ASR AI 3. This will make the enemy AI slightly smarter but unfortunately the squad AI is still very boneheaded.
There is also the problem of glitches and bugs. They occur often and sometimes completely break your game. There are times where I had to restart a whole campaign because my inventory would stop working or again AI would not follow its coding and either get stuck or get into a car and proceed to run me over. The worst are the UI bugs because they literally break your game and you usually have to restart the scenerio. I have also had a couple crashes and game freezing issues.
The GOOD~
Now that we have that out of the way this is why this game is one of the best games I ever played.
Personally I have been in the military for a couple years and know how things work. This game is simply amazing. Although I haven't played multiplayer yet (waiting on my new mic) I have watched videos of different scenario's and mods like altis life. After playing arma 3 for 27 hours and playing user made scenario's like pilgrimage and whole lotta stratis with mods like TPW mods, allintextures, blastcore, JSRS3 DragonFyre and some other mods I am simply blown away by this game. The mods listed with whole lotta stratis will make your gameplay insane. You are thrown into an all out war. The first time I played it I was literally blown out of my seat from the sequence of events that fell before me. I remember pausing the game sitting in disbelief on how amazing the game is. This is just an example of my most recent in game events
In the first 15 min of gameplay of whole lotta stratis this is as short as possible synopsis on what occured.
-Inserted in dinghy with 4 squad members during night time a see distant battle on land. Its pitch black and the only lights are near the shore where I see a little village and where my rebel contact is marked on the map. Even further I see lights glaring by as tracer rounds fly by, explosions erupted and war rages on.
-Head to LZ and talk to rebel contact.
-Get mission to cover LZ from enemy so that a civilian can get extracted
-Suddenly interrupted by explosions on the outside of the hut that I was in talking with rebel.
-Run out, tell squad to take cover.
-See enemy Apache in the distance and its firing rockets at my parked dingy parked beside shore about 75m away.
-Hear explosions and run for cover behind some house while Apache flies closer and hovers above us firing its machine gun.
-Then see the Ghost Hawk (heli) is flying over to pickup civilian for said extraction mission. Wondering how the hell will be cover the extraction point if there is an Apache above us.
-But its too late, Apache turns around and fires multiple rockets and shoots down the extraction heli we were waiting for.
I was confused on what to do, no way of taking it out and  started thinking that we will probably be dead any second now after literally 10 min of gameplay.
-Suddenly out of distance over the vast ocean horizon I see rockets flying towards the Apache and it gets hit. The Apache turns around and tries flying away while failing to time its flare release, then BAM another rocket hits it.
-Apache goes behind some cliffs trying to emergency  land but its too late as another rocket hits it and it explodes
-Then  I see my saviors as 2 friendly Apaches fly by over a hilltop and zoom by towards another mountain.
-I continue with my tasks and then hear huge explosions in the distance where a couple second ago my saviors where headed to. I see flashes in the distance.
----
I have other stories like getting for example hunted by a tank after I took out a patrol unit but they called for support before their demise. In my profile I have a screenshot on how the tank almost ran over me when I was hiding from it, laying in some bushes. It's pretty hilarious and was scary at the time.
This game is simply amazing and even though the AI is a massive, almost game breaking con everything else is very good. If you are a veteran and miss the good days of service go ahead and get this because you will be satisfied. This is the best game I own on steam and in general. Get the mods, get a mic (for multiplayer) and have a blast.
One thing to note is that I can see this game being NOT FOR EVERYONE. You do need to have patience because there is a major learning curve. Every key on the keyboard and mouse is used. But once you have some basic commands down and learn to properly navigate in terrain while avoiding getting killed the game becomes challenging but fun. When I started I was dying very quickly even with turned down difficulty. Now I simply allowed myself to raise the difficulty and even though I do die I feel like I'm surviving longer. Usually its my squad AI that screws me over. Anyway hope you enjoy the game as much as I am.
Before purchasing I advise you to download the demo, which can be found online and which will allow you to see if you want to learn how to play it.

ARMA 3 is simply the best tactical shooter available to the general public at this time.
9.5/10
If you want a realistic virtual platform to practise and test real-world military tactics this is the one. Plug in TrackIR or Oculus rift and you'll soon be working harder than you have in your life to move your squad 20m deeper into a heavily defended enemy town whilst your attached armed personell carriers volley in suppressive fire from the elevated position you stationed them 1 km South. And when you need those APC's to prioritize their fire onto an enemy weapons squad that's pinning you down, issue the order and they will comply.
On a less serious note, if you want a great multiplayer combined-arms experience which feels less "gamey" than the generic FPS this will also satisfy you. Want an fast-paced urban-combat experience where real skill is rewarded and spray and pray is punished? This is it.
In reality ARMA is somewhat difficult to compare to anything else available because there is nothing else with the level of detail that ARMA has when it comes to weapon models, ballistics, wounding systems (in ARMA there are memory locations for each major bone in the human body, which means you can break your lower arm bone, upper arm bone, lower leg bone, e.t.c.), AI, material penetration (walls do not stop large rounds) and the maps are pretty huge. 270km squared is bigger than a lot of real-world cities and often having a skilled pilot who can get your squad to the combat area using the terrain as cover so as to avoid lockon by enemy AA missiles will be the difference between a win and a loss. ARMA is actually not even a video game in many sense. It's more a realistic training tool which can be played as a game.
Teamplay. Nothing like it. Struggle together, or die alone. The level of danger and lethality in the ARMA series has always promoted teamwork and cooperation leading to incredibly satisfying experiences where you and friends, and sometimes total strangers, will overcome staggering odds. The combat medic drags a wounded teammate out of an open killzone. He's taking fire. The wounded man remembers to give his contact report - he saw muzzle flash from an enemy weapon 0.2 seconds before he went down, and he knows to use muzzle velocity to calculate the distance; "In the building two-hundred-and-fifty-meters to the North. First floor." His radio goes silent. He has passed out from a combination of blood loss and shock. You realise the passed out man is your teamleader so you assume command, ordering your machinegunner and grenadier to direct heavy fires into the first floor windows and smoke grenades in front of the enemy position to suppress and reduce the accuracy of the enemy shooter, keeping your medic from catching 2 lethal 7.62 rounds in the torso. The enemy shooter is determined, and smart. He's moved back in the room and is firing through a sliver of window. He knows your machinegunner doesn't know exactly where he is. The fire is still coming in. The enemy shooter hits the window rim and the round deflects way off target. His next shot is interrupted by a hail of incoming rounds from your teams machinegunner; blind-fire still kills, but after ducking for a moment the shooter is back on target. As he aims he is shook by a 40mm grenade exploding on the exterior of his building, but he knows high explosive ain't getting through a concrete wall and an enemy medic is a prize target. His weapon raises... Your medic is only 25 meters from cover now but that might as well be a mile. Dragging a 90kg man along with a combined total of 50kg of weapons and equipment is slowing his movement substantially. You know if your medic goes down, it's game over. Your team will scramble to treat the two men, become combat-ineffective and be surrounded and killed in that construction site. You know you can't go to help him because the first rule of infantry combat is use cover and don't get shot - the last thing your team needs is two men wounded instead of one. You know your machinegunner doesn't have an exact target, and with the amount of fire he's putting down he'll be lucky to hit anything. You know 40mm high explosive grenades don't penetrate concrete walls... It seems like the medic will go down soon. Surely the enemy machinegunner will deploy and deliver grazing fire across the field in a matter of seconds, cutting down everything under two meters for a long, long way, including your medic. You lean out and blindly fire to the North, feeling in the back of your mind that the mission will soon fail. Unless... Suddenly you hear a single shot from a rifle. It sounds very different to the machinegun fire that has been crackling for the past 10 seconds. A second shot, a moment later. Looking over your left shoulder you see a trail of smoke disappating around a tree about 30 meters behind your position. The smoke is from the business end of the rifle of your teams designated marksman. "Enemy marksman neutralized, North building, first floor. Enemy machinegunner neutralized, West corner of that building", he says on the radio. Enemy fire starts coming in from the North-West, but its sporadic and innacurate; the enemy squad is trying to keep you pinned whilst it reorganizes after having lost its long range and volume-fire capabilities, but those rounds are being deflected by the wind, and they're landing way off target. You calculate from the delay between impact and report that it's from over 600 meters out. Your marksman reports on the radio again; "Engaging enemy rifleman. 550 meters, North-North-West". You smile watching your medic treat your teamleader, both now in cover. Your marksman will be on the radio again soon, you feel...
Another amazing thing about ARMA 3 is its versatility; you can load up almost any scenario imaginable and jump right in - there's a reason the militaries of the world use software from the same development house to train real-world troops.
The level of support from the developers is also unparallelled. At the time of this review it's 2 years after release date and they are about to release the 2nd of 3 major updates which add massive value to the game, and they do it free.
500 000 Euro's prize money to the people who develop the best content for ARMA 3? Yes. And what great content it has been. Years of campaigns and multiplayer gamemodes and thousands of kilometers of official and community terrains.
In short it's the best realistic military simulator with more gamemodes than you could imagine and more than 1000 square kilometers of map to run, swim, drive, fly, and most of all strategize on, in, around, through, and above.
If your interest in or studies of military procedures and tactics is urging you to test your mettle, ARMA 3 is the place to do it. I even know some real-world soldiers who train with friends on the ARMA platform.
Do it.

Great game, but some things that we need to talk about.
This is my first review so it might be bad or good, I don't really know.
WARNING - THIS IS A LONG POST(ALSO I DON'T KNOW IF IT IS GOOD REVIEW).
I have played this game for abotu 23 hours and I will still play it for much longer. I love the intensity of the game and how it makes you feel. I love the rush of adreneline when you get that first kill of the match or when your hiding out in a cabin in the top 10. The feeling is insane. I love the game, but there are a few things.
Things We Need to Address :
1. The Loading Screen - Sometimes this gets me killed. I will press accept to join a game almost instantly, and then it loads the lobby but I don't go into the lobby. I sometimes get redirected to the game without being in the lobby. Sometimes I just sit there with the loading screen and it comes up saying I have died. I haven't even got into the f**king game yet.
2. The Queue - This isn't a major problem to me, but it does need to happen faster. I will sit there for about 5-20 minutes just waiting for a game. I love this game, but why make me wait 20 minutes when I will get killed in 2.
3. The Learning Curve/Skill Required - In this game you can win purely on luck(I did playing Duos and won with a friend), but also you need to be skilled with shooting in this game. If you miss even one shot, its over for you usually. I know there is a training option, but it doesn't do it justice. They should have an "Easy Mode" for the newbies. It should only be accessible until you are level 5. It will teach you the basics, while playing with other noobs(make sure to have some kind of Anti-Smurf detection).
4. The Cars - The driving is great in my opinion, but there is one problem. I don't like how when I run over someone, I just go right through them. Its total bulls**t.
5. The Map - The map is great(I haven't even explored the whole thing), but I do think there should be maybe another map. You need to spice things up a bit with different terrian. It would make it harder for the vets, and level the playing field out(it would give new players a chance to play).
6. The Stat Board - The stats board is great and all, but I would love something that would tell me how many kills I average. Or it could tell me what my average placement is, or how many kills I have had overall and how many deaths. It could tell me my overall k/d. Its just a few thoughts, but I think it would make a lot more people stress about their stats and go for more kills.
7. Some Members of the Community - I have played this for a while and some people are good sports(for instance my friends and I). My friends and I say good game and tell them that they hope they win. Sometimes we get the same thing back, but sometimes they just call us d**chebags, fa**ots, d*ckheads, and f**kers.
Overall I love playing this game with my friends, but if the4y implement and think about some of the things I have stated, then I think this could be one of the best games I have ever played. Anyways hope you liked my review, and I would recommend this game to anyone. I can't wait until this game is out of Early Access.

Great game, but some things that we need to talk about.
This is my first review so it might be bad or good, I don't really know.
WARNING - THIS IS A LONG POST(ALSO I DON'T KNOW IF IT IS GOOD REVIEW).
I have played this game for abotu 23 hours and I will still play it for much longer. I love the intensity of the game and how it makes you feel. I love the rush of adreneline when you get that first kill of the match or when your hiding out in a cabin in the top 10. The feeling is insane. I love the game, but there are a few things.
Things We Need to Address :
1. The Loading Screen - Sometimes this gets me killed. I will press accept to join a game almost instantly, and then it loads the lobby but I don't go into the lobby. I sometimes get redirected to the game without being in the lobby. Sometimes I just sit there with the loading screen and it comes up saying I have died. I haven't even got into the f**king game yet.
2. The Queue - This isn't a major problem to me, but it does need to happen faster. I will sit there for about 5-20 minutes just waiting for a game. I love this game, but why make me wait 20 minutes when I will get killed in 2.
3. The Learning Curve/Skill Required - In this game you can win purely on luck(I did playing Duos and won with a friend), but also you need to be skilled with shooting in this game. If you miss even one shot, its over for you usually. I know there is a training option, but it doesn't do it justice. They should have an "Easy Mode" for the newbies. It should only be accessible until you are level 5. It will teach you the basics, while playing with other noobs(make sure to have some kind of Anti-Smurf detection).
4. The Cars - The driving is great in my opinion, but there is one problem. I don't like how when I run over someone, I just go right through them. Its total bulls**t.
5. The Map - The map is great(I haven't even explored the whole thing), but I do think there should be maybe another map. You need to spice things up a bit with different terrian. It would make it harder for the vets, and level the playing field out(it would give new players a chance to play).
6. The Stat Board - The stats board is great and all, but I would love something that would tell me how many kills I average. Or it could tell me what my average placement is, or how many kills I have had overall and how many deaths. It could tell me my overall k/d. Its just a few thoughts, but I think it would make a lot more people stress about their stats and go for more kills.
7. Some Members of the Community - I have played this for a while and some people are good sports(for instance my friends and I). My friends and I say good game and tell them that they hope they win. Sometimes we get the same thing back, but sometimes they just call us d**chebags, fa**ots, d*ckheads, and f**kers.
Overall I love playing this game with my friends, but if the4y implement and think about some of the things I have stated, then I think this could be one of the best games I have ever played. Anyways hope you liked my review, and I would recommend this game to anyone. I can't wait until this game is out of Early Access.

My only major complaints/problems with the game are:
-The lack of ping lock, allowing other region players (Asia mostly) to play on NA servers and pretty much flying around on your screen making it very hard to kill
-The lack of banning for people who team up in solo matches
-The fact that the November update still hasn't come out... and it's December.
*Post-December Update Edit*
So, the game was FINALLY updated... we got a new season (or preseason), we got some new skins, they sorta kinda fixed the shotgun and they fixed one of the major exploits... was this patch good? No. Was it bad? No.
Daybreak has some major issues at their headquarters, they are either understaffed or just dont give a ♥♥♥♥ when it comes to this game sometimes. To their credit they did address one of the major problems, the shotgun and now its about 95% consistent, which is much better than the 50/50 you'd get pre-patch. However, there are still many exploits and bugs they haven't addressed. Daybreak I know you care about your fanbase and want to see this game do well, so for the love of god address some of these issues please!
- Ban. Teamers. In. Solos. Add a different reporting technique for reporting teamers rather than Ctrl+R, perhaps do Ctrl+"any other letter" if you see this player is teaming in solos... It's the most frustrating thing ever to be killed by teamers in solos, believe me.
- The snaking/prone glitch was addressed in the most recent patch, yet people are still doing it... fix it. Don't allow for people to get into a car while prone, simple. There's no reason that you would legitimately ever need to get into a car while prone if you WEREN'T trying to preform some type of exploit.
- Reduce the solos que time in lobbies. The wait time, once you spawned into the Fort Destiny Box used to be like 90 seconds, now it is around 150 seconds, I know we're talking about the difference of a minute but it's noticable and quite annoying, at least lower it to 120 and meet in the middle.

Arma2: OA was great for mods such as Overpoch and the best thing in Arma2: OA is that there is no physics :D
but...
Arma 3: Brings allot to the table when fighting in wars I mean when I first played Arma 3 and that was when it was free on steam I instantly played the campaign and it was amazing, Not as great as Battlefield and Call Of Duty campaigns.
Now lets cut this boring crap and talk about running the game.
Intel HD 4000+ Graphics Card: Will run the game, But on Low settings and will get over 30 FPS witch is all you need really to get a good feel of the game exept obviously crap graphics.
It can run Arma 3 on a mixed scaled of Low and Medium settings but will get around 20 FPS depending on what settings you have changed to Medium ( I allways have Vsync off, Not sure if that improved FPS but I do it anyway :p ).
However once you are flying in the air in combat like Apache's or Armed Little Birds for example your FPS goes up obviously because it does not render as much stuff around you as when you are on the ground you loose FPS.
AMD Graphics Card: Not sure about this graphics card as my old I3 Intel HD Graphics 4000 Laptop can run arma 3 in the ways I spoke about above but lets bring Arma 2: OA back here for a second, On Arma2: OA I get about 40-60 FPS witch is great and in the air about 70-80 FPS and thats perfect but I came across someone who uses a PC with a AMD graphics card and even on low settings he gets like 15 FPS and maybe 25 FPS if he is lucky.
So Arma 3 wise I am not too sure on what FPS you will get.
I do not recommend anything like FPS boosters or Contig ect, As they may contain a virus and can slow down your computer badly.

Team Fortress 2: Redbubble Simulator
The stakes are usually quite different when reviewing a free product. A poorly written or biased review in a paid scenario can lead to you spending your money in the wrong places, while with free products the most you're losing is time.
And hard drive space.
I bring this up as I present Team Fortress 2, a free game that is surely worth a looking at. This is a game like Minecraft or Garry's Mod, where the actual content and experience you have with that content tends to vary from what the developers intended.
Team Fortress 2 is a multiplayer team-based first-person shooter. The game allows you to pick from nine classes to play as, and you may switch class at any time while playing. I find that this game is way better designed and generally better put together than Overwatch. Let's just get a quick rundown on the nine classes:
Scout: Has low health, but high mobility. Can run fast and has as double jump. Uses a gun that does reasonable damage that can be fired quickly.
Soldier: Has good health, but mixed mobility. Runs slow, but uses a rocket launcher that causes massive splash damage upon contact with anything. (other than teammates) The explosions made by the Rockets also push the player that launched them, leading to a strategy called "rocket jumping" where the player shoots the ground to get high into the air, to reach higher spaces or get around quicker.
Pyro: Decent health and mobility. Uses a flamethrower to incinerate enemies at a close range.
Demoman: Good health and below average mobility. Uses explosives to cause massive splash damage. Can also use the same trick as the soldier to blast themselves high into the sky with own explosives.
Heavy: High health and low mobility. Uses a minigun to cause massive damage quickly and simply.
Engineer: Decent health and mobility. Builds various buildings on the battlefield, such as sentry guns which automatically shoot enemies, dispensers, which automatically heal teammates and replenish their ammo, and teleporters, to allow teammates to get to the front line quicker.
Medic: Decent health and above average mobility. Heals teammates with a medigun that dispenses a medical beam that may heal any teammate to full health.
Sniper: "We gave 'em a bloody drubbin'!"
Spy: Decent health and mobility. Can disguise self as an enemy. If the spies melee, a butterfly knife, is used from behind, the enemy will instantly be killed.
Team Fortress 2 is amazingly well balanced. Every single thing a class can do can be countered by something else. Games tend to flow very nicely, with attempts to dominate being shut down by the player's counter class.
The game comes with a map editor to create custom maps, and you may create custom servers with plugins for your own experience.
The game also includes bots, but their support is limited. They only currently work on a limited amount of game modes.
The game has many weapons to choose from to find a playstyle that fits you.
This game is a barrel of fun, I promise you will see something good in it.

Arma 3, like Arma 2 is one of the most realistic war games you're going to get. When I jump into this world, I feel really immersed and in control of my character. I love running to the chopper with my squad whilst talking to them about the objective and what the plan is. This game is really awesome if you can find a realistic server. I personally am not into deathmatch and all of the other gamemodes in Arma, as it feels weird to play after I've gotten used to the realism. In Arma I personally want the most realistic experience I can get, and Arma 3 delivers. There is no better feeling than rushing through the fields with your squad, getting shot at, shooting back. It feels very immersive, and it's interesting to see how the different situations escalate. If I would have to rate it, I would give the game an 8.5/10 because of the amount of immersion, and interesting situations that you encounter throughout your experience with the game. It truly is like no other experience.
There is, however, some negative points to the game. It's not all just positives. I wish i could give it a 10 or a 9.5, but I can't. This game does have a lot, and I mean a lot of bugs. It's almost impossible to play just a couple of hours in this game without encountering multiple bugs, and that really takes away from the experience. I wish they could at least fix some of these bugs, because some of them are close to game breaking. I do recommend this game for people who want a realistic and immersive experience, but if you want a really good shooter, this might not be it. The only reason I play this so much is not for the shooting. It's for the communication with other people, and the realism. Hope you somehow enjoyed reading my review... if anyone actually did... read my review. Anyway, cheers ;)

Team Fortress 2: Redbubble Simulator
The stakes are usually quite different when reviewing a free product. A poorly written or biased review in a paid scenario can lead to you spending your money in the wrong places, while with free products the most you're losing is time.
And hard drive space.
I bring this up as I present Team Fortress 2, a free game that is surely worth a looking at. This is a game like Minecraft or Garry's Mod, where the actual content and experience you have with that content tends to vary from what the developers intended.
Team Fortress 2 is a multiplayer team-based first-person shooter. The game allows you to pick from nine classes to play as, and you may switch class at any time while playing. I find that this game is way better designed and generally better put together than Overwatch. Let's just get a quick rundown on the nine classes:
Scout: Has low health, but high mobility. Can run fast and has as double jump. Uses a gun that does reasonable damage that can be fired quickly.
Soldier: Has good health, but mixed mobility. Runs slow, but uses a rocket launcher that causes massive splash damage upon contact with anything. (other than teammates) The explosions made by the Rockets also push the player that launched them, leading to a strategy called "rocket jumping" where the player shoots the ground to get high into the air, to reach higher spaces or get around quicker.
Pyro: Decent health and mobility. Uses a flamethrower to incinerate enemies at a close range.
Demoman: Good health and below average mobility. Uses explosives to cause massive splash damage. Can also use the same trick as the soldier to blast themselves high into the sky with own explosives.
Heavy: High health and low mobility. Uses a minigun to cause massive damage quickly and simply.
Engineer: Decent health and mobility. Builds various buildings on the battlefield, such as sentry guns which automatically shoot enemies, dispensers, which automatically heal teammates and replenish their ammo, and teleporters, to allow teammates to get to the front line quicker.
Medic: Decent health and above average mobility. Heals teammates with a medigun that dispenses a medical beam that may heal any teammate to full health.
Sniper: "We gave 'em a bloody drubbin'!"
Spy: Decent health and mobility. Can disguise self as an enemy. If the spies melee, a butterfly knife, is used from behind, the enemy will instantly be killed.
Team Fortress 2 is amazingly well balanced. Every single thing a class can do can be countered by something else. Games tend to flow very nicely, with attempts to dominate being shut down by the player's counter class.
The game comes with a map editor to create custom maps, and you may create custom servers with plugins for your own experience.
The game also includes bots, but their support is limited. They only currently work on a limited amount of game modes.
The game has many weapons to choose from to find a playstyle that fits you.
This game is a barrel of fun, I promise you will see something good in it.

The game had an actual alpha and beta on steam, but from the player's point of view, not much changed between alpha and release day except for a few new assets and the main map being released. It never should have left the alpha, and the problem is that bohemia doesn't seem to have admitted to even themselves that their game came out unfinished. From release day, they have been treating it like a final product, with only a few small polishes and fixes needed. This is beyond the exact opposite of how it actually is. On release day, it was laughably broken. It had the most bugs I have ever seen in a game, and felt like a joke. Now, after 1.5 years, many obvious bugs have been ironed out. I can say that the very surface game experience is acceptable. The problem today is that while they fixed some of the basic gameplay issues, about 40% of the features feel unfinished, but that is coming from someone with 1000 hours of experience. As I said, the surface experience is acceptable, but if you REALLY start playing, you will notice inexcusable holes in the experience. Along with all of this, the game is set in 2035, so none of the objects in the game are real, and at best partially resemble real things. The NATO and AAF factions are okay, but the CSAT faction, the only opfor faction available, looks terrible. The CSAT people literally look like aliens, and I get depressed every time I see one of them. What was bohemia thinking? Why would you put space aliens in a military simulator, especially ARMA? Atleast put terrorists, or north koreans, or normal russians, but space aliens? This is very controversial, especially for a military simulator, in particular arma.

It was sad to hear they were charging 15$ for something that should have been included with the game, but I could live with that. What really set me off is that for 15$ you get only TWO helicopters. Yes, 2 helicopters that you should already have for 15 dollars. With the arma 2 OA expansion, we literally got more assets than arma 3 will probably ever have for 20 dollars. Now we pay 15 dollars for 2 helicopters. Currently, from what I can see, Arma 3 is doomed. They are going to continue charging money for each baby step towards a finished game, and with that, only make a few baby steps, and then run off with the money. The only DLC remaining will be a DLC called marksmen which adds 7 weapons, all of which I've played with, and most of which look like laser guns, almost as bad as the CSAT faction. There may also be an expansion way after the marksmen dlc comes out, but nothing has been confirmed about it.

I suggest waiting for it to come on sale, then it is definitely worth it. I will forwarn you, the game does not really seem complete at purchase. However, the modding community is amazing and their mods have not ceased in amazing me. I would strongly suggest the mods that add the old arma 2 units and maps (MARSOC and Spetznaz maybe on armaholic for units?). It is really great to go back and see these remastered maps, then playing on them with the updated engine.... WHEW BOY, thats some good stuff. Id say that finding people to play with is really important too, I dont do the altis life games, but i have friends that do and they enjoy it. Finding squads that are nice enough to allow pubbies on are generally the way to go. If you will be playing MILSIM, then for the love of all that is good.... GET TASK FORCE ARROWHEAD RADIO! It will enhance the gameplay experience tenfold. The only real con to it is that sometimes good games are few and far between, but the time you spend to find one is well worth the reward when you get to play! Make sure to star it in your server list. I am not a part of a squad, but if you really want to boost your gameplay, then i would strongly suggest it.
Overall, Im not impressed by BI's work, but moreso the modders. (AND TO ALL THE MODDERS OUT THERE... THANK YOU :D) If you wanna game thats run and gun, this isnt for you. If you wanna game that will challenge you and put your skills to the test, this is it. I will honestly say one thing that pisses me off more than anything is the AI's accuracy, but it is possible to change. Nothing like getting capped in the head by and AI with a pistol 45 yards away...
I would definitely recommend it to people who are tired of COD or BF, or are like me and never really liked those other two in the first place because I jumped into arma :P  Enjoy it and have some good times, you may even make a friend along the way!

I might not have hundreds of hours on Arma 3 but it only took me an hour to see the same greatness that I saw and felt in it's predecessors, Arma and Arma 2 which I spent hundreds if not thousands of hours playing with friends, from milsim to Overpoch.
You have to understand that Arma 3 is not like any other game. If you are new to this franchise it will put you down, it will drag your balls through a river of broken glass. It will not forgive any mistakes, only if you're lucky. It will be harsh for you to understand that you have to put an effort to be as good as you possibly can.
Learn all the basics, learn how to move and know every specific button and what it does, familiarize and set your controls to your liking because everything counts. Read about military tactics, about terrain, urban warfare, gorilla warfare, that's what you should expect in Arma.
Anybody that played this game knows the feeling, the feeling that you rarely get. That heartbeat, that short breath, that hot feeling when you're under enemy fire. That nerve wracking feel that you only maybe get in C.S GO when you're clutching in a 15:14 scenario.
If you deliver, the reward comes as if God himself laid it upon you. When you're playing with friends, taking a difficult task and you pull it together and your pilot picks you up and everybody on your team is safe and you fly from that point while you still see the smoke from the burning defeated enemies you know you're smiling and you know you're friends are smiling because that's how this game makes you feel.
It's nerve wrecking because sometimes even if you give your everything, you might lose it in a blink of an eye. Your friends getting shot to pieces, mines, traps, bombings.
Just to repeat it again, play it and I bet that you will feel that fast heartbeat and melting feeling when under pressure.
I doubt there is any other game that makes you feel it. It's addictive, it's like cocaine.
Beautiful graphics and sometimes buggy but that's unfortunately a really small price to pay for a game with so many possibilities.

Best military sandbox out there. This is not just a game. It is a playground where you can wage war in any shape or form (with great graphics btw):

-Control a team.

-The Zeus mode will let you create and edit any part of the game on the fly (be a god).
-The list goes on and on.
The only thing that is not as polished as in other AAA war games is the cinematics, this is more a simlulator kind of game. But then, it's like comparing a toy car and a toy car made out of lego. Take it apart, put it together and you'll have a completely different toy.

Where do I start?
Team Fortress 2 was one of the first games I downloaded when I got Steam on my new computer because it was free and I had heard good things about it. I slowly started to emerge myself into the TF2 world and next thing I knew, I had over 100 hours in the game and had spent some real cash for cosmetics in the game.
Many people say that this game is just a hat simulator, but I really think that if you can look past that you can really see how great this game really is. Team Fortress 2 is one of my favorite games of all time.
Now, 300+ hours later, I'm going to write a full and complete honest review of TF2 in it's current state.
Pros:
- The game is a blast to play. I wouldn't have 300+ hours if it wasn't.
- There is a variety of classes so you'll surely be able to find one that fits your playstyle.
- The game forces you to work with your team and help eachother to win.
- The game, even in casual mode can be pretty competitive.
- The cosmetics just make your character look cool, so the game isn't pay to win.
- Different weapons offer different playstyles.
- Mann VS Machine is a very fun wave based survival mode to try out.
- Community servers can be fun also.
- Awesome cartoony art style.
Cons:
- Competitive mode is completely dead.
- Games are often pretty empty.
- People quit games early.
- Game can get boring after a while.
- A lot of people don't communicate or contribute towards the team.
- *SOME* people in the community are extremely toxic.
- Valve has kinda kicked this game to the curb, so there aren't many new updates that come around.
- There is pretty much no tutorials in the game to actually help you learn to play the game. I'd recommend looking at youtube videos or livestreams of people playing and asking them for tips.
Team Fortress 2, for a free game, is a must have in your Steam library. It can offer you hours and hours of fun filled, goofy gameplay. While it may not be a perfect game and it may have problems that need to be ironed out, it is still an amazing game. 7/10.

You have to understand that Arma 3 is not like any other game. If you are new to this franchise it will put you down, it will drag your balls through a river of broken glass. It will not forgive any mistakes, only if you're lucky. It will be harsh for you to understand that you have to put an effort to be as good as you possibly can.
Learn all the basics, learn how to move and know every specific button and what it does, familiarize and set your controls to your liking because everything counts. Read about military tactics, about terrain, urban warfare, gorilla warfare, that's what you should expect in Arma.
Anybody that played this game knows the feeling, the feeling that you rarely get. That heartbeat, that short breath, that hot feeling when you're under enemy fire. That nerve wracking feel that you only maybe get in C.S GO when you're clutching in a 15:14 scenario.
If you deliver, the reward comes as if God himself laid it upon you. When you're playing with friends, taking a difficult task and you pull it together and your pilot picks you up and everybody on your team is safe and you fly from that point while you still see the smoke from the burning defeated enemies you know you're smiling and you know you're friends are smiling because that's how this game makes you feel.
It's nerve wrecking because sometimes even if you give your everything, you might lose it in a blink of an eye. Your friends getting shot to pieces, mines, traps, bombings.
Just to repeat it again, play it and I bet that you will feel that fast heartbeat and melting feeling when under pressure.
I doubt there is any other game that makes you feel it. It's addictive, it's like cocaine.
Beautiful graphics and sometimes buggy but that's unfortunately a really small price to pay for a game with so many possibilities.

Best military sandbox out there. This is not just a game. It is a playground where you can wage war in any shape or form (with great graphics btw):
-Use land, water and air vehicles.

The only thing that is not as polished as in other AAA war games is the cinematics, this is more a simlulator kind of game. But then, it's like comparing a toy car and a toy car made out of lego. Take it apart, put it together and you'll have a completely different toy.
Just to finish: DayZ came out of this concept (in arma 2). What else do you need to know?

Here's to hoping that some really great developers will put out a similar game that runs well in the near future.

text:
Once you get past the initial learning curve, the core mechanics of this game are unparalleled by any other game I've ever played. Most of the game modes are extremely fun with or without friends, and the modding community only makes it better. Plus, the graphics are quite amazing.
Only issue is that you need a VERY powerful PC to run it at even above 30fps.
A very recent purchase of mine. It is overall a great game with many amazing features. Then after you get kinda good on the campaign, you can take place in the anal penetration that is multiplayer.

NOTE: This game takes a very realistic approach and you will probably die a lot if you act like it's COD or Battlefield. And that's why I love it. It encourages teamwork and tactics above lone wolf run an guns. Enemies will use tactics against you and help each other in order to kill you and your whole squad, so you need to do the same to them. Personally I don't play online with other people unless they are my friends, but that is fine ebcause there is literally an unlimited amount of singleplayer content. The workshop has thousands of mods and missions that enhance gameplay, add new weapons, provide a fun experience, or show off the game's features. Each mission can have dozens of ways to aproach it, and some are much more effective and fun than ohers. Yes, this is a realistic game, so you will probably die in only a few shots, and maybe even one shot if you get hit in the right place. But that makes it even more fun. Every move you make adds pressure as you expose yourself to enemy fire, or are sprinting from cover to cover with bullets flying over your head. The campaign is ok, and can be challanging at points, but still entertaining, and the story is fine, but nothing like a COD like story with nukes, terrorist leaders, WW3, etc. Arma 3 is by far the closest you will get to a real war simulator as of today, and with the right mods, if actually feels like it. The game may be slow at some parts, while you drive or walk from point A to point B, or spend 10min searching for any surviving enemies, but that's how it is in real life. Even when you have cleared out most of the enemies, the last man still poses a threat to you and your team if you don't handle it right. The editor in this allows you to create any mission you can think of, as long as you take some serious time to learn it, but in the end, the editor is one of my favorite parts, because you get to make the perfect mission to fit you style and liking. It may take a while to get used to it, but just read and watch tutorials, practice, and once you get the hang of it, that's when it really gets fun...

Where do I start?
Team Fortress 2 was one of the first games I downloaded when I got Steam on my new computer because it was free and I had heard good things about it. I slowly started to emerge myself into the TF2 world and next thing I knew, I had over 100 hours in the game and had spent some real cash for cosmetics in the game.
Many people say that this game is just a hat simulator, but I really think that if you can look past that you can really see how great this game really is. Team Fortress 2 is one of my favorite games of all time.
Now, 300+ hours later, I'm going to write a full and complete honest review of TF2 in it's current state.
Pros:
- The game is a blast to play. I wouldn't have 300+ hours if it wasn't.
- There is a variety of classes so you'll surely be able to find one that fits your playstyle.
- The game forces you to work with your team and help eachother to win.
- The game, even in casual mode can be pretty competitive.
- The cosmetics just make your character look cool, so the game isn't pay to win.
- Different weapons offer different playstyles.
- Mann VS Machine is a very fun wave based survival mode to try out.
- Community servers can be fun also.
- Awesome cartoony art style.
Cons:
- Competitive mode is completely dead.
- Games are often pretty empty.
- People quit games early.
- Game can get boring after a while.
- A lot of people don't communicate or contribute towards the team.
- *SOME* people in the community are extremely toxic.
- Valve has kinda kicked this game to the curb, so there aren't many new updates that come around.
- There is pretty much no tutorials in the game to actually help you learn to play the game. I'd recommend looking at youtube videos or livestreams of people playing and asking them for tips.
Team Fortress 2, for a free game, is a must have in your Steam library. It can offer you hours and hours of fun filled, goofy gameplay. While it may not be a perfect game and it may have problems that need to be ironed out, it is still an amazing game. 7/10.

- This is why Arma 3 is my favorite game of all times. The gameplay is unique and realistic. You can actually feel the realism when you play, especially mixed with the awesome community.

-  There are a lot of things to do, from diving onto land and then sneaking around a guerilla camp, to using advanced high-tech mortars together with armored vehicles assaulting a large fortified base. If you combine these things (Combined Arms) you can have some really epic missions.

NOTE: This game takes a very realistic approach and you will probably die a lot if you act like it's COD or Battlefield. And that's why I love it. It encourages teamwork and tactics above lone wolf run an guns. Enemies will use tactics against you and help each other in order to kill you and your whole squad, so you need to do the same to them. Personally I don't play online with other people unless they are my friends, but that is fine ebcause there is literally an unlimited amount of singleplayer content. The workshop has thousands of mods and missions that enhance gameplay, add new weapons, provide a fun experience, or show off the game's features. Each mission can have dozens of ways to aproach it, and some are much more effective and fun than ohers. Yes, this is a realistic game, so you will probably die in only a few shots, and maybe even one shot if you get hit in the right place. But that makes it even more fun. Every move you make adds pressure as you expose yourself to enemy fire, or are sprinting from cover to cover with bullets flying over your head. The campaign is ok, and can be challanging at points, but still entertaining, and the story is fine, but nothing like a COD like story with nukes, terrorist leaders, WW3, etc. Arma 3 is by far the closest you will get to a real war simulator as of today, and with the right mods, if actually feels like it. The game may be slow at some parts, while you drive or walk from point A to point B, or spend 10min searching for any surviving enemies, but that's how it is in real life. Even when you have cleared out most of the enemies, the last man still poses a threat to you and your team if you don't handle it right. The editor in this allows you to create any mission you can think of, as long as you take some serious time to learn it, but in the end, the editor is one of my favorite parts, because you get to make the perfect mission to fit you style and liking. It may take a while to get used to it, but just read and watch tutorials, practice, and once you get the hang of it, that's when it really gets fun...
