- This is why Arma 3 is my favorite game of all times. The gameplay is unique and realistic. You can actually feel the realism when you play, especially mixed with the awesome community.
- There are a lot of different combinations of controls. Advanced stances for peeking is a great feature that I hope more games will have in the future. Mod-creators can also have their own controls added very easily. I have yet to see a game with these many control functions.
- Sometimes the AI is completely ♥♥♥♥ed up and this is something the devs need to improve! Especially when you are inside forests and such, where they shoot you through bushes etc.
- Good graphics, though watch out for FPS drops!
- No furniture in buildings and other stuff, which makes the game feel empty. But the outside (which you mostly play in) has alot of rocks and bushes that can actually save your life in some severe situations. Though mission makers can add stuff in the Scenario Editor.
-  There are a lot of things to do, from diving onto land and then sneaking around a guerilla camp, to using advanced high-tech mortars together with armored vehicles assaulting a large fortified base. If you combine these things (Combined Arms) you can have some really epic missions.
- Also I love the soundtrack, it's just pure epicness.
- Since the Marksmen platform update got released, the sound got a huge upgrade. The gunfire does different echoes/sounds depending on environment and distance. The guns also sound even more realistic.
- The game has alot of glitches and stuff like that, but sometimes it's just hilarious and doesn't affect gameplay that much. Luckily it's not as bad as
.
- AMAZING COMMUNITY, even the russians stick to their own servers. Though there are some veerry rare occasions of hackers. Also a huge amount of community-mods to use! Probably the most mature community in a game I've found.
- At the start of Arma 3 alot of people were saying it was unfinished and they only added expensive DLC (But it looks like they forgot the free platform update!!). Back in Arma 2 the DLC was very worth it and full of new stuff to play with. Recently, the developers announced their secret project which is a whole new terrain located at an Island in South America! There are a lot of new features such as Jetskis and Airplanes which I'm looking forward to! They've updated the Anti-Hacker protection A.K.A Battleye for increased protection, and since then I haven't encountered any hackers.
- I don't really know about this. It's not really explained that much and you have to make up the theories yourself. No clear explanation whatsoever.
- I think the campaign is about 25 hours long...
- There is alot of optimization, you can even switch colors of the teams.
- The frame drops, the thing everyone talks about. The problem is that it mostly depends on the server which FPS you get, not what type of PC you have. Singleplayer works fine, and so does local servers. As long as you have a good server there shouldn't be too much trouble.
Not too many crashes.
- There are 3 DLCs at the moment, some people think it's way to expensive (13.99 € for 2 Helicopters!?), but they always put A LOT of effort into them, and a platform update also gets released for free.
UPDATE: The release of Tanoa in 2016 looks like a very good DLC. Looking forward to it.

The game revolvs around a "Hunger games" sort of concept, with players dropping in and having to kill one-another until one (Or 1 team, depending on game mode) remains.
Now, where does this game go wrong?

H1Z1 is not a recent game. It's been around since 2015 all though the standard version is just like any other DayZ ripoff. What is truely shameful is the fact that even though H1Z1 Just survive (the name of the first title) is STILL IN EARLY ACCESS when they decided to make this game which is: Big surprise, an early access game.
I won't lie, this game is a buggy damn mess, it has lots of crashing issues, bugs where you drop from the sky without a parachute non of which seem to grab the attention of the devs even though they are common known issues.
I've experiened:
-Dying from walking into a desk

The only reason for this would be if someone made lots of alt Daybreak accounts just to spam recive items but they have a plugin for that which locks the game to the daybreak account that first started the game, so why keep having this annoying trade restriction?

Pros: +
Excellent modding community which gives you anything from WWII to zombies.
As a simulator and unlike the typical CoD/Battlefield shooter you feel a lot more immersed as you really have to plan how you want to approach your mission in order to succeed.
The scale of the game - the original Altis island being over 270 square kilometers - provides further immersion and creativity in all aspects. It really brings the large landscapes of Flight Simulator X to the battlefield while there's another world to explore on foot.
etc.
Cons: -
Performance issues with larger numbers of AI and some servers. I can spawn 500 AI on the Altis map outside the viewdistance and it still hogs another 30-50 FPS or so while the game works fluently on almost highest settings with 60-100 FPS. I really hope Bohemia Interactive improves AI performance (perhaps by introducing simpler algorithms for AI in the distance) for future ArmA/expansion/patches.
Being teased by the much more improved actual simulator Virtual Battlespace 3 developed by BI: Simulations which also solves some performance issues.

ARMA 3 is THE combat simulator, combine Flashpoint and the previous ARMA titles then take out the bugs and glitches then ADD more realism and you've got ARMA 3. Just walking from point A to point B reveals a level of control that i personally have not seen before, and it's awesome, do I walk at the speed of a crawl, pick up the pace slightly, jog, sprint or just stand around waiting to get shot? And even then when I walk am I in a relaxed form, is my gun ready to raise at a moments notice, is my weapon raised to be fired from the hip or am I looking down the sights as I move along. Chuck in free-look, so that you can scan your environment while maintaining the same trajectory and you've got a pretty full-on walking simulator, add warfare and you've got the best military game around.
That said, this game is not for the impatient. I am not a soldier and this game revolves around realism. If you are like me you will die, over and over again before making it past many firefights, essentially if you're a gamer and not a soldier trial and error may be the only thing that gets you through. This actually works to demonstrate ARMA3's appeal, a game must be good if you're willing to replay the same section twenty-five times over to see it through and continue the story.
Speaking of story ARMA 3 delivers on that front in my opinion also, not that it's neccesary given the great gameplay. Toss in Steam Workshop scenarios and you've got plenty of original content to get through.
It should be said though that the game will not respond well on lower end systems while maintaining any of the beautiful scenery that makes up the two islands on which the story takes place, and the eye candy is definitely a bonus.
Another note- Recent update wiped my saves, second time i've lost my save file, the first being due to Steam not syncing my saves. This is not an in-game issue and I have experience nothing game breaking during my playtime but it should be noted as many could be quite devestated at losing 50+ hours of gameplay especially when much of the game truly boils down to trial and error.

This is war.
Following the ArmA series, this game surely doesn't dissapoint, nor did its prequels.
Being thrown into a massive world that is on the brink of a world war, fighting - or better suited - surviving through the crysis that broke out on the island of Altis, you are given the equipment and vehicles of a modern soldier of the 21st. century.
The game is - without any doubt - this generation's most realistic shooter, likely even referred to as a military simulator for the "wider public". If you are a military enthousiast, and are searching for a game with up to date graphical design and playability, this is what you are looking for. From being deployed as a simple foot soldier, an artillery operator, tank crewman or a pilot, the options are limitless.
You are placed in an open, free roamable world with an immersive campaign, but can also enter the so called "editor" sandbox mode where you can design complex missions that can be later played by yourself, together with your friends or shared with the community.
The game includes massive open world multiplayer, with its playstyle completely relying on the missions that the server utilises, including missions uploaded by the community itself.
The game did initially have some performance issues and similar drawbacks, including the lack of units, but the problems have been solved since the game left its alpha stage. There are still issues remaining, but that is due the scale of the landscape the game utilises and the number of different units. Luckily, the game is updated regularly and the developers are active at assisting their fellow players.
Since the game can be modded freely like its predecessors, it has nearly no boundaries in the ways it can be played and therefore has a bright and long future infront of it.
Looking for an experience, soldier?
- Highly Recommended for mature audiences and military enthousiasts
- Graphical design and sound 8/10 (can vary due to the likelyhood of utilising mods)
- Amount of ingame content 9/10  (can vary due to the likelyhood of utilising mods)
- Playability, AI quality 8/10 (can vary due to the likelyhood of utilising mods)
- Replayability 10/10
Personal final score 8.7/10

Arma 3 is an awesome game in my opinion. It caters to people who are interested in the miltary, tactical thinking, and simulators. It is much more than a fps game, it takes tactics, restraint, communication, being careful, and being calm. It has a hard learning curve to become an effective soldier, but thats the best part. The heli was shot down by enemy aa in a matter of seconds. next we took a jeep for some reason which was shot by a tank and blew up. We then were shot off quad bikes. Then crashed another heli. Finally we reached the combat area. Then we were hacked. Our heads were replaced with street cones or burlap bags. Then the hacker shut down the server. This did no matter because I was with the funniest and nicest people. We made jokes and laughed. It was just a great time.
I have made countless other memories like getting a colleteral with a sniper rifle, shooting 20 people in the matter of 5 minutes, and huddling in a 10mx10m chapel with 20 men hiding from an attack helicopter. Although people say Arma is boring and uneventful, if you have a decent amount of patcience, you will be rewarded with a great playing experience.

I don't know what to say about this game but heres a pancake recipe!
Ingredients:
100g plain flour
2 eggs
300ml semi-skimmed milk
1 tbsp sunflower oil or vegetable, plus extra for frying
pinch salt
Method:
1: Blending in the flour: Put the flour and a pinch of salt into a large mixing bowl and make a well in the centre. Crack the eggs into the middle, then pour in about 50ml milk and 1 tbsp oil. Start whisking from the centre, gradually drawing the flour into the eggs, milk and oil. Once all the flour is incorporated, beat until you have a smooth, thick paste. Add a little more milk if it is too stiff to beat.
2: Finishing the batter: Add a good splash of milk and whisk to loosen the thick batter. While still whisking, pour in a steady stream of the remaining milk. Continue pouring and whisking until you have a batter that is the consistency of slightly thick single cream. Traditionally, people would say to now leave the batter for 30 mins, to allow the starch in the flour to swell, but there’s no need.
3: Getting the right thickness: Heat the pan over a moderate heat, then wipe it with oiled kitchen paper. Ladle some batter into the pan, tilting the pan to move the mixture around for a thin and even layer. Quickly pour any excess batter into a jug, return the pan to the heat, then leave to cook, undisturbed, for about 30 secs. Pour the excess batter from the jug back into the mixing bowl. If the pan is the right temperature, the pancake should turn golden underneath after about 30 secs and will be ready to turn.
4: Flipping pancakes: Hold the pan handle, ease a fish slice under the pancake, then quickly lift and flip it over. Make sure the pancake is lying flat against base of the pan with no folds, then cook for another 30 secs before turning out onto a warm plate. Continue with the rest of the batter, serving them as you cook or stack onto a plate. You can freeze the pancakes for 1 month, wrapped in cling film or make them up to a day ahead.

No matter what FPS game you play, you can thank Team Fortress for making it possible. The original Team Fortress was a free mod for Quake 1 that came out in 1996, and it forever changed FPS games. TF was the first game that really focused on class based team play. So many games follow that model now. Team Fortress 2 is not quite the same game as its 1996 incarnation. The game no longer has grenades, it has a slower pace, and at a competitive level, it actually requires teamwork to win. Team Fortress 2 has been out for over 10 years now and it is only growing in popularity. The competitive community is getting bigger, and it shows no signs of slowing down. If you are looking for a fun FPS with lasting appeal, Team Fortress 2 is for you.

No matter what FPS game you play, you can thank Team Fortress for making it possible. The original Team Fortress was a free mod for Quake 1 that came out in 1996, and it forever changed FPS games. TF was the first game that really focused on class based team play. So many games follow that model now. Team Fortress 2 is not quite the same game as its 1996 incarnation. The game no longer has grenades, it has a slower pace, and at a competitive level, it actually requires teamwork to win. Team Fortress 2 has been out for over 10 years now and it is only growing in popularity. The competitive community is getting bigger, and it shows no signs of slowing down. If you are looking for a fun FPS with lasting appeal, Team Fortress 2 is for you.

I'll start off saying that a friend of mine gifted this game to me (thanks man, you know who you are). And now, on to the review!
The game is pretty damn fun, no questions asked. It's basically the Hunger games on steroids. Over 100 people per match, you get guns, there is deadly gas trying to end your life, and you're slowly forced into the fray with everyone else. It's pure PVP, and you can join matches with up to 5 people coop, OR try to fly solo in an everyone vs everyone setting.
The graphics are decent, there's a slightly confusing crafting system that takes bit to learn, and a H U G E map to play on. Overall, I really love this game. It's normally 19.99, and I would gladly pay that for a game with this much content. If you like PVP, you will love this game.
That said, there are a few things I did dislike. The bullet drop is too much, imo. It takes a lot of practice to be able to even hit anything when shooting--it's worse than Battlefield 1 as far as that goes! It was expected in a game like Battlefield though. Here, I was not expecting it, so it took several games for me to be able to even damage anyone.
I think some of the weapons need balanced as well. I've seen revolvers just beast someone, meanwhile 3 shotgun blasts and they still lived.
No survival: This can be taken good or bad. You don't need food, water, and you really don't even NEED to craft, but the option is there for you. When I first got it, I was expecting to have to do those basic survival needs. Is this a good thing or a bad thing? Well, that depends on what you're looking for.
One map: A game like this really needs more variety. There is only one map right now, and I really hope the developers add a few more, that way we can switch things up a bit.
Aside from the above, this game is awesome. I don't see why it gets negative reviews. Also ignore people that say it is dead, I *never* have a problem getting qued up pretty quickly. It never takes me any more than a few minutes to get into a  match. There are a lot of players out there! I enjoy this game a lot, and will be putting many more hours into it!

I'll start off saying that a friend of mine gifted this game to me (thanks man, you know who you are). And now, on to the review!
The game is pretty damn fun, no questions asked. It's basically the Hunger games on steroids. Over 100 people per match, you get guns, there is deadly gas trying to end your life, and you're slowly forced into the fray with everyone else. It's pure PVP, and you can join matches with up to 5 people coop, OR try to fly solo in an everyone vs everyone setting.
The graphics are decent, there's a slightly confusing crafting system that takes bit to learn, and a H U G E map to play on. Overall, I really love this game. It's normally 19.99, and I would gladly pay that for a game with this much content. If you like PVP, you will love this game.
That said, there are a few things I did dislike. The bullet drop is too much, imo. It takes a lot of practice to be able to even hit anything when shooting--it's worse than Battlefield 1 as far as that goes! It was expected in a game like Battlefield though. Here, I was not expecting it, so it took several games for me to be able to even damage anyone.
I think some of the weapons need balanced as well. I've seen revolvers just beast someone, meanwhile 3 shotgun blasts and they still lived.
No survival: This can be taken good or bad. You don't need food, water, and you really don't even NEED to craft, but the option is there for you. When I first got it, I was expecting to have to do those basic survival needs. Is this a good thing or a bad thing? Well, that depends on what you're looking for.
One map: A game like this really needs more variety. There is only one map right now, and I really hope the developers add a few more, that way we can switch things up a bit.
Aside from the above, this game is awesome. I don't see why it gets negative reviews. Also ignore people that say it is dead, I *never* have a problem getting qued up pretty quickly. It never takes me any more than a few minutes to get into a  match. There are a lot of players out there! I enjoy this game a lot, and will be putting many more hours into it!

With the right mods and people, this is about as close as you want to get to actual combat [at least for the ground warfare]
Arma's best feature is the dedicated modding community, you can find a mod for just about anything for Arma. the game simulates fatigue, breathing and pain effect, as well as weapon weight, meaning that there won't be anybody out shooting a sub machine gun with a long rifle after being shot in the chest at near point blank range. There is a pretty good balistic simulation for vanilla arma but you can find mods for very realistic ballistics. I love pretty much everything about Arma except these two things, of course, nothing is perfect. The game requires a pretty powerful computer setup to run effectively, even with my Nvidia 770 graphics card, larger battles decrease frames quite a bit. And finally, Arma's controls can be rather clunky at times, the stance/lean controls specificly. It can be a problem at close range where a real human could move much faster.
Overall- 9.5/10  definetly worth the price if you can run it and enjoy Teamwork and tactical combat.

- Most wide maps of any shooting game that I have played.

- Modding community is really good
- Powerful map editor and scripting language
Cons:
- Really badly implemented multi-threading resulting in horrible performance
- Inconsistent and buggy scripting language with many flaws.
- Netcode is still not very stable
- Game and mods require approximately 100GB hard disk space
- Modding community is scattered, so compability is a issue
- Arma with many mods is generally hugely instable that there is saying "arma happened" when you crash or die for unknown reason
- Game is only 32-bit so it will use your PAGEFILE AS RAM EXTENSION !
- Game can only use 25% of CPU or GPU, because the mainthread is full of bottlenecs crippeling the performance
This game makes me feel very controversial as I love the game and the concept of the game, but the game engine is based on technology from 19th century, thus making the game unplayable.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

No matter how many times someone recommends this game, don't listen to them. I can't recommend this game to even my biggest enemy, now. Since the game is free, you may think it's easy to pick up and play, but you'd be wrong on so many levels. TF2 doesn't teach you any mechanics besides: Walking, jumping, shooting, using a melee weapon, and capturing a point. Not the more complex features like, for instance, ROCKET JUMPING! You have to look up on Youtube or the TF2 Wiki when to fire, jump, and what buttons to press. Airblasting is also barely touched upon. You can blast nearly every projectile in the game with a quick press of the mouse 2 button, yet Valve chose to give it the rocket jumping treatment of, leaving it to experience. Then, you have free-to-plays, the bad kind. They most likely just installed or recently installed TF2, but know little about it. This results in them ruining fun for eveyone. Like killing friendly players, crashing experiments into to dusty ground and sometimes, helping the enemy. But even worse, the community just casts you out of the game like you don't exist if you're new to the game. Some veterans of TF2 simply use all of their time to make fun of new players of all variaty, with very few trying to teach them. And I don't even want to *think* about balancing issues. Though optional team swap to go to the team with less players is there, it offers no reward, making barely anyone swap sides. After that, you get thrown into a server where you're on the team with three snipers who have no idea what they're doing, an AFK veteran with 2,500 hours in the game, and are just about to lose. Then, you get a kid who thinks he's funny by glitching thru the wall and setting up a sentry gun to kill everyone who passes by.
Hackers...EVERYWHERE...Moving on.
Unless the next update restores TF2 to it's glory like everyone says it had, don't poke the game with a pole of any size.

Team Fortress 2 is an excellent game that, while may have aged in ways that are undeniably avoidable, still manages to hold up and be a ton of fun. I myself have only started playing about half a year ago (as much as I hate to say it), and while I've had some trouble with things like autobalance, fair matchmaking, and time to get into a match (we have Meet Your Match to thank for that), the things that this game has kept people coming back to play is quite a feat in my opinion. With charming characters, fun gameplay, and the wonderous E key, Team Fortress 2, even by itself without the community working on it as well, is a game well worth some 2,000 hours of time (I get it. At this point I have around 96 hours. Leave me be). But, while the game by itself is quite nice, with the community working on it as well, and with consistent ideas and dedication, Team Fortress 2, in a way, becomes even better, with community-created maps that, sometimes, are even better than Valve's maps (no hate on Valve, the maps that they have made are truly amazing and great fun to play on, but come on. Don't tell me you haven't seen some creative maps and ideas. Props to whoever came up with convoy). All in all, Team Fortress 2 may be old and have shown its age quite a bit, but it is, by no means, dead whatsoever. With a dedicated community and some really good gameplay, this is a game that is quite fun to pick up, and is almost profitable when mastering. That is, if your willing to put in thousands of hours, but that's for people who've been playing since the Orange Box. Oh, and on your first time through, just be sure to expect some complaints, since the community has had problems with the new players. Probably not too much of a problem, but it can get downright obnoxious at times.

Team Fortress 2. Look, I'm not gonna write an actual review of this game. I'm a bit crap at that. But I can tell you what I liked.
1. The madness.
Team Fortress 2 is not a game you go into expecting teamwork. That you can find in organized groups and "competitive" play. Most of my enjoyment comes from being suprised by the oddness that pubs can spawn. Emote spaming demos, engineers who build right outside of the spawn, etc. Even when I think I've seen it all, something will show up that makes me go "Just... what?". It never ceases to amuse. This can be an issue for some people, as they get cranky that those people aren't "Playing the game", but in the end, who can decide what that even means?
2. The characters.
I own Overwatch, and play it about the same amount of time as this game. I love those characters, and their stories, and interactions. But in the end, I find TF2's more memorable. Not to say Overwatch's are bad or anything, but the smaller roster and more cartoony nature lend themselves well to fun interactions.
3. The feeling
Playing TF2 is a profound experience. It's relaxing in a way no other game can be. No matter how angry I am, TF2 can make me laugh. It's just that... joyful for me.
TL;DR : Team Fortress is a fun game. Play it. You'll probably like it.

No matter how many times someone recommends this game, don't listen to them. I can't recommend this game to even my biggest enemy, now. Since the game is free, you may think it's easy to pick up and play, but you'd be wrong on so many levels. TF2 doesn't teach you any mechanics besides: Walking, jumping, shooting, using a melee weapon, and capturing a point. Not the more complex features like, for instance, ROCKET JUMPING! You have to look up on Youtube or the TF2 Wiki when to fire, jump, and what buttons to press. Airblasting is also barely touched upon. You can blast nearly every projectile in the game with a quick press of the mouse 2 button, yet Valve chose to give it the rocket jumping treatment of, leaving it to experience. Then, you have free-to-plays, the bad kind. They most likely just installed or recently installed TF2, but know little about it. This results in them ruining fun for eveyone. Like killing friendly players, crashing experiments into to dusty ground and sometimes, helping the enemy. But even worse, the community just casts you out of the game like you don't exist if you're new to the game. Some veterans of TF2 simply use all of their time to make fun of new players of all variaty, with very few trying to teach them. And I don't even want to *think* about balancing issues. Though optional team swap to go to the team with less players is there, it offers no reward, making barely anyone swap sides. After that, you get thrown into a server where you're on the team with three snipers who have no idea what they're doing, an AFK veteran with 2,500 hours in the game, and are just about to lose. Then, you get a kid who thinks he's funny by glitching thru the wall and setting up a sentry gun to kill everyone who passes by.
Hackers...EVERYWHERE...Moving on.
Unless the next update restores TF2 to it's glory like everyone says it had, don't poke the game with a pole of any size.

TL;DR:
Hello, dear, let me guess... Arma2/DayZ-mod fan?
As of now, I have 833 hrs on record playing Arma 2: OA (primarily DayZ-mod and derivations).
At the beginning of this review I'd like to write down my expectations before rating this
game
Many of you know (if you don't, it might actually be a good thing), ArmA 2, especially talking about the DayZ mod, had more bugs than the whole african tropical rainforest. Most of the bugs were depressing, but some were really funny and those became true insider jokes among my mates.
Back to the "not-so-funny-bugs" and the laggy game engine which only could effectively use 1 CPU core (-> 70FPS at most on a 2011 mid/high-end PC). Those were the reasons I bought Arma 3. I wanted a better game, which has better graphics, less bugs and most important: higher FPS.
1) Arma 3 has better graphics (what else would you expect?)
2 and 3) Bohemia Interactive did a great job on their part, applause. /sarcasm off: (surprisingly) Arma 3
. Thanks, now I have even LESS FPS than in Arma 2. The average FPS for me is 15-30 and there's
to increase the FPS. Firstly, because the CPU is the limiting factor (game uses max. 1.5 cores of total 4), so lowering the graphics settings doesn't change much.
Secondly, RAM is still an issue. We now live in the 64-bit era. In case you didn't know, 64-bit applications not only can use more RAM (theoretically more than 4GB, on Windows more than 2GB) but also perform a little better (5-20%). As you guessed, Arma 3 is still running 32-bit only. This mainly results in heavy lags on my machine (same applies to Arma 2, but this is an old game, why bother?). After a while, when Arma 3 uses up all of the 2GB RAM provided by Windows, The Great Lag begins. Every now and then I get this Lag Spike, giving me 2-4FPS for a second or two. The game becomes practically unplayable (everyone with a better CPU have a huge advantage over you in terms of FPS).
When Arma 3 hits the allocation limit for 32-bit applications (Win32: 2GiB), it begins (or Windows does; doesn't matter) to offload additional memory objects to the pagefile.sys file, which is on your HDD. Hard drives are muuuuuuuuuch slower than RAM and everytime the game requests memory chunks from this file, you run into the 2-4FPS lag spike as the game has to sit here and wait for the data. Pagefiles on SSDs reduce the lag spikes, but don't :csgogun:eliminate them completely, so #blameBohemia #blameArma
Now, what's about the bugs? It has got even worse probably. Vehicle damage has become
. A slightly damaged wheel? (that's what the HUD tells you). Visually still 100%, but the vehicle will crap out and drive at 70% speed, if at all.
El helicóptero with a fully broken main rotor? I DON'T CARE, STILL GOING UP IN THE AIR LIEK A GOD, ROFL-COPTER IS ON THE WAY.
Next example: Playing King of the Hill (Fun gamemode with all vehicles and weapons). You are the pilot of a transport helicopter with 10 passengers in. A rocket hits your heli and it either goes down or explodes instantly, all good so far. So, what's about a little reward for the guy who fired that rocket and killed all the people in the helicopter? NOPE, ♥♥♥♥ER! They all died because of magic/suiciding/Ebola-chan/african bees/♥♥♥♥ing cactuses. Again: We would like to politely inform you, the player who did kill all these innocent soldiers will not get any kills for that in reward.
Do you still want to pay so much for a game? Don't forget, you'll need a PC costing at least 25 times as much to play the game comfortably.

Just to start, I'd like to say this is my replacement for Battlefield, which replaced Call Of Duty.
I feel like I stumbled across one of the funnest gametypes one day when I was playing ArmA II (Not III, it hadn't come out at this point), I found a server that was hosting a gametype called "Domination" and I had bought that game for DayZ pretty much alone because I was one of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. I got sucked into Domination, its effectively a gametype where you live in a post-scarcity world and are killing a ton of insurgents in Takistan/Chernarus (Its right next to Atlantis on a Soviet era map).
Right after DayZ was hitting its peak of Popularity, ArmA 3 got a ton of news, they showed off an awesome trailer of underwater stuff and the new inventory menu and the ability to use disguises to blend in with the enemy. (That didn't make into any public build ever, but I really hope that it does at some point) This got me super hyped for ArmA 3 and then one day, out of the blue they just released an Alpha and the entire start of the Early Access program (This is one of few sucesses in that program)
Few people buy this game for its singleplayer components, or hardly ever learn how to use the entire game to its full potential, but when you learn how, this game really shows the spirit of teamwork and co-operation. For example: when you are in A-164 Wipeout and your buddies on the ground are getting nailed by an Opfor Fire Team and one of them has a Laser Designator, they can lase the infantry and you can drop a GBU on them while the US National Anthem plays out and feel like a ♥♥♥♥ing badass, but you don't know why. I think I know why, its like the 101% concentrated super-dense hyper-realised version of teamwork, I know I'm using hyperbole to the n-Th degree, but hoooly♥♥♥♥♥♥when everyone on the team can compliment you (This acutally happens a lot in Domination, in my experience at least) for doing, good efficient work for the team, while being a cool buy and everyone on the team can compliment each other for doing badass♥♥♥♥♥♥like flying a C-130 full of actual other players and you all HALO jump out, and wipe out the AO in minutes because you're all in sync and communicating with each other, THAT is teamwork and the spirit of it. I've really only seen this in the ArmA series, in Battlefield and Call of Duty you see it but its only because its a group of friends or an established clan that are in sync together, but in ArmA; you see that with random strangers, some ex/current-military, some 11 year old squeakers thinking they are the coolest, all working together becuase of that strange force.
Anyway, thats my pitch for you to try out ArmA III, or II. Hopefully my excessive run-on sentances don't stop you from getting the jist of my review.

Team Fortress 2 is an excellent game that, while may have aged in ways that are undeniably avoidable, still manages to hold up and be a ton of fun. I myself have only started playing about half a year ago (as much as I hate to say it), and while I've had some trouble with things like autobalance, fair matchmaking, and time to get into a match (we have Meet Your Match to thank for that), the things that this game has kept people coming back to play is quite a feat in my opinion. With charming characters, fun gameplay, and the wonderous E key, Team Fortress 2, even by itself without the community working on it as well, is a game well worth some 2,000 hours of time (I get it. At this point I have around 96 hours. Leave me be). But, while the game by itself is quite nice, with the community working on it as well, and with consistent ideas and dedication, Team Fortress 2, in a way, becomes even better, with community-created maps that, sometimes, are even better than Valve's maps (no hate on Valve, the maps that they have made are truly amazing and great fun to play on, but come on. Don't tell me you haven't seen some creative maps and ideas. Props to whoever came up with convoy). All in all, Team Fortress 2 may be old and have shown its age quite a bit, but it is, by no means, dead whatsoever. With a dedicated community and some really good gameplay, this is a game that is quite fun to pick up, and is almost profitable when mastering. That is, if your willing to put in thousands of hours, but that's for people who've been playing since the Orange Box. Oh, and on your first time through, just be sure to expect some complaints, since the community has had problems with the new players. Probably not too much of a problem, but it can get downright obnoxious at times.

It's difficult to compare Arma to another game since it's so unique. The gameplay is not your typical shooter as it incorporates strategic elements and doesn't play like a traditional FPS. Console gamers will have no issues with this game's controls even as their first shooter on a PC.
Arma has a slight learning curve, it may be a little confusing at first until you learn how things work and learn to take cover. Arma has a lot of little details to gameplay that you can improve upon to give yourself and edge such as the stance adjustment controls. But they aren't vital for successful gameplay. Arma is only as complex as you want it to be. Even though it is a simulation game, it feels much more natural to play than other simulations.
Singleplayer - The story is actually pretty good, some of the scenarios definitely have a challenging OP:Flashpoint feel to it which I'm a fan of. It's divided into 3 episodes with their own chapters, each episode giving a new perspective to the conflict and upping the scales of battle. There's also a Bootcamp mini-campaign which will help new players a lot.
Multiplayer and Community - Arma is a great game to play alone, it's even better together. There's lots of public servers with a variety of gamemodes that you can just jump into. Lots of awesome custom scenarios too such as the Co-Op scenario Invade and Annex, as well as the PvP scenarios such as KoTH and Wasteland. But the best experience is playing with an organized group. There are casual co-op groups, PvP clans as well as hardcore roleplaying "milsim units". You can feel around for what's right for you.
Editor - Arma has always had a very powerful Mission Editor tool and has open support for custom scripts. This alone is all we needed to make missions. Then BI gave us Zeus - an in-game editor, look up some videos - this alone will entertain you for hours by yourself. Now BI has also promised a 3D Mission Editor to cover even finer details.
Mods - The game is advertised as a military simulator and it does a great job of that just as-is. But really it's whatever you want it to be and you can deepen the simulation aspects with user content. The community is actively pumping out amazing mods for this game and BI has always been highly supportive of community content (even to the point of cash giveaways from the Make Arma Not War competition). If you can think of something cool to add to Arma, it's probably already got a download link.
Criticism - Although the game engine gets some flak for being "unoptimized" (BI has been improving on the game's performance significantly) when you think about it, how many game engines have this kind of attention to detail in such a wide scope of gameplay? You can be infantry (even fight underwater with certain assault rifles), skydive/HALO jump, pilot a transport chopper, fly a jet, drive a tank, use artillery, anything. Not to mention the detail of the environment even to the starmap. What other game can you think of tracks the temperature the ground depending on time of day and when last it rained therefore affecting your thermal optics? Yea, thought so.
DLC - Arma 3's DLC is optional, and you can just get modded content which are not affected. Even if you don't buy the DLCs you'll get the improvements to the game and still be able to play with anyone who has/doesn't have DLC. Just wanted to clear up the myths of Arma 3's DLC.
I've been playing since the Alpha/Beta with 1,000+ online hrs and I'm still not bored. Arma 3 and Arma overall as a series has come a long way and has improved tremendously and BI listens and improves from community feedback. Arma games have a long lifespan and there are a lot of people just buying it now. It's been almost 2 years since the Alpha was released, and expect Arma 3 to be active for at least another 3-5 years, probably more. Think about it, why buy a bunch of other games when Arma can be all of them for one price? Definitely the most well-spent money I've ever spent on a game for the enjoyment I've gotten so far and will continue to have. No doubt about it. I'm glad I could support such an awesome studio, keep up the great work BI.

The game portion of this game is missing.  I've literally won matches before without running into a single other player (in 5 man teams).  The beginning part of the game is frustrating - if you land near someone its a race to the first gun.  If you don't land near someone you just go hide, wait for everone else to murder each other, then move on.  The middle part of the game is boring, you either go looking for players or you bunker down while the map gets smaller, but the map is HUGE and there's usually only 50 or so people left.  The end portion of the game is rage inducing.  You can die from a single shot, there is no radar, and no hit indicator to show you where you're being shot from.  The surround sound is usually good enough to figure it out, but there's loud "THUD" sounds when you get hit that drown out the gunfire - if you are being hit by someone you don't see it is game over.
The worst part is (my opinion) there is no matchmaking system.  At all.  You can be matched with pro players, top streamers, or window lickers, regardless of which group you belong with.  You wait in queue, then wait for the match to start, then wait to parachute in, then you gather some supplies, wait to find another person, and die.  A full match can take 30+ minutes, maybe 1-2 minutes of actual play time.
All in all, save your money and go play a different shooter.

Most of these reviews are subjectively affected due to what happened to the respective people 5 minutes ago, so here is a rather neutral review.
In its current state and the way it's progressing, this game is really good. I've been playing for over a month now and I can say that developers actually look after this game, as I went from barely any hit registration to almost perfect every match - there are still problems with desync here and there, weirdly mostly in duos/fives matches, but in solo it's really good right now.
However, problems like randomly disconnecting from a game, doors being synced up (being open for one guy, closed for another) or stuff like that make the game look like it's the worst - it just blends over the good things when said problems actually occur, maybe even consecutively. It's like a girl on her period, you don't know what you will get each day, or even every 15 minutes.
From what I can see, the developers are trying to get this game somewhere, I imagine it's just rather difficult to pinpoint most bugs when there are many features missing that would make this way easier - for example, this whole hit registration/desync thing many people moan about would be rather easier to solve if the developers had some kind of server-sided demo they could correspondly review when being sent a clip of ghost bullets or whatever, so they could compare what the server is thinking happens with what the player sees.
If I was you, and I was quite unsure about this game, maybe try it out at a friend's house for a bit, try to get into it a bit, and then follow the scene. See what the developers do, and if it's getting better gradually, and most problems seem to be fixed, you can still purchase it - because this game can get you heated quickly if you let it.

It's difficult to compare Arma to another game since it's so unique. The gameplay is not your typical shooter as it incorporates strategic elements and doesn't play like a traditional FPS. Console gamers will have no issues with this game's controls even as their first shooter on a PC.
Arma has a slight learning curve, it may be a little confusing at first until you learn how things work and learn to take cover. Arma has a lot of little details to gameplay that you can improve upon to give yourself and edge such as the stance adjustment controls. But they aren't vital for successful gameplay. Arma is only as complex as you want it to be. Even though it is a simulation game, it feels much more natural to play than other simulations.
Singleplayer - The story is actually pretty good, some of the scenarios definitely have a challenging OP:Flashpoint feel to it which I'm a fan of. It's divided into 3 episodes with their own chapters, each episode giving a new perspective to the conflict and upping the scales of battle. There's also a Bootcamp mini-campaign which will help new players a lot.
Multiplayer and Community - Arma is a great game to play alone, it's even better together. There's lots of public servers with a variety of gamemodes that you can just jump into. Lots of awesome custom scenarios too such as the Co-Op scenario Invade and Annex, as well as the PvP scenarios such as KoTH and Wasteland. But the best experience is playing with an organized group. There are casual co-op groups, PvP clans as well as hardcore roleplaying "milsim units". You can feel around for what's right for you.
Editor - Arma has always had a very powerful Mission Editor tool and has open support for custom scripts. This alone is all we needed to make missions. Then BI gave us Zeus - an in-game editor, look up some videos - this alone will entertain you for hours by yourself. Now BI has also promised a 3D Mission Editor to cover even finer details.
Mods - The game is advertised as a military simulator and it does a great job of that just as-is. But really it's whatever you want it to be and you can deepen the simulation aspects with user content. The community is actively pumping out amazing mods for this game and BI has always been highly supportive of community content (even to the point of cash giveaways from the Make Arma Not War competition). If you can think of something cool to add to Arma, it's probably already got a download link.
Criticism - Although the game engine gets some flak for being "unoptimized" (BI has been improving on the game's performance significantly) when you think about it, how many game engines have this kind of attention to detail in such a wide scope of gameplay? You can be infantry (even fight underwater with certain assault rifles), skydive/HALO jump, pilot a transport chopper, fly a jet, drive a tank, use artillery, anything. Not to mention the detail of the environment even to the starmap. What other game can you think of tracks the temperature the ground depending on time of day and when last it rained therefore affecting your thermal optics? Yea, thought so.
DLC - Arma 3's DLC is optional, and you can just get modded content which are not affected. Even if you don't buy the DLCs you'll get the improvements to the game and still be able to play with anyone who has/doesn't have DLC. Just wanted to clear up the myths of Arma 3's DLC.
I've been playing since the Alpha/Beta with 1,000+ online hrs and I'm still not bored. Arma 3 and Arma overall as a series has come a long way and has improved tremendously and BI listens and improves from community feedback. Arma games have a long lifespan and there are a lot of people just buying it now. It's been almost 2 years since the Alpha was released, and expect Arma 3 to be active for at least another 3-5 years, probably more. Think about it, why buy a bunch of other games when Arma can be all of them for one price? Definitely the most well-spent money I've ever spent on a game for the enjoyment I've gotten so far and will continue to have. No doubt about it. I'm glad I could support such an awesome studio, keep up the great work BI.

Arma 3 is the sequel to the successful arma series. We cannot simply define Arma as a simple FPS game; it's more than a military simulator. Everything in the game is build to mirror their real life counterpart to the most extent from recoil, sound, bullet physics,.. You are a "real" soldiers on an actual battlefield in which the weight you carry will affect your movement and aiming. You will not be able to sprint infinitely and have laser beam like accuracy like in COD or battelfield. The fatigue system however is a little it overwhelm in the vanilla game but can be fix with mod. In the single player campaign, you play as a normal soldiers involved in an actual conflict, not a superhero that save the world from nuclear crisis. The campaign definitely lacking a proper story and your decision does not influence the ending that much. Vehicles in this game are the absolute beast in this game unlike Battlefield. However, you will not a have a health pool or get repaired with a blowtorch like in battlefield. If the enemy punch through your armor and damage your crew, you're done. Since the landscape in this game is gigantic and so many things have to be render out, you computer will take a hit on frame-rate unless you have a $2000 rig. The editor and mods will fill in the end game content. This game offer a great replaylability and you will see people still play this game after 5-6 years from now. Only buy the game if you enjoy a good military sim, it has a big learning curve but you will enjoy it if you take times to explore the game.

We were a group of 3 soldiers stranded in a city in the middle of nowhere, with only sidearms to protect ourselves.
9mm's in our hands which compared to the firepower of our enemy, it would make them have good laughs.
Our top priority was scavanging for supplies and guns.
We found an old SUV parked in the middle of a town hall, with apparent damaged transmission and busted wheel. I procede to repair the SUV, while our squad's sniper and combat medic scout for any enemy infantry or vehicles. I was a professional engineer with 10 years of duty repairing stuff no one cares about until they are broken. After the repairing took place with no problems, we look to the trunk of the SUV.
Boy, it was like looking at the Lord.
Two assault rifles accompanied by their respective ammo. Now we were loaded, and looking at our next mission.
We saw a convoy 2 clicks away from our position. We took this as a chance to gear up and scavenge food and water while fighting the enemy at the same time. While en route to our ambush location we found a military truck with a big anti-tank weapon sitting of top of it. It was the perfect setting, except the engine didn't work. We had to toe it to our SUV. Even with all my experience I couldn't put the engine up and running, but the gun worked.
We set up at the ambush point waiting for the enemy.
But while waiting we saw a big white vehicle in the mountain north coming toward us, which was being towed.
"Is that a god damn boat sailing on land on the back on a truck!?" - said our sniper.
It had miniguns attached to it, and the instance we saw them, we proceded to open fire with our anti-tank weapon.
It was a tough fight.
They shot back as soon as they heard our shots and fought the best way they could. But our weaponry was too strong for them. The truck catched fire and exploded after a couple rounds into it, killing all the enemies in the vicinity. It looked like a scene from a Michael Bay film.
After that, we ambushed the convoy, stole a couple of anti-tank RPG's and sold them into the black market to buy a tank.
10/10

Spending enough time in this game to fully appreciate the good and the bad, I have decided to put some words down.  I love this game more than any other game that comes to mind.
Where do I start?  I'll start with the hard stuff.
You will stuggle with this game.  You will have moments where you hate the way it's coded.  You will die to stupid things, like stairs or rocks.  You will hate the fatigue system and the weapon sway. You will get annoyed at the reskins for outfits.
Eventually, you will mod it.
This is not a simple run and gun game.  You will not find yourself 'no scoping' after sprinting for 2 kliks.  Arma 3 is a simulator first and a game second.  The groundwork is solid for the most part.  The modding community is devoted.  The game modes are varied.  There is something that almost everyone will find appealing inside this package.
Halo jumping dressed like the UK Special Forces? Check.  Thank a modder.
Driving a hatchback that's colored like the American flag? Check. Thank a modder.
Want to build a mission around the Tet Offensive? Check. Thank a modder.
Am I biased? Yes. Do I have a huge amount of respect for modders? Yes.
Arma 3 is a cpu intensive game.  You will have to tweek the hell out of it to make it just right.  You aren't going to get 60 fps on poorly coded MP servers. Please don't think it's your hardware, it's not.  Well, probably not.
But this game really shines in the graphic department once she's setup just right.  I'm constantly trying to squeeze as much performance as possible, but I'm not going to go over everything I've done, it would take too long.  If you google it, you will find it.
Playing the game by yourself is hindering your fun to an extent I can't even explain.  Ok, since you asked so nicely, I'll try.
Playing to campaign alone left me yearning for more.  I really disliked the interface when assigning targets, or handing out orders to the AI squadmates I had been shackled with.  It doesn't feel very fluid, nor does it give me the feeling of teamwork.  The AI, at times, can go 'full retard' and just stand there while being mowed down by the enemy forces.  You may order them to get into the truck you're sitting in, only to find one of them has the great idea to run right into the AO and alert everyone to your presence.  Ok, I guess stealth is off the table.  At least I have superior numbers?  Ha, they won't get out of the truck and that rpg is headed this way.  I'll just reload my save then.
Now, replay that with real people that communicate and know how to play.  Completely different outcome.  I'm not typing that hypothetical situation out again, just trust me.
Now, onto the really fun part.  That part that makes my genitals tingle.
The Mods.
OMG Becky, look at those mods.  They're so big!
No, they aren't all large downloads.  Even some of the smallest mods can change the game to a large extent.
Take AGM for example.  It has different frag throwing options. A medical system that includes epi's, blood bags, adrenaline and the ability to drag people to safety.  No longer can you see how many rounds are left in your mag, you can only 'see' the weight.  It has weapon resting, fast roping, cook offs, vehicle repair options and a bunch of other things I can't think off.

ArmA 3. A 'tacticool' shooter. Sorry, that was terrible.
ArmA 3 is an apparent military simulator. I'd personally call it a casual simulator, considering the bugs (the engine is riddled with them, but the devs are active on fixing bugs and creating new ones in the process).
There are issues such as:
- The movement system (transitions can be jarring- a sprint can becoming a walk just because the terrain is *slightly* steeper, which has got me killed more than a few times in the past, though it can be solved by running in weird ways up hills)
- Over zealous stamina system (60lb of equipment will drain your stamina whilst jogging in a few minutes, 10lb will do so in a few seconds later) and issues like that. The guys I play with tend to disable it, and for good reason.
- 'Futuristic' theme through the use of various real world vehicles and weapons - no AKs, M4/16s and countless other classic weapons we all know and love. Sucks, in my opinion.
- Really dumb ai. Some improvements over the ArmA 2 ai - ai reacts faster and better, but can react a little... Overzealous. A single soldier in a good position can lock up squads by taking random shots, preventing them from being ordered around (units love to crawl when under fire), requiring a lot of micromanaging as a squad leader - if you're playing as Zeus or using High Command  for squads, good luck.
There are many others, but I can't think of them at the moment. But, now for some good news.
You can install mods, fixing a large number of gameplay related issues. Sadly the first issue with the movement system can't be fixed (or hasn't, at least), but the stamina system has been fixed by a number of mods to be somewhat more realistic and more managable.
Mods such as RHS: Escalation (the US forces and Russian Armed Forces parts) plus the HLC packs solve the lack of modern weapons - the two mods / packs are my faviourites for this sort of thing.
Various realism mods around such as AGM and CSE also help improve the realism of the game.
DLC is also free with the game, sort of. Similar to what they did in ArmA 2, you get the content but with some restrictions - so you can play with people who have it, though you may not be able do access all the features, and there may be some annoying notifications. ;p

Spending enough time in this game to fully appreciate the good and the bad, I have decided to put some words down.  I love this game more than any other game that comes to mind.
Where do I start?  I'll start with the hard stuff.
You will stuggle with this game.  You will have moments where you hate the way it's coded.  You will die to stupid things, like stairs or rocks.  You will hate the fatigue system and the weapon sway. You will get annoyed at the reskins for outfits.
Eventually, you will mod it.
This is not a simple run and gun game.  You will not find yourself 'no scoping' after sprinting for 2 kliks.  Arma 3 is a simulator first and a game second.  The groundwork is solid for the most part.  The modding community is devoted.  The game modes are varied.  There is something that almost everyone will find appealing inside this package.
Halo jumping dressed like the UK Special Forces? Check.  Thank a modder.
Driving a hatchback that's colored like the American flag? Check. Thank a modder.
Want to build a mission around the Tet Offensive? Check. Thank a modder.
Am I biased? Yes. Do I have a huge amount of respect for modders? Yes.
Arma 3 is a cpu intensive game.  You will have to tweek the hell out of it to make it just right.  You aren't going to get 60 fps on poorly coded MP servers. Please don't think it's your hardware, it's not.  Well, probably not.
But this game really shines in the graphic department once she's setup just right.  I'm constantly trying to squeeze as much performance as possible, but I'm not going to go over everything I've done, it would take too long.  If you google it, you will find it.
Playing the game by yourself is hindering your fun to an extent I can't even explain.  Ok, since you asked so nicely, I'll try.
Playing to campaign alone left me yearning for more.  I really disliked the interface when assigning targets, or handing out orders to the AI squadmates I had been shackled with.  It doesn't feel very fluid, nor does it give me the feeling of teamwork.  The AI, at times, can go 'full retard' and just stand there while being mowed down by the enemy forces.  You may order them to get into the truck you're sitting in, only to find one of them has the great idea to run right into the AO and alert everyone to your presence.  Ok, I guess stealth is off the table.  At least I have superior numbers?  Ha, they won't get out of the truck and that rpg is headed this way.  I'll just reload my save then.
Now, replay that with real people that communicate and know how to play.  Completely different outcome.  I'm not typing that hypothetical situation out again, just trust me.
Now, onto the really fun part.  That part that makes my genitals tingle.
The Mods.
OMG Becky, look at those mods.  They're so big!
No, they aren't all large downloads.  Even some of the smallest mods can change the game to a large extent.
Take AGM for example.  It has different frag throwing options. A medical system that includes epi's, blood bags, adrenaline and the ability to drag people to safety.  No longer can you see how many rounds are left in your mag, you can only 'see' the weight.  It has weapon resting, fast roping, cook offs, vehicle repair options and a bunch of other things I can't think off.
What about vehicles?  I really like the hummvees from Arma 2.  There are a few different options for mods for that.
Do you hate that you stop moving when you switch weapons?  There's a mod for that.
Tactical glasses have no use in the game? There's a mod that gives you a hud when wearing the glasses in first person.
I hate the stock sounds. JSRS3 baby!
Want a Canadian mohawk?  Reskin mod.
Tired of playing Altis or Stratis?  Bornholm, Tilos, Chernobyl, Chernarus, Utes, Panthera. Just to name a few of the many user made maps available with a few clicks.
Be warned.
Mods don't always work 'right out of the box™'.  If you don't have patience, you're just going to have a bad time.  Sometimes mods don't work well with each other, or give you graphical errors, or aren't compatible with user made missons.  In short, when they work, oh baby do they. When they don't, you deal with it or stop using them.
Look, I'm biased.  I really am.  I love the milsim aspect of this game.  I love the squad play.  I love the vehicles and the guns. I love the guys I play with.
They say that the best things in life are the things you have to work for.  That's what Arma 3 is.
You have to work for it.  But it really shines in the long run.

Hey Guys,
H1Z1: KotK got many good things, but for the reason that it's still in Early Access there are some bugs and relatively low content. BUT for me that game makes a lot of fun. It's very hard to learn the aiming because of Bullet Drop and Bullet Flying times. So you should have some FPS skills, if you want to play that game. Pros:
+ Good to very good graphics
+ Many Players
+ A lot of fun to play
+ Easy to learn, hard to master
+ Very competitive
+ Simple HUD and Menu
+ Events some times ( I never joined one )
+ Big Map
+ Cars are fun :D
Cons:
- Still many Bugs (like hovering Loot)
- Laggy Servers (especially on EU, where I play)
- Long Queue times
- only one map (and only one Game mode so far)
- very expensive for relatively low content
- I have experienced Micro Freezes (more like big freezes with >10 secs freezetime)
- high recommondations for good graphic and performance
- Performance not that great
Conclution:
H1Z1 makes a lot of fun (once again). I really like to play it and if you played like CS GO before, you will enjoy it, especially if you play with one or more Friends. You should give it a try, if you like competetive FPS's, but you should buy it, when it's off ;)

Never Forget The Alamo
The Battle of the Alamo (February 23 – March 6, 1836) was a pivotal event in the Texas Revolution. Following a 13-day siege, Mexican troops under President General Antonio López de Santa Anna launched an assault on the Alamo Mission near San Antonio de Béxar (modern-day San Antonio), Texas, United States, killing all of the Texian defenders. Santa Anna's cruelty during the battle inspired many Texians—both Texas settlers and adventurers from the United States—to join the Texian Army. Buoyed by a desire for revenge, the Texians defeated the Mexican Army at the Battle of San Jacinto, on April 21, 1836, ending the revolution.
Several months previously, Texians had driven all Mexican troops out of Mexican Texas. About 100 Texians were then garrisoned at the Alamo. The Texian force grew slightly with the arrival of reinforcements led by eventual Alamo co-commanders James Bowie and William B. Travis. On February 23, approximately 1,500 Mexicans marched into San Antonio de Béxar as the first step in a campaign to retake Texas. For the next 10 days, the two armies engaged in several skirmishes with minimal casualties. Aware that his garrison could not withstand an attack by such a large force, Travis wrote multiple letters pleading for more men and supplies, but the Texians were reinforced by fewer than 100 men.

Not recommended, even for people who like a good military simulation game.
Good:
- Lots of potential for realism and immersion
- Massive variety of ways to interact with game elements
Bad:
- Lack of variety in terms of gear (three colours don't make three different items)
- Lack of any real weapons: it's all near-future stuff
- Gunshots sound too mechanical or like movie sound effects
- Weapon animations are loose: effects don't sync up right (two gunshots when you shoot three bullets, etc.)
- Vehicles are very difficult to control without dedicated joystick/wheel
VERY Bad:
- Needlessly complicated control scheme which will take hours on hours to get used to (literally)
- To say the learning curve is steep implies that there is a learning curve
- Many functions of the game are hidden, unexplained, unintuitive, or poorly implemented
- Potential for realism is destroyed when each mission becomes a sprint between ambushes
There are several different tutorials - some in the "virtual reality", some on the islands, some as text-only, and none of which are adequate. Each tutorial is about ten-thirty seconds long and involves no actual help, assuming that because you pressed the right buttons once, you now know how to do it in combat. The team seems to have put zero effort into making the game intuitive: you will spend much of your time looking up various controls and reading about methods of interaction.
This game is not finished. If you're looking for a good, intuitive, fun military simulator to get away from the Call of Duty bullcrap, pick up Operation Flashpoint: Red River. It might not be as extensive, and it suffers from a lack of replayability, but it isn't nearly as frustrating as Arma.

I have played this game for over 3,100 hours, so definitely take my word for it when I say this game is worth buying! I've had the game for years now and I have thoroughly enjoyed it not only by myself, but also with my best friend. This game will offer hundreds and hundreds of hours of enjoyment. Below I'll detail the things they did right and wrong!
The developers of this game (Bohemia Interactive) are top-notch game developers. They know how to make a quality product. Their DLC's aren't pay $30 more for a few planes it's more practical and a heck of a lot more reasonable, especially for what you get in return. Take in account their new DLC "Arma 3 Apex" the cost is $30, in return you get a HUGE, intrinsicly designed island that the developers put thousands of hours into designed and creating. 13+ vehicles ranging from drones to planes, cars and boats. Loads of new uniforms, hats, weapons, weapon attachments, etc to go with the three new factions. All of that versus a DLC for say a Total War game, you pay $30 and you get one faction that's the exact same as the other vanilla units just retextured and renamed. With Bohemia Interactive, you don't get that. You get quality DLC for a good price, and for an excellent game.
The game itself is overwhelmingly fun to play. This isn't your average 'shooter' game, this game involves strategy, especially in multiplayer. It's not a point and shoot, it involves the mind in thinking what your next move will be before you make it, a lot like chess. Make a wrong move, and your king's dead. The multiplayer is fun, lots and lots of servers to play on, never a time when servers aren't up!
The three Islands: Altis, Stratis, and Tanoa are loads of fun to play on, each having their own uniqueness! Each Island is a completely different battlefield, requiring different strategies to survive, or win, or whatever it happens to be that you are doing. Each Island was again very well thought out and excellently designed and crafted. You will not be disappointed.
The uniforms, gear, guns, attachments, and all that good stuff is AMAZING! Unlike previous Arma games, you can now wear your own hats, and the uniforms are excellently designed and look great! The weapons have new sounds, look nice, and have great customization options. The weapon attachments system is new, now, you can attach lights, laser pointers, supressors, and a bunch of new optics and more to your guns.
Gameplay and mechanics couldn't be better. The contols are not difficult to utilise and are quite easy to learn. The missions people have made for this game are just great. There's really no other adjective that can describe it. There's so much variety so you can choose from anything! Want underwater but still above water, they have that! Or all fixed-wing missions that involve protecting ground assets, they have everything! Trust me when I say that, because they really do.
My favorite part: The workshop! The workshop is extensively crafted and has so many options to choose from. They have weapon mods, weapon attachment mods, vehicle mods (adds new vehicles made by players) gameplay mods that change how the game is played such as adding a radio to communicate with your friends via a realistic looking radio that pops up on screen. THEY EVEN HAVE DINOSAURS!
Things they did wrong:
The developers did, like any other game make some mistakes. A lot of which that have fixed, but err's still persist. None that make the game unplayable though, so thats a plus. I feel as a player of previous Arma games, there's a lot they didn't add. I get they want to get people to use the workshop and share with the community and their mods, but things like two seater jets are missing, and I really think that this is a minus being a huge fan of two seater jets. They have made an improvement of walkable buildings, MOST buildings are enterable but not all, this is kind of a let down but again it's a massive improvement compared to Arma 2. Other than that, I really cannot complain about this game.
In the end, this game has so much to offer, it's totally worth the money to buy. For what you get, it's a great price, and you will completely enjoy this game as much as I and so many others have.

My experience with TF2 started back in 2010, when i was using my first steam account.Keep in mind that this was my first fps game played and it got a lot of love, updates and that means lots of content.
I was very happy playing it with my friends at first, but than i started to understand how the game works, so i started playing it alone too, i can say that i got pretty good at sniping, rocket jumping and trick stabbing. :3
And then this happened... Someone hacked my account! I got really upset and i didn't knew what to do, i made another account but i didn't want to buy TF2 again cuz *money*. BUT GABEN WAS WITH ME! AND AFTER A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME IT GOT FTP! I WAS IN HAVEN! I started playing it immediately!
I called my friends and started playing it again.
I was watching some anime when a friend came to me and said: Hey ASimpleGamer (My first steam name) wanna play some cs:go?
And i told him: Uhm? Sure but i don't have any money right now...
No problem, i am gonna buy it for you.
Dude that's awesome! Thank you!
And so, we started playing cs:go, i was so fascinated by the game mechanics and how different it is from TF2.I pretty much got into it and i am still playing it to this day.
CS:GO made me play less and less TF2 till i got my cs:go account vac banned.So i was playing more tf2 again i got 1.000 hours on it so i thought i'll better make a new account before i get 10.000 hours or something. And so the story goes getting banned on many different accounts till i got to this one...hope it will be the last.
I quess i have about 5.000 hours in TF2, so i can kinda call myself a "veteran", and say that the game has changed, in good and bad ways. I am only gonna talk about the bad ones seens is a negative rewiew. There were some updates... *cough* Meet your Match *cough* that totally ruined it. Of course is not only the Meet your Match update, there are some more, but the idea in general is that Valve has hurried a bit with some updates and just almost abandoned it with 1 or 2 small updates per. year.The last 2-3 years were so amazangly dissapointing...Valve we don't mind waiting 1 year for an update as long as it's good and it brings lots of content.
Anyway with all that said it's still a nice game to play, but the problems just made me stop enjoying it.In it's current state i have to give it a negative review, hope i am gonna change my mind and write another positive review for this awesome game that still brings up memories.

The majority of the time spent on this game is online. However, it is almost impossible to come accross good servers with good players these days (Asia/Oceania/Europe). Servers are generally running non-vanilla gamemodes. While this can be charming for others (and apparently it is), it is very irritating to me as it eliminates the seriousness during the gameplay. ArmA 3 was meant to be the most realistic, strategic battle simulation game on the market. Therefore, user expectations are usually high and how much of these expactations are met is a very controversial topic.
When you play ArmA 3 with a good bunch of game-buddies this is the best game ever, but you will find the most idiotic insufficiencies even though it has been more than 2 years FYI !
CONS :
-No secondary arms visible on holster (WTF?)
-Explosions are quiet childish and unrealistic
-You can't jump without mods
-Death animations are funny
-Gore is minimized as possible
-Woundings are boringly simple
-Most important objects are not modelled for the animations. For example, healing animation is basically self-injecting a syringe of adrenalin to the leg. Ermm.. There is no syringe. Have I mentioned the animation for healing other players ? Well, no need because it is also self-injection animation. Another example, reloading the rocket launchers. There is no rockets. How about that ?
-Musics.
-Everyone plays individually in multiplayer. There is no teaming up, this is mostly due to language barriers. But these can be and should be solved with visuals.
PROS:
-Graphics.
-The world. It is practically real. I have personally went to one of the maps (islands) that actually exists. Nature and environment is very very real.
-Physics, sounds, dynamics, realism, weapons. Thumbs up.
-Openness to development
-Customizations
-My high hopes and never-ending expectations

I cannot enjoy the game in its current state but it is still addictive since I have so many fond memories with friends on it.

I can't recommend the game to anyone in its current state.

Pros:
- Unique game aspect which has yet to be challenged by another company
- Community is friendly for the most part
- Extremely fun and addicting, easy to play with friends

- Offer a ranking system, though incomplete and lacks complexity
Cons:
- You will find more bugs in this game than most
- Daybreak will try to hide behind the fact that the game is Early Access, though it's been this way for 2 years..
- Daybreak will also try to compensate the amount of bugs and fixes by providing luxurious new skins instead of dealing with major issues
- You will hear it from most people who have played this game a long time: H1Z1 has a plethora of potential, but will cease to develop under the direction of Daybreak Games, or at least at a terribly slow speed
- Updates are far and few between. Also, when there is an update, expect two things to break for every one item fixed
--------------
Despite more pros than cons, I personally recommend this game, as it a fun game to play and carries a unique structure. At the same time, expect the game to be extremely frustrating at first, as you can see many people with less than one hundred hours are very frustrated. Check out the game for yourself, as it's not terribly expensive compared to other games.
